questionEn: Which central verse of Surah Al-Fatihah combines declaring exclusive worship of Allah with seeking His help in every affair?
optionsEn: Maliki yawmid-din
Ghayril-maghdubi ‘alayhim
Iyyaka na‘budu wa iyyaka nasta‘in
Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin
explanationEn: Saying 'You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help' grounds every supplication in sincerity and dependence on Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fatihah, what specific path do believers ask Allah to guide them onto in every unit of Salah?
optionsEn: As-Sirat al-Mustaqim — the straight path of those whom Allah has favored
The path of debating angels in the heavens
The path of uninterrupted worldly wealth
The path of silent isolation from society
explanationEn: Guidance to the straight path (Sirat al-Mustaqim) is the most frequently repeated Qur'anic supplication in a Muslim's daily life.

questionEn: What supplication did Prophets Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS) recite while raising the foundations of the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
Rabbi la tadharni farda
Rabbana taqabbal minna innaka Antas-Sami‘ul-‘Alim
Rabbish-rah li sadri wa yassir li amri
explanationEn: Even while building the Sacred House itself, Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS) humbly asked Allah to accept their deed, teaching believers never to rely on deeds alone.

questionEn: Alongside asking Allah to make them and their descendants submissive Muslims (2:128), what pilgrimage-specific request did Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS) make?
optionsEn: Wa sakhkhir lanar-rih
Wa anzil ‘alayna ma'idatan minas-sama'
Wa hab lana as-sab‘al-mathani
Wa arina manasikana — 'And show us our rites of worship/pilgrimage'
explanationEn: Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS) asked Allah to teach them the sacred rites (manasik) of Hajj and accept their repentance.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:129), what did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) ask Allah to send among the descendants of Makkah?
optionsEn: A Messenger from among themselves to recite Allah's verses, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them
A king who would conquer Rome and Persia immediately
Rainstorms every single day of the year
A river of gold beneath Mount Safa
explanationEn: Allah answered this supplication centuries later by sending Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Makkah.

questionEn: What two qualities of Allah conclude the Kaaba-building dua 'Rabbana taqabbal minna' in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:127?
optionsEn: Al-Khafid and Ar-Rafi‘
Al-Muhyi and Al-Mumit
Al-Qahhar and Al-Jabbar
As-Sami‘ (The All-Hearing) and Al-‘Alim (The All-Knowing)
explanationEn: Invoking As-Sami‘ and Al-‘Alim affirms that Allah hears every whispered prayer and knows the sincerity inside the heart.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah 2:200–201, how does the Qur'an contrast shallow pilgrimage prayers with the comprehensive dua 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah...'?
optionsEn: Some ask silently while others are commanded to shout from rooftops
Some only ask for worldly good and have no share in the Hereafter, whereas believers ask for good in both worlds and protection from the Fire
The dua may only be recited outside the month of Dhul-Hijjah
Only scholars may ask for the Hereafter while merchants ask for trade
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201 teaches balanced aspiration: seeking lawful goodness in this life, eternal felicity in the next, and safety from Hellfire.

questionEn: Which believers in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:250) prayed: 'Rabbana afrigh ‘alayna sabran wa thabbit aqdamana wansurna ‘alal-qawmil-kafirin'?
optionsEn: The people of Lut before leaving their city at dawn
The sleepers of the Cave upon waking after three centuries
The companions of Hud when the barren wind approached
The faithful companions of Talut (Saul) when they marched out to face Jalut (Goliath) and his army
explanationEn: Outnumbered by Jalut's forces, the steadfast believers asked Allah to pour patience over them, make their feet firm, and grant victory.

questionEn: In the dua of Talut's faithful soldiers (2:250), what does the verb 'afrigh' ('pour out') vividly express about patience (Sabr)?
optionsEn: Asking Allah to drench the heart abundantly in patience from above, like cooling water over heat
Asking to postpone the battle until winter
Asking to forget all previous promises
Asking for patience only for a single hour
explanationEn: The imagery of pouring patience ('afrigh ‘alayna sabran') shows that true steadfastness is a gift poured by Allah into trembling hearts.

questionEn: What short supplication of the believers appears in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:285 immediately after affirming faith in Allah, His angels, Books, and Messengers?
optionsEn: Rabbi hab li min ladunka sultanan nasira
Rabbi inni massaniyad-durr
Allahumma Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir ('Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return')
explanationEn: Following 'Sami‘na wa ata‘na' ('We hear and we obey'), believers immediately ask for Allah's forgiveness, acknowledging human imperfection.

questionEn: In the closing verse of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:286), what two human slips do believers ask Allah not to hold against them?
optionsEn: Eating lawful meat or wearing new garments
Asking questions of scholars or writing contracts
Forgetting (in nasina) or making an unintentional mistake (aw akhta'na)
Traveling by sea or sleeping past noon
explanationEn: Authentic Hadith (Sahih Muslim 126) relates that Allah responded 'I have done so' to each petition in the closing verse of Al-Baqarah.

questionEn: Which three final petitions close the supplication at the end of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:286)?
optionsEn: Hide us from rain, speed up time, and silence thunder
Exempt us from fasting, charity, and pilgrimage
Pardon us (Wa‘fu ‘anna), forgive us (waghfir lana), and have mercy on us (warhamna)
Enrich us, crown us, and lengthen our shadows
explanationEn: After asking not to be burdened beyond capacity, the verse concludes with pardon, forgiveness, mercy, and victory over disbelievers.

questionEn: What does 'isran' refer to in the Al-Baqarah 2:286 plea: 'Rabbana wa la tahmil ‘alayna isran kama hamaltahu ‘alal-ladhina min qablina'?
optionsEn: Carrying luggage on a caravan journey
Ordinary daily fatigue after farming
The obligation to greet guests warmly
Heavy, restrictive legal burdens and severe covenants placed upon earlier nations
explanationEn: This dua thanks Allah for the ease of the Shariah and asks Him not to impose crushing burdens like those placed on previous communities.

questionEn: Who utters the dua in Surah Al ‘Imran (3:8): 'Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba‘da idh hadaytana wa hab lana min ladunka rahmah'?
optionsEn: The kings of ancient Persia
Those firmly grounded in knowledge (ar-rasikhuna fil-‘ilm)
Angels recording deeds at the left shoulder
Hypocrites seeking excuses to stay behind from battle
explanationEn: True scholars never feel immune to deviation; they beg Allah not to let their hearts swerve after He has guided them.

questionEn: Which Divine Name ends the Surah Al ‘Imran (3:8) prayer for steadfast hearts?
optionsEn: Al-Muqsit (The Equitable)
Ad-Darr (The Distresser)
Al-Wahhab (The Bestower of Gifts)
Al-Muntaqim (The Avenger)
explanationEn: Because steadfastness and mercy are pure gifts from Allah, the verse invokes Al-Wahhab — the Bestower without expectation of return.

questionEn: What do the God-conscious say in Surah Al ‘Imran (3:16) right before asking for forgiveness and protection from the Fire?
optionsEn: Rabbana inni nadhartu laka ma fi batni
Rabbana atina min ladunka rahmatan fil-kahf
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idatan minas-sama'
Rabbana innana amanna ('Our Lord, indeed we have believed')
explanationEn: Presenting one's faith humbly before making a request is a classic Qur'anic etiquette of dua seen in 3:16 and 3:193.

questionEn: Which majestic Qur'anic praise and supplication in Surah Al ‘Imran (3:26) begins 'Qulillahumma Malikal-mulk'?
optionsEn: Asking for permission to shorten prayers during rain
Requesting rainfall during severe drought
Acknowledging that Allah gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, honors whom He wills, and humbles whom He wills
Seeking refuge from envy when entering a marketplace
explanationEn: Surah Al ‘Imran 3:26 reminds the believer that all authority, honor, and provision belong solely to Allah's Hand.

questionEn: Who made the heartfelt prenatal vow and dua in Surah Al ‘Imran (3:35): 'Rabbi inni nadhartu laka ma fi batni muharraran fataqabbal minni'?
optionsEn: The wife of ‘Imran (mother of Maryam, AS), dedicating her unborn child to the service of Bayt al-Maqdis
Hajar (AS) while standing between Safa and Marwah
Asiyah, the wife of Fir‘awn, near the Nile river
Sarah, the wife of Ibrahim (AS), upon receiving glad tidings
explanationEn: Her sincere dedication of her child exclusively to Allah's service led to Maryam (AS) growing up in extraordinary piety and care.

questionEn: When the wife of ‘Imran gave birth to a daughter (Maryam), what protection did she immediately ask Allah for in 3:36?
optionsEn: She asked for royal wealth and silver palaces
She asked to relocate to Yemen immediately
She sought Allah's refuge for Maryam and her offspring from Satan the outcast (ash-Shaytanir-rajim)
She asked that Maryam never speak to anyone
explanationEn: Her protective dua for Maryam and her son (‘Isa AS) was honored by Allah in a unique spiritual protection.

questionEn: Seeing fresh out-of-season fruit provided miraculously to Maryam (AS) inspired which Prophet to pray 'Rabbi hab li min ladunka dhurriyyatan tayyibah'?
optionsEn: Prophet Dawud (AS)
Prophet Shu‘ayb (AS)
Prophet Hud (AS)
Prophet Zakariyya (AS)
explanationEn: Witnessing Allah's power to provide fruit out of season gave Zakariyya (AS) renewed hope to ask for righteous offspring in old age.

questionEn: What specific quality of Allah did Zakariyya (AS) invoke in Surah Al ‘Imran 3:38 when praying for a pious child?
optionsEn: Al-Mutakabbir (The Supreme)
Al-Qabid (The Withholder)
Sami‘ud-du‘a (The Hearer of Supplication)
Shadidul-‘iqab (Severe in Punishment)
explanationEn: Calling upon Allah as 'Sami‘ud-du‘a' reflects deep conviction that no whispered prayer from an aging servant goes unheard.

questionEn: Who recited the dua in Surah Al ‘Imran (3:53): 'Rabbana amanna bima anzalta wattaba‘nar-rasula faktubna ma‘ash-shahidin'?
optionsEn: The companions of Yusuf (AS) in Egypt
The fishermen of Aylah
The elders of Madyan welcoming Musa (AS)
The faithful disciples (Hawariyyun) of Prophet ‘Isa (AS)
explanationEn: After affirming their commitment as Allah's helpers, the disciples asked to be written among those who bear witness to the truth.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:147), what did the steadfast followers of past prophets ask Allah to forgive alongside their sins (dhunubana)?
optionsEn: Our writing poetry about nature
Our travelling on unpaved roads
Israfana fi amrina — our excesses/transgressions in our affairs
Our eating honey and dates
explanationEn: Asking forgiveness for both clear sins and overstepping bounds in one's affairs teaches comprehensive self-accountability in hardship.

questionEn: What five consecutive 'Rabbana' petitions appear at the close of Surah Al ‘Imran (3:191–194) for those who reflect on creation?
optionsEn: Shorten Friday prayers, abolish charity, silence wind, hide stars, and remove mountains

Save us from the Fire (3:191), recognize none saved from disgrace if cast in (3:192), forgive sins & erase misdeeds after hearing the caller to faith (3:193), and grant promised reward without disgrace on Judgment Day (3:194)
Bless our caravans, double silver coins, punish rivals immediately, end winter, and bring rain
Grant us wings to fly, invisibility, control over tides, immunity from aging, and palaces of pearl
explanationEn: These verses in Al ‘Imran (3:190–194) were recited by the Prophet ﷺ when waking up at night to look at the sky before Tahajjud.

questionEn: What did the oppressed men, women, and children in Makkah cry out for in Surah An-Nisa (4:75)?
optionsEn: To delay the sunrise until midday
To be excused from fasting Ramadan
To be given vineyards in Ta'if
To be rescued from the town of oppressors and granted a protector (waliyyan) and helper (nasira) from Allah
explanationEn: This verse validates praying urgently for the oppressed and seeking Allah's appointed protection and relief.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:114), what two purposes did Prophet ‘Isa (AS) mention when praying 'Allahumma Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idatan minas-sama''?
optionsEn: That it replace the obligation of prayer forever
That it turn all stones of Jerusalem into gold
That it last for one hour only and remain hidden from everyone
That it be a recurring celebration (‘Id) for the first and last of us, and a clear Sign from Allah
explanationEn: ‘Isa (AS) framed even a request for heavenly sustenance around spiritual gratitude, calling it an ‘Id and an Ayah, ending with 'wa Anta khayrur-raziqin'.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:162–163), what comprehensive declaration of devotion is a believer commanded to proclaim?
optionsEn: Rabbana afrigh ‘alayna sabra
Rabbi hab li min ladunka dhurriyyatan tayyibah
Qul inna salati wa nusuki wa mahyaya wa mamati lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin
Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil
explanationEn: Dedicating one's prayer, sacrifice, life, and death purely to Allah aligns every daily act with worship.

questionEn: Which supplication of repentance did Prophet Adam and Hawwa (AS) utter after eating from the forbidden tree in Surah Al-A‘raf (7:23)?
optionsEn: Rabbish-rah li sadri wa yassir li amri
Rabbi inni massaniyad-durru wa Anta arhamur-rahimin
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina qurrata a‘yun
Rabbana zalamna anfusana wa in lam taghfir lana wa tarhamna lanakunanna minal-khasirin
explanationEn: Unlike Iblis who blamed others arrogantly, Adam and Hawwa (AS) immediately owned their mistake and begged for Allah's forgiveness and mercy.

questionEn: What short defensive dua do the People of the Heights (Ashab al-A‘raf) make when their gaze turns toward the dwellers of the Fire (7:47)?
optionsEn: Rabbana taqabbal minna
Rabbana la taj‘alna ma‘al-qawmiz-zalimin ('Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people')
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
Rabbi zidni ‘ilma
explanationEn: Witnessing the consequence of injustice makes the believers instantly seek refuge with Allah from ever sharing the company of wrongdoers.

questionEn: When threatened with expulsion by his people's arrogant leaders, how did Prophet Shu‘ayb (AS) ask Allah to judge between them (7:89)?
optionsEn: Rabbi inni nadhartu laka ma fi batni
Rabbanaftah baynana wa bayna qawmina bil-haqqi wa Anta khayrul-fatihin
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idatan minas-sama'
Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahadin min ba‘di
explanationEn: Asking Allah — 'the Best of Judges/Openers' — to decide with truth expresses total reliance when human mediation fails.

questionEn: Facing Fir‘awn's threat of crucifixion immediately after embracing faith, what did the former magicians pray in Surah Al-A‘raf (7:126)?
optionsEn: Rabbana afrigh ‘alayna sabran wa tawaffana muslimin ('Pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims')
Rabbana hab lana kanza
Rabbi la tadharni farda
Rabbana akhrijna ilal-bahr
explanationEn: Their sole concern at the moment of death was dying in complete submission to Allah — showing that faith transforms fear into courage.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:151), after his anger subsided over the golden calf incident, for whom did Prophet Musa (AS) ask Allah's forgiveness?
optionsEn: For Qarun and his treasurers
For himself and for his brother Harun (AS): 'Rabbighfir li wa li-akhi wa adkhilna fi rahmatik'
For the merchants of Madyan
For Fir‘awn's charioteers
explanationEn: Musa (AS) immediately softened toward his brother Harun (AS) and united both of them under a single plea for forgiveness and mercy.

questionEn: Which title of Allah closes Prophet Musa's (AS) heartfelt supplication for himself and Harun in Surah Al-A‘raf 7:151?
optionsEn: Wa Antal-mutakabbir
Wa Anta arhamur-rahimin ('And You are the Most Merciful of the merciful')
Wa Anta shadidul-mihal
Wa Anta sari‘ul-hisab
explanationEn: This same tender closing ('Wa Anta arhamur-rahimin') also appears in the dua of Prophet Ayyub (AS) in 21:83.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:156), what response did Allah give after Musa (AS) prayed 'Waktub lana fi hadhihid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirah'?
optionsEn: Allah declared that His punishment strikes whom He wills, while His mercy encompasses all things ('wa rahmati wasi‘at kulla shay'')
Allah restricted His mercy to a single valley
Allah told them to stop praying for forty years
Allah ordered them to build ships immediately
explanationEn: Allah answered Musa's plea by reminding humanity of His all-encompassing mercy, specially decreed for those who fear Him, give zakah, and believe.

questionEn: In Surah Yunus (10:85–86), what did the oppressed believers with Musa (AS) ask Allah not to make them when confronting Fir‘awn's tyranny?
optionsEn: Builders of stone pyramids
Fitnatan lil-qawmiz-zalimin ('a trial/temptation for the wrongdoing people')
Rulers over Rome
Travelers across the desert
explanationEn: To ask not to become a 'fitnah' for oppressors means praying that oppressors never prevail over us in a way that makes them think falsehood is right.

questionEn: In Surah Hud (11:47), after Allah corrected Prophet Nuh (AS) regarding his disbelieving son, what did Nuh immediately seek refuge from?
optionsEn: Asking Allah for something of which he had no true knowledge ('an as'alaka ma laysa li bihi ‘ilm')
Returning to dry land after the flood
Preaching to his people for another day
Speaking with the animals aboard the Ark
explanationEn: Nuh (AS) modeled immediate prophetic humility: when corrected by revelation, he sought refuge from improper requests and begged for mercy.

questionEn: When pressured toward sin in Egypt, what did Prophet Yusuf (AS) tell Allah he preferred in Surah Yusuf (12:33)?
optionsEn: Prison (as-sijn) rather than answering the call to immorality, asking Allah to turn their plot away from him
Becoming a palace guard immediately
Wealth in exchange for silence
Fleeing across the sea to Yemen
explanationEn: Yusuf's (AS) dua shows that protecting one's faith and chastity outweighs worldly freedom, while acknowledging one needs Allah's help not to incline toward temptation.

questionEn: Reunited at last with his parents and given authority in Egypt, what ultimate ending did Prophet Yusuf (AS) pray for in Surah Yusuf (12:101)?
optionsEn: Erase every memory of Canaan from my mind
Make all my brothers kings of separate continents
Tawaffani musliman wa alhiqni bis-salihin ('Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous')
Let my kingdom last forever without death
explanationEn: At the pinnacle of worldly reunion and power, Yusuf (AS) stayed focused on the ultimate goal: dying in submission to Allah and joining the righteous.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:35), what two blessings did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) request for Makkah and his family?
optionsEn: Prevent all travelers from ever entering Makkah
Build seven walls of iron around the valley
Fill the city with gold mines and snow-capped peaks
Make this city (Makkah) safe/secure, and keep him and his children away from worshipping idols
explanationEn: Ibrahim (AS) linked outer security (baladan aminan) with inner spiritual purity from shirk — neither safety nor comfort suffices without pure Tawhid.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:37), why did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) explain he settled part of his family in Makkah's barren valley?
optionsEn: To mine precious stones beneath Mount Abu Qubays
Rabbana li-yuqimus-salah ('Our Lord, so that they may establish prayer')
To escape paying taxes to a northern king
To graze camels on lush green pastures
explanationEn: Even before commerce or crops existed in Makkah, its founding purpose in Ibrahim's dua was establishing Salah around Allah's Sacred House.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:40), what daily act of worship did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) ask Allah to keep alive in himself and his descendants?
optionsEn: Establishing Salah ('Rabbij‘alni muqimas-salati wa min dhurriyyati')
Building stone towers along trade routes
Fasting silently without speaking for months
Reciting poetry at seasonal fairs
explanationEn: Immediately after praying to establish Salah across generations, Ibrahim (AS) added 'Rabbana wa taqabbal du‘a' ('Our Lord, accept my supplication').

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) include in his closing forgiveness prayer in Surah Ibrahim (14:41)?
optionsEn: Only prophets and angels
Himself, his parents, and all the believers on the Day the Reckoning is established
Only the residents of Makkah during his lifetime
Only travelers aboard ships
explanationEn: Ibrahim's (AS) broad-hearted dua ('wa lil-mu'minina yawma yaqumul-hisab') teaches believers to pray for the entire Ummah alongside their parents.

questionEn: Which concise Qur'anic dua for one's parents is commanded in Surah Al-Isra (17:24) alongside lowering the wing of humility?
optionsEn: Rabbana la taj‘alna ma‘al-qawmiz-zalimin
Rabbi inni lima anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqir
Rabbi a‘udhu bika min hamazatish-shayatin
Rabbir-hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira ('My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small')
explanationEn: This verse reminds children to reciprocate their parents' lifelong care with mercy-filled supplications in both life and after their passing.

questionEn: What dual request about entering and exiting does Surah Al-Isra (17:80) teach?
optionsEn: Rabbi adkhilni mudkhala sidqin wa akhrijni mukhraja sidqin waj‘al li min ladunka sultanan nasira
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina qurrata a‘yun
Allahumma Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Rabbi zidni malan wa banin
explanationEn: Whether entering a new phase, city, or mission—like the Prophet's ﷺ Hijrah—believers ask for a truthful entry, a truthful exit, and supporting authority from Allah.

questionEn: When the young believers fled religious persecution into the cave (Surah Al-Kahf 18:10), what two things did they ask Allah for?
optionsEn: Mercy directly from Him (min ladunka rahmah) and right guidance/facility in their affair (rashada)
A vast army of elephants and horses
Immunity from hunger without ever waking up
Immediate destruction of all cities
explanationEn: Not knowing how they would survive in a bare cave, they trusted Allah to bestow special mercy and arrange a wise way forward.

questionEn: How did Prophet Zakariyya (AS) describe his old age humbly when opening his private dua in Surah Maryam (19:4)?
optionsEn: My bones have weakened and my head has glistened with white hair, yet I have never been unblessed in praying to You
I have grown too proud to ask anyone else
I have traveled across seven seas in vain
I have forgotten all the scriptures of my youth
explanationEn: Recalling Allah's past faithfulness ('wa lam akun bi-du‘a'ika Rabbi shaqiyya') fuels certainty when asking for something humanly improbable.

questionEn: In Surah Maryam (19:5–6), what was Prophet Zakariyya's (AS) deeper concern behind asking for a son to inherit from him and the family of Ya‘qub?
optionsEn: Wanting to retire from teaching prayer
Wanting someone to guard gold coins in a vault
Fearing spiritual decline among his relatives after him and wanting an heir who would carry forward prophethood, knowledge, and faith pleasing to Allah
Seeking fame in royal courts of Damascus
explanationEn: Zakariyya (AS) asked that the child be 'radiyya' (pleasing to Allah), proving his prayer sought righteous legacy rather than mere worldly lineage.

questionEn: Standing before the daunting mission of confronting Fir‘awn, what four-part dua did Prophet Musa (AS) make in Surah Ta-Ha (20:25–28)?
optionsEn: Make me wealthier than Qarun, grant me a stone palace, silence my critics, and spare me travel
Send thunderbolts, sink the Nile, turn staffs into eagles, and hide me in Sinai
Give me forty years of rest before speaking to anyone
Expand my chest, ease my task, untie the knot from my tongue so they understand my speech
explanationEn: Musa's (AS) dua is cherished by teachers, students, and speakers seeking inner calm, ease in effort, and clarity of expression.

questionEn: Immediately after asking Allah to untie the knot in his tongue (20:27–29), whom did Musa (AS) ask Allah to appoint as his helper from his family?
optionsEn: His father-in-law Shu‘ayb, to lead the army
A royal scribe from Fir‘awn's palace
His cousin Qarun, to manage supplies
His brother Harun (AS), to strengthen his back and share in his task
explanationEn: Musa (AS) valued righteous companionship so that together they could glorify and remember Allah abundantly ('kay nusabbihaka kathira').

questionEn: Which short three-word Qur'anic dua in Surah Ta-Ha (20:114) is the only thing Allah explicitly instructed the Prophet ﷺ to ask an increase in?
optionsEn: Rabbi zidni jaha ('Increase me in status')
Rabbi zidni ‘ilma ('My Lord, increase me in knowledge')
Rabbi zidni mala ('Increase me in wealth')
Rabbi zidni ‘umra ('Increase me in lifespan')
explanationEn: Allah did not instruct His Messenger ﷺ to pray for more gold or territory, but specifically commanded him to pray: 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'

questionEn: After years of severe illness and loss, how did Prophet Ayyub (AS) phrase his dignified supplication in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:83)?
optionsEn: Anni massaniyad-durru wa Anta arhamur-rahimin ('Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful')
Punish those who abandoned my home
Take away my patience so I may complain loudly
Why have You left me alone without wealth?
explanationEn: Ayyub (AS) gently stated his condition and praised Allah's boundless mercy without complaint or impatience, and Allah immediately healed and restored him.

questionEn: Inside the darkness of the belly of the whale, what three spiritual realities did Prophet Yunus (AS) combine in his famous dua (21:87)?
optionsEn: Reciting historical genealogies of Nineveh
Asking for wealth, fame, and a ship of cedar
Blaming the sailors, questioning the storm, and demanding dry land
Tawhid ('La ilaha illa Anta'), Glorification ('subhanaka'), and humble confession ('inni kuntu minaz-zalimin')
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said no Muslim calls upon Allah with the dua of Dhun-Nun (Yunus AS) in any matter except that Allah responds to him.

questionEn: What did Prophet Zakariyya (AS) call Allah when praying in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:89): 'Rabbi la tadharni fardan...'?
optionsEn: Wa Anta khayrul-warithin ('And You are the Best of Inheritors')
Wa Anta khayrul-fasilin
Wa Anta khayrul-munzilin
Wa Anta khayrul-makirin
explanationEn: Even while asking not to be left childless, Zakariyya (AS) affirmed that Allah alone remains forever as the Best of Inheritors.

questionEn: Upon embarking on the Ark after the flood began, what supplication did Allah command Prophet Nuh (AS) to say in Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:29)?
optionsEn: Rabbi anzilni munzalan mubarakan wa Anta khayrul-munzilin ('My Lord, land me at a blessed landing place, for You are the Best to accommodate')
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina qurrata a‘yun
Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li
Rabbi sakhkhir liyad-dawabba fil-barr
explanationEn: Travelers often recite this Qur'anic prayer when arriving at a new destination, hotel, or city, asking Allah for a blessed stay.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:97–98), what spiritual protection is the Prophet ﷺ taught to seek from Allah?
optionsEn: Refuge from forgetting poetry verses
Refuge from the whisperings/incitements of devils (hamazatish-shayatin) and refuge from their very presence near him (an yahdurun)
Refuge from speaking with travelers
Refuge from cold mountain winds in winter
explanationEn: Seeking refuge both from demonic suggestions and from their presence guards the heart during worship, anger, and daily interactions.

questionEn: What concise, all-encompassing dua concludes Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:118)?
optionsEn: Rabbighfir warham wa Anta khayrur-rahimin ('My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the Best of the merciful')
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
Rabbi hab li hukman wa alhiqni bis-salihin
Rabbi zidni ‘ilma
explanationEn: Short enough to memorize in seconds, this concluding verse of Al-Mu'minun gathers the two greatest needs of every servant: pardon and mercy.

questionEn: How do the 'Servants of the Most Merciful' (‘Ibadur-Rahman) pray regarding Hellfire in Surah Al-Furqan (25:65)?
optionsEn: Rabbanas-rif ‘anna ‘adhaba jahannama inna ‘adhabaha kana gharama ('Avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is an inseparable ruin')
Let us taste its heat for one day only
Delay its mention until old age
Turn it away only from scholars
explanationEn: Despite their night prayers, humility, and charity, ‘Ibadur-Rahman never feel safe from Allah's punishment and earnestly ask Him to turn it away.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Furqan (25:74), what two blessings do ‘Ibadur-Rahman ask regarding their spouses, children, and spiritual leadership?
optionsEn: That they be appointed kings over neighboring tribes
That their families own the largest palaces and fleets
That their children never travel away from home
That spouses and offspring be the coolness/comfort of their eyes (qurrata a‘yun), and that Allah make them leaders/models for the righteous (lil-muttaqina imama)
explanationEn: 'Coolness of the eyes' means seeing loved ones obey Allah joyfully, while being an 'imam for the righteous' means inspiring others in goodness.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu‘ara (26:83–85), what four gifts did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) ask Allah for regarding wisdom, legacy, and Paradise?
optionsEn: Wisdom/sound judgment (hukm), joining the righteous, a truthful reputation among later generations (lisana sidq), and inheritance of the Garden of Bliss
Exemption from pilgrimage, endless sleep, and secret caves
Mastery over storms, silence of critics, palaces in Babylon, and silver crowns
Gold shields, swift horses, long wars, and desert fortresses
explanationEn: Ibrahim's (AS) plea for 'lisana sidqin fil-akhirin' was answered as billions across Judaism, Christianity, and Islam honor his name to this day.

questionEn: What did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) specifically ask not to experience on the Day of Resurrection in Surah Ash-Shu‘ara (26:87)?
optionsEn: Do not let me speak before angels
Do not let the sun shine upon me
Do not ask me about my travels
Wa la tukhzini yawma yub‘athun ('And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected')
explanationEn: This precedes the famous verses (26:88–89) declaring that neither wealth nor sons will avail on that Day—only one who brings Allah a sound heart (qalbin salim).

questionEn: When Prophet Sulayman (AS) smiled upon hearing the ant warn its colony, what gratitude dua did he immediately make in Surah An-Naml (27:19)?
optionsEn: Rabbi awzi‘ni an ashkura ni‘matakallati an‘amta ‘alayya wa ‘ala walidayya wa an a‘mala salihan tardah
Rabbi hab li mulkan akbara min hadha
Rabbinsurni ‘alal-qawmil-kafirin
Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li
explanationEn: Realizing the miracle of understanding the ant's speech, Sulayman (AS) felt humbled rather than proud, asking Allah to inspire him to be grateful and righteous.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas (28:16), after accidentally striking a man fatally in Egypt, how did Prophet Musa (AS) seek immediate repentance?
optionsEn: He waited seven years before making istighfar
Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li ('My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me')
He blamed the bystander and refused to pray
He offered a gold coin to the court guard
explanationEn: Musa (AS) recognized Satan's provocation, owned his slip immediately before Allah, and Allah forgave him at once.

questionEn: Arriving exhausted, hungry, and homeless in Madyan after helping two women water their flock, what did Prophet Musa (AS) pray in the shade (28:24)?
optionsEn: Give me the throne of Egypt before nightfall
Rabbi inni lima anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqir ('My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me')
Send rain of silver upon these wells
Let me never speak to strangers again
explanationEn: Even in dire need, Musa (AS) asked with utmost courtesy—simply expressing his poverty before Allah's goodness, which brought him shelter, work, and marriage that very day.

questionEn: What did Prophet Musa (AS) say while fleeing Egypt alone toward Madyan without knowing the road (Surah Al-Qasas 28:22)?
optionsEn: I need no guidance in the desert
‘Asa Rabbi an yahdiyani sawa'as-sabil ('Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound, straight way')
Hide the sun behind clouds forever
Return me back to Fir‘awn's palace
explanationEn: This short hopeful phrase is an inspiring dua whenever someone feels lost on a road, career path, or life decision.

questionEn: Which brief prayer of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) in Surah As-Saffat (37:100) was answered with the glad tidings of a forbearing boy (Isma‘il AS)?
optionsEn: Rabbi anzilni munzalan mubaraka
Rabbi hab li minas-salihin ('My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous')
Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
Rabbi inni massaniyad-durr
explanationEn: When migrating away from his people for Allah's sake, Ibrahim (AS) asked simply for a righteous child—and Allah blessed him with Isma‘il (AS).

questionEn: In Surah Sad (38:35), what did Prophet Sulayman (AS) ask Allah for right before asking for an unmatched kingdom?
optionsEn: Give me forty ships
Rabbighfir li ('My Lord, forgive me')
Make iron melt like wax
Silence the birds forever
explanationEn: Sulayman (AS) began his monumental request with seeking forgiveness ('Rabbighfir li') and closed it by invoking Allah's Name Al-Wahhab.

questionEn: According to Surah Ghafir (40:7–9), who continuously praises Allah and makes heartfelt dua for believers who repent and follow His path?
optionsEn: Only pilgrims standing on Mount Uhud
The angels who bear the Throne and those around it
The scribes of ancient Babylon
The stars in the northern sky
explanationEn: The Throne-bearing angels invoke Allah's vast mercy and knowledge, praying that He admit believers—along with their righteous parents, spouses, and offspring—into Gardens of Eternity.

questionEn: At what milestone of human maturity does Surah Al-Ahqaf (46:15) teach the righteous believer to pray 'Rabbi awzi‘ni an ashkura ni‘matak...'?
optionsEn: When reaching full strength and the age of forty years
Upon turning seven years old
At the age of ninety only
Only after crossing the ocean
explanationEn: At age forty, the mature believer reflects gratefully on blessings to oneself and parents, prays for righteous offspring, and turns back in repentance.

questionEn: After centuries of patient preaching met with mockery and rejection, what concise three-word dua did Prophet Nuh (AS) make in Surah Al-Qamar (54:10)?
optionsEn: Anni maghlubun fantasir ('Indeed, I am overpowered, so help/vindicate [me]')
Give me another thousand years of wealth
Send gold upon their rooftops
Sink the mountains before dawn
explanationEn: When every human avenue was exhausted, Nuh's (AS) brief cry of helplessness opened the gates of the sky.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hashr (59:10), what negative feeling toward earlier and fellow believers do later generations pray Allah removes from their hearts?
optionsEn: Ghill — rancor, malice, or envy ('wa la taj‘al fi qulubina ghillan lilladhina amanu')
Joy during Eid celebrations
Love of traveling to Makkah
Respect for elders and scholars
explanationEn: Praying for those who preceded us in faith while asking Allah to purify our hearts of resentment preserves unity across generations of the Ummah.

questionEn: What gentle dua of surrender did Ibrahim (AS) and those with him make in Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:4)?
optionsEn: Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Rabbi zidni ‘ilma
Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
Rabbana ‘alayka tawakkalna wa ilayka anabna wa ilaykal-masir
explanationEn: Even when taking a firm stand for faith, Ibrahim (AS) anchored his heart in reliance (tawakkul), turning back to Allah (inabah), and remembering the final return.

questionEn: On the Day of Judgment, what light-focused dua will the believers make according to Surah At-Tahrim (66:8)?
optionsEn: Rabbana atmim lana nurana waghfir lana innaka ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir
Give us lamps made of bronze
Darken the sky above the plains
Return us to worldly markets
explanationEn: As the hypocrites lose their light before the Bridge, true believers beg Allah to perfect their light and forgive them completely.

questionEn: Facing torture under Fir‘awn's roof, what noble home did Asiyah (RA) pray for in Surah At-Tahrim (66:11)?
optionsEn: A treasury of gold coins in Memphis
A marble palace beside the Nile
A ship to sail back to Madyan
Rabbi-bni li ‘indaka baytan fil-jannah ('My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise')
explanationEn: Notice her refined priority: she asked 'near You' (‘indaka) even before mentioning 'a house in Paradise', valuing closeness to Allah above the mansion itself.

questionEn: In Surah Nuh (71:28), what special group did Prophet Nuh (AS) include in his closing forgiveness prayer alongside his parents and all believing men and women?
optionsEn: Whoever brings gifts of silver to his palace
Whoever memorizes desert constellations
Wa li-man dakhala baytiya mu'minan ('and whoever enters my house as a believer')
Whoever trades timber along the river
explanationEn: Scholars note this teaches hospitality with spiritual generosity: praying for the believing guests who enter our homes.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:186), what immediate reassuring answer does Allah give right after saying 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me'?
optionsEn: Ask an angel to speak on your behalf first
Wait until you reach Jerusalem before praying
Fa-inni qarib — 'Indeed, I am near; I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me'
Send a messenger with written petitions every month
explanationEn: Unlike other questions in the Qur'an where Allah says 'Say (Qul)...', in 2:186 Allah removes any intermediary phrase and answers directly: 'Indeed, I am near.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Baqarah (2:186), what two responses are required from believers so that they may be rightly guided when calling on Allah?
optionsEn: Let them travel alone without provisions
Let them memorize astronomical charts
Let them fast silently for a full year and wear wool
Let them respond to Allah's call (fal-yastajibu li) and believe firmly in Him (wal-yu'minu bi)
explanationEn: Allah promises nearness and response to dua, while inviting believers to respond to His commands and trust Him completely.

questionEn: In Surah Ghafir (40:60), what promise and stern warning accompany Allah's command 'Ud‘uni astajib lakum' ('Call upon Me; I will respond to you')?
optionsEn: Only spoken Arabic poetry counts as supplication
Those who are too arrogant to worship/supplicate to Him will enter Hell in humiliation
Dua is valid only once a year in Sha‘ban
Supplication is optional only for prophets
explanationEn: Allah links dua directly to worship (‘ibadah): refusing to ask Allah out of self-sufficiency is treated as spiritual arrogance.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-A‘raf (7:55), what two inner and outer manners are commanded when calling upon Allah?
optionsEn: Shouting as loudly as possible in markets
Speaking casually while laughing in distraction
Competing with neighbors over poetic rhymes
Tadarru‘an (in humility/earnestness) and khufyah (privately/quietly), avoiding transgression (mu‘tadin)
explanationEn: Sincere, humble, quiet supplication without shouting or asking for sinful/impossible things reflects Prophetic and Qur'anic etiquette.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:56), what two contrasting attitudes should reside together in a believer's heart during dua?
optionsEn: Doubt and impatience
Khawfan wa tama‘a — fear (of His displeasure) and ardent hope (in His mercy)
Anger and despair
Pride and carelessness
explanationEn: Balancing reverent awe (khawf) with hopeful longing (tama‘) keeps dua from turning into either presumption or hopelessness.

questionEn: Which Divine attribute does Surah Al-A‘raf (7:180) instruct believers to use when making supplication?
optionsEn: Names of ancient kings and palaces
Secret numerical codes unknown to humanity
Titles invented by tribal poets
Al-Asma' al-Husna — Allah's Most Beautiful Names ('So invoke Him by them')
explanationEn: Choosing the Beautiful Name that matches your need—such as Ya Ghaffar for forgiveness or Ya Razzaq for provision—is a Qur'anic key to dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:110), which two Names of Allah are believers told they may call upon equally, as all Beautiful Names belong to Him?
optionsEn: Al-Malik or Sultan only in winter
Ad-Dahr or Al-Layl
Allah or Ar-Rahman ('Call upon Allah or call upon Ar-Rahman')
Al-Qalam or Al-Mizan
explanationEn: When polytheists in Makkah mocked the Prophet ﷺ for saying 'Ya Rahman', revelation clarified that invoking Allah or Ar-Rahman invokes the One True Lord.

questionEn: What gentle balance of voice in Salah and dua does Surah Al-Isra (17:110) prescribe?
optionsEn: Shout louder than thunder at all times
Neither raise your voice too loudly nor whisper it completely inaudibly, but seek a middle way between them
Sing every phrase in theatrical melodies
Never move your tongue even in private
explanationEn: Seeking a measured middle tone protects focus and reverence without disturbing others or slipping into mere silent thought.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Furqan (25:77), what gives human beings their true worth in the sight of Allah?
optionsEn: The length of their genealogies
The height of their stone fortresses
The number of gold coins they hoard
Their supplication and worship ('Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your dua/prayer')
explanationEn: Without turning to Allah in prayer and humility, human existence loses its spiritual purpose and honor.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ was mocked and felt his heart constricted by opponents' words, what worship remedy did Allah prescribe in Surah Al-Hijr (15:97–99)?
optionsEn: Glorifying Allah with praise (Sabbih bi-hamdi Rabbik), being among those who prostrate, and worshipping until certainty (death) comes
Abandoning Makkah for a desert island
Writing angry satires back to the poets
Refusing to speak to anyone for a year
explanationEn: Tasbih, Sujud, and steadfast worship heal a bruised heart far more deeply than trading insults.

questionEn: In Surah Maryam (19:2–3), how is the manner of Prophet Zakariyya's (AS) supplication described?
optionsEn: A public proclamation from the Temple roof
A loud debate before the Sanhedrin
Nida'an khafiyya — a quiet, discreet, private call to his Lord
An engraved letter buried under olive trees
explanationEn: Zakariyya (AS) prayed softly in private ('nida'an khafiyya'), showing that sincerity needs no audience when calling upon the All-Hearing.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Anbiya (21:90), what three spiritual habits characterized Zakariyya's (AS) household so that Allah answered their prayers?
optionsEn: Hastening to good deeds, calling upon Allah in hope and awe, and remaining deeply humble (khashi‘in) before Him
Building tall stone monuments, hoarding silver, and fasting only on Mondays
Memorizing riddles, wearing silk, and speaking only in metaphors
Avoiding all neighbors, sleeping all afternoon, and traveling constantly
explanationEn: Proactive goodness combined with humble, hopeful dua attracts Allah's swift response.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:76), what should severe hardship normally prompt a people to do before Allah?
optionsEn: Boast about their resilience
Stop giving charity until times improve
Blame the stars and seasons
Humble themselves before their Lord and supplicate earnestly (yattadarra‘un)
explanationEn: Trials are wake-up calls meant to soften hearts into humility and sincere dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:45), what two spiritual supports are paired together for seeking help in life's difficulties?
optionsEn: Silence and fasting alone
Debate and solitude
Commerce and travel
Patience (Sabr) and Prayer (Salah)
explanationEn: Turning to Salah with steadfast patience anchors the believer even when solutions take time.

questionEn: What comfort did Allah give Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Surah Ad-Duha (93:3–5) that inspires hopeful dua during quiet seasons?
optionsEn: Wait until rain falls before praying
Leave all worship during winter nights
Your Lord has neither forsaken you nor is displeased; the Hereafter is better for you than the first life, and soon your Lord will give you until you are well-pleased
Never ask for anything in this world
explanationEn: When revelation paused briefly, Surah Ad-Duha reassured the Prophet ﷺ of Allah's unwavering love and future bounty.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Sharh (94:5–6), what hopeful principle accompanies hardship?
optionsEn: Ease comes only to kings
Hardship lasts forever without relief
Prayer stops working during distress
Indeed, with hardship comes ease ('Inna ma‘al-‘usri yusra'), repeated twice for certainty
explanationEn: Note the phrasing 'ma‘al-‘usri' (WITH hardship, not merely after it): Allah plants seeds of relief inside the very test itself.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Sharh (94:7–8), what are believers told to do immediately upon finishing one demanding duty or task?
optionsEn: Seek praise from rulers
Forget prayer until next Friday
Boast to friends about finishing early
Stand upright in further worship/effort (fansab) and direct all longing and hope toward your Lord (wa ila Rabbika farghab)
explanationEn: Turning one's longing ('farghab') toward Allah after every completed task keeps the heart spiritually alive.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:9), how did Allah respond when the believers cried out for help (tastaghithuna Rabbakum) at the Battle of Badr?
optionsEn: He delayed answering for ten years
He told them to retreat to Makkah
He answered immediately by reinforcing them with a thousand angels following one after another
He sent a snowstorm across Madinah
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ intense, tearful dua at Badr—raising his hands until his cloak fell—brought swift angelic aid.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:156), what short phrase of return (Istirja‘) do the patient say whenever calamity strikes?
optionsEn: La ilaha illa Anta only on Eid
Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil only at weddings
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un ('Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return')
Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi when eating
explanationEn: Saying Istirja‘ immediately upon loss opens the door to Allah's blessings, mercy, and guidance (2:157).

questionEn: What phrase did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) say when cast into the fire, and which the Companions also recited at Hamra' al-Asad (Surah Al ‘Imran 3:173)?
optionsEn: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi
Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil ('Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs')
explanationEn: Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) narrated that both Ibrahim (AS) facing the fire and Muhammad ﷺ facing renewed threat spoke these fearless words of reliance.

questionEn: When Prophet Ya‘qub (AS) suffered overwhelming grief over Yusuf and Binyamin, to whom alone did he address his complaint (Surah Yusuf 12:86)?
optionsEn: Innama ashku baththi wa huzni ilallah ('I only complain of my suffering and grief to Allah')
To passing merchant caravans
To the royal court of Egypt
To the elders of neighboring tribes
explanationEn: Pouring out raw sorrow to Allah is not impatience—it is the highest form of intimacy and trust in Him.

questionEn: What comforting words of Prophet Ya‘qub (AS) in Surah Yusuf (12:87) forbid despairing during prolonged unanswered tests?
optionsEn: La tay'asu min rawhillah ('Do not despair of relief/mercy from Allah')
Stop praying once seven years pass
Seek comfort in astrology
Accept sorrow without ever hoping again
explanationEn: Ya‘qub (AS) reminded his sons that only disbelieving hearts lose hope in Allah's soothing relief (rawhillah).

questionEn: When Prophet Musa (AS) was trapped with the sea ahead and Fir‘awn's army behind (26:62), what fearless statement of trust did he declare?
optionsEn: We are surely overtaken with no escape
Let us surrender our belongings to Fir‘awn
Kalla, inna ma‘iya Rabbi sayahdin ('No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me')
Wait until winter freezes the water
explanationEn: Before the sea even parted, Musa's (AS) certainty in Allah's companionship unlocked the miracle.

questionEn: In Cave Thawr with pursuers right outside (Surah At-Tawbah 9:40), what reassuring words did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ speak to Abu Bakr (RA)?
optionsEn: Wait until next month
La tahzan innAllaha ma‘ana ('Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us')
We have brought a hidden army
Climb down the cliff silently
explanationEn: Allah then sent down His tranquility (sakinah) upon him and aided him with unseen forces.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:129), what seven-word-style statement of complete reliance is taught if people turn away?
optionsEn: Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
HasbiyAllahu la ilaha illa Huwa, ‘alayhi tawakkaltu wa Huwa Rabbul-‘arshil-‘azim
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
explanationEn: This majestic closing verse of Surah At-Tawbah also became a cherished daily morning and evening dhikr.

questionEn: What did Prophet Dawud (AS) do immediately in Surah Sad (38:24) upon realizing his test in judgment?
optionsEn: He locked the palace gates
He sought forgiveness from his Lord (fastaghfara Rabbahu), fell down bowing in prostration, and turned back in repentance (anab)
He argued with the angels for three days
He dismissed the litigants and went hunting
explanationEn: Dawud's (AS) instant combination of istighfar, sujud, and turning back to Allah models noble prophetic responsiveness.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Kahf (18:23–24) instruct a believer to frame any promise or future plan?
optionsEn: Swear by the sun and moon
Never say 'I will do that tomorrow' without saying 'In sha Allah' ('If Allah wills'), and remember your Lord if you forget
Keep every plan completely secret until midnight
Sign three copies in ink before speaking
explanationEn: Attaching 'In sha Allah' to future intentions is a continuous mini-dua acknowledging that all outcomes depend on Allah's will.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf (18:39), what phrase of gratitude and humility should the owner of a thriving garden say upon entering it?
optionsEn: Fortune favors the bold alone
Look what my own cleverness produced
Ma sha'Allahu la quwwata illa billah ('What Allah wills [occurs]; there is no power except through Allah')
Nothing can ever harm my harvest
explanationEn: Remembering Allah when admiring blessings guards against arrogance and invites His ongoing protection.

questionEn: When Prophet Ibrahim (AS) discovered his elder guests were angels in disguise in Surah Hud (11:69–72), what impossible-seeming glad tiding amazed his wife Sarah?
optionsEn: Finding a buried chest of emeralds under Hebron
Giving birth to Ishaq (AS), and after Ishaq, Ya‘qub (AS), despite both parents' advanced old age
Flying across the desert on clouds
Ruling over Egypt for fifty years
explanationEn: The angels reminded Sarah: 'Do you wonder at the decree of Allah?' — reinforcing that nothing lies beyond Allah's power in dua.

questionEn: What did the righteous man in Surah Yasin (36:26–27) wish when admitted immediately to Paradise after being martyred by his people?
optionsEn: If only I had never spoken a single word
If only my house were rebuilt with marble
If only my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored ones
If only my people were struck with lightning at once
explanationEn: Even after death, his compassionate heart wished his people could taste the beauty of Allah's forgiveness and turn toward faith.

questionEn: In Surah Az-Zumar (39:53), what sweeping call of hope does Allah address to His servants who have transgressed against themselves?
optionsEn: Conceal your repentance until old age
Only scholars may seek mercy
La taqnatu min rahmatillah — 'Do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins'
Forgiveness is closed after ten mistakes
explanationEn: Known as one of the most hopeful verses in the entire Qur'an, 39:53 invites immediate repentance and trust in Al-Ghafur Ar-Rahim.

questionEn: In Surah Az-Zumar (39:46), what opening invocation did the Prophet ﷺ recite in his Tahajjud opening dua (alongside 'Creator of the heavens and earth')?
optionsEn: Rabbi inni massaniyad-durr
Allahumma Fatiras-samawati wal-ard, ‘Alimal-ghaybi wash-shahadah, Anta tahkumu bayna ‘ibadik...
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ combined this exact Qur'anic verse (39:46) with the names of Jibril, Mika'il, and Israfil when beginning night prayer.

questionEn: What protective dua is taught by the opening command of Surah Al-Falaq (113:1)?
optionsEn: Qul at‘imu al-miskin
Qul a‘udhu bi-Malikil-bahr
Qul a‘udhu bi-Rabbil-falaq ('Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak')
Qul siru fil-ard
explanationEn: Surah Al-Falaq teaches seeking refuge in Allah from created harms, the darkness of night, sorcery, and the envier when he envies.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nas (114:1–6), what three titles of Allah does the believer invoke when seeking protection from whispering evil?
optionsEn: Shadid al-‘iqab, Al-Muntaqim, and Al-Qabid
Rabb ash-shams, Rabb al-qamar, and Rabb an-nujum
Rabb an-nas (Lord of mankind), Malik an-nas (Sovereign of mankind), and Ilah an-nas (God of mankind)
Khaliq al-jibal, Basiṭ al-bahr, and Munzil al-matar
explanationEn: Invoking Allah's Lordship, Kingship, and Divinity protects the heart from the retreating whisperer (al-waswas al-khannas) among jinn and humans.

questionEn: What specific form of harm is mentioned in the final verse of Surah Al-Falaq (113:5)?
optionsEn: From traveling by camel at noon
From the coldness of mountain springs
Min sharri hasidin idha hasad ('From the evil of an envier when he envies')
From forgetting trade invoices
explanationEn: Reciting Al-Falaq and An-Nas daily shields the believer from envy, malice, and unseen spiritual harm.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:109), what humble group of believers used to say 'Rabbana amanna faghfir lana warhamna wa Anta khayrur-rahimin'?
optionsEn: The scribes of ancient Babylon
The righteous believers whom arrogant disbelievers used to mock and laugh at in worldly life
The builders of the Tower of Haman
The sailors of Prophet Yunus's ship
explanationEn: Allah honored their steady, mocked supplication by rewarding them with eternal success on the Day of Judgment.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:197), when Allah commands Hajj pilgrims to take provisions, what does He identify as the very best provision?
optionsEn: Letters of recommendation from tribal chiefs
Extra chests of silk robes
At-Taqwa — God-consciousness and piety ('Fa-inna khayraz-zadi at-taqwa')
Seven jars of spiced honey
explanationEn: Packing supplies for a journey is wise, yet Taqwa is the spiritual luggage that carries a pilgrim into accepted worship and answered dua.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Baqarah (2:198), where are pilgrims specifically reminded to remember Allah abundantly upon pouring down from ‘Arafat?
optionsEn: On the summit of Mount Uhud
‘Indal-Mash‘aril-Haram (at Muzdalifah)
Inside the marketplace of Ta'if
At the port of Yanbu
explanationEn: Standing at Al-Mash‘ar al-Haram in Muzdalifah at Fajr is a prime moment of dhikr and dua during Hajj.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:200), what comparison is drawn for remembering Allah after completing the rites of Hajj?
optionsEn: Speak only in rhymed proverbs
Remember only the dates of market fairs
Remain completely silent for forty days
Remember Allah as you remember your forefathers, or with even greater intensity of remembrance
explanationEn: Allah redirected pre-Islamic boasting about ancestors after pilgrimage into fervent dhikr and gratitude to Him.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:27–28), what purpose of the annual pilgrimage call proclaimed by Prophet Ibrahim (AS) relates directly to remembrance of Allah?
optionsEn: That they may trade gemstones without paying tax
That they may construct personal cottages inside the Haram
That they may compete in horse racing alone
That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the Name of Allah on known days over what He provided them
explanationEn: Pronouncing Allah's Name ('yadhkurusmallah') in Talbiyah, Takbir, and sacrifice infuses all pilgrimage acts with gratitude.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nur (24:36–37), how are the houses Allah permitted to be raised and His Name mentioned in them described?
optionsEn: Stone watchtowers along mountain borders
Caravanserais used strictly for wool auctions
Masajid where His Name is glorified morning and evening by people whom neither trade nor sale distracts from remembrance of Allah
Private palaces closed to travelers
explanationEn: Entering the Masjid to remember Allah morning and evening keeps commerce and worldly tasks from crowding out the soul.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab (33:41–42), how are believers commanded to remember Allah?
optionsEn: Only when traveling across deserts
Only after completing a business contract
Dhikran kathira ('with abundant remembrance') and glorifying Him morning and evening
Only once a month on the crescent night
explanationEn: Abundant dhikr softens the heart and brings Allah's mercy and peace upon the believer (33:43).

questionEn: According to Surah Ar-Ra‘d (13:28), what priceless inner state is produced specifically by the remembrance of Allah?
optionsEn: Tranquility and reassurance of hearts ('Ala bi-dhikrillahi tatma'innul-qulub')
Forgetfulness of family duties
Fear of lawful livelihood
Restless ambition for fame
explanationEn: Anxiety eases and hearts settle into deep peace when anchored in regular remembrance of Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:152), what reciprocal promise does Allah make when believers remember Him?
optionsEn: Forget your duties and focus solely on travel
Fadhkuruni adhkurkum ('So remember Me; I will remember you')
Remember kings and I will honor you
Remember Me only in Makkah and I will send rain
explanationEn: Knowing that the Creator of the universe remembers His servant the moment the servant remembers Him transforms every tasbih into a sacred encounter.

questionEn: In Surah Taha (20:14), why did Allah command Prophet Musa (AS) to establish Salah at the sacred valley of Tuwa?
optionsEn: To collect tribute from passing caravans
To build a brick wall around the bush
Li-dhikri ('for My remembrance')
To announce new lunar calendars
explanationEn: Prayer itself exists to keep the remembrance of Allah alive in the heart.

questionEn: In Surah Al-‘Ankabut (29:45), what does Allah say is 'greater' (akbar) even than Salah's protection against indecency and evil?
optionsEn: Traveling across seven seas
Wa la-dhikrullahi akbar ('And the remembrance of Allah is greater')
Accumulating silver coins
Building stone bridges
explanationEn: Allah's remembrance is both the soul of prayer and Allah's remembrance of His servant, surpassing all else in spiritual weight.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab (33:56), what loving practice are believers commanded regarding Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Sallu ‘alayhi wa sallimu taslima ('Send blessings upon him and greet him with abundant peace')
Mention him only during Rajab
Build bronze statues in his honor
Avoid mentioning his name in Masjid prayers
explanationEn: Because Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, believers join that celestial choir with Salawat—especially before dua and on Fridays.

questionEn: In Surah Nuh (71:10–12), what worldly and family blessings does Prophet Nuh (AS) promise accompany regular Istighfar?
optionsEn: Wings to cross mountain ranges
Turning all desert sand into pearls
Exemption from aging and never needing sleep
Abundant rain from the sky, increase in wealth and children, and gardens and rivers
explanationEn: Seeking forgiveness sincerely not only purifies sins—it opens doors of sustenance, rain, family blessing, and inner relief.

questionEn: In Surah Hud (11:3 & 11:52), what two steps does Prophet Hud (AS) pair together to bring strength upon strength?
optionsEn: Digging deep wells and building high towers
Fasting silently and traveling alone
Seeking forgiveness from your Lord (Istighfar) and turning to Him in repentance (Tawbah)
Accumulating weapons and storing grain
explanationEn: Prophet Hud (AS) taught that returning to Allah through Istighfar and Tawbah brings spiritual and physical strength ('quwwatan ila quwwatikum').

questionEn: In Surah Hud (11:90), which two Beautiful Names did Prophet Shu‘ayb (AS) remind his people of when urging them to seek forgiveness and repent?
optionsEn: Jabbar and Mutakabbir
Qabid and Khafid
Rahim (Merciful) and Wadud (Affectionate/Loving)
Qahhar and Muntaqim
explanationEn: 'Inna Rabbi Rahimun Wadud' assures the repentant soul that Allah does not merely pardon reluctantly—He loves those who turn back to Him.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:222), which two types of people does Allah explicitly declare He loves?
optionsEn: Those who boast of lineage and hoard gold
Those who sleep past dawn and avoid neighbors
Those who constantly repent (at-tawwabin) and those who purify themselves (al-mutatahhirin)
Those who debate endlessly without acting
explanationEn: Inner repentance and outer purity (wudu/ghusl) both attract Allah's love and prepare the servant for accepted dua.

questionEn: When Prophet Ibrahim (AS) prayed in Surah Ash-Shu‘ara (26:78–82) describing his Lord, which acts of care did he attribute solely to Allah?
optionsEn: He controls only the heavens while stars rule earth
He created me and guides me, feeds me and gives me drink, heals me when I am ill, and will cause me to die then bring me to life
He delegates mercy to idols of stone
He leaves me to heal myself without help
explanationEn: Notice Ibrahim's (AS) courtesy: 'When I am ill, it is He who heals me'—attributing illness to himself and healing to Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:112), what concise prayer did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ offer concerning truth and slanderers?
optionsEn: Rabbiahkum bil-haqq, wa Rabbunar-Rahmanul-musta‘anu ‘ala ma tasifun
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
Rabbi la tadharni farda
explanationEn: Asking Allah to judge with truth and seeking help from Ar-Rahman against false accusations keeps the believer dignified under slander.

questionEn: In Surah Maryam (19:18), what spontaneous prayer of protection did Maryam (AS) utter when an angel appeared before her in human form?
optionsEn: Bring me fruit from the garden
Tell me the future of Egypt
Stay and speak until sunset
Inni a‘udhu bir-Rahmani minka in kunta taqiyya ('Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you fear Allah')
explanationEn: Seeking refuge in Ar-Rahman immediately in a moment of alarm shows deep spiritual instinct and modesty.

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf (12:64), as Prophet Ya‘qub (AS) reluctantly sent Binyamin to Egypt, to whose protection did he entrust him?
optionsEn: To the merchants' silver scales
To written amulets from Canaan
Fallahu khayrun hafizan wa Huwa arhamur-rahimin ('Allah is the Best Guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful')
To the caravan guards of Damascus
explanationEn: Reciting 'Fallahu khayrun hafizan' when parting from loved ones places them in the safest possible care.

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf (12:18), what phrase did Prophet Ya‘qub (AS) utter when his sons brought Yusuf's bloodstained shirt?
optionsEn: Leave my home and never return
There is no hope left in this world
I shall break every staff in sorrow
Fa-sabrun jamil, wallahul-musta‘anu ‘ala ma tasifun ('So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One sought for help against what you describe')
explanationEn: Sabr jamil (beautiful patience) means bearing heartbreak with dignity and complaining only to Allah, not lashing out at creation.

questionEn: What did Prophet Musa (AS) ask Allah in Surah Al-A‘raf (7:143) that revealed both his intense love for Allah and human limits in this world?
optionsEn: Show me the palaces of future kings
Give me wings to visit the moon
Show me the treasures beneath Sinai
Rabbi arini anzur ilayk ('My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You')
explanationEn: Allah gently told Musa (AS) 'Lan tarani' ('You will not see Me' in this earthly body), reserving the Beatific Vision for the believers in Paradise.

questionEn: Upon recovering from fainting when the mountain crumbled in Surah Al-A‘raf (7:143), what words did Prophet Musa (AS) immediately proclaim?
optionsEn: Call Harun to bring witnesses
Let the mountain be rebuilt instantly
Subhanaka tubtu ilayka wa ana awwalul-mu'minin ('Exalted are You! I turn to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers')
I demand to try again tomorrow
explanationEn: Awed by Allah's majesty, Musa (AS) responded with tasbih, repentance, and renewed declaration of faith.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:111), what opening praise ('Wa qulil-hamdulillahi...') summarizes pure Tawhid?
optionsEn: Praise to ancestors who built cities
Praise to the stars of winter
Praise to the winds that guide ships
Praise to Allah who has not taken a son, has no partner in dominion, and has no protector out of weakness — and magnify Him with great magnification
explanationEn: Known in tradition as 'Ayat al-‘Izz' (the Verse of Glory), 17:111 closes Surah Al-Isra with pure praise and Takbir.

questionEn: In Surah As-Saffat (37:180–182), which three short verses are often recited to conclude gatherings, sermons, and written supplications?
optionsEn: Subhana Rabbika Rabbil-‘izzati ‘amma yasifun, wa salamun ‘alal-mursalin, wal-hamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin
Tabbat yada Abi Lahab
Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun
Idha zulzilatil-ard
explanationEn: Ending with Allah's transcendence, peace upon all Messengers, and praise to the Lord of the worlds seals speech in blessing.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ explain about saying 'Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin' in terms of the scale of deeds?
optionsEn: It equals only one drop of rain
Alhamdulillah fills the scales (tamla'ul-mizan)
It weighs less than a date pit
It counts only on Mondays
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that 'Alhamdulillah' fills the Scale, while 'SubhanAllah wal-hamdulillah' fill what is between the heavens and the earth.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:269), what does Allah call 'a great deal of good' (khayran kathira) that He grants to whom He wills?
optionsEn: Gold mines in deserts
Al-Hikmah — sound wisdom and understanding
Fast Arabian horses
Tall towers of stone
explanationEn: Praying for wisdom (hikmah) alongside knowledge asks Allah for the discernment to apply knowledge rightly.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:2), what happens inside believers' hearts when Allah is remembered/mentioned?
optionsEn: Their hearts tremble with awe (wajilat qulubuhum), and when His verses are recited, their faith increases
They grow sleepy at once
They feel indifferent and hurried
They turn away to count coins
explanationEn: True dhikr awakens humility and awe, deepening reliance (tawakkul) upon Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qalam (68:87–90), why was Prophet Yunus (AS) saved from remaining inside the whale until the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Because he carried a golden horn
Because he swam faster than all ships
Because the sailors returned to rescue him
Because he was of those who glorified Allah (minal-musabbihin) in his life and in his distress
explanationEn: Consistent tasbih in times of ease prepares a believer to be remembered by Allah in sudden crisis.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Munafiqun (63:9), what two earthly attachments are believers warned never to let distract them from remembering Allah?
optionsEn: Reading Qur'an and helping orphans
Watering trees and greeting guests
Fasting and Salah
Your wealth (amwalukum) and your children (awladukum)
explanationEn: Wealth and children are blessings when they help us obey Allah, not when they crowd out His remembrance.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:93–94), what did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah regarding any punishment promised to stubborn deniers?
optionsEn: Let me watch from a royal balcony
Spare only the merchants of Ta'if
If You should show me what they are promised, my Lord, then do not place me among the wrongdoing people
Hasten it before sunset today
explanationEn: Seeking safety from being grouped with wrongdoers shows prophetic awe of Allah's justice.

questionEn: When Prophet Ibrahim (AS) faced his father's harsh rejection in Surah Maryam (19:47), what parting blessing did he still offer?
optionsEn: I shall erase your name from all records
I will bring an army against your house
Salamun ‘alayk, sa-astaghfiru laka Rabbi innahu kana bi hafiyya ('Peace be upon you; I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord')
May thunder strike your workshop tonight
explanationEn: Ibrahim (AS) exemplified gentle filial courtesy—until later revelation clarified that prayer for forgiveness for those who die in disbelief is not permitted (9:114).

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:155), when seventy elders collapsed at Mount Sinai, how did Musa (AS) plead for his community?
optionsEn: Leave them in the desert without water
Replace them with new travelers
Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is only Your trial... You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us
Punish them further until tomorrow
explanationEn: Musa's (AS) intercession shows a leader's tender mercy—acknowledging Allah's sovereignty while pleading for pardon for his people.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:83–84), what tears and dua followed when truthful Christians heard the Qur'an recited?
optionsEn: They demanded gold seals from Madinah
Their eyes overflowed with tears from recognizing the truth, and they prayed: 'Our Lord, we have believed, so write us among the witnesses'
They asked to delay belief until next spring
They disputed the grammar of the verses
explanationEn: Softness of heart upon hearing Allah's revelation leads naturally to humble faith and sincere dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:255), which majestic verse is widely called the greatest verse of the Qur'an and serves as a daily shield of protection?
optionsEn: Ayat al-Kursi ('Allahu la ilaha illa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum...')
The ending of Surah Al-Fil
Ayat ad-Dayn (2:282)
The opening of Surah Al-Masad
explanationEn: Reciting Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory Salah and before sleep guards the believer with Allah's protection.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hashr (59:22–24), why are the final verses rich fuel for heartfelt dua?
optionsEn: They list historical caravan routes across Syria
They prescribe seasonal farming measurements
They string together nearly twenty of Allah's Beautiful Names—including Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, Al-Mu'min, Al-Muhaymin, Al-‘Aziz, Al-Jabbar
They explain inheritance fractions of livestock
explanationEn: Calling upon Allah by His Names in 59:22–24 aligns the supplicant's heart with Allah's majesty, peace, and perfection.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:107), how is Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ mission described, inspiring believers to include mercy in their duas for humanity?
optionsEn: Sent only to angels in the heavens
Sent to judge harshly without mercy
Sent only to one valley in Arabia
Wa ma arsalnaka illa rahmatan lil-‘alamin ('We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds')
explanationEn: Following the Prophet of Mercy ﷺ means praying for guidance, well-being, and mercy for people everywhere.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab (33:21), who is declared the supreme 'Uswah Hasanah' (beautiful model) whose example guides our worship and supplication?
optionsEn: The merchants of Tyre
The emperors of Rome
The Messenger of Allah, Muhammad ﷺ
The philosophers of Athens
explanationEn: Learning how the Prophet ﷺ prayed in ease, grief, travel, and Salah connects our duas directly to the Sunnah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-‘Asr (103:1–3), alongside faith and righteous deeds, what two mutual duties save humanity from loss?
optionsEn: Competing over tall buildings and hoarding silver
Enjoining one another to truth (tawasaw bil-haqq) and enjoining one another to patience (tawasaw bis-sabr)
Memorizing genealogies and hunting at night
Traveling in silence and avoiding neighbors
explanationEn: Encouraging one another toward truth and patience includes praying for each other's steadfastness.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:5), what delicate plea do Ibrahim (AS) and his companions make regarding disbelievers?
optionsEn: Give us their camels before sunrise
Hide the moon from their caravans
Prevent them from speaking Arabic
Rabbana la taj‘alna fitnatan lilladhina kafaru waghfir lana Rabbana ('Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us')
explanationEn: Believers ask Allah not to let their defeat or moral failings become an excuse for disbelievers to reject the truth.

questionEn: What does Prophet Lut (AS) ask Allah in Surah Ash-Shu‘ara (26:169) regarding the wicked deeds of his town?
optionsEn: Let us remain inside the town forever
Let me rule over their market squares
Send rain of gold upon their gardens
Rabbi najjini wa ahli mimma ya‘malun ('My Lord, save me and my family from what they do')
explanationEn: Lut (AS) prayed for moral and physical deliverance for himself and his household before Allah commanded their night departure.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ankabut (29:30), what concise prayer did Prophet Lut (AS) utter against persistent corruption?
optionsEn: Rabbinsurni ‘alal-qawmil-mufsidin ('My Lord, support me against the corrupting people')
Rabbi zidni ‘ilma
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
explanationEn: After years of sincere warnings met with mockery, Lut (AS) turned to Allah for decisive aid against corruption.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:96), what noble ethical practice accompanies seeking refuge from devils in 23:97?
optionsEn: Cutting off ties with all relatives
Refusing to greet strangers
Repelling evil with that which is best ('Idfa‘ billati hiya ahsanus-sayyi'ah')
Returning every insult twofold
explanationEn: Combining outward graciousness toward people with inward dua for protection from Satan creates balanced character.

questionEn: In Surah Fussilat (41:30–31), what comforting assurance do angels bring to those who say 'RabbunAllah' and remain upright (istaqamu)?
optionsEn: Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive glad tidings of Paradise; we are your allies in worldly life and in the Hereafter
Wait alone in silence for seventy years
Expect no peace until the end of time
Avoid all mosques during winter
explanationEn: Steadfastness upon Tawhid invites angelic reassurance and eternal companionship.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:256), what strong metaphor describes holding fast to Allah after rejecting false deities?
optionsEn: Building a sandcastle beside waves
Chasing desert mirages at noon
Grasping the most trustworthy handhold (al-‘urwatil-wuthqa) that never breaks
Carrying water in a woven basket
explanationEn: Sincere faith and dua anchor the servant to an unbreakable bond with Al-Sami‘ Al-‘Alim.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:196), how did Allah teach Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to declare his true protector?
optionsEn: Inna waliyyiyAllahu-lladhi nazzalal-kitab wa Huwa yatawallas-salihin ('Indeed, my protector is Allah who sent down the Book, and He protects the righteous')
I rely solely on silver armor
My protector is the strongest tribe in Makkah
My protector is the governor of Syria
explanationEn: This verse reassures every believer that Allah Himself takes charge of the affairs of the righteous.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:7), what promise did Allah proclaim regarding gratitude (shukr)?
optionsEn: Gratitude ends future blessings
Thanks need only be felt once a decade
La-in shakartum la-azidannakum ('If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]')
Gratitude applies only to kings
explanationEn: Thanking Allah verbally and through obedience is itself a catalyst for greater blessings.

questionEn: In Surah Luqman (31:12), why was Luqman given wisdom (al-hikmah), starting with 'Anishkur lillah' ('Be grateful to Allah')?
optionsEn: So he could avoid speaking to his son
So he could charge fees for riddles
Whoever is grateful is grateful only for the benefit of his own soul, for Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy
So he could conquer Egypt
explanationEn: True wisdom begins with a grateful heart toward Al-Ghani Al-Hamid.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shura (42:26), how does Allah respond to those who believe and do righteous deeds?
optionsEn: He forbids them from asking twice
He grants them only worldly dust
He ignores their prayers until old age
He answers their supplications (wa yastajibu lilladhina amanu) and increases them from His bounty
explanationEn: Faith coupled with righteous action opens both answered prayer and unasked-for bounty (fadl).

questionEn: In Surah Ar-Rahman (55:29), what continuous cosmic reality encourages believers to keep asking Allah every day?
optionsEn: He rests on weekends without listening
Requests are reviewed only once every century
Only angels may speak during daylight
Whoever is in the heavens and earth asks Him; every day He is in [bringing about] a matter ('kulla yawmin Huwa fi sha'n')
explanationEn: Because every creature depends on Allah moment by moment, turning to Him daily in need is completely natural.

questionEn: In Surah Fatir (35:15), what foundational truth of dua does Allah remind humanity of?
optionsEn: Humanity needs Allah only during famine
Only travelers are needy before Allah
O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah (antumul-fuqara'u ilallah), while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy
Wealth makes a person independent of prayer
explanationEn: Recognizing our perpetual neediness (iftiqar) before Allah is the very essence of sincere supplication.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk (67:2), why did Allah create death and life?
optionsEn: To see who accumulates the heaviest chests of gold
To keep creation in perpetual sleep
To test you as to which of you is best in deed (ahsanu ‘amala)
To see who travels the farthest without praying
explanationEn: Note 'best in deed' (ahsanu ‘amala), not merely 'most in quantity'—sincerity and Sunnah quality matter most.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf (18:110), what two conditions make any act of worship or dua acceptable to Allah?
optionsEn: Reciting in public squares for applause
Hopeful sincerity for meeting Allah without associating any partner (shirk) and righteous deeds aligned with His guidance
Praying only when the moon is full
Paying silver coins to onlookers
explanationEn: Ikhlas (pure sincerity for Allah) and Ittiba‘ (following Prophetic guidance) are the two wings of accepted worship.

questionEn: In Surah An-Naml (27:62), who is uniquely described as answering the distressed person when he calls upon Him and removing harm?
optionsEn: Winds blowing from the Red Sea
Stone statues carved in desert valleys
The constellations of Aries and Orion
Allah alone ('Amman yujibul-mudtarra idha da‘ahu wa yakshifus-su'')
explanationEn: Even those who forget Allah in comfort instinctively cry out to Him alone in desperate crises.
