questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:63–64), what happens when people promise gratitude upon being rescued from the terrors of land and sea?
optionsEn: Everyone enters Paradise without any deeds
Allah rescues them from distress, yet many afterward associate partners with Him instead of remaining thankful
The ocean turns to fresh honey forever
Travelers never board ships again
explanationEn: This verse reminds believers to keep thanking and remembering Allah in safety just as fervently as in storms.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:216), what wise reassurance helps a believer whose specific dua seems answered differently than expected?
optionsEn: Happiness exists only in sudden wealth
Perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you; Allah knows while you know not
Never ask Allah for guidance in choices
All delays mean Allah has forgotten you
explanationEn: Trusting Allah's infinite knowledge brings serenity whether He grants what we asked, wards off harm, or substitutes something better.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:24), what life-giving metaphor describes answering Allah and His Messenger?
optionsEn: That which isolates you from kindness
That which burdens you without purpose
That which puts the mind to sleep
Respond to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life (lima yuhyikum)
explanationEn: Revelation, Salah, and Sunnah duas revive the spiritual heart just as water revives parched earth.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Infitar (82:6), what gentle question reminds careless hearts not to take Allah's patience for granted?
optionsEn: Why do you travel in autumn?
Why do you drink cold water?
Why have you built small houses?
What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous (al-Karim)?
explanationEn: Remembering Allah as Al-Karim inspires awe, gratitude, and immediate repentance rather than negligence.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hijr (15:49–50), what balanced self-description does Allah instruct the Prophet ﷺ to convey to His servants?
optionsEn: Tell them punishment falls even on the repentant
Tell them mercy exists without accountability
Tell My servants that I am indeed the Forgiving, the Merciful—and that My punishment is the painful punishment
Tell them nobody should ever hope for pardon
explanationEn: Balancing Allah's vast mercy with reverence for His justice keeps the supplicant both hopeful and conscientious.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hashr (59:18), what forward-looking habit is commanded to prepare for tomorrow's Meeting with Allah?
optionsEn: Leave all charity until your grandchildren grow old
Focus solely on predicting lunar eclipses
Ignore your daily intentions completely
Fear Allah, and let every soul look closely at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow (ma qaddamat li-ghad)
explanationEn: Calling the Hereafter 'tomorrow' (ghad) stresses how near it is and motivates sincere deeds and duas today.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hadid (57:4), what comforting reality about Allah's knowledge accompanies a believer anywhere on earth?
optionsEn: Wa Huwa ma‘akum aynama kuntum ('And He is with you wherever you are')
He knows only public speeches
He listens only during daylight hours
He watches only inside stone temples
explanationEn: Whether praying alone on a flight, in a hospital, or at the Kaaba, Allah is with His servant by His all-encompassing knowledge, hearing, and support.

questionEn: In Surah Qaf (50:16), how near does Allah describe His awareness of the human being's inner whispers?
optionsEn: Closer to him than his own jugular vein (aqrabu ilayhi min hablil-warid)
Recorded only once a week on Fridays
As far as the distant stars
Limited to spoken words above a whisper
explanationEn: Allah knows even the unspoken struggles of the heart before they cross our lips in dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:8–9), what combination of worship and trust is urged upon the believer at night?
optionsEn: Stay awake arguing over merchants' debts
Sleep straight through until midday
Remember the Name of your Lord, devote yourself to Him wholeheartedly (tabtila), and take Him as Disposer of Affairs (Wakil)
Seek patronage from rival governors
explanationEn: Nightly devotion and trusting Allah as Al-Wakil anchor the believer before facing demanding days.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:20), what are believers encouraged to read as much of as is easy for them during night prayer?
optionsEn: Avoid reading Qur'an if you are traveling
Fa-qra'u ma tayassara minal-Qur'an ('So recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur'an')
Recite the entire Qur'an every single night without rest
Recite only while standing on one foot
explanationEn: Islam balances lofty aspiration with mercy for the sick, travelers, and workers seeking livelihood.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Insan (76:9), what pure intention characterizes the righteous when feeding the needy, orphan, and captive?
optionsEn: We feed you so you praise us in the market
We feed you only during wedding feasts
We feed you only for the Countenance of Allah; we desire from you neither reward nor thanks
We feed you in exchange for future labor
explanationEn: Serving others purely for Allah's sake ('li-wajhillah') makes our own duas deeply beloved to Him.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Bayyinah (98:5), what concise summary defines the essence of all revealed religion?
optionsEn: To worship Allah sincerely (mukhlisina lahud-din), inclining to truth, establishing Salah, and giving Zakah
To wear identical colors on journeys
To memorize riddles from ancient kings
To build ornate monuments over rivers
explanationEn: Sincerity, uprightness, prayer, and charity form the timeless core of devotion.

questionEn: In Surah Al-‘Alaq (96:19), what final command pairs disobedience refusal with drawing near to Allah?
optionsEn: Wait for a royal decree
Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near to Allah (wasjud waqtarib)
Argue loudly until dawn
Flee into the mountains without praying
explanationEn: Sujud is the physical and spiritual pinnacle of nearness to Allah, where dua is most earnestly heard.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nasr (110:1–3), when victory and triumph finally arrive, what three acts of humility is the Prophet ﷺ instructed to perform?
optionsEn: Host seven weeks of proud parades
Carve his own name onto city gates
Stop fasting and night prayers
Glorify Allah with praise (fasabbih bi-hamdi Rabbika) and seek His forgiveness (wastaghfirh)
explanationEn: Even at the height of conquest, the Qur'an ends with tasbih, hamd, and istighfar—never self-congratulation.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1–4), calling upon Allah as 'As-Samad' affirms what unique attribute relevant to every dua?
optionsEn: He asks creation for sustenance
He is the Eternal Refuge upon whom all creation depends, while He needs none
He delegates small prayers to planets
He sleeps during the midday heat
explanationEn: Turning to Allah As-Samad means directing every need to the Only One who is completely self-sufficient and able to fulfill all needs.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kawthar (108:1–2), what two acts of devotion are commanded in response to Allah's abundant goodness?
optionsEn: Pray to your Lord (fa-salli li-Rabbika) and sacrifice (wanhar)
Hoard gold and stay indoors
Travel aimlessly without greeting anyone
Stop giving gifts to neighbors
explanationEn: Gratitude for Allah's abundant gifts (al-Kawthar) expresses itself through worship (Salah) and generous sacrifice for others.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma‘un (107:4–7), why is a person's Salah warned against despite appearing outwardly observant?
optionsEn: Being heedless of their prayer, doing deeds merely to be seen (yura'un), and withholding simple neighborly kindnesses (al-ma‘un)
Praying in clean linen garments
Reciting short surahs during travel
Making dua quietly after taslim
explanationEn: True prayer and dua harmonize inward sincerity with outward kindness toward orphans, the needy, and neighbors.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qadr (97:1–5), what fills the earth until the emergence of dawn on the Night of Decree?
optionsEn: Complete silence from all believers
Angels and the Spirit (Jibril) descend by Allah's permission with every decree, and it is pure peace (Salam)
Heavy winter snow across all deserts
Closing of all mosques before midnight
explanationEn: Seeking Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights of Ramadan with dua and Qur'an connects the believer to a night better than a thousand months.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hujurat (49:10), what duty naturally follows the statement 'Indeed, the believers are brothers'?
optionsEn: Avoid praying for fellow Muslims
Never forgive minor misunderstandings
Compete bitterly for tribal honors
Make reconciliation/peace between your brothers and fear Allah so you may receive mercy
explanationEn: Praying for reconciliation and forgiveness among believers honors the sacred bond of Islamic brotherhood.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13), what determines true nobility in Allah's sight above lineage, nationality, or wealth?
optionsEn: Inna akramakum ‘indallahi atqakum — 'Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous (has the greatest Taqwa)'
The size of one's silver caravan
The altitude of one's homeland
The number of languages spoken fluently
explanationEn: Remembering that Allah looks at Taqwa and hearts removes arrogance from worship and unites pilgrims of every nation.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hadid (57:16), what warning should awaken believers whose hearts feel dry during prayer and dhikr?
optionsEn: Abandon dhikr whenever you feel tired
Has not the time come for believers' hearts to humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth?
Wait until you grow too old to walk
Seek distraction in idle chatter
explanationEn: Recalling 57:16 melts hardness of heart and invites renewed humility before Allah.

questionEn: In Surah At-Taghabun (64:11), what happens to the heart of one who believes in Allah when a calamity strikes by His permission?
optionsEn: Allah guides his heart (yahdi qalbah) to calm acceptance and clarity
He stops remembering Allah for a year
His heart breaks permanently into despair
He loses all memory of gratitude
explanationEn: Belief in Allah's wise decree transforms sudden hardship into an avenue for inner guidance.

questionEn: In Surah At-Talaq (65:2–3), what twofold promise does Allah give to the one who fears Him (yat-taqillah) and relies upon Him?
optionsEn: Allah makes for him a way out (makhraja), provides for him from where he never expected, and suffices him
Allah removes all tests from worldly life
Allah sends him gold bars on every doorstep
Allah exempts him from ever working
explanationEn: Taqwa and Tawakkul unlock unexpected provision and exits from seemingly impossible dead-ends.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:17), what sobering truth reminds us why dua must be directed solely to Allah?
optionsEn: Amulets override Allah's decree
If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, He is over all things competent
Fortune comes purely from lucky dates
Angels decide prosperity independently
explanationEn: Knowing Allah alone holds harm and benefit frees the heart from superstition and deepens sincerity in dua.

questionEn: In Surah Yunus (10:107), what happens if Allah intends favor (khayr) for a servant?
optionsEn: There is none who can repel His bounty ('fa-la radda li-fadlih')
Only kings can approve it
It expires before sunrise
Envious people can permanently block it
explanationEn: Trusting that no human envy or obstacle can turn back Allah's destined grace gives profound peace to the supplicant.

questionEn: In Surah Fatir (35:2), what truth about Allah's mercy encourages patience and hope?
optionsEn: People can open mercy without Allah's leave
Time alone decides what opens
Whatever mercy Allah opens for people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him
Mercy belongs only to certain tribes
explanationEn: Every door of opportunity, healing, or relief opens solely by the key of Al-Fattah Al-Hakim.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:177), how does the Qur'an define true righteousness (al-birr) beyond merely facing east or west?
optionsEn: Firm faith, giving wealth out of love for Allah to relatives, orphans, the needy, travelers, and beggars, establishing Salah, giving Zakah, keeping promises, and patience in hardship
Debating legal technicalities without charity
Wearing identical white robes on Mondays
Facing north while fasting silently
explanationEn: True piety weaves together creed, Salah, charity, integrity, and patience.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:133–135), what immediate action brings forgiveness to the God-conscious when they commit a sin or wrong themselves?
optionsEn: They remember Allah at once, seek forgiveness for their sins, and do not knowingly persist in what they did
They hide from prayer for forty days
They blame fate and continue sinning
They pay a small fine to neighbors without repentance
explanationEn: Instant dhikr and istighfar after slipping keeps a believer on the path to Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nisa (4:110), what assurance does Allah give anyone who does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness?
optionsEn: He loses all previous good deeds forever
He will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful (yajidillaha Ghafuran Rahima)
He is forgiven only if nobody ever saw him
He must wait seven years before praying
explanationEn: Returning swiftly to Allah guarantees encountering His mercy rather than rejection.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:261), what uplifting multiplication is promised for spending sincerely in Allah's path?
optionsEn: Reward deducted if given in secret
Reward only if given to wealthy merchants
Like a single grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains—and Allah multiplies for whom He wills
A flat return of one-for-one only
explanationEn: Generous charity often accompanies heartfelt dua, inviting extraordinary barakah and multiplication.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:273), how does Allah describe the dignified needy whom believers should seek out for charity and prayers?
optionsEn: Those who boast loudly in city squares
Those who refuse to work despite full health
Restrained in Allah's cause, unable to move about the land, whom the unaware think rich because of their self-restraint (ta‘affuf)
Those who demand silver at every gate
explanationEn: Recognizing quiet dignity in others inspires compassionate giving and secret prayers for their relief.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:2), what two principles govern cooperation among believers?
optionsEn: Cooperate in rivalry and gossip
Cooperate only within your own clan
Cooperate in righteousness and piety (al-birri wat-taqwa), and do not cooperate in sin and aggression
Avoid working together on charitable projects
explanationEn: Supporting one another in piety and making dua for mutual goodness strengthens every community endeavor.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:97), what twofold reward does Allah promise both men and women who do righteous deeds while having faith?
optionsEn: A good, pure life in this world (hayatan tayyibah) and their reward according to the best of what they used to do
Automatic rulership over empires
Exemption from every earthly test
A life free of ever needing guidance
explanationEn: Hayatan tayyibah means inner contentment, lawful provision, and peace of heart granted equally to believing men and women.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:208), what holistic commitment are believers invited into?
optionsEn: Enter into Islam/submission completely (udkhulu fis-silmi kaffah) and do not follow the footsteps of Satan
Adopt only the parts that require no effort
Practice faith only on Fridays
Keep worship separate from family and business
explanationEn: Bringing Prophetic duas into meals, work, travel, sleep, and marriage helps a believer live Islam wholeheartedly.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shura (42:38), how are believers who 'answer their Lord' and establish Salah described when making community decisions?
optionsEn: They consult horoscopes before traveling
Their affairs are conducted through mutual consultation (shura baynahum), and they spend from what Allah provided them
They act impulsively without seeking counsel
They keep all plans hidden from family
explanationEn: Pairing Istikharah (seeking Allah's guidance) with Shura (wise consultation) is a timeless Sunnah methodology.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:159), after consulting companions in affairs, what final anchor completes a believer's decision?
optionsEn: Second-guess every step until sunset
Wait for a dream before acting
Fa-idha ‘azamta fa-tawakkal ‘alallah ('And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah')
Blame advisors if difficulties arise
explanationEn: Consultation, firm resolve, and reliance on Allah prevent paralysis and bring peace to outcomes.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:165), how is the love of true believers toward Allah described?
optionsEn: Smaller than love for gold
Seasonal only during harvest
Cool and merely formal
Ashaddu hubban lillah — stronger and deeper in love for Allah than anything else
explanationEn: Loving Allah above all else turns dua from a chore into an eagerly awaited conversation with the Beloved.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:44), who glorifies Allah with His praise across the universe?
optionsEn: The seven heavens, the earth, and whatever is in them—there is not a single thing except that it exalts Allah with His praise
Only prophets and scholars
Only human beings inside mosques
Only rivers during spring
explanationEn: Making tasbih joins the believer in harmony with the entire cosmos already glorifying its Creator.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hashr (59:21), what striking comparison shows the weight and power of Allah's revelation?
optionsEn: Oceans would freeze instantly
Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and splitting apart from fear of Allah
Mountains would turn into silver coins
Trees would stop growing leaves
explanationEn: Reflecting on the Qur'an's majesty softens our hearts so they tremble and respond when we recite its duas.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:25), what glad tidings await those who believe and do righteous deeds?
optionsEn: Temporary stays of a thousand years only
Palaces without companions
Gardens beneath which rivers flow, with pure spouses and eternal residence
Endless worldly travel
explanationEn: Remembering the promise of Jannah elevates our prayers beyond temporary troubles.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf (18:46), what does Allah say is better in reward and hope than wealth and children—the adornments of worldly life?
optionsEn: Marble monuments in capitals
Vast orchards of date palms
Al-Baqiyat as-Salihat — enduring righteous deeds (such as sincere dhikr, prayer, and charity)
Stories of ancient kings
explanationEn: Many scholars note that 'SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illAllah, Allahu Akbar' are foremost among al-Baqiyat as-Salihat.

questionEn: In Surah Maryam (19:76), how does Allah reward those who already seek guidance?
optionsEn: He limits guidance to scholars only
He removes guidance during travel
Allah increases those who were guided in guidance (wa yazidullahul-ladhinah-tadaw huda)
He stops guiding them after youth
explanationEn: Every sincere step toward Allah in prayer or Qur'an invites further light and clarity.

questionEn: In Surah Muhammad (47:7), what reciprocal law of victory and firmness does Allah promise believers?
optionsEn: If you support [the cause of] Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet (wa yuthabbit aqdamakum)
Wait passively without upholding justice
Rely strictly on numerical superiority
Abandon worship during crises
explanationEn: Supporting Allah's truth through obedience, integrity, and prayer brings divine aid and steadiness.

questionEn: In Surah Muhammad (47:19), what command pairs knowledge of Tawhid directly with seeking forgiveness?
optionsEn: Ask forgiveness only for yourself and never for others
Wait until Friday afternoon before speaking
Learn astronomy before making dua
Know that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women
explanationEn: Pairing 'La ilaha illAllah' with Istighfar for oneself and all believers captures the twin pillars of faith and humility.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:24–25), what parable illustrates a good word (kalimatan tayyibah) like 'La ilaha illAllah'?
optionsEn: A fleeting spark blown out by wind
A shallow puddle dried by noon heat
A dry reed broken by footsteps
A goodly tree whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches reach into the sky, yielding fruit in every season by its Lord's permission
explanationEn: Deeply rooted words of faith and dhikr produce steady beauty, shade, and fruit in every season of life.

questionEn: In Surah Fatir (35:10), what ascends to Allah alongside 'the good word' (al-kalimut-tayyib)?
optionsEn: Decorated parchment scrolls alone
Boastful speeches in marketplaces
Righteous deeds elevate it (wal-‘amalus-salihu yarfa‘uh)
Empty promises without action
explanationEn: Beautiful duas and words of dhikr soar highest when carried upward by sincere righteous action.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:138), what beauty is referred to as 'SibghatAllah' ('the coloring/baptism of Allah')?
optionsEn: The pure natural imprint of faith and submission to Allah—and who is better than Allah at coloring?
Carving symbols onto shields
Dyeing robes indigo before travel
Painting walls of houses with saffron
explanationEn: Being 'colored' by Allah's way means faith shapes our speech, prayers, ethics, and gratitude.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:16), out of what does Allah guide those who pursue His pleasure through His Light?
optionsEn: From darknesses into the light (minaz-zulumati ilan-nur) and onto a straight path
From certainty into doubt
From peace into confusion
From gardens into barren deserts
explanationEn: Seeking Allah's pleasure (ridwan) in prayer and conduct illuminates every confused crossroad.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:29), what discerning gift does Allah promise those who have Taqwa of Him?
optionsEn: Control over ocean currents
Immunity from winter cold
Knowledge of hidden gold veins
A criterion (Furqan) to distinguish truth from falsehood, removal of misdeeds, and forgiveness
explanationEn: Taqwa sharpens moral and spiritual clarity (Furqan), guiding everyday decisions.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:195), which attitude toward good deeds is declared beloved to Allah?
optionsEn: Al-Ihsan — excellence and doing good ('InnAllaha yuhibbul-muhsinin')
Showing off for applause
Withholding help from travelers
Careless haste
explanationEn: Excellence in worship (Ihsan)—worshipping Allah as though you see Him—transforms ordinary duas into heartfelt devotion.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas (28:77), what balanced advice was given to Qarun regarding the Hereafter and this world?
optionsEn: Spread corruption in the streets
Seek the home of the Hereafter through what Allah has given you, do not forget your lawful share of this world, and do good as Allah has done good to you
Abandon all lawful work and hide in caves
Hoard every coin and refuse charity
explanationEn: Islam honors balanced gratitude—using earthly blessings ethically to invest in eternal peace.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:73), what habits marked the righteous leaders whom Allah guided by His command?
optionsEn: Seeking praise from poets
Ruling through fear and withholding charity
Traveling without ever praying
Doing good deeds, establishing Salah, giving Zakah, and worshipping Allah steadfastly
explanationEn: True spiritual leadership grows from personal worship, generosity, and consistency.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:238), which prayer does Allah highlight when commanding believers to guard all prayers?
optionsEn: Only the Eid prayer twice a year
As-Salat al-Wusta (the Middle Prayer, identified by the Prophet ﷺ as ‘Asr), standing before Allah in devout obedience
Only voluntary prayers before noon
Only prayers offered while on a ship
explanationEn: Guarding Salah—especially ‘Asr when worldly tasks peak—and standing humbly ('qanitin') anchors the entire day.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:78), why is reciting the Qur'an at Fajr (Qur'anal-Fajr) especially praised?
optionsEn: Because only short surahs are allowed at Fajr
Because voices echo louder in winter
Because no one else is awake on earth
Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed (mashhuda) by the angels of night and day
explanationEn: Night and day angels gather at Fajr and ‘Asr, witnessing the believer's recitation, prayer, and morning adhkar.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:79), what special station did Allah promise Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as a reward for night prayer (Tahajjud)?
optionsEn: Command over northern seas
Exemption from visiting Makkah
A castle built of red coral
Maqaman Mahmuda — a praised, honored station of intercession on the Day of Judgment
explanationEn: This verse links waking in the stillness of night to the Prophet's ﷺ beloved Maqam Mahmud, echoed in our dua after the Adhan!

questionEn: In Surah As-Sajdah (32:16), how are true believers described during the stillness of night?
optionsEn: They gather in markets until dawn
They count gold coins by candlelight
Their sides forsake their beds as they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spend out of what We provided them
They sleep soundly without ever waking for worship
explanationEn: Rising even briefly at night to make dua in fear and hope is rewarded with hidden joy no eye has seen (32:17).

questionEn: In Surah Adh-Dhariyat (51:17–18), what two habits characterized the righteous inhabitants of Paradise during their earthly nights?
optionsEn: They slept from sunset until midday
They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn (bil-ashar) they would seek forgiveness
They held noisy banquets every midnight
They avoided praying until sunrise
explanationEn: Istighfar in the pre-dawn hour (sahar) is among the most blessed moments for cleansing the heart.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:17), alongside the patient, truthful, devout, and charitable, who are specially named among the righteous?
optionsEn: Those who collect rare manuscripts only
Al-Mustaghfirina bil-ashar — those who seek forgiveness before dawn
Those who sleep past noon daily
Those who travel without provisions
explanationEn: Pre-dawn istighfar crowns patience, truthfulness, obedience, and generosity.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:112), what twofold reward awaits whoever submits his whole self to Allah while being a doer of good (muhsin)?
optionsEn: He will become a king in his hometown
He will be excused from charity
He will never experience winter or rain
His reward is with his Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them nor will they grieve
explanationEn: Surrendering sincerely to Allah and practicing excellence removes paralyzing fear and grief.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:125), what physical metaphor describes how Allah opens a heart to Islam and guidance?
optionsEn: Yashrah sadrahu lil-Islam — He expands his chest/breast wide with openness and light
He turns his footsteps westward
He freezes his hands in cold water
He dims his sight until dusk
explanationEn: Remembering this expansion of the chest echoes Musa's (AS) dua 'Rabbish-rah li sadri' and Allah's gift to Muhammad ﷺ in Surah Ash-Sharh.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf (18:28), what kind of companions is the Prophet ﷺ commanded to keep himself patiently with?
optionsEn: Those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His Countenance
Those who mock quiet worship
Those whose eyes look solely at worldly glitter
Those whose hearts are heedless of dhikr
explanationEn: Surrounding oneself with people of morning and evening remembrance protects sincerity and keeps dua alive.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:205), when and how is the believer instructed to remember Allah within himself?
optionsEn: Shout loudly only at midnight on Tuesdays
Remember Him only while inside royal halls
Write His Name on coins without speaking
Remember your Lord within yourself in humility and awe, without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless
explanationEn: Daily morning and evening dhikr—rooted in Surah Al-A‘raf 7:205—keeps the heart vigilant against heedlessness (ghaflah).

questionEn: In Surah Ar-Rum (30:17–18), which daily times are highlighted for glorifying Allah ('Fa-subhanAllahi hina tumsuna wa hina tusbihun')?
optionsEn: Only when crossing mountain passes
Only on the first day of spring
Only during solar eclipses
When you reach the evening, when you enter the morning, in the late afternoon (‘ashi), and at midday (tuzhirun)
explanationEn: These verses anchor the rhythm of the five daily prayers and morning/evening adhkar across every 24-hour cycle.

questionEn: In Surah Qaf (50:39–40), when is glorifying Allah with praise specifically encouraged?
optionsEn: Before the rising of the sun (Fajr), before its setting (‘Asr), during part of the night, and after the prostrations (adbar as-sujud)
Only after trading in the market
Only during the month of Shawwal
Only when rain falls on rooftops
explanationEn: Sunrise-to-sunset adhkar and post-Salah tasbih trace directly back to these Qur'anic rhythms of praise.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tur (52:48–49), what comforting reminder accompanies the command to be patient for your Lord's judgment?
optionsEn: Wait until your enemies apologize first
Travel alone without telling anyone
Fa-innaka bi-a‘yunina — 'For indeed, you are in Our eyes/care,' and glorify Allah when you rise, in the night, and at the fading of the stars
Stop praying until peace returns
explanationEn: Knowing you are under Allah's watchful care ('bi-a‘yunina') turns patience and dawn tasbih into sources of serenity.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:1–2), what is the very first trait of the believers who attain true success (aflaha)?
optionsEn: Those who build the tallest towers
Those who speak in obscure riddles
Those who are humble and deeply attentive (khashi‘un) in their Salah
Those who own the fastest horses
explanationEn: Khushu‘ in Salah—heart-presence and humility—is the gateway to all spiritual success.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:144), turning one's face toward Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah fulfills what longing of the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Relocating Madinah toward Syria
Seeing his face repeatedly turn skyward in silent prayer for a Qiblah that would please him
Shortening Fajr prayer to one rak‘ah
Changing the fasting month to winter
explanationEn: Even an unspoken longing in the Prophet's ﷺ heart—expressed by looking toward heaven—was lovingly answered by Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:248), what comforting gift was placed inside the Ark of the Covenant for the Israelites?
optionsEn: Maps of hidden silver mines
Contracts with neighboring emperors
Sakinah (tranquility and reassurance) from their Lord
Seven crowns of bronze
explanationEn: Sakinah—divine tranquility descending upon anxious hearts—is a recurring gift of faith and Qur'anic remembrance.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fath (48:4), into what did Allah send down Sakinah (tranquility) so that believers might grow in faith upon faith?
optionsEn: Into the hearts of the believers (fi qulubil-mu'minin)
Onto stone pillars outside Hudaybiyyah
Into desert wells only
Into sealed leather scrolls
explanationEn: At moments of tension like Hudaybiyyah, Allah calms believers' hearts from within so trust deepens.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:11), how did Allah bring peace to the fatigued companions on the eve of Badr?
optionsEn: He lit bonfires across every hill
He concealed the wells beneath sand
He instructed them to march without sleep for three days
He enveloped them in calming drowsiness (nu‘as) as security from Him and sent down pure water from the sky to cleanse them and steady their feet
explanationEn: Calm sleep before a daunting day and refreshing rain are tangible mercies from Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:126), why does Allah say He sent angelic aid and glad tidings at Badr?
optionsEn: To make warriors careless of prayer
To let people boast of their swords
Only as glad tidings for you and so that your hearts might be reassured by it—for victory comes from Allah alone, the Almighty, the Wise
To replace reliance on Allah with pride
explanationEn: Even miraculous help reminds believers that victory belongs exclusively to Al-‘Aziz Al-Hakim.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:249), what timeless lesson did Talut's small faithful force demonstrate before reciting their dua in 2:250?
optionsEn: Patience weakens resolve in battle
Large numbers always guarantee victory without faith
How often a small group has overcome a mighty host by Allah's permission—and Allah is with the patient
Only royal armies should pray before hardship
explanationEn: Faith, discipline, and patience outweigh sheer numbers when Allah's permission supports the sincere.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu‘ara (26:50), how did the believing magicians respond to Fir‘awn's threats of mutilation?
optionsEn: La dayr, inna ila Rabbina munqalibun ('No harm! Indeed, to our Lord we will surely return')
Give us ten days to consult our families
Spare us and we will return to sorcery
Hide us inside the temple
explanationEn: Certainty in returning to Allah's mercy stripped tyranny of its power to intimidate their hearts.

questionEn: In Surah Yunus (10:10), what eternal greeting and closing praise will resound among the dwellers of Paradise?
optionsEn: Counting days until winter ends
Endless debates over worldly history
Their call therein is 'SubhanakAllahumma', their greeting is 'Salam', and the end of their call is 'Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin'
Silent solitude without speaking
explanationEn: Tasbih, Salam, and Hamd—the very words we practice in earthly duas—become the joyous melody of Paradise.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Waqi‘ah (56:25–26), what are the inhabitants of Paradise spared from hearing, and what word fills their ears instead?
optionsEn: Loud trumpets and market arguments
They hear neither idle speech nor sinful talk—only the saying: 'Salam, Salam!' (Peace, Peace!)
Nothing at all in total silence
Whispered rumors and complaints
explanationEn: Guarding our tongues today through dhikr and gentle speech prepares our hearts for the peace of Jannah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:163–164), before inviting people to reflect on skies, ships, rain, and winds, what foundational truth is declared?
optionsEn: Winds blow without purpose
Stars control human prayers
Wa ilahukum ilahun wahid, la ilaha illa Huwar-Rahmanur-Rahim ('And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Merciful')
Nature governs itself independently
explanationEn: Seeing creation as signs of Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim turns everyday nature—rain, sea travel, night and day—into prompts for dua.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:53), where does every single blessing you enjoy originate?
optionsEn: From bargaining alone without grace
From chance alignment of stars
Wa ma bikum min ni‘matin fa-minallah ('Whatever favor you have, it is from Allah')
Solely from ancestral inheritance
explanationEn: Recognizing every health, meal, friend, and safe flight as a gift from Allah fuels genuine shukr.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:18), what happens if you try to count the favors of Allah?
optionsEn: They fit easily on a single page
They number exactly three hundred
They apply only to wealthy merchants
You could never enumerate them ('wa in ta‘uddu ni‘matallahi la tuhsuha'); indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
explanationEn: Even our shortfall in thanking Allah for uncountable blessings is met by His forgiveness and mercy.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:70), how has Allah honored the children of Adam across land and sea?
optionsEn: Restricting them to desert caves
Denying them speech and reason
Providing them with pure, good things (at-tayyibat) and favoring them clearly over many of those He created
Forbidding them from crossing seas
explanationEn: Human dignity and pure provision inspire thankful stewardship and respectful dua.

questionEn: In Surah Luqman (31:17), what four lifelong pillars did wise Luqman advise his son to hold onto?
optionsEn: Seek applause, hide from neighbors, hoard silver, and travel alone
Wait until wealth arrives before praying
Avoid responsibility and speak harshly
Establish Salah, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and bear patiently whatever befalls you
explanationEn: Calling patience in adversity one of the resolute affairs ('‘azmil-umur') gives courage when practicing righteousness.

questionEn: In Surah Luqman (31:18–19), what outer demeanor reflects inner humility toward Allah and people?
optionsEn: March loudly in marketplaces
Walk boastfully and shout above everyone
Do not turn your cheek in arrogance, do not walk insolently on earth, be moderate in your pace, and lower your voice
Ignore greetings from elders
explanationEn: Modesty in gait and gentleness in voice harmonize seamlessly with humble supplication.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:83), what kind of speech are believers commanded to offer to all people?
optionsEn: Speak kindly only to close cousins
Wa qulu lin-nasi husna ('And speak to people good/kind words')
Speak harshly to strangers
Remain completely mute in markets
explanationEn: Polite, healing speech toward every person complements a tongue moist with dhikr.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:53), why are Allah's servants instructed to speak only that which is best (allati hiya ahsan)?
optionsEn: Because short sentences save ink
Because Satan sows discord among people ('inna sh-shaytana yanzaghu baynahum')
Because silence is forbidden at noon
Because loud voices wake birds
explanationEn: Choosing the kindest wording blocks Satan's attempts to spark unnecessary quarrels.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:199), what three-part ethic of relational grace did Allah command Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Escalate every petty dispute
Never pardon anyone who errs
Hold to forgiveness/pardon (khudhil-‘afw), enjoin what is right/kind, and turn away from the ignorant
Keep meticulous grudges for years
explanationEn: Practicing pardon toward others mirrors our own plea in dua for Allah's pardon (‘afw).

questionEn: In Surah An-Nur (24:22), what question did Allah ask Abu Bakr (RA) when urging him to forgive and continue supporting a relative who had erred?
optionsEn: Should you not cut off all charity forever?
Demand double repayment in gold?
Ala tuhibbuna an yaghfirAllahu lakum? ('Would you not love that Allah should forgive you?')
Wait ten years before speaking again?
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) immediately cried, 'Yes, by Allah, I love that You forgive me!'—showing that forgiving people unlocks Allah's forgiveness for us.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shura (42:40), who directly rewards a person who pardons and makes reconciliation?
optionsEn: Nobody unless written on stone
Fa-ajruhu ‘alallah ('His reward is directly upon Allah Himself')
Only passing historians
Only local judges
explanationEn: Leaving the reward of pardoning directly to Allah frees the heart from bitterness.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shura (42:43), how does the Qur'an describe one who exercises patience and forgives?
optionsEn: Indeed, that is among the matters requiring great resolve (min ‘azmil-umur)
Permitted only for children
Forbidden for travelers
A sign of weakness to be mocked
explanationEn: True strength shows in self-restraint, patience, and forgiveness rather than revenge.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:263), what does Allah say is better than a charity followed by hurtful words or reminders?
optionsEn: A large gift given angrily
Qawlun ma‘rufun wa maghfiratun ('A kind word and forgiveness')
A loud announcement at noon
Closing one's door abruptly
explanationEn: Kind words and pardon carry deep spiritual weight before Al-Ghani Al-Halim.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:153), who does Allah explicitly promise He is with ('InnAllaha ma‘a...')?
optionsEn: The hasty ones
The boastful ones
The ungrateful ones
As-Sabirin — the patient ones
explanationEn: Allah's special companionship (ma‘iyyah khassah) of aid and comfort stays beside the patient.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:155), what five tests does Allah mention as ways humanity is tested before receiving glad tidings for the patient?
optionsEn: Only rainy Fridays
Something of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and fruits
Excessive leisure without duties
Forgetting poetry lines
explanationEn: Expecting tests as part of earthly life prepares believers to respond swiftly with 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un'.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:157), what three gifts descend upon those who respond patiently to calamity with Istirja‘?
optionsEn: Forgetfulness of all loved ones
Exemption from all prayers
Immediate gold coins
Blessings (salawat) from their Lord, mercy (rahmah), and being rightly guided (muhtadun)
explanationEn: No earthly loss can outweigh receiving Allah's own blessings, mercy, and guidance.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:51), what anchoring declaration reminds believers that nothing befalls them outside Allah's wise decree?
optionsEn: Luck rules the seasons independently
Qul lan yusibana illa ma katabAllahu lana Huwa mawlana wa ‘alallahi fal-yatawakkalil-mu'minun
Misfortune strikes outside Allah's knowledge
Only travel carries risk
explanationEn: Saying 'ma katabAllahu LANA' (written FOR us, not merely against us) sees divine mercy even inside trials.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hadid (57:22–23), why does Allah inform us that every calamity on earth or within ourselves was recorded in a Book before He brought it into being?
optionsEn: So you never comfort grieving friends
So you stop making dua altogether
So you avoid earning lawful livelihood
So that you may not despair over what escaped you, nor exult arrogantly over what He has given you
explanationEn: Belief in Qadar steadies the soul against both crushing despair and arrogant boasting.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:54), what welcome message did Allah instruct the Prophet ﷺ to announce to those who believe in His verses?
optionsEn: Never greet strangers with peace
Mercy applies only once every ten years
Stay silent outside the mosque
Salamun ‘alaykum; kataba Rabbukum ‘ala nafsihir-rahmah ('Peace be upon you! Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy')
explanationEn: Allah's self-decreed mercy ensures that anyone who errs out of ignorance and then repents and amends finds Him Forgiving and Merciful.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk (67:19), watching birds spread and fold their wings in the sky points to which attribute of Allah?
optionsEn: Only mountain winds carry birds
Birds fly without any creator
Ma yumsikuhunna illar-Rahman ('None holds them up except the Most Merciful')
Birds never depend on mercy
explanationEn: Even a bird gliding overhead is held aloft by Ar-Rahman—encouraging frequent travelers to trust Him on flights.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk (67:30), what simple daily question awakens gratitude for clean drinking water?
optionsEn: Who could count grains of sand?
If your water were to sink deep into the earth tomorrow, who could bring you flowing spring water?
Who could weave finer silk?
Who could build taller bridges?
explanationEn: Drinking water—especially Zamzam—becomes an act of profound shukr when we remember who keeps springs flowing.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:168 & 2:172), what two qualities of food are believers commanded to eat and give thanks for?
optionsEn: Uncooked and tasteless
Halalan tayyiba — lawful and pure/wholesome
Expensive and rare only
Secret and unshared
explanationEn: Eating lawful, pure sustenance (halal tayyib) is a foundational prerequisite for accepted duas.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:31), what balance of enjoyment and moderation is taught when visiting mosques and dining?
optionsEn: Wear torn rags to every mosque
Take your adornment at every place of prayer, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive (la tusrifu)
Eat until unable to stand
Fast every single day without breaking
explanationEn: Clean attire at the masjid and moderation at the table honor both body and spirit.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:26–27), whom does Allah call 'brothers of the devils'?
optionsEn: Al-Mubadhdhirin — wasteful spendthrifts who squander blessings ungratefully
Hospitality hosts feeding guests
Travelers asking directions
Students buying notebooks
explanationEn: Avoiding wasteful extravagance preserves wealth to share with relatives, the needy, and stranded travelers.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Furqan (25:67), how do the Servants of Ar-Rahman spend their money?
optionsEn: Neither extravagantly wasteful nor stingily tight, but balanced firmly in between (qawama)
Spending everything in one night
Locking every coin inside wells
Lending only at high interest
explanationEn: Balanced stewardship reflects inner equilibrium and gratitude.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:267), what standard of quality should believers choose when giving charity?
optionsEn: Expired grain saved at the bottom
Only broken items you dislike yourself
From the good, pure things (min tayyibati) you earned and Allah brought forth—not aiming to give away the rotten/inferior
Coins borrowed without permission
explanationEn: Giving what is wholesome and beloved reflects genuine reverence for Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:92), what level of generosity unlocks true righteousness (al-birr)?
optionsEn: Spending only unwanted scraps
Spending only when forced by law
Waiting until inheritance is divided
You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love (mimma tuhibbun)
explanationEn: Giving from what our hearts value loosens attachment to materialism and deepens love for Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:183), what overarching spiritual goal is stated for fasting Ramadan?
optionsEn: To lose weight before summer
Merely to endure daytime thirst
To stay silent for thirty days
La‘allakum tattaqun ('So that you may attain Taqwa / God-consciousness')
explanationEn: Fasting nurtures Taqwa, making the fasting person's dua at iftar deeply cherished by Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185), what are believers told to do upon completing the prescribed days of Ramadan?
optionsEn: Avoid visiting family on Eid
Forget prayer until next year
Hold silent fasts throughout Shawwal
Magnify Allah (wa li-tukabbirullaha) for having guided you, and perhaps you will be grateful (tashkurun)
explanationEn: The Takbirat of Eid al-Fitr directly fulfill this Qur'anic call to glorify and thank Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Jumu‘ah (62:10), what should believers do once Friday prayer (Jumu‘ah) is concluded?
optionsEn: Disperse in the land, seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah abundantly (wadhkurullaha kathira) so you may succeed
Avoid speaking to coworkers
Cease all lawful trade on Fridays
Lock themselves indoors until Sunday
explanationEn: Islam blends sacred worship with purposeful work, threaded together by abundant dhikr.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:8), how does Allah permit and encourage Muslims to treat peaceful people of other faiths?
optionsEn: To speak unkindly to peaceful travelers
To act kindly/righteously (tabarruhum) and deal justly (tuqsitu ilayhim) with those who do not fight you over religion or drive you from your homes
To break contracts whenever convenient
To refuse fair trade with neighbors
explanationEn: Justice and kindness (birr) toward peaceful neighbors reflect Allah's love for al-muqsitin (the just).

questionEn: In Surah An-Nisa (4:86), what gracious Prophetic and Qur'anic standard applies when someone greets you with a greeting?
optionsEn: Walk past silently if busy
Greet in return with something better than it, or at least return the like of it
Ignore greetings from younger people
Reply only to close relatives
explanationEn: Answering 'As-salamu ‘alaykum' with 'Wa ‘alaykumus-salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh' spreads a daily dua of peace.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nur (24:27 & 24:61), what blessed practice should accompany entering homes—even empty ones?
optionsEn: Avoid saying Salam inside your own home
Knock once and enter unannounced
Enter through back windows
Ask permission warmly and greet the inhabitants (or yourselves when entering houses) with a blessed, pure greeting of peace from Allah
explanationEn: Saying 'As-salamu ‘alaykum' upon entering brings barakah into the household.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:51), what command links pure sustenance directly to righteous deeds for all Messengers?
optionsEn: Separate moral integrity from daily food
Abstain from all cooked meals
O Messengers, eat from the pure, good foods and do righteous deeds ('kulu minat-tayyibati wa‘malu saliha')
Eat anything regardless of its source
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ cited this exact verse to explain how halal, pure provision empowers righteous deeds and accepted dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:88), immediately after narrating Prophet Yunus's (AS) dua, what universal promise does Allah add?
optionsEn: Rescues happen only once every century
Only prophets in ancient ships are rescued
Wa kadhalika nunjil-mu'minin ('And thus do We rescue the believers')
Believers must never face distress
explanationEn: This verse guarantees that Yunus's (AS) sincere plea remains an open doorway of rescue for every believer across time.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:130–132), what parting bequest did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and Prophet Ya‘qub (AS) leave to their sons?
optionsEn: Move to the coast of Greece
Build towering stone statues
Divide the silver mines equally
Allah has chosen this religion for you, so do not die except while you are Muslims (wa antum muslimun)
explanationEn: Praying to remain steadfast in Islam until our very last breath echoes the testament of the prophets.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:79), what declaration of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) became part of the Sunnah opening dua (Istiftah) in Salah?
optionsEn: Inni wajjahtu wajhiya lilladhi fataras-samawati wal-arda hanifan wa ma ana minal-mushrikin
Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi
Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
explanationEn: Reciting Ibrahim's (AS) words of turning whole-heartedly toward the Originator of the heavens and earth centers the heart at the start of Salah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:250), what four-part structure makes the dua of Talut's soldiers a masterpiece for any overwhelming challenge?
optionsEn: Requesting postponement, retreat, silence, and comfort
Complaining of heat, distance, thirst, and armor
Asking for wealth, leisure, sleep, and applause
Asking for inner endurance (patience), outer steadiness (firm feet), and ultimate divine victory over opposition
explanationEn: Combining inner calm with firm action and reliance on Allah's aid covers every dimension of human struggle.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:193), how do believers call upon Allah before asking Him to forgive their sins and erase their bad deeds?
optionsEn: Rabbana innana sami‘na munadiyan yunadi lil-iman an aminu bi-Rabbikum fa-amanna
We have conquered surrounding valleys
We have built three grand mosques first
We have fasted without interruption
explanationEn: Acknowledging the gift of hearing the call to faith—the Qur'an and Messenger ﷺ—and responding to it frames our plea for forgiveness.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:195), how did Allah immediately honor the earnest prayers of those believers in 3:191–194?
optionsEn: He delayed all responses until winter
He excluded travelers from reward
He answered only the eldest elders
Fastajaba lahum Rabbuhum anni la udi‘u ‘amala ‘amilin minkum min dhakarin aw untha ('Their Lord responded to them: Never will I allow the work of any worker among you, male or female, to be lost')
explanationEn: Every sincere effort, tear, and prayer by any believing woman or man is preserved with honor by Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:124), when Prophet Ibrahim (AS) asked 'And of my descendants?' upon being made a spiritual leader (Imam), what did Allah clarify?
optionsEn: La yanalu ‘ahdiz-zalimin ('My covenant does not include the wrongdoers')
Only the wealthiest heir receives the covenant
Every descendant is guaranteed leadership regardless of deeds
Lineage replaces righteousness automatically
explanationEn: Spiritual honor in Islam rests on righteousness and justice, never mere bloodline.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:118), what tender plea did Prophet ‘Isa (AS) leave in Allah's hands regarding his followers on Judgment Day?
optionsEn: Exempt them from resurrection
If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed it is You who are the Exalted in Might, the Wise
Punish them swiftly without mercy
Judge them by earthly wealth
explanationEn: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ wept through an entire night repeating this verse in Tahajjud out of compassion for his Ummah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:12), why is Allah's mercy greater than human imagination when we turn to Him in dua?
optionsEn: Mercy is rationed only during spring rains
Mercy expires after forty years of age
Kataba ‘ala nafsihir-rahmah ('He has decreed mercy upon Himself')
Mercy applies only to those who never err
explanationEn: Because Allah Himself bound His own decree to mercy, His mercy outstrips His wrath.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:37), how did Prophet Adam (AS) receive the exact words of repentance that restored him?
optionsEn: Fa-talaqqa Adamu min Rabbihi kalimatin fa-taba ‘alayh ('Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance')
He invented poetic rhymes after seventy years
He waited silently without speaking
He carved requests onto mountain boulders
explanationEn: Even the very words to repent properly ('Rabbana zalamna anfusana...') were a merciful gift taught by Allah Himself.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196), what does Allah say upon completing Umrah and Hajj sincerely?
optionsEn: To rush through rites without reflection
To fulfill Hajj and Umrah completely for Allah ('Wa atimmul-hajja wal-‘umrata lillah')
To perform rites merely for titles
To omit dua at Arafah if tired
explanationEn: Completing pilgrimage purely for Allah aligns every step—from Ihram to Tawaf and Sa‘i—with sincerity.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:203), what flexibility and focus on Taqwa are given for pilgrims remembering Allah during the Days of Tashriq at Mina?
optionsEn: Avoid making Takbir at Mina
Stay in Mina for thirty consecutive days
Remember Allah during the appointed days; whoever hastens off in two days incurs no sin, and whoever delays incurs no sin—for whoever fears Allah
Leave Mina before Fajr on the 10th
explanationEn: Making Takbir and dua during the blessed days of Mina blends ease with reverent Taqwa.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:214), what did the Prophet ﷺ and early believers ask in extreme hardship, showing that even the faithful feel tested before victory?
optionsEn: Let us abandon Madinah permanently
Why should anyone worship at all?
Help comes only to kings
Mata nasrullah? ('When is the help of Allah?')—answered with: 'Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near!'
explanationEn: Feeling exhausted in prolonged hardship does not negate faith; Allah reassures sincere hearts that His relief is always close.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:200), what final four commands conclude the entire surah as a blueprint for endurance?
optionsEn: Withdraw from society, hoard supplies, avoid neighbors, and sleep late
Compete in boasting, neglect prayer, seek praise, and hurry
Be patient (isbiru), outlast in patience (sabiru), stand firm/guard frontiers (rabitu), and fear Allah (wattaqullah) so you may succeed
Stop striving once youth ends
explanationEn: Collective endurance (musabarah) and watchfulness (ribat) alongside Taqwa bring lasting success.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nisa (4:1), what awareness of family ties and Allah's watchfulness opens the surah?
optionsEn: Respect only wealthy uncles
Fear Allah through whom you ask one another, and respect the wombs/ties of kinship (al-arham)—indeed Allah is ever over you an Observer
Sever family bonds during travel
Forget distant relatives once married
explanationEn: Honoring family ties and praying for relatives brings barakah in lifespan and sustenance.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:128), what two qualities earn Allah's special supportive presence?
optionsEn: Pride and haste
Laziness and secrecy
InnAllaha ma‘al-ladhinat-taqaw wal-ladhina hum muhsinun ('Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good')
Wealth and harshness
explanationEn: Combining reverent restraint (Taqwa) with active kindness and excellence (Ihsan) keeps Allah's help beside you.

questionEn: In Surah Al-‘Ankabut (29:69), what happens to those who strive earnestly in Allah's cause (jahadu fina)?
optionsEn: They must figure out guidance alone
La-nahdiyannahum subulana ('We will surely guide them to Our ways')—and Allah is with the doers of good
Their striving is ignored until old age
They are left to wander without light
explanationEn: Consistent spiritual effort—such as learning dua, waking for Fajr, and serving others—opens path after path of divine guidance.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:143), how does Allah describe the Muslim community when explaining the sanctity of the Qiblah?
optionsEn: An extreme nation isolated in caves
A nation forbidden from travel
Ummatan wasata — a balanced, just, upright middle nation
A nation focused solely on commerce
explanationEn: Moderation and balance in worship, charity, and daily life reflect this Qur'anic identity.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:268), how do Satan's whispers differ from Allah's promise regarding generosity?
optionsEn: Allah promises scarcity to generous people
Both warn against helping travelers
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty (fadl)
Satan encourages secret charity
explanationEn: Recognizing that anxiety about giving comes from Shaytan frees believers to give joyfully while trusting Allah's bounty.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:27), what daily cosmic transition demonstrates Allah's power to bring relief out of difficulty?
optionsEn: Daylight remains fixed for forty days
Seasons never change across earth
He merges night into day and day into night, brings the living out of the dead, and provides for whom He wills without account
Provision is capped at fixed wages
explanationEn: Watching dawn break after dark night reminds the supplicant that Al-Hayy Al-Razzaq brings life and light out of every dark season.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu‘ara (26:88–89), what alone will benefit a human being on the Day when neither wealth nor children avail?
optionsEn: One who speaks ten ancient dialects
Illa man atallaha bi-qalbin salim ('Except one who comes to Allah with a sound, pure heart')
One who brings marble deeds of sale
One who built tall towers
explanationEn: Purifying the heart of shirk, malice, and arrogance through dhikr and repentance is the core purpose of all dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:257), what role does Allah fulfill for those who believe?
optionsEn: He leaves them to navigate darkness unaided
He assists only during harvest months
He turns light back into shadow
Allahu waliyyul-ladhina amanu yukhrijuhum minaz-zulumati ilan-nur ('Allah is the ally/protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darknesses into light')
explanationEn: Notice 'darknesses' is plural (zulumat) while 'light' is singular (an-nur): confusion has many paths, while Allah's truth is one clear light.

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf (12:40), what declaration did Prophet Yusuf (AS) share even while inside prison?
optionsEn: Stars govern human hearts
Inil-hukmu illa lillah ('Legislation/judgment belongs to Allah alone'); He has commanded that you worship none except Him
Prison wardens hold ultimate destiny
Silence is better than sharing faith
explanationEn: Whether in prison or palace, Yusuf's (AS) unwavering focus on Allah's sovereignty anchored his prayers and counsel.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:188), what humility did Allah instruct Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to state regarding unseen harm and benefit?
optionsEn: No earthly trial can ever touch a prophet
I hold keys to every unseen treasure
I possess not for myself any benefit or harm except what Allah wills; if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much good and no evil would touch me
I control rainfall across Arabia
explanationEn: Because only Allah knows the unseen and holds benefit and harm, all supplication is directed exclusively to Him.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:90), what three virtues does Allah command alongside three vices He forbids?
optionsEn: Commands isolation from family and trade
Commands justice, excellence (ihsan), and giving to relatives; forbids immorality, bad conduct, and oppression
Commands boasting, hoarding, and vengeance
Commands silence in mosques and harshness outdoors
explanationEn: Recited every Friday in Khutbahs worldwide, 16:90 outlines the moral landscape that keeps a believer's prayers pure.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:190–193), what ethical boundary governs even legitimate self-defense?
optionsEn: Strike civilians and orchards freely
Reject reconciliation even if peace is offered
Ignore peace treaties whenever convenient
Do not transgress limits ('wa la ta‘tadu'); indeed Allah does not love transgressors
explanationEn: Refusing transgression preserves moral integrity and keeps Allah's support with the believer.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:1), how did Allah honor Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at night from Al-Masjid al-Haram to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi asra bi-‘abdihi laylan ('Exalted is He who took His servant by night')—calling him 'His servant' (‘abdihi) at the pinnacle of honor
Sending him on a commercial caravan
Leaving him in Makkah without revelation
Calling him king of earthly empires
explanationEn: Being Allah's loving servant (‘abd) is the highest spiritual title a human can bear, honored in Al-Isra and in Salawat.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fath (48:29), how are the Prophet ﷺ and his companions described in worship and mutual tenderness?
optionsEn: Competing for marble palaces
Avoiding prostration during travels
Harsh toward one another and proud before Allah
Merciful among themselves (ruhama'u baynahum), seen bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure, with traces of prostration on their faces
explanationEn: Tenderness toward fellow believers paired with deep devotion in Ruku‘ and Sujud defines Prophetic companionship.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hashr (59:9), what noble quality of the Ansar in Madinah is praised forever?
optionsEn: They kept orchards locked during famine
They love those who emigrated to them, feel no envy over what immigrants were given, and prefer others over themselves even when in need (ithar)
They charged high rents to emigrants
They refused to share water wells
explanationEn: Selfless generosity (ithar) toward guests and pilgrims echoes the spirit of Madinah and brings Allah's ultimate success.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas (28:55), how do wise believers respond when exposed to foolish, idle, or abusive speech?
optionsEn: They argue until midnight
They abandon prayer out of anger
They turn away from it and say: 'For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds; peace be upon you, we do not seek the ignorant'
They memorize insults to repeat later
explanationEn: Preserving dignity and peace keeps the heart calm and ready for dhikr.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Furqan (25:63), what serene reply do ‘Ibadur-Rahman give when the ignorant address them rudely?
optionsEn: They boast of ancestral battles
They respond with harsher insults
They slam doors in frustration
Qalu salama ('They say words of peace') while walking gently upon the earth
explanationEn: Walking humbly and answering rudeness with peace embodies lived Sunnah grace.

questionEn: In Surah Ar-Ra‘d (13:22), what four traits earn the eternal Peace of the Gardens of ‘Adn?
optionsEn: Seeking fame in public squares
Hoarding silver, sleeping late, avoiding neighbors, and boasting
Patience seeking the Countenance of their Lord, establishing Salah, spending secretly and openly from what Allah provided, and repelling evil with good
Traveling without greeting family
explanationEn: Notice how secret charity and answering evil with good crown patience and prayer.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:105), what inheritance did Allah record in the Zabur after the Reminder?
optionsEn: That the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants (‘ibadiyas-salihun)
Only by those who build iron fortresses
Never by peaceful worshippers
Only by the strongest gold merchants
explanationEn: Long-term hope in Allah's promise keeps believers steadfast in prayer and righteous service.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:115), what comforting realization applies when direction or circumstance prevents knowing every outward detail?
optionsEn: Allah hears only inside two cities
Prayers must wait until landmarks appear
To Allah belong the east and the west; so wherever you turn, there is the Countenance/presence of Allah—indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing
Worship stops whenever skies are overcast
explanationEn: While we face the Qiblah in Salah whenever possible, remembering Allah's boundless presence fills every direction with reverence.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:32), how is honoring the sacred symbols and rites of Allah (sha‘a'irillah) described?
optionsEn: An unnecessary burden for travelers
Whoever honors the sacred symbols of Allah—indeed, it is from the piety/Taqwa of hearts
Limited to stone carvings
A mere cultural custom without inner meaning
explanationEn: Revering the Kaaba, Safa and Marwah, Arafah, the Qur'an, and Salah nurtures deep Taqwa inside the heart.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:37), what reaches Allah from sacrificial offerings during Eid al-Adha and Hajj?
optionsEn: Only public praise from onlookers
Only the weight of the animal's horns
Only the price paid in silver coins
Neither their meat nor their blood reaches Allah, but what reaches Him is Taqwa (piety and sincerity) from you
explanationEn: In every sacrifice, charity, and dua, Allah gazes straight at the sincerity and Taqwa of the heart.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:158), how does Allah reassure pilgrims walking between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: Only scholars may climb Safa

Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah; whoever performs Hajj or Umrah has no blame in walking between them—and whoever volunteers good, Allah is Appreciative (Shakir) and Knowing
Running replaces all dua
Walking between them is discouraged in summer
explanationEn: Allah's Name Ash-Shakir ('The Appreciative') honors every drop of sweat and whispered prayer during Sa‘i.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:96–97), what three clear signs and blessings mark the First House established for mankind in Makkah?
optionsEn: Gold gates, snowfalls, and cedar groves
Blessed (mubarakan), guidance for the worlds (hudan lil-‘alamin), and the Station of Ibrahim (Maqam Ibrahim) with sanctuary security
Exclusive access for one tribe only
Royal palaces and sea harbors
explanationEn: Standing before the Kaaba and praying behind Maqam Ibrahim connects the pilgrim directly to Ibrahim's (AS) legacy.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Quraysh (106:3–4), why are the inhabitants of Makkah urged to worship the Lord of this House (the Kaaba)?
optionsEn: Who exempted them from prayer
Who gave them snowy winters
Who isolated them from caravans
Who has fed them, saving them from hunger, and made them safe, saving them from fear
explanationEn: Remembering that Al-Razzaq feeds us and Al-Mu'min grants us security inspires grateful worship in Makkah and at home.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:125), what two roles did Allah decree for the Sacred House (the Kaaba) in Makkah?
optionsEn: A place of frequent return/gathering for mankind (mathabatan lin-nas) and a place of sanctuary/safety (amna)
A monument visited only once a century
A seasonal warehouse for spices
A fortress closed to pilgrims
explanationEn: Every pilgrim who leaves Makkah longing immediately to return experiences the answered miracle of 'mathabatan lin-nas'.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:126), when Prophet Ibrahim (AS) prayed for Makkah's security and fruits, who did Allah say would receive worldly provision?
optionsEn: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day—and even disbelievers enjoy temporary provision in this world before final accountability
Provision is withheld until Judgment Day
Only kings who arrive with gold
Only farmers living near Yemen
explanationEn: Allah's general mercy sustains all inhabitants in Makkah, while eternal honor belongs to faithful gratitude.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:77–78), what closing sequence of worship closes the surah of pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Boast of your journey upon returning home
Argue over tribal precedence
Stop praying once you leave Mina
Bow, prostrate, worship your Lord, and do good so you may succeed—and hold fast to Allah, He is your Protector (Mawla), an excellent Protector and Helper
explanationEn: Ending Hajj reflections with Ruku‘, Sujud, doing good, and holding fast to Allah keeps the pilgrimage spirit alive year-round.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab (33:43), what happens when Allah and His angels send blessings (yusalli ‘alaykum) upon believers who remember Him?
optionsEn: To bring you out of darknesses into the light—and ever is He, to the believers, Merciful
To double silver coins overnight
To silence windstorms
To grant immunity from aging
explanationEn: Remembering Allah draws down His own mercy and angelic prayers upon the believer.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nisa (4:103), when are believers instructed to continue remembering Allah even after finishing Salah?
optionsEn: Standing, sitting, and lying on your sides ('qiyaman wa qu‘udan wa ‘ala junubikum')
Only while seated inside a masjid
Never while resting in bed
Only during daylight hours
explanationEn: Dhikr is unbound by posture or location—connecting our busy day directly to Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:239), if a traveler faces urgent danger or fear during Salah, what concession of prayer and dhikr is granted?
optionsEn: Pray only silently without movement
Pray on foot or while riding, and once secure, remember Allah as He has taught you what you did not know
Wait until returning home before praying
Abandon prayer for the entire month
explanationEn: Even in danger, Salah stays alive, and returning safety is met with grateful dhikr.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:23), alongside worshipping Allah alone, what noble duty carries the highest human priority?
optionsEn: Sending gifts once every five years
Excellence and kindness toward parents (wa bil-walidayni ihsana), never even uttering 'uff' to them
Speaking gently only to wealthy elders
Addressing parents impatiently when tired
explanationEn: Serving and praying for parents softens the heart and is one of the surest keys to answered dua—as shown in the famous story of the three men trapped in a cave.

questionEn: In Surah Luqman (31:14), what two expressions of gratitude are uniquely commanded together in one sentence?
optionsEn: Give thanks to merchants and governors
Give thanks only in winter
Anishkur li wa li-walidayk ('Give thanks to Me and to your parents')
Give thanks only to neighbors
explanationEn: Placing gratitude to parents right beside gratitude to Allah highlights how deeply Allah honors filial devotion.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:7), what hopeful reminder does Allah give when relationships feel strained?
optionsEn: ‘Asallahu an yaj‘ala baynakum wa baynal-ladhina ‘adaytum minhum mawaddah ('Perhaps Allah will put affection between you and those with whom you have enmity')
Hostility between people can never heal
Never pray for reconciliation
Cut ties permanently after one disagreement
explanationEn: Praying for Allah to plant mawaddah (affection) between estranged hearts rests on His power as Al-Qadir Ar-Rahim.

questionEn: In Surah Maryam (19:96), what gift does Allah promise to plant in creation for those who believe and do righteous deeds?
optionsEn: Constant rivalry in markets
Sayaj‘alu lahumur-Rahmanu wudda ('The Most Merciful will appoint for them affection/love')
Fear in the eyes of children
Total forgetfulness among neighbors
explanationEn: Pure faith and goodness quietly draw love from Allah and sincere hearts alike.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:7), what covenantal phrase of total responsiveness did the believers utter?
optionsEn: We hear and we will debate later
We agree only on easy days
We will wait for another sign
Sami‘na wa ata‘na ('We hear and we obey')
explanationEn: Hearing Allah's guidance with eager obedience is the posture of an answered heart.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:46), what deep conviction makes humble worshippers find Salah light rather than burdensome?
optionsEn: Alladhina yazunnuna annahum mulaqu Rabbihim ('Those who are certain they will meet their Lord and to Him they will return')
Counting minutes until lunch
Seeking public praise in rows
Rushing through without reflection
explanationEn: Remembering our joyful meeting with Allah transforms Salah and dua from duty into sanctuary.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:199), why did the Qur'an command Quraysh to join all other pilgrims in standing at ‘Arafat and pouring down from there?
optionsEn: To abolish tribal arrogance so every pilgrim stands equal before Allah seeking His forgiveness
To reserve ‘Arafat for caravan merchants
To let Quraysh stay inside Muzdalifah exclusively
To shorten Hajj to a single morning
explanationEn: Everyone standing together on the plains of ‘Arafat in identical humility captures the brotherhood of Islam.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab (33:35), how does Allah honor both believing men and women who remember Him abundantly (adh-dhakirinAllaha kathiran wadh-dhakirat)?
optionsEn: Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a tremendous reward (maghfiratan wa ajran ‘azima)
Only men are rewarded for abundant dhikr
Reward applies only after age sixty
Dhikr counts only inside Madinah
explanationEn: Women and men share equal spiritual stature and tremendous reward in every tasbih, fast, charity, and dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:57–61), why do the awed believers hasten to good deeds despite already worshipping sincerely?
optionsEn: Because they fear losing money in markets
Their hearts tremble knowing they will return to their Lord, so they race forward in good deeds (yusari‘una fil-khayrat)
Because they boast to neighbors
Because they want earthly trophies
explanationEn: Reverent awe inspires eager goodness rather than complacency.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:35), what reminder accompanies the truth that every soul shall taste death?
optionsEn: We test you with evil and with good as trial, and to Us you will be returned
Only hardship is a test, never prosperity
Prosperity proves unconditional favor
Life has no accountability
explanationEn: Both ease and hardship are tests—ease tests gratitude, and hardship tests patience and dua.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shura (42:30), what principle of spiritual mercy reminds believers that Allah pardons far more than He holds us accountable for?
optionsEn: He never pardons any slip
Whatever misfortune strikes you is for what your own hands have earned, and He pardons much ('wa ya‘fu ‘an kathir')
Every slip brings instant ruin
Only kings receive pardon
explanationEn: Remembering 'wa ya‘fu ‘an kathir' fills the heart with gratitude for Allah's daily forbearance.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:26), what happens to sincere hearts when Allah sets forth a parable?
optionsEn: They dismiss it as idle legend
They ask for worldly payment
They ignore its moral lesson
Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord, and Allah guides many by it
explanationEn: Approaching the Qur'an with humility turns every verse into guidance and personal dua.

questionEn: In Surah Yunus (10:57–58), what four descriptions are given to the Qur'an as a source of joy greater than anything people hoard?
optionsEn: An admonition from your Lord, a healing (shifa') for what is in the breasts, guidance, and mercy for the believers
A seasonal farming almanac
A book of commercial tax laws only
A collection of tribal war songs
explanationEn: Reciting the Qur'an as a healing for anxious hearts ('shifa'un lima fis-sudur') precedes every joyful dua.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:82), what twofold blessing does Allah send down in the Qur'an for believers?
optionsEn: A healing (shifa') and a mercy (rahmah) for the believers
Secret charms for merchants
Material gold for collectors
Exemption from daily prayers
explanationEn: Turning to the Qur'an during physical or emotional pain seeks Allah's promised shifa and mercy.

questionEn: In Surah Fussilat (41:44), how is the Qur'an described for those who believe?
optionsEn: Applicable only in ancient Arabia
A riddle understood only by astrologers
Huwa lilladhina amanu hudan wa shifa' ('It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing')
Restricted to scholars over seventy
explanationEn: Guidance and healing walk hand-in-hand whenever we open the Book of Allah sincerely.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hashr (59:20), who alone are declared 'the attainers of success' (humul-fa'izun)?
optionsEn: Those who collect the heaviest silver
Ashab al-Jannah — the companions of Paradise, contrasted with those who forgot Allah so He caused them to forget their own souls
Those who rule coastal cities
Those who memorize royal lineages
explanationEn: Remembering Allah keeps us mindful of our own soul's true welfare and eternal success.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:189), what wisdom did Allah teach when companions asked about the crescent moons (ahillah)?
optionsEn: Climb through back walls for piety
They are measurements of time for people and for Hajj—and righteousness is entering houses by their doors and fearing Allah
Crescents control human luck
Never travel during a new moon
explanationEn: Welcoming the new crescent moon with the Sunnah dua for security and faith connects lunar timekeeping to Allah's guidance.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fath (48:18), what descended upon the companions who pledged allegiance beneath the tree at Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: Allah was well-pleased with them, knew what was in their hearts, sent down tranquility (sakinah) upon them, and rewarded them with an imminent conquest
They were told to abandon Umrah forever
They were denied access to Makkah permanently
A sudden flood scattered their camp
explanationEn: Sincerity in the heart earned Allah's Ridwan and Sakinah even before Makkah opened.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:25), what reassurance comforts anyone trying earnestly to honor their parents and make dua for them?
optionsEn: Only perfect people receive mercy
Never ask forgiveness after mistakes
One accidental sigh erases all good deeds
