Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves; if you are righteous, indeed He is ever Forgiving to those who repeatedly turn back to Him (lil-awwabin ghafura)
explanationEn: Allah's mercy welcomes the 'awwabin'—those who constantly turn back to Him in love and humility.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:284), what awe-inspiring truth precedes the closing dua of Surah Al-Baqarah?
optionsEn: Whether you reveal what is within your selves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it—reminding us why 2:286 begs for pardon and mercy
Only spoken contracts matter to Allah
Mercy is withheld from secret sins
Concealed intentions carry no value
explanationEn: Because Allah knows even secret intentions, purifying our inner thoughts through dua and repentance is essential.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:45), what two essentials are commanded when facing any formidable challenge or adversary?
optionsEn: Rely solely on iron shields
Stand firm (fathbutu) and remember Allah abundantly (wadhkurullaha kathira) so that you may succeed
Boast loudly about past victories
Retreat immediately and stay silent
explanationEn: Steadfastness paired with abundant dhikr keeps courage grounded in Allah rather than ego.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:194), how does the Qur'an sum up Allah's constant support for mindful believers?
optionsEn: Wa‘lamu annAllaha ma‘al-muttaqin ('And know that Allah is with those who have Taqwa')
Taqwa brings no help in hardship
Wait until peace returns before being mindful
Allah supports only the strongest tribes
explanationEn: Practicing Taqwa—mindfulness of Allah in private and public—ensures His protective companionship.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:11), how are believers reminded to maintain reliance on Allah after escaping plots unharmed?
optionsEn: Forget past rescues once safety arrives
Avoid thanking Allah publicly
Credit solely your watchmen
Remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you, and He withheld their hands—so fear Allah and upon Allah let believers rely
explanationEn: Recalling past moments when Allah quietly averted unseen harm deepens gratitude and daily Tawakkul.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shura (42:15), what firm yet peaceful supplication-declaration expresses total trust in Allah's justice?
optionsEn: Let us settle every disagreement with anger
Avoid mentioning Allah before strangers
Claim victory without patience
Allahu Rabbuna wa Rabbukum; lana a‘maluna wa lakum a‘malukum; la hujjata baynana wa baynakum; Allahu yajma‘u baynana wa ilayhil-masir
explanationEn: Leaving final judgment to Allah preserves clarity of faith alongside dignified peace.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:254), before what inevitable Day are believers urged to spend from what Allah provided?
optionsEn: A spring harvest fair
A royal jubilee
A Day in which there will be no bargaining, no worldly friendship of escape, and no unauthorized intercession
A winter caravan crossing
explanationEn: Giving charity and making sincere dua today invests in the Day when worldly currencies vanish.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab (33:70–71), what two outcomes does Allah promise those who fear Him and speak 'qawlan sadida' (truthful, upright words)?
optionsEn: He will make you silent forever
He will delay your prayers
He will double merchant taxes
He will amend/rectify your deeds for you (yuslih lakum a‘malakum) and forgive you your sins
explanationEn: Truthful, upright speech purifies our daily deeds and invites Allah's forgiveness.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:98), what protective Sunnah phrase are believers commanded to recite before reading the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Wait until midnight before reciting
Seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed (A‘udhu billahi minash-Shaytanir-rajim)
Say Amin before opening the cover
Bismillah only at the end of a surah
explanationEn: Saying Isti‘adhah clears distractions and opens the heart to reflect on Allah's words.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A‘raf (7:204), what courteous attitude is commanded when the Qur'an is being recited?
optionsEn: Listen attentively to it and remain silent (fastami‘u lahu wa ansitu) so that you may receive mercy
Walk out before the verse finishes
Speak softly with friends while listening
Count tasbih beads loudly over the reciter
explanationEn: Attentive, respectful silence during Qur'anic recitation draws down Allah's mercy.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:121), how do true reciters of the Book engage with it?
optionsEn: They read only for competition prizes
Yatlunahu haqqa tilawatih ('They recite it with its true observance'—believing in it, pondering it, and acting upon it)
They keep it wrapped unread on high shelves
They speed-read without reflection
explanationEn: True tilawah unites correct recitation, humble reflection, and living its guidance in dua and character.

questionEn: In Surah Sad (38:29), for what dual purpose did Allah reveal the blessed Book?
optionsEn: To settle commercial bargains
Solely to decorate stone walls
Li-yaddabbaru ayatihi wa li-yatadhakkara ulul-albab ('That they might reflect deeply upon its verses and that people of understanding might take heed')
To memorize without understanding
explanationEn: Pondering the Qur'an's verses (tadabbur) nourishes heartfelt, personal duas.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qamar (54:17), what comforting phrase is repeated four times to encourage every seeker learning Qur'anic duas?
optionsEn: It requires fifty years to learn one surah
Memorization is reserved for prophets
Wa laqad yassarnal-Qur'ana lidh-dhikri fahal min muddakir ('And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?')
Only scholars born in Makkah can memorize it
explanationEn: Allah Himself made His Book easy to memorize, understand, and remember—welcoming every sincere learner.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:105), what gentle reminder guards believers against despair when others ignore good counsel?
optionsEn: ‘Alaykum anfusakum ('Upon you is your own soul'); those who go astray cannot harm you when you have been guided—to Allah is the return of you all
Force faith upon unwilling hearts
Abandon your own Salah when neighbors err
Stop praying for humanity
explanationEn: Staying steady in one's own faith, prayer, and good example protects the soul while leaving outcomes to Allah.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:111), what noble transaction does Allah describe with the believers?
optionsEn: Trading prayer for earthly titles
Buying exemption from charity
Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for Paradise
Selling spiritual loyalty for silver coins
explanationEn: Dedicating one's life and resources to Allah brings joy to worship and certainty in His promise.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:136), what inclusive faith statement do Muslims affirm regarding all Prophets of Allah?
optionsEn: We believe in Allah and what was revealed to us and to Ibrahim, Isma‘il, Ishaq, Ya‘qub, the Tribes, Musa, ‘Isa, and all prophets—we make no distinction among any of them
We honor only one prophet and reject earlier ones
Duas of past prophets have no value
Earlier prophets never taught Tawhid
explanationEn: Loving and honoring all prophets (AS) explains why Muslims cherish and recite the Qur'anic duas of Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Yunus, Ayyub, and Zakariyya (AS).

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:110), what moral responsibility earns this Ummah the honor of being the best community brought forth for mankind?
optionsEn: Enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and believing firmly in Allah
Withdrawing from public kindness
Hoarding grain in cities
Boasting about ancestry
explanationEn: Active moral care for humanity alongside steadfast Iman reflects prophetic compassion.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:125), what three gentle principles must guide inviting others to Allah's path?
optionsEn: With harshness in public squares
With wisdom (hikmah), goodly instruction (maw‘izah hasanah), and arguing/discussing in the best, kindest manner
With mockery and raised voices
With impatience toward beginners
explanationEn: Wisdom and gracious dialogue reflect the prophetic warmth of Islam.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:197), what three behaviors must pilgrims strictly guard against during Hajj?
optionsEn: Praying behind Maqam Ibrahim
Rafath (immodest/intimate talk or relations), fusuq (sinful disobedience), and jidal (quarrelling/disputing)
Making Talbiyah while walking
Drinking Zamzam, smiling, and helping elders
explanationEn: Keeping one's tongue free of arguments and sins during pilgrimage protects the spiritual purity of Hajj.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hijr (15:45–46), what welcoming greeting awaits the God-conscious as they enter the Gardens and springs of Paradise?
optionsEn: Enter silently without companions
Bring letters from worldly governors
Udkhuluha bi-salamin aminin ('Enter it in peace, safe and secure')—with every trace of rancor removed from their hearts
Wait outside the gates until winter
explanationEn: Peace and security (Salam and Amn) crowned by pure, loving hearts summarize the eternal home believers pray for.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:27), what warning safeguards trust and integrity in family and community life?
optionsEn: Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts (amanatikum) while you know
Break small trusts in private
Ignore borrowed belongings
Keep promises only when witnessed in writing
explanationEn: Honoring trusts (amanah)—including secrets, promises, and public duties—keeps one's prayers pure and upright.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:8), what twin traits of reliability characterize successful believers?
optionsEn: Those who forget borrowed items
Those who faithfully guard their trusts (li-amanatihim) and their covenants/promises (wa ‘ahdihim ra‘un)
Those who break oaths when traveling
Those who postpone every promise
explanationEn: Trustworthiness in daily dealings aligns outward integrity with sincere devotion in Salah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:277), what three pillars lead to peace free from fear and grief?
optionsEn: Seeking fame in markets
Living in solitude without community
Faith, righteous deeds, establishing Salah, and giving Zakah
Hoarding silver and avoiding charity
explanationEn: Faith, Salah, and Zakah weave a safety net for both the individual soul and the broader society.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas (28:88), what majestic truth concludes the story of Musa and Qarun, grounding all worship?
optionsEn: Stars outlive Allah's decree
Earthly kingdoms never change
Call not upon any other deity alongside Allah; everything will perish except His Countenance (illa Wajhah)—to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned
Silver vaults endure forever
explanationEn: Directing every dua purely to the Eternal Countenance of Allah leaves temporary anxieties behind.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:160), what promise awaits those who repent, amend their ways (aslahu), and make the truth clear?
optionsEn: They remain barred from forgiveness
Fa-ula'ika atubu ‘alayhim wa ana Tawwabur-Rahim ('Upon those I will turn in acceptance, for I am the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful')
They must flee their homeland
Their past deeds stay unaccepted
explanationEn: Repentance combined with upright repair (islah) meets Allah's eager welcome as At-Tawwab Ar-Rahim.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:11), what human flaw in hasty moments is highlighted regarding dua?
optionsEn: Man sometimes prays for evil/harm in rash anger just as eagerly as he prays for good—for man is ever hasty (‘ajula)
Man only prays when asleep
Man never asks for anything quickly
Man always speaks calmly in anger
explanationEn: This verse warns parents and believers never to curse themselves, their children, or their wealth in anger, lest it coincide with an hour of acceptance.

questionEn: In Surah Yunus (10:12), what contrast in human prayer does Allah warn believers to overcome?
optionsEn: Calling upon Allah earnestly when affliction touches them—lying, sitting, or standing—yet walking away forgetfully as soon as the harm is removed
Forgetting to ask during storms
Praying only on sunny afternoons
Thanking Allah excessively after healing
explanationEn: Remembering Allah in comfort and health keeps our relationship with Him loyal rather than merely crisis-driven.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:202), what do those who recite balanced duas like 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah...' receive?
optionsEn: A rightful share (nasib) of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account
Only half of one worldly blessing
Reward deducted for asking about this world
No share until after a century
explanationEn: Asking Allah for both worldly good and Hereafter bliss honors Islam's balanced view of life.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:133), what reassurance did Ya‘qub's (AS) sons give their father on his deathbed regarding whom they would worship?
optionsEn: We will worship only stars
We will adopt new idols in Egypt
We will abandon prayer until harvest
We will worship your God and the God of your fathers—Ibrahim, Isma‘il, and Ishaq—one God, and to Him we are Muslims
explanationEn: Passing down pure Tawhid and living prayers from parents to children is the greatest inheritance a family can leave.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:84), how did Allah respond to Prophet Ayyub's (AS) humble dua?
optionsEn: He removed his affliction, restored his family and the like of them with them as a mercy from Him, and made it a reminder for worshippers
He replaced his patience with wealth alone
He hid his story from future nations
He left him ill for another fifty years
explanationEn: Allah called Ayyub's restoration 'dhikra lil-‘abidin'—an enduring reminder for all worshippers never to lose hope in Allah's mercy.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya (21:90), how did Allah answer Prophet Zakariyya's (AS) prayer despite his wife's barrenness?
optionsEn: He told him to adopt a royal prince
He refused because of old age
He postponed the answer to the next generation
We responded to him, granted him Yahya, and made his wife fertile/sound for him (wa aslahna lahu zawjah)
explanationEn: When Allah answers a dua, He removes every natural barrier—even healing barrenness to bring forth Yahya (AS).

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas (28:25–27), how swiftly did Allah answer Prophet Musa's (AS) brief dua 'Rabbi inni lima anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqir'?
optionsEn: He walked back alone to Egypt empty-handed
He remained hungry in the shade for ten years
The flock wandered away permanently
One of the two women returned walking bashfully, inviting him to her father's home where he found safety, honest work, and marriage
explanationEn: Musa (AS) first served others selflessly, then stood back and humbly asked Allah—and relief knocked immediately.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:127), how did Allah honor Ibrahim and Isma‘il's (AS) humility while building the Kaaba?
optionsEn: He accepted their work, turned the Kaaba into the Qiblah of billions, and kept their 'Rabbana taqabbal minna' on Muslim tongues forever
He erased their footprints from Makkah
He kept their names secret
He ordered the Kaaba torn down later
explanationEn: Sincere work coupled with 'Rabbana taqabbal minna' never goes unnoticed by As-Sami‘ Al-‘Alim.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An‘am (6:164), what principle of personal responsibility and divine justice brings clarity to daily striving?
optionsEn: Strangers pay for one's choices
Ancestors carry all sins of descendants
Wealth transfers moral responsibility
Every soul earns only upon itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another; then to your Lord is your return
explanationEn: Standing personally accountable before Allah encourages sincere individual repentance and mindful living.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk (67:13–14), why is it pointless to disguise insincerity in supplication?
optionsEn: Whispered prayers are ignored by angels
Allah hears only inside mosques
Whether you conceal your speech or publicize it, indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts—should not He who created know?
Only written scrolls are read
explanationEn: Al-Latif Al-Khabir (the Subtle, the All-Aware) knows every hidden ache inside the heart even before words form.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:207), what supreme dedication describes believers who sacrifice comfort for Allah's pleasure?
optionsEn: Those who hide from duties in comfort
Those who bargain for temporary applause
And among people is he who sells/gives himself seeking the pleasure of Allah (mardatillah), and Allah is Kind (Ra'uf) to His servants
Those who seek praise in markets
explanationEn: Seeking Allah's Ridwan (pleasure) makes every sacrifice feel light under the gaze of Ar-Ra'uf.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fajr (89:27–30), what tender invitation awaits the tranquil soul (an-nafsul-mutma'innah) at death?
optionsEn: Return to your Lord well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]; enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise
Wander endlessly across empty plains
Remain forgotten outside the gates
Wait alone without companions
explanationEn: Consistent dhikr, Salah, and dua nurture the 'tranquil soul' that hears Allah's warmest welcome home.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:154), why are believers told not to say that those slain in Allah's cause are dead?
optionsEn: Rather, they are alive [with their Lord], though you perceive it not
Because they return to build stone houses
Because death never exists for anyone
Because they continue trading in earthly markets
explanationEn: Trusting Allah's honor for the righteous gives comfort to grieving hearts and perspective to earthly life.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:46), what warning guards the spiritual strength of a community?
optionsEn: Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute (wa la tanaza‘u) lest you lose courage and your strength/wind depart—and be patient
Split into rival factions before prayer
Avoid consulting elders
Argue loudly over minor preferences
explanationEn: Unity, obedience, and patience preserve collective barakah and strength.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:215), when companions asked what they should spend in charity, whom did Allah prioritize in the answer?
optionsEn: Only public monuments
Parents, near relatives, orphans, the needy, and the stranded traveler—and whatever good you do, Allah is Knowing of it
Only wealthy guild masters
Only distant emperors
explanationEn: Caring first for parents, family, orphans, the poor, and travelers ('ibn as-sabil') turns charity into lived mercy.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:245), what inspiring metaphor does Allah use for giving generously in His cause?
optionsEn: Losing wages to strangers permanently
Paying tax with zero return
Dropping coins into bottomless oceans
Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan (qardan hasana), so He will multiply it for him many times over?
explanationEn: Giving purely for Allah is an investment guaranteed by the Owner of all treasures, who constricts and expands provision.

questionEn: In Surah Al ‘Imran (3:186), what serene response is taught when facing hurtful words from critics?
optionsEn: Respond with bitter insults immediately
Hide from every neighbor
Stop doing good deeds altogether
You will certainly be tested in your wealth and yourselves and hear much insult—but if you are patient and fear Allah, that is of the matters of resolve
explanationEn: Patience and Taqwa keep believers steady above provocation.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu‘ara (26:80), how did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) express absolute certainty regarding illness and recovery?
optionsEn: Only desert herbs hold healing power
Medicine works independently of Allah
Wa idha maridtu fa-Huwa yashfin ('And when I am ill, it is He who cures me')
Illness means Allah forgot the believer
explanationEn: Taking lawful medical treatment while knowing Ash-Shafi (the Healer) alone grants cure unites wisdom with Tawhid.

questionEn: Which supplication did the Prophet ﷺ title 'Sayyid al-Istighfar' (the Master Supplication for Seeking Forgiveness)?
optionsEn: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil-‘Azim
Allahumma Anta Rabbi la ilaha illa Anta, khalaqtani wa ana ‘abduk...
Allahumma inni as'alukal-huda wat-tuqa
HasbiyAllahu la ilaha illa Huwa
explanationEn: Sayyid al-Istighfar combines Tawhid, servitude, covenant loyalty, gratitude for Allah's favors, confession of sin, and seeking pardon.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 6306, what immense promise is given to a believer who recites Sayyid al-Istighfar with firm conviction in the morning and dies before evening?
optionsEn: He will receive only half of his daily deeds
He must wait until Friday before mercy reaches him
He will be among the people of Paradise (min ahlil-jannah)
His family must recite it forty times on his behalf
explanationEn: The same promise applies if recited with conviction in the evening and he passes away before morning.

questionEn: In Sayyid al-Istighfar, what two contrasting realities does the supplicant acknowledge right before begging 'faghfir li' ('so forgive me')?
optionsEn: Abū'u laka bi-ni‘matika ‘alayya, wa abū'u bi-dhanbi ('I acknowledge Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin')
I boast of my night prayers and blame my neighbors
I list my travels and excuse my mistakes
I recall my wealth and complain of winter
explanationEn: Pairing gratitude for Allah's blessings with honest confession of our sins melts pride and attracts Allah's forgiveness.

questionEn: What closing truth ends Sayyid al-Istighfar: 'fa-innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba...'?
optionsEn: illa yawmal-‘Id ('...except on Eid day')
illa bil-mal ('...except through gold')
illa Anta ('...for none forgives sins except You')
illa fil-Madinah ('...except in Madinah')
explanationEn: Concluding with 'none forgives sins except You' seals the prayer in pure Tawhid and desperate hope.

questionEn: In Sayyid al-Istighfar, what does 'wa ana ‘ala ‘ahdika wa wa‘dika mastata‘tu' express?
optionsEn: I pledge never to travel across seas
I vow to fast every single day of the year
I promise never to sleep during daylight
I remain faithful to Your covenant and Your promise to the best of my ability
explanationEn: Adding 'mastata‘tu' ('as much as I am able') balances earnest commitment with humble realism about human limitation.

questionEn: Which three surahs recited three times each in the morning and evening did the Prophet ﷺ say 'will suffice you against everything'?
optionsEn: Al-Fil, Quraysh, and Al-Ma‘un
Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas (the Three Quls)
Al-Kafirun, Al-Kawthar, and Al-‘Asr
Ad-Duha, Ash-Sharh, and At-Tin
explanationEn: Telling ‘Abdullah ibn Khubayb (RA) to recite these three surahs three times morning and evening gives complete spiritual protection.

questionEn: What protection is promised to one who recites 'Bismillahilladhi la yadurru ma‘asmihi shay'un fil-ardi wa la fis-sama'i wa Huwas-Sami‘ul-‘Alim' three times every morning and evening?
optionsEn: All his debts vanish without repayment
He will automatically memorize ten chapters overnight
He will never need to eat meals again
Nothing will harm him (unexpectedly) during that day or night
explanationEn: Invoking Allah's Name—the All-Hearing, All-Knowing—shields the believer from sudden calamity.

questionEn: In the morning/evening dhikr 'Raditu billahi Rabban wa bil-Islami dinan wa bi-Muhammadin ﷺ nabiyyan', what three joyful satisfactions are affirmed three times?
optionsEn: Being pleased with travel, commerce, and sleep
Being well-pleased with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet
Being pleased with one's wealth, house, and climate
Being pleased with lineage, status, and clothing
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever says this three times morning and evening has a right upon Allah to please him on the Day of Resurrection.

questionEn: How does the wording of 'Allahumma bika asbahna wa bika amsayna...' change when moving from morning to evening?
optionsEn: Evening replaces 'Allahumma' with 'SubhanAllah' ten times
Morning omits mentioning life and death altogether
Morning begins 'bika asbahna' and ends 'wa ilaykan-nushur' (resurrection); evening begins 'bika amsayna' and ends 'wa ilaykal-masir' (final return)
Both morning and evening use identical words with no change
explanationEn: Linking waking morning to resurrection (nushur) and restful evening to returning home (masir) turns time itself into a spiritual reminder.

questionEn: Which brief morning and evening supplication entrusts every affair completely to Allah without leaving oneself alone even for 'the blink of an eye'?
optionsEn: Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi ‘adada khalqih
Allahu Akbar kabira wal-hamdulillahi kathira
Ya Hayyu ya Qayyumu bi-rahmatika astaghith, aslih li sha'ni kullahu wa la takilni ila nafsi tarfata ‘ayn
Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised Fatimah (RA) to recite this timeless plea for self-rectification and total dependence on the Ever-Living Sustainer.

questionEn: When Juwayriyah bint al-Harith (RA) stayed seated making dhikr from Fajr until mid-morning, what four-phrase tasbih did the Prophet ﷺ say outweighed all she had recited?
optionsEn: La ilaha illAllah once silently
SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi ‘adada khalqihi, wa rida nafsihi, wa zinata ‘arshihi, wa midada kalimatih (three times)
Amin repeated thirty-three times
Allahu Akbar seven times at noon
explanationEn: Measuring Allah's praise by the number of His creation, His own pleasure, the weight of His Throne, and the ink of His words multiplies reward effortlessly.

questionEn: What immense forgiveness is promised in Sahih Muslim 2692 for reciting 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi' one hundred times in the morning and evening?
optionsEn: No one will bring anything better on the Day of Resurrection except someone who said the same or more (and sins like sea foam are wiped away)
Guarantee of never experiencing rain
Immediate doubling of silver coins
Exemption from Friday prayer
explanationEn: Simple, steady remembrance keeps the heart light and earns unmatched weight on the Day of Judgment.

questionEn: What three areas of bodily health and perception does the believer ask Allah to keep sound three times morning and evening in 'Allahumma ‘afini fi badani...'?
optionsEn: Sleep, appetite, and travel speed
Voice, footsteps, and memory of poetry
Body (badani), hearing (sam‘i), and sight (basari)
Hands, feet, and silver coins
explanationEn: Immediately after asking for soundness of body, hearing, and sight, the supplication seeks refuge from disbelief, poverty, and punishment of the grave.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ teach Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) to recite 'Allahumma ‘alimal-ghaybi wash-shahadati fatiras-samawati wal-ard...' morning, evening, and before sleep?
optionsEn: To predict next month's desert weather
To choose profitable camel trade routes
To seek refuge from the evil of one's own soul (sharri nafsi), the evil and shirk of Satan, and harming oneself or another Muslim
To shorten obligatory prayers during summer
explanationEn: Asking protection against our own lower ego (nafs) alongside Satan recognizes that inner negligence is as dangerous as outer temptation.

questionEn: What personal covenant did the Prophet ﷺ never leave reciting morning and evening asking Allah for soundness (‘afiyah) in religion, worldly life, family, and wealth?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni as'alukal-‘afwa wal-‘afiyata fid-dunya wal-akhirah; Allahumma inni as'alukal-‘afwa wal-‘afiyata fi dini wa dunyaya wa ahli wa mali...
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: This comprehensive Sunnah dua also asks Allah to conceal one's faults, calm one's fears, and guard one from front, back, right, left, above, and below.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5074 / Sunan Ibn Majah 3871

questionEn: In the ‘afiyah morning and evening dua (Abu Dawud 5074), from which unusual direction does the believer specifically seek refuge against being 'swallowed up' (an ughtala min tahti)?
optionsEn: From inside marketplaces
From beneath me (min tahti)
From behind mountain ranges
From inside libraries
explanationEn: Asking Allah's protection from all six directions—ahead, behind, right, left, above, and beneath—wraps the day in divine security.

questionEn: According to Sunan Abi Dawud 5073, whoever says 'Allahumma ma asbaha bi min ni‘matin aw bi-ahadin min khalqika fa-minka wahdaka...' in the morning has fulfilled what daily duty?
optionsEn: He has completed his annual Zakah
He has replaced Fajr Sunnah
He has finished voluntary Hajj
He has fulfilled his gratitude (adda shukra yawmih) for that day
explanationEn: Crediting Allah alone for every blessing upon oneself and every creature discharges the morning's duty of shukr—and the evening version discharges the night's shukr.

questionEn: In the morning dhikr 'Asbahna ‘ala fitratil-Islam...', what four foundational affiliations does a Muslim renew upon waking?
optionsEn: Philosophical schools, star signs, royal charters, and poetry
Tribal ancestry, city dialect, trade guild, and seasonal calendar
Only fasting, charity, pilgrimage, and silence
The natural way of Islam (fitratil-Islam), the word of pure sincerity (kalimatil-ikhlas), the religion of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the upright path of Ibrahim (AS)
explanationEn: Starting the morning by renewing loyalty to Fitrah, Ikhlas, Sunnah, and Ibrahim's pure monotheism resets identity and purpose.

questionEn: When saying 'Allahumma inni asbahatu ushhiduka wa ushhidu hamalata ‘arshika wa mala'ikataka...' four times morning and evening, what protection does Allah grant?
optionsEn: Automatic mastery of ten languages
Exemption from traveling in summer
Immunity from ever feeling hungry
Allah frees the reciter from the Fire (one quarter per repetition, all four quarters upon saying it four times)
explanationEn: Calling Allah, the Throne-bearing angels, and all creation to witness our Shahadah four times deepens conviction and seeks deliverance from Hellfire.

questionEn: What short evening protection dua did the Prophet ﷺ guarantee prevents scorpion or venomous stings and nocturnal harm when recited three times at dusk?
optionsEn: SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
A‘udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq ('I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created')
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Narrated in Sahih Muslim 2708–2709, this dua also protects travelers whenever they halt at any stopover or hotel.

questionEn: What special reward does Sahih Muslim 2691 mention for reciting 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir' 100 times a day?
optionsEn: Replacing all five daily prayers
Counting as ten full Hajj pilgrimages
Equal to freeing ten slaves, 100 good deeds written, 100 sins erased, and a fortress of protection against Satan all day until evening
Guaranteeing earthly kingship within a week
explanationEn: Even reciting the ten-times version morning and evening brings immense protection, forgiveness, and elevation of ranks.

questionEn: In the morning adhkar 'Asbahna wa asbahal-mulku lillahi...', what two opposing vices does the supplicant ask refuge from at the close of the dua?
optionsEn: Studying Qur'an and helping guests
Walking briskly and waking early
Giving charity and speaking gently
Laziness and evil old age (al-kasali wa su'il-kibar), as well as torment in the Fire and torment in the grave
explanationEn: Seeking refuge from laziness (kasal) energizes the believer for purposeful worship, service, and livelihood.

questionEn: Right after giving the Salam of Fajr prayer, what three-fold morning request did the Prophet ﷺ regularly make according to Sunan Ibn Majah 925?
optionsEn: Tall palaces, fast horses, and quiet winters
Fame among poets, gold mines, and long sleep
Silence, solitude, and zero effort
Beneficial knowledge (‘ilman nafi‘an), pure lawful provision (rizqan tayyiban), and accepted deeds (‘amalan mutaqabbalan)
explanationEn: Starting the workday after Fajr with this exact trio aligns study, career, and worship toward Allah's pleasure.

questionEn: Which Quranic verse, if recited in the morning, protects a person from jinn until evening, and if recited in the evening, protects until morning?
optionsEn: Ayat al-Kursi (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:255)
Surah Al-Fil (105)
Surah Al-‘Asr (103)
Surah Al-Kawthar (108)
explanationEn: Authentic narrations transmitted by Ubayy ibn Ka‘b (RA) confirm Ayat al-Kursi's powerful protection morning, evening, after Salah, and before sleep.

questionEn: In morning and evening adhkar, what does reciting 'SubhanAllahil-‘Azimi wa bihamdihi' or 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi' plant for the believer in Paradise according to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3464?
optionsEn: A palm tree is planted for him in Paradise (ghurisat lahu nakhlah fil-jannah)
A marble pillar in Cairo
A wooden ship in the Red Sea
An empty tent in the desert
explanationEn: Every sincere 'SubhanAllahil-‘Azimi wa bihamdih' effortlessly gardens one's eternal home in Jannah.

questionEn: When is the ideal time window scholars recommend for reciting the Morning Adhkar (Adhkar al-Sabah)?
optionsEn: Only after midnight
Only on Mondays and Thursdays
Between Fajr prayer and sunrise (or extending into mid-morning if missed)
Strictly between Dhuhr and ‘Asr
explanationEn: Following Fajr before the day's busyness begins—echoing Qaf 50:39 ('before sunrise')—is best, though late completion remains rewarded.

questionEn: When is the ideal time window scholars recommend for reciting the Evening Adhkar (Adhkar al-Masa')?
optionsEn: Only at midday noon
Only during Ramadan
Immediately after Fajr sunrise
Between ‘Asr prayer and sunset/Maghrib (or continuing into early night if delayed)
explanationEn: Entering the transition from day to night with ‘Asr-to-Maghrib remembrance aligns with Surah Qaf 50:39 ('before sunset').

questionEn: What concise phrase of praise, forgiveness, and repentance did the Prophet ﷺ say up to 70 or 100 times in a single morning or gathering?
optionsEn: Astaghfirullaha wa atubu ilayh (or Rabbighfir li wa tub ‘alayya innaka Antat-Tawwabur-Rahim)
Allahu Akbar only once at noon
Labbayk only in Muharram
Bismillah at bedtime only
explanationEn: Even though all his past and future errors were forgiven, the Prophet ﷺ practiced constant istighfar out of gratitude and servitude.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6307 / Sahih Muslim 2702 / Abu Dawud 1516

questionEn: In the morning dua 'Asbahna wa asbahal-mulku lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin...', what five things does the believer ask for regarding the coming day?
optionsEn: Rain, snow, thunder, eclipse, and wind
Its goodness: its opening/victory (fathahu), its help (nasrahu), its light (nurahu), its blessing (barakatahu), and its guidance (hudahu)
Gold, applause, leisure, speed, and silence
Fame, sleep, titles, mirrors, and armor
explanationEn: Asking for the day's opening, aid, light, barakah, and guidance—and seeking refuge from its evil—consecrates the entire day to Allah.

questionEn: Which phrase of morning and evening dhikr teaches that no worldly or spiritual benefit occurs except by Allah's gift alone?
optionsEn: Luck turns randomly each season
Fortune favors only the sleepless
Allahumma ma asbaha bi min ni‘matin... fa-minka wahdaka la sharika lak
I earned every blessing strictly on my own
explanationEn: Recognizing every blessing—breath, eyesight, family, guidance—as purely from Allah cures hidden ingratitude.

questionEn: What does 'Wa ma lahmuna bi-yadika...' / 'Ya Hayyu ya Qayyum' teach a believer when starting an exhausting morning after poor sleep?
optionsEn: To rely solely on caffeine without prayer
To complain angrily to family members
To ask the Ever-Living Sustainer by His mercy to rectify ALL of our affairs without leaving us to our own fragile strength for a blink
To skip Fajr and sleep until Dhuhr
explanationEn: Admitting our own helplessness ('do not entrust me to myself for a blink of an eye') invites Allah's gentle competence into our fatigue.

questionEn: In morning and evening adhkar, how many times did the Prophet ﷺ say 'Allahumma salli wa sallim ‘ala nabiyyina Muhammad' is recommended in authentic-chain encouragement (morning & evening Salawat)?
optionsEn: Never outside Makkah
Only during rainy Fridays
Ten times in the morning and ten times in the evening to attain his intercession (shafa‘ah) on the Day of Resurrection
Once a year on Rajab only
explanationEn: Sending abundant Salawat morning and evening keeps the Prophet's ﷺ love fresh and connects us to his promised intercession.

questionEn: What short morning/evening dhikr combines four majestic phrases that the Prophet ﷺ called the most beloved speech to Allah after the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka only after sleep
Bismillah at meals only
SubhanAllah, wal-Hamdulillah, wa la ilaha illAllah, wallahu Akbar
Amin after sneezing
explanationEn: Saying these four phrases—and knowing it matters not which one you begin with—fills the heart with light and gratitude.

questionEn: Which two phrases did the Prophet ﷺ describe in the final hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari as 'light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful'?
optionsEn: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil-‘Azim
Allahu Akbar kabira
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Rabbana taqabbal minna
explanationEn: Imam al-Bukhari ended his entire Sahih collection with these two effortless yet weighty words of praise.

questionEn: In the morning dua taught in Sunan Abi Dawud 5085, what four protections from harm in one's heart and towards others are affirmed?
optionsEn: Avoiding trade with neighbors
Seeking refuge from committing evil against oneself (an aqtarifa ‘ala nafsi su'an) or dragging evil upon any Muslim (aw ajurrahu ila muslim)
Staying indoors every Tuesday
Refusing to greet strangers in streets
explanationEn: This sensitivity trains the believer to guard both personal integrity and social harmlessness before stepping out each day.

questionEn: What does reciting 'HasbiyAllahu la ilaha illa Huwa, ‘alayhi tawakkaltu wa Huwa Rabbul-‘arshil-‘azim' seven times morning and evening promise according to Sunan Abi Dawud 5081?
optionsEn: He will never encounter rain while walking
He can omit all optional prayers
Allah suffices the reciter against whatever worries him in this world and the Hereafter
He will receive silver ingots under his pillow
explanationEn: Whether worried about health, visas, family, or provision, trusting the Lord of the Mighty Throne dissolves anxiety.

questionEn: Why does the morning/evening dhikr 'Allahumma inni as'alukal-‘afwa wal-‘afiyata...' ask for BOTH ‘Afw (pardon) and ‘Afiyah (well-being)?
optionsEn: ‘Afiyah applies strictly after death
‘Afw erases past sins completely, while ‘Afiyah protects faith, body, family, and wealth from future trials and harm
‘Afw is only for wealth and ‘Afiyah only for food
They are identical synonyms with no nuance
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said no supplication after faith is better than asking Allah for ‘Afiyah.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ woke up in the morning, what short dua of resurrection gratitude did he recite?
optionsEn: Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana ba‘da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Calling sleep a minor death ('amatana') and waking a mini-resurrection ('ahyana') trains the believer to start every morning grateful for a fresh day.

questionEn: According to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3401, what three gifts does a waking believer thank Allah for in the morning dua 'Alhamdulillahilladhi ‘afani fi jasadi...'?
optionsEn: Forgetfulness of yesterday's tasks
Double wages, cold rain, and stone walls
Granting soundness in my body, returning my soul to me, and permitting me to remember Him ('wa adhina li bi-dhikrih')
Silent nights, empty roads, and full vaults
explanationEn: Viewing the ability to even remember Allah ('adhina li bi-dhikrih') as a divine permission turns dhikr into an honor.

questionEn: What gentle Sunnah action did the Prophet ﷺ perform with the three Quls (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas) every night before going to sleep?
optionsEn: Cupped his palms, blew lightly into them, recited the three surahs, and wiped his face, head, and as much of his body as he could reach—three times
Recited only Surah Al-Fil once without moving
Stood outside facing west for twenty minutes
Wrote the verses onto paper under his pillow
explanationEn: Narrated by ‘A'ishah (RA), the Prophet ﷺ maintained this loving nightly shield even during his final illness, when she wiped with his blessed hands.

questionEn: In the famous Sahih al-Bukhari 2311 narration involving Abu Hurayrah (RA), what did the captured nocturnal intruder reveal about reciting Ayat al-Kursi before sleep?
optionsEn: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi when going to bed will have a guardian from Allah watching over him, and no devil can come near him until morning
It guarantees dreams of buried silver
It excuses a sleeper from waking for Fajr
It shortens winter nights by two hours
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ confirmed this truth to Abu Hurayrah (RA), noting: 'He spoke the truth to you, even though he is an inveterate liar.'

questionEn: What blessing did the Prophet ﷺ announce for reciting the final two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:285–286) before sleeping at night?
optionsEn: They bring rain before dawn
Kafatah — 'They will suffice him' (against nocturnal evil, Satan, or even as minimum night worship)
They replace morning Fajr prayer
They double trade profits at sunrise
explanationEn: Quick to recite in less than a minute, the final two verses of Al-Baqarah guard the sleeper spiritually and physically.

questionEn: What practical physical Sunnah did the Prophet ﷺ advise doing three times with the inner edge of one's garment before lying down on a bed?
optionsEn: Sprinkling salt around the headboard
Placing shoes directly beside the pillow
Brushing/dusting the bed while mentioning Allah's Name, because one does not know what may have crawled onto it after leaving it
Folding all blankets into triangles
explanationEn: Combining hygiene/safety with dhikr ('Bismika Rabbi wada‘tu janbi...') reflects Islam's practical care for body and soul.

questionEn: When lying down on one's right side and placing the right hand beneath the right cheek before sleep, what short dua did the Prophet ﷺ say (often three times)?
optionsEn: Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi ‘adada khalqih
Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Allahumma qini ‘adhabaka yawma tab‘athu ‘ibadak ('O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants')
explanationEn: Sleep resembles death, so remembering the Day of Resurrection softly at bedtime keeps the heart tender and sincere.

questionEn: In the bedtime dua 'Bismika Rabbi wada‘tu janbi wa bika arfa‘uh...', what two possibilities does the sleeper acknowledge regarding his soul during the night?
optionsEn: If it rains tonight, flood the crops; if dry, withhold water
If dreams appear, reveal hidden treasures
If trade rises, double silver; if low, stay asleep
If You take my soul (in amsakta nafsi), have mercy on it; and if You release it back (wa in arsaltaha), guard it as You guard Your righteous servants
explanationEn: Surrendering our soul knowingly to Allah each night removes dread of sleep or sudden death.

questionEn: What bedtime tasbih formula—totalling 100—did the Prophet ﷺ gift to Fatimah and ‘Ali (RA) as 'better for you than a servant'?
optionsEn: Labbayk 33 times and Bismillah 33 times
La ilaha illAllah 12 times only
Astaghfirullah 10 times and Amin 90 times
SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times, and Allahu Akbar 34 times
explanationEn: ‘Ali (RA) reported that after hearing this from the Prophet ﷺ, he never missed Tasbih Fatimah even on the night of Siffin!

questionEn: What short five-word bedtime dua did the Prophet ﷺ say right before closing his eyes to sleep?
optionsEn: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya ('In Your Name, O Allah, I die and I live')
explanationEn: Paired symmetrically with 'Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana...' upon waking, this brackets every night's sleep in Allah's Name.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 247 & 6311, when the Prophet ﷺ taught Al-Bara' ibn ‘Azib (RA) the final bedtime dua ('Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk...'), why did he gently correct Al-Bara' for saying 'rasulika'?
optionsEn: He told him: 'No, say wa nabiyyika alladhi arsalta' ('and Your Prophet whom You sent') so the exact revealed wording is preserved
Because it could only be recited in Makkah
Because 'rasulika' was too short to remember
Because only travelers say 'rasulika'
explanationEn: Teaching exact wording ('wa nabiyyika alladhi arsalta') shows how carefully Prophetic adhkar were preserved—and whoever dies that night dies upon the natural fitrah.

questionEn: What prerequisite of outward purification is recommended right before reciting 'Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk...' at bedtime?
optionsEn: Performing Wudu just as you do for Salah, then lying down on your right side
Walking around the house seven times
Drinking salted milk
Washing only one's sandals
explanationEn: Sleeping in a state of Wudu turns even hours of rest into peaceful worship guarded by an angel praying for your forgiveness.

questionEn: What deeply grateful bedtime dua in Sahih Muslim 2715 reminds the sleeper of countless people lacking shelter or support?
optionsEn: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah only
Allahumma barik lana fil-matar
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Alhamdulillahilladhi at‘amana wa saqana wa kafana wa awana, fa-kam mimman la kafiya lahu wa la mu'wi
explanationEn: Pausing before sleep to thank Allah for food, drink, sufficiency, and a safe roof cultivates compassion for refugees and the unhoused.

questionEn: In the comprehensive bedtime dua from Sahih Muslim 2713 ('Allahumma Rabbas-samawatis-sab‘...'), what specific burden does the sleeper ask Allah to settle and remove?
optionsEn: Iqdi ‘annad-dayna wa aghnina minal-faqr ('Settle our debt for us and enrich/free us from poverty')
Silence early morning roosters
Remove winter clouds from Syria
Excuse us from Fajr prayer
explanationEn: Asking Al-Awwal wal-Akhir, Az-Zahir wal-Batin to relieve debt and poverty right before sleeping brings restful trust.

questionEn: Which two surahs did the Prophet ﷺ make a habit of reciting every single night before falling asleep according to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2892?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah (5) and Surah At-Tawbah (9)
Surah Al-Jumu‘ah (62) and Surah Al-Munafiqun (63)
Surah As-Sajdah (32) and Surah Al-Mulk (67)
Surah Yusuf (12) and Surah Nuh (71)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mulk is famously called 'Al-Mani‘ah' (the Protector), interceding for its reciter against the punishment of the grave.

questionEn: What extraordinary promise is given in Sahih al-Bukhari 1154 for someone who wakes up spontaneously at night and recites 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah...' followed by 'Allahu Akbar, SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' and 'Allahummaghfir li'?
optionsEn: He loses the reward of earlier sleep
Only scholars receive answered dua at night
He must stay awake for seven days
If he then makes dua, it will be answered; and if he performs Wudu and prays, his Salah will be accepted
explanationEn: Even a 30-second waking moment in the middle of the night becomes a golden gate to answered dua.

questionEn: When someone suffers sudden terror, panic, or nightmares during sleep, what protective dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sunan Abi Dawud 3893?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
A‘udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min ghadabihi wa ‘iqabihi wa sharri ‘ibadihi wa min hamazatish-shayatin wa an yahdurun
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
explanationEn: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (RA) taught this exact dua to his older children and wrote it for younger ones before they memorized it—emphasizing its power against nocturnal fear.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 2261 and Sahih al-Bukhari 6995, what four Sunnah steps should a Muslim take if woken by a disturbing bad dream?
optionsEn: Write it down to interpret via astrology
Stay in the exact same position and cry loudly
Seek refuge in Allah from Satan and the dream's evil 3x, spit lightly/dryly to the left 3x, turn over onto the other side, and tell no one about it (and pray if desired)
Announce the dream immediately to every neighbor
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ promised that following these gentle steps ensures the disturbing dream cannot harm the sleeper.

questionEn: What should a believer do upon seeing a joyful, comforting good dream (ru'ya salihah) according to Sahih al-Bukhari 6985?
optionsEn: Keep gratitude silent and deny seeing it
Assume it replaces obligatory fasting
Praise Allah (Alhamdulillah), recognize it is from Allah, and share it only with those whom he loves
Share it primarily with envious critics
explanationEn: Thanking Allah and sharing good dreams only with trustworthy loved ones guards against envy and keeps gratitude alive.

questionEn: In the bedtime dua 'Allahumma khalaqta nafsi wa Anta tawaffaha...', what two states of one's soul are placed in Allah's Hand?
optionsEn: Its death and its life ('laka mamatuha wa mahyaha')—asking Him to protect it if kept alive and forgive it if taken in death
Its dreams of markets
Its travel tickets and luggage
Its wealth and its clothing
explanationEn: Narrated in Sahih Muslim 2712, this brief bedtime supplication nurtures peaceful surrender before sleep.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ noticed a companion struggling with sleeplessness (insomnia), what serene dua did he teach him (as reported in al-Adhkar / Ibn as-Sunni)?
optionsEn: Read historical chronicles loudly until dawn
Allahumma gharatin-nujum wa hada'atil-‘uyun, wa Anta Hayyun Qayyumun la ta'khudhuka sinatun wa la nawm; ya Hayyu ya Qayyumu ahdi' layli wa anim ‘ayni
Walk around the city marketplace
Count sheep backwards from one thousand
explanationEn: Calling upon the Ever-Living who neither slumbers nor sleeps ('la ta'khudhuka sinatun wa la nawm') to quiet the night and grant rest reflects tender Prophetic care.
reference: Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah (Ibn as-Sunni) / Hisn al-Muslim

questionEn: Why is sleeping on one's stomach (al-idti‘a‘ ‘ala al-batn) discouraged in the Sunnah while sleeping on the right side is encouraged?
optionsEn: Because it is forbidden during Ramadan only
Because it invalidates Wudu automatically
The Prophet ﷺ gently awakened a man lying on his stomach and noted it is a posture Allah dislikes, whereas lying on the right side with dhikr follows Prophetic beauty
Because only kings slept on their right side
explanationEn: Pairing the right-side posture with bedtime adhkar aligns physical rest with Sunnah mindfulness.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5040 / Sunan Ibn Majah 3723

questionEn: When Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stood up to pray Tahajjud in the stillness of the night, what majestic opening praise did Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) hear him recite (Sahih al-Bukhari 1120)?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina qurrata a‘yun
Allahumma lakal-hamd, Anta qayyimus-samawati wal-ardi wa man fihinn... Antal-Haqq, wa wa‘dukal-haqq, wa liqa'ukal-haqq...
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Affirming six truths in sequence—Allah is True, His promise is true, meeting Him is true, His Word is true, Paradise and Fire are true, the Prophets and Muhammad ﷺ are true—and then surrendering completely.

questionEn: In that same Sahih al-Bukhari 1120 Tahajjud dua, what four sins does the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah to forgive across time and intention?
optionsEn: Only slips made during childhood
Only forgotten promises to neighbors
Only errors committed on journeys
What I sent forward and left behind, what I concealed and what I revealed ('ma qaddamtu wa ma akhkhartu, wa ma asrartu wa ma a‘lantu')
explanationEn: Covering past, future, private, and public shortcomings leaves nothing unaddressed before Al-Muqaddim Al-Mu'akhkhir.

questionEn: What light-filled dua did the Prophet ﷺ recite while walking to Fajr prayer or after Tahajjud according to Sahih Muslim 763 and Bukhari 6316?
optionsEn: Allahummaj‘al fi qalbi nura, wa fi lisani nura, waj‘al fi sam‘i nura, waj‘al fi basari nura...
Ghufranaka
Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
SubhanAllahil-‘Azim only
explanationEn: Asking for Allah's Light in heart, tongue, hearing, sight, behind, ahead, above, and below makes the believer a walking beacon of light.

questionEn: What opening dua did the Prophet ﷺ frequently recite at the start of his night prayer (Tahajjud) invoking Allah as Lord of Jibril, Mika'il, and Israfil?
optionsEn: Bismillahi tawakkaltu ‘alallah
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Allahumma innaka ‘afuwwun tuhibbul-‘afwa
Allahumma Rabba Jibra'ila wa Mika'ila wa Israfil, fatiras-samawati wal-ard, ‘alimal-ghaybi wash-shahadah... ihdini limakhtulifa fihi minal-haqqi bi-idhnika
explanationEn: Naming the three archangels tied to revelation, sustenance, and the Resurrection asks Allah to guide our hearts to truth wherever people differ.

questionEn: What noble supplication of Qunut al-Witr did the Prophet ﷺ teach his beloved grandson al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali (RA) to recite in Witr prayer?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahummahdini fiman hadayt, wa ‘afini fiman ‘afayt, wa tawallani fiman tawallayt, wa barik li fima a‘tayt, wa qini sharra ma qadayt...
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Rabbana taqabbal minna
explanationEn: Asking for guidance, well-being, Allah's guardianship, blessing in what He gave, and protection from decreed evil ends with glorifying His justice.

questionEn: What humble closing line in Qunut al-Witr affirms Allah's supreme authority over judgment?
optionsEn: Wealth guards those who hoard it
Only nights of winter are blessed
None can pray except scholars
Fa-innaka taqdi wa la yuqda ‘alayk; innahu la yadhillu man walayt [wa la ya‘izzu man ‘adayt]; tabarakta Rabbana wa ta‘alayt
explanationEn: Affirming that whoever Allah befriends is never truly humiliated fills Witr prayer with unshakeable dignity.

questionEn: Immediately after concluding Witr prayer with Salam, what three-word praise did the Prophet ﷺ say three times, stretching and raising his voice on the third?
optionsEn: Alhamdulillah rabbil-‘alamin
Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim
Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil
Subhanal-Malikil-Quddus ('Glory be to the Sovereign, the Pure/Holy')
explanationEn: Closing Witr—the seal of night prayer—with 'Subhanal-Malikil-Quddus' (sometimes adding 'Rabbil-mala'ikati war-ruh') crowns the night in awe.

questionEn: What brief protective dua did the Prophet ﷺ make in the final prostration or end of Witr prayer according to Sunan Abi Dawud 1427 and Muslim 486?
optionsEn: SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bi-ridaka min sakhatik, wa bi-mu‘afatika min ‘uqubatik, wa a‘udhu bika mink; la uhsi thana'an ‘alayk, Anta kama athnayta ‘ala nafsik
explanationEn: Seeking refuge in Allah's pleasure from His displeasure, and in Allah Himself from Himself, ends by confessing human inability to praise Him adequately.

questionEn: How strongly did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize Salat al-Istikharah (prayer for seeking Allah's guidance) to his companions according to Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA)?
optionsEn: He reserved it solely for kings signing treaties
He used to teach us Istikharah in ALL matters just as carefully as he taught us a surah from the Qur'an
He forbade using it for marriage or travel decisions
He taught it only once during Hajj
explanationEn: Whether choosing a career, spouse, journey, or investment, Istikharah turns uncertainty into confident reliance on Al-‘Alim Al-Qadir.

questionEn: In Salat al-Istikharah, how many voluntary rak‘ahs are prayed before reciting the Istikharah dua?
optionsEn: Twelve rak‘ahs at midnight only
One single rak‘ah without Wudu
Four obligatory rak‘ahs only after Dhuhr
Two voluntary rak‘ahs (not an obligatory prayer), followed by the Istikharah supplication
explanationEn: Praying two quiet rak‘ahs first places the seeker directly before Allah before asking Him to choose what is best.

questionEn: In the Istikharah dua, through which four attributes of Allah does the supplicant seek guidance and ability?
optionsEn: Friends' applause, dreams, and lucky numbers
Allah's stars, winds, oceans, and mountains
Allah's Knowledge (‘ilmika), Allah's Power (qudratika), Allah's Great Bounty (fadlikal-‘azim), and His total Sovereignty ('taqdiru wa la aqdir, wa ta‘lamu wa la a‘lam, wa Anta ‘Allamul-ghuyub')
Our own cleverness, speed, wealth, and connections
explanationEn: Confessing 'You have power and I do not; You know and I do not' strips away ego so we happily accept whatever door Allah opens or closes.

questionEn: What two outcomes does the Istikharah dua ask Allah for depending on whether the matter is good or harmful for our religion, livelihood, and final outcome?
optionsEn: Delay the answer for seven months
If good, decree it for me, make it easy, and bless it for me; if bad, turn it away from me, turn my heart away from it, decree good wherever it may be, and make me content with it
Send a glowing dream within two hours or cancel it
Force the choice through even if it harms my faith
explanationEn: Notice the beauty of 'wa raddini bih' ('and make me pleased/content with it')—asking Allah not just to change external events, but to bring peace to our heart.

questionEn: What common misconception about Salat al-Istikharah do scholars clarify based on Sahih al-Bukhari 1162?
optionsEn: It replaces consulting knowledgeable people completely
You do NOT need to see a special dream; rather, combine Istikharah with wise counsel (Shura), take practical steps, and observe how Allah facilitates or blocks the path
You may only perform Istikharah once in your lifetime
You must see green or white colors in a dream or repeat seven nights
explanationEn: When Allah answers Istikharah, He often makes the good path smooth and closes unhealthy doors naturally without requiring a dream.

questionEn: What special prayer of need (Salat al-Hajah) and praise did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 479 (though its chain has scholarly discussion, its dhikr words are pure Tawhid)?
optionsEn: Asking angels instead of Allah
Skipping Salah and waiting for midnight comets
Fasting for forty days without speaking
Performing Wudu well, praying two rak‘ahs, praising Allah, sending Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ, and saying 'La ilaha illallahul-Halimul-Karim, subhanAllahi Rabbil-‘arshil-‘azim...'
explanationEn: Starting any urgent plea with Wudu, two rak‘ahs, praising Al-Halim Al-Karim, and Salawat models Prophetic etiquette in hardship.

questionEn: When Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stayed awake in Tahajjud, how did he balance length of recitation and rest?
optionsEn: He forced himself awake for seven straight nights without ever sleeping
He raced through surahs as fast as possible
He prayed calmly with deep reflection, pausing to ask mercy at verses of mercy and refuge at verses of warning, without harming his family's rights or health
He prayed Tahajjud only during travel
explanationEn: When told of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr fasting daily and praying all night, the Prophet ﷺ taught moderation: 'Your body has a right over you, your eyes have a right, and your spouse has a right.'

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 757, what special nightly hour did the Prophet ﷺ promise exists every single night without exception?
optionsEn: An hour during the night in which no Muslim asks Allah for good of this world and the Hereafter except that He gives it to him—and that occurs every night
Only one night in Ramadan every five years
Only when rain falls at midnight
Only Friday mornings after sunrise
explanationEn: Unlike the Friday hour which occurs weekly, this hidden hour of accepted dua is gifted every single night!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA) 'What an excellent man ‘Abdullah would be if only he prayed at night'?
optionsEn: Because he wanted him to stop sleeping altogether
Because praying at night is obligatory upon every adult
To gently inspire him toward the sweetness of Qiyam al-Layl (night prayer) and private dua
Because daytime prayers do not count without Tahajjud
explanationEn: From that day onward, Ibn ‘Umar (RA) reportedly slept only a small portion of the night!

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise doing when drowsiness overcomes a worshipper during late-night prayer (Qiyam)?
optionsEn: Shout louder to stay awake
Continue reciting half-asleep regardless of mistakes
Go back to sleep until sleep leaves you, lest you intend to seek forgiveness and accidentally pray against yourself
Splash ice water continuously until sunrise
explanationEn: Islam honors presence of heart over drowsy exhaustion.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1142, how does Satan try to keep a believer asleep through Tahajjud and Fajr, and what three acts untie all three knots?
optionsEn: Drinking cold juice unties all three knots
Satan ties three knots at the back of the head saying 'You have a long night, sleep on'; waking to remember Allah unties the first, performing Wudu unties the second, and praying unties the third
Setting three brass bells beside the bed
Reading poetry before breakfast
explanationEn: Waking with dhikr ('Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana...'), making Wudu, and praying leaves the believer energetic and cheerful of soul.

questionEn: In Sunan Abi Dawud 1308, what affectionate blessing did the Prophet ﷺ invoke upon a husband or wife who wakes their spouse gently at night to pray two rak‘ahs together?
optionsEn: May they pray in separate houses
May they fast every Monday forever
May Allah have mercy on a man/woman who rises at night, prays, and awakens his/her spouse—and if they refuse, lightly sprinkles water on their face
May they never speak during breakfast
explanationEn: Encouraging one another gently toward night worship and shared dua fills marriage with spiritual warmth.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1308 / Sunan Ibn Majah 1336

questionEn: What reward is promised in Sunan Abi Dawud 1309 when a husband and wife wake together at night and pray two rak‘ahs?
optionsEn: They need not pray Sunnah during the day
They earn double travel rewards
They are both recorded among the men and women who remember Allah abundantly (adh-dhakirina Allaha kathira wadh-dhakirat)
They receive exemption from Zakah
explanationEn: Even two brief rak‘ahs prayed together in the stillness of night elevate a couple to the rank praised in Surah Al-Ahzab 33:35.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1145, what nightly descent of divine mercy invites believers to wake in the last third of the night?
optionsEn: Angels close the gates of forgiveness until dawn
Requests are delayed until Friday

Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of every night saying: 'Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive him?'
Only pilgrims in Makkah may pray at that hour
explanationEn: No earthly appointment compares to being personally invited by Al-Karim in the pre-dawn hush.

questionEn: When is the 'last third of the night' calculated between Maghrib and Fajr?
optionsEn: Only between midnight and 1:00 AM year-round
Divide the total hours between sunset (Maghrib) and true dawn (Fajr) by three; the final segment right before Fajr is the last third
Always the hour immediately after ‘Isha
Always fixed from 10:00 PM to 11:00 PM
explanationEn: Because night length shifts across seasons, calculating from Maghrib to Fajr helps believers find Sahar accurately everywhere on earth.

questionEn: Which brief practice makes every night count toward Qiyam al-Layl even for busy workers or students according to Sahih Muslim 656?
optionsEn: Staying awake watching news until 2 AM
Praying ‘Isha in congregation equals half the night in prayer, and praying Fajr in congregation equals praying the entire rest of the night
Reading one word before bed
Sleeping with shoes on
explanationEn: Guarding ‘Isha and Fajr with congregation—plus even a brief Witr before sleeping—gives immense nightly standing reward.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 755, what counsel did the Prophet ﷺ give to someone who fears not waking up at the end of the night versus one hopeful of waking up?
optionsEn: Pray Witr twice in one night
Never pray Witr before midnight under any condition

Whoever fears not waking at the end of the night should pray Witr before sleeping; whoever is confident of waking at the end of the night should pray Witr then, for late-night prayer is witnessed (mashhudah) and better
Skip Witr entirely on workdays
explanationEn: Remember the Sunnah principle: 'Make the last of your night prayers Witr' (odd-numbered), without repeating Witr twice in one night.

questionEn: What gentle daily Morning Charity (Sadaqah) upon every single joint (360 joints) of the body is effortlessly fulfilled by two rak‘ahs of Salat ad-Duha?
optionsEn: Praying two rak‘ahs of Duha suffices as charity for all 360 joints—alongside every Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, Takbir, and kind act
Giving 360 gold coins every dawn
Walking 360 miles before noon
Fasting 360 days continuously
explanationEn: Starting the morning with morning adhkar and two rak‘ahs of Duha after sunrise fills the joints with gratitude and barakah.

questionEn: What comprehensive morning dua did Umm Salamah (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ often recited right after the Fajr prayer?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma inni as'aluka ‘ilman nafi‘an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa ‘amalan mutaqabbalan
Allahumma barik lana fil-mayt
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
explanationEn: Asking for beneficial knowledge, pure halal income, and accepted deeds sets clear priorities right at dawn.

questionEn: What morning and evening remembrance asks Allah for steadfastness in faith and gratitude for His blessings—taught by Shaddad ibn Aws (RA) in Sunan an-Nasa'i 1304?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
Ghufranaka
Allahumma inni as'alukath-thabata fil-amri wal-‘azimata ‘alar-rushd, wa as'aluka shukra ni‘matika wa husna ‘ibadatik...
explanationEn: This rich Sunnah dua also asks for a sound heart (qalban salima), a truthful tongue (lisanan sadiqa), and forgiveness for sins Allah knows.

questionEn: In that same noble dua of Shaddad ibn Aws (RA) (Tirmidhi 3407), what extraordinary inner gift is paired with 'a truthful tongue'?
optionsEn: Forgetfulness of past mistakes
A loud voice in debates
Skill in counting silver
Qalban salima — a pure, sound heart free from malice, hypocrisy, and corruption
explanationEn: Asking for 'thabat fil-amr' (firmness in faith) and '‘azimah ‘alar-rushd' (determination upon right guidance) alongside a sound heart covers both resolve and purity.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach ‘Ali (RA) in Sahih Muslim 2725 to ask Allah for two core guides in life?
optionsEn: Allahummahdini wa saddidni ('O Allah, guide me and keep me upright/on target'), picturing guidance like knowing the road and uprightness like aiming an arrow straight
Rabbi hab li mulkan
Allahumma aghnini ‘anis-salah
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
explanationEn: Knowing the right path (hidayah) and hitting the right mark in execution (sadad) summarizes every need in daily decision-making.

questionEn: When Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA) was held affectionately by the hand by the Prophet ﷺ, what four-word commitment did he urge Mu‘adh never to omit at the end of EVERY Salah?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
Allahumma a‘inni ‘ala dhikrika, wa shukrika, wa husni ‘ibadatik ('O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You in the best manner')
explanationEn: Even thanking and worshipping Allah requires Allah's own help—which is why the Prophet ﷺ prefaced it with 'By Allah, O Mu‘adh, I truly love you!'

questionEn: What does the morning/evening phrase 'Bismillahi tawakkaltu ‘alallah...'—or more generally 'Ya Hayyu ya Qayyum'—remind a tired believer when duties pile up?
optionsEn: That stress can only be healed by complaining
That strength to fulfill every duty comes from Allah's mercy and life-giving support, not human willpower alone
That tired people are excused from remembering Allah
That work should replace Salah
explanationEn: Leaning on Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum turns overwhelming to-do lists into calm, purposeful reliance.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2721, what four spiritual treasures did the Prophet ﷺ regularly ask Allah for?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni as'alukal-huda, wat-tuqa, wal-‘afafa, wal-ghina (Guidance, Piety/Taqwa, Chastity/Self-restraint, and Contentment/Self-sufficiency)
Leisure, speed, luxury, and silence
Fame, silver, power, and applause
Palaces, gardens, gold, and steeds
explanationEn: True 'ghina' is richness and contentment of the soul—freeing a person from greed or humiliating dependence on people.

questionEn: When reciting the morning and evening dhikr 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi' or 'Astaghfirullah', why did scholars of Hisn al-Muslim emphasize saying them with present reflection rather than rushing?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ reminded that Allah does not answer a dua from a heedless, distracted heart (qalbin ghafilin lahin)
Because fast pronunciation invalidates Wudu
Because angels record only slow handwriting
Because rushing doubles the required count to 500
explanationEn: Even ten mindful phrases felt deeply in the heart carry far greater spiritual illumination than hundreds muttered mechanically.

questionEn: What soothing morning/evening practice helps when feeling weary, as taught through 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi' and Ayat al-Kursi?
optionsEn: Consistent brief remembrances anchor the heart daily, for the most beloved deeds to Allah are those done regularly even if small (adwamuha wa in qall)
Waiting until retirement to learn adhkar
Doing 5,000 repetitions once a year and none afterward
Stopping adhkar completely during busy workweeks
explanationEn: Building a steady daily rhythm of morning, evening, and bedtime adhkar—even 5 minutes—transforms a believer's resilience.

questionEn: What short phrase did the Prophet ﷺ teach Umm Hani' (RA) when she grew elderly and unable to do strenuous exertion?
optionsEn: Sit silently without speaking to family

Say 'SubhanAllah' 100 times (equals freeing 100 slaves), 'Alhamdulillah' 100 times (equals 100 saddled horses in Allah's path), 'Allahu Akbar' 100 times (equals 100 accepted sacrificial camels), and 'La ilaha illAllah' 100 times (fills heaven and earth)
Fast every alternate week without water
Walk barefoot across deserts at noon
explanationEn: Dhikr empowers elders, sick believers, and busy parents to earn mountains of reward right from their seat or bed.

questionEn: What morning/evening dua praises Allah while testifying to His Oneness alongside His angels and messengers?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma inni asbahtu/amsaytu ushhiduka wa ushhidu hamalata ‘arshika...
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
explanationEn: Affirming that 'Muhammad ﷺ is Your servant and Messenger' protects both reverence for him and pure monotheism.

questionEn: When starting the morning adhkar with 'A‘udhu billahis-Sami‘il-‘Alimi minash-shaytanir-rajim' followed by the last three verses of Surah Al-Hashr (59:22–24), what blessing is narrated in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2922?
optionsEn: It prevents rain from falling on crops
It cancels the need for Wudu
It replaces the obligatory Dhuhr prayer

Allah appoints 70,000 angels to pray for mercy upon the reciter until evening (though scholars note chain grading is weak, reciting Al-Hashr 59:22–24 for its Beautiful Names remains deeply beneficial)
explanationEn: Reflecting on Allah's Names in Al-Hashr 59:22–24—Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam—is spiritually enriching in its own right.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2714, why did the Prophet ﷺ teach reciting 'Bismika Rabbi wada‘tu janbi...' even for a quick daytime nap or nightly sleep?
optionsEn: Because only night sleep counts as rest
Because naps are forbidden without a written log
Because every sleep places our soul temporarily in Allah's custody until He returns it upon waking
Because it shortens afternoon heat
explanationEn: Remembering Allah when lying down and waking up makes even rest an act of conscious servitude.

questionEn: What short dua did ‘A'ishah (RA) ask the Prophet ﷺ what to say if she knew which night was Laylat al-Qadr—widely also loved during all last-ten-night prayers?
optionsEn: Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Allahumma innaka ‘afuwwun tuhibbul-‘afwa fa‘fu ‘anni ('O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me')
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma hab li mulkan ‘azima
explanationEn: Asking for ‘Afw—complete erasure of sins without even a trace left in the record—is the crowning prayer of Ramadan nights.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2720, what four evils did the Prophet ﷺ frequently seek refuge from in a concise Prophetic dua—suitable both morning, evening, and after Tashahhud?
optionsEn: Cold rain, long roads, simple meals, and quiet mornings
Growing plants, reading books, and drinking water
Teaching children, greeting neighbors, and working honestly
Knowledge that does not benefit, a heart that is not humble (la yakhsha‘), a soul that is never satisfied (la yashba‘), and a supplication that is not answered (la yustajabu laha)
explanationEn: Realizing that even knowledge can lack benefit or a heart lack humility keeps our spiritual goals crystal clear.

questionEn: What comprehensive eight-part refuge dua in Sahih al-Bukhari 6369 guards a believer's emotional resilience, courage, generosity, and daily focus?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab wa Sha‘ban
Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan, wal-‘ajzi wal-kasal, wal-jubni wal-bukhl, wa dala‘id-dayni wa ghalabatir-rijal
Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi ‘adada khalqih
explanationEn: Pairing worry & grief (past/future), incapacity & laziness, cowardice & stinginess, and crushing debt & oppression covers eight major human struggles.

questionEn: In that eight-item refuge dua (Bukhari 6369), what is the difference between 'al-hamm' and 'al-hazan'?
optionsEn: Al-hamm is anxious worry about what may happen in the future; al-hazan is sorrow over what already happened in the past
Al-hamm means joy and al-hazan means hunger
Al-hamm means travel and al-hazan means sleep
Both refer strictly to physical toothaches
explanationEn: Seeking refuge from both frees the believer from getting trapped in future anxiety or past regret so they can live faithfully right now.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6369 / Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim

questionEn: In that same Bukhari 6369 dua, what is the difference between 'al-‘ajz' and 'al-kasal'?
optionsEn: Al-‘ajz means sleeping early and al-kasal means fasting
Al-‘ajz applies only to animals
Al-‘ajz is lacking capability or willpower when needed; al-kasal is feeling sluggish and lazy despite having the capability
Both refer to speaking softly
explanationEn: Asking Allah's refuge from both inability and laziness empowers purposeful energy for worship, family, and work.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach asking Allah for protection against sudden reversal of blessings?
optionsEn: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min zawali ni‘matik, wa tahawwuli ‘afiyatik, wa fuja'ati niqmatik, wa jami‘i sakhatik
explanationEn: Seeking protection against blessings vanishing, health shifting into illness, sudden calamity, and Allah's displeasure nurtures constant humility.

questionEn: What protection dua guards a believer against four painful endings in old age and beyond?
optionsEn: Praying never to work with one's hands
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-bukhli, wal-jubni, wa su'il-‘umur (or an uradda ila ardhalil-‘umur), wa fitnatid-dunya, wa ‘adhabil-qabr
Seeking refuge from visiting mosques in winter
Asking only for youthful eyesight while ignoring faith
explanationEn: Asking Allah to preserve dignity of mind and body rather than falling into decrepit helplessness (‘ardhal al-‘umur') honors both life and aging.

questionEn: What short phrase did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah protection from regarding personal character and deeds?
optionsEn: Protection from honest neighbors
Protection from memorizing short surahs
Protection from walking to Fajr
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-‘ajzi wal-kasali, wal-jubni wal-harami, wa a‘udhu bika min ‘adhabil-qabri, wa a‘udhu bika min fitnatil-mahya wal-mamat
explanationEn: Asking refuge from trials of living ('fitnatil-mahya') and trials at the moment of death ('fitnatil-mamat') safeguards faith through life's final breath.

questionEn: What comprehensive morning/evening spiritual fitness dua is recorded in Sahih Muslim 2722 asking Allah to grant our soul its Taqwa and purify it?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
Allahumma ati nafsi taqwaha, wa zakkiha Anta khayru man zakkaha, Anta waliyyuha wa mawlaha
explanationEn: Confessing that Allah alone is the Guardian and Master of our soul—and the Best One to purify it—roots self-improvement in divine grace.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2720, right after asking refuge from four things (unbeneficial knowledge, un-humble heart, insatiable soul, unanswered dua), what attitude does this foster?
optionsEn: Avoiding making dua altogether
Self-reflection: ensuring our learning produces humility, our lifestyle stays content, and our heart remains sincere when making dua
Refusing to eat cooked food
Stopping all study of Islamic sciences
explanationEn: Authentic dua always transforms character alongside outward ritual.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ frequently repeat to align his entire life—religion, worldly affairs, and Hereafter?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Ghufranaka
Allahumma aslih li dini alladhi huwa ‘ismatu amri, wa aslih li dunyaya allati fiha ma‘ashi, wa aslih li akhirati allati fiha ma‘adi...
explanationEn: Asking Allah to make life an increase in every good and death a gentle relief from every evil harmonizes faith, career, and eternity.

questionEn: In that same Sahih Muslim 2720 dua ('Allahumma aslih li dini...'), how does the believer ask Allah to frame both long life and death?
optionsEn: Hasten death immediately whenever troubles begin
Grant me endless youth without ever meeting Allah
Waj‘alil-hayata ziyadatan li fi kulli khayr, waj‘alil-mawta rahatan li min kulli sharr
Keep my wealth untouched forever
explanationEn: Because Islam forbids wishing for death out of hardship, this Sunnah phrasing gracefully asks for life full of goodness and death only as mercy.

questionEn: What short night-and-day supplication taught to Umm al-Mu'minin Juwayriyah (RA) reminds believers that Allah's words and pleasure outweigh endless mechanical counting?
optionsEn: Writing lists of worldly desires
SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi ‘adada khalqihi wa rida nafsihi wa zinata ‘arshihi wa midada kalimatih
Reciting only once per lunar year
Counting pebbles silently for hours without meaning
