explanationEn: It combines concise Arabic beauty with boundless cosmic praise.

questionEn: When feeling a pang of fear about losing faith or wavering in commitment, what frequent Prophetic dua did Anas (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ recited more than almost any other?
optionsEn: Ya Muqallibal-qulub, thabbit qalbi ‘ala dinik ('O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion')
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Explaining why he recited it so often, the Prophet ﷺ reminded that all human hearts lie between two fingers of the Most Merciful, who turns them as He wills.

questionEn: What close companion to 'Ya Muqallibal-qulub' appears in Sahih Muslim 2654, turning hearts toward obedience?
optionsEn: Allahumma Musarrifal-qulub, sarrif qulubana ‘ala ta‘atik ('O Allah, Director of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience')
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Reciting both 'Ya Muqallibal-qulub' and 'Musarrifal-qulub' keeps the heart resilient in seasons of doubt or temptation.

questionEn: What evening protection did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sahih al-Bukhari 3371 to place children and grandchildren under Allah's care—just as Prophet Ibrahim (AS) did for Isma‘il and Ishaq?
optionsEn: Hanging iron horseshoes above doorways
Leaving lamps lit without dhikr
U‘idhukuma (or A‘udhu) bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min kulli shaytanin wa hammah, wa min kulli ‘aynin lammah
Tying red ribbons around cradles
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ used these exact Prophetic words to protect his grandsons al-Hasan and al-Husayn (RA) from devils, harmful pests, and the evil eye.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid wearing amulets (tama'im) and teach morning/evening Qur'anic and Sunnah adhkar instead?
optionsEn: Because only travelers wore jewelry
Because relying on Allah's own revealed words and Names fosters direct Tawakkul in Tawhid, whereas hanging superstitious charms weakens faith in Allah alone
Because parchment was expensive in Madinah
Because children dislike necklaces
explanationEn: Reciting Ayat al-Kursi, the Three Quls, and 'U‘idhukum bi-kalimatillahit-tammah' replaces superstition with authentic Prophetic protection.

questionEn: In Sunan Abi Dawud 5074, what gentle plea appears inside the morning/evening ‘afiyah dua regarding personal secrets and fears?
optionsEn: Increase my anxiety before journeys
Keep my doors unlocked at night
Allahummas-tur ‘awrati wa amin raw‘ati ('O Allah, conceal my faults/vulnerabilities and calm my fears')
Expose my faults to neighbors for correction
explanationEn: Asking Al-Sattir to cover our shortcomings and Al-Mu'min to soothe our anxieties speaks directly to modern emotional struggles.

questionEn: In Hisn al-Muslim's morning/evening adhkar, what single phrase recited 100 times (or 10 times when busy) wipes out sins and brings 100 good deeds daily?
optionsEn: SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik only once
Amin after lunch
La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir
MashaAllah when greeting
explanationEn: Keeping this Tahlil daily—or 10 times morning & evening—is one of the highest-yield daily habits in Islam.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3293 / Sahih Muslim 2691 / Abu Dawud 5077

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ say when turning over from side to side during sleep at night (Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra / Ibn as-Sunni)?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
La ilaha illallahul-Wahidul-Qahhar, Rabbus-samawati wal-ardi wa ma baynahumal-‘Azizul-Ghaffar
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
explanationEn: Turning restless tossing in bed into brief remembrance of the One, the Almighty, the Oft-Forgiving invites restful sleep.

questionEn: When waking up in a startle or feeling frightened at night, why does 'A‘udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min ghadabihi wa ‘iqabihi...' mention Allah's anger first?
optionsEn: Because devils only appear in winter
Because only children feel afraid at night
Because true safety starts with being right with Allah, before seeking refuge from evil humans and whispers of devils
Because physical illness never happens at night
explanationEn: Placing reverence for Allah first puts every created fear into proper proportion.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 6314, what happens when a Muslim sleeps on their right side after reciting 'Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk...' and passes away that night?
optionsEn: He dies upon the pure natural faith (al-fitrah)—and if he wakes up alive, he attains great good
Only scholars receive this blessing
He must repeat the dua seven times next day
His deeds from that week are erased
explanationEn: Making this the very last words before falling asleep turns bedtime into peaceful readiness for meeting Allah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach companions if someone sincerely oversleeps past Fajr despite setting intention and taking precautions?
optionsEn: He must fast thirty days immediately
He is banned from praying Dhuhr
There is no negligence in sleep itself; let him wake, make Wudu, and pray Fajr immediately upon remembering, without despairing
He must wait until next day's Fajr
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ comforted companions after an unintended oversleep on a tiring journey: 'There is no sin in sleep; negligence is only while awake.'

questionEn: Which prophetic practice before sleep helps ensure waking cleanly for Tahajjud or Fajr alongside setting alarms?
optionsEn: Drinking heavy coffee right at midnight
Holding loud gatherings past 2 AM
Avoiding heavy late meals or idle late-night chatter after ‘Isha, sleeping with Wudu and adhkar, and making a sincere intention before closing your eyes
Sleeping without Wudu or intention
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ disliked idle conversation after ‘Isha specifically so believers could rest early and rise refreshed for night worship and Fajr.

questionEn: What did ‘A'ishah (RA) report regarding the Prophet's ﷺ Witr prayer timing across his life?
optionsEn: He prayed Witr at every part of the night—early, middle, and late—eventually settling most often right before dawn (sahar)
He prayed Witr only once a week on Fridays
He skipped Witr whenever staying at home
He prayed Witr strictly before Maghrib
explanationEn: This flexibility shows any believer can preserve Witr whether praying before bed or before Fajr.

questionEn: What humble phrase from Sahih Muslim 486 did the Prophet ﷺ recite in Witr and prostration acknowledging that human praise can never exhaust Allah's perfection?
optionsEn: My worship exceeds my capacity
Angels owe me extra reward
La uhsi thana'an ‘alayk, Anta kama athnayta ‘ala nafsik ('I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself')
I have praised You completely with ten words
explanationEn: Recognizing that human praise can never exhaust Allah's perfection keeps even deep night worshippers free of self-righteousness.

questionEn: What morning and evening remembrance from Musnad Ahmad 15360 asks for staying upon 'millati abina Ibrahim hanifan musliman'?
optionsEn: Asbahna/Amsayna ‘ala fitratil-Islam, wa ‘ala kalimatil-ikhlas, wa ‘ala dini nabiyyina Muhammadin ﷺ, wa ‘ala millati abina Ibrahima hanifan muslima...
HasbiyAllahu la ilaha illa Huwa
Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi ‘adada khalqih
explanationEn: Connecting morning and evening faith to both Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Prophet Ibrahim (AS) highlights the unbroken chain of Tawhid.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ encourage regarding making dua during the quiet stillness between the Adhan and Iqamah of Fajr (as well as every Salah)?
optionsEn: Duas then apply only to weather
Only silent gestures are allowed then
Talking about business is preferred then
Supplication between the Adhan and the Iqamah is never rejected (la yuradd)
explanationEn: Using those precious minutes before Fajr Iqamah for personal dua turns waiting into treasure.

questionEn: What morning habit immediately after Fajr prayer did the Prophet ﷺ maintain in the Masjid according to Sahih Muslim 670?
optionsEn: Sleeping on the mosque floor until Dhuhr
Remaining seated in his prayer spot remembering Allah until the sun rose fully
Speaking loudly about caravan prices
Running straight to the marketplace before sunrise
explanationEn: Sitting in dhikr from Fajr until sunrise (followed by two rak‘ahs after the sun rises to spear-height) carries the reward of a complete Hajj and Umrah—'complete, complete, complete'!

questionEn: In Sunan al-Tirmidhi 586, what three-fold emphasis did the Prophet ﷺ repeat about sitting in dhikr after Fajr in congregation until sunrise and praying two rak‘ahs?
optionsEn: It counts only inside Makkah
It applies only during winter months
It replaces the obligatory Hajj of a lifetime
It carries the reward like that of a Hajj and an Umrah—'Tammah, tammah, tammah' ('complete, complete, complete')
explanationEn: While never replacing the obligatory Hajj of Islam, this radiant morning practice fills ordinary mornings at one's local masjid with pilgrimage-like sweetness.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say happens when people gather in a house of Allah reciting and studying His Book together?
optionsEn: Silence is required without questions
Angels leave the room once study begins
Only the teacher receives reward
Tranquility (sakinah) descends upon them, mercy covers them, angels surround them, and Allah mentions them to those in His presence
explanationEn: Attending morning or evening Qur'an circles bathes the heart in angelic companionship and divine mention.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, how did the Prophet ﷺ compare a person who remembers his Lord versus one who does not remember his Lord?
optionsEn: Like the living and the dead (mathalul-hayyi wal-mayyit)
Like tall trees and small pebbles
Like fast horses and quiet ships
Like silver coins and copper pots
explanationEn: Regular morning, evening, and bedtime adhkar keep the soul vibrantly alive rather than spiritually asleep.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 779, how did the Prophet ﷺ contrast a home where Allah is remembered versus a home where Allah is NOT remembered?
optionsEn: Like stone walls and mud huts
Like winter and autumn
Also like the living and the dead—turning a house filled with dhikr, Qur'an, and dua into a living sanctuary
Like large gates and narrow doors
explanationEn: Filling our bedrooms, kitchens, and hallways with morning/evening adhkar keeps the household peaceful and spiritually alive.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ explain happens to a house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited according to Sahih Muslim 780?
optionsEn: Windows rattle from loud winds
Guests stop visiting the house
Only scholars may enter
Satan flees from that house ('inna sh-shaytana yanfiru minal-baytilladhi tuqra'u fihi Suratul-Baqarah')
explanationEn: Playing or reciting Surah Al-Baqarah regularly at home reinforces daily morning and evening adhkar.

questionEn: When teaching Istikharah in Sahih al-Bukhari 1162, at which point in the prayer is the Istikharah dua recited?
optionsEn: Only during Ruku‘ of Dhuhr prayer
Instead of reciting Surah Al-Fatihah
Before making Wudu
After concluding the two voluntary rak‘ahs with Salam (or scholars also permit right before Salam, with after Salam being the literal wording 'thumma yaqul')
explanationEn: Saying the Istikharah dua peacefully after the two rak‘ahs lets you hold the specific decision clearly in mind before Allah.

questionEn: In the Istikharah dua, what should replace the Arabic pronoun/phrase 'hadhal-amr' ('this matter') when praying?
optionsEn: You explicitly name or intend your specific matter (e.g., marrying this person, taking this job, traveling on this date)
You can only insert travel destinations
You must write it in calligraphy first
You must leave it vague without thinking of the choice
explanationEn: Naming your concrete decision makes Istikharah deeply personal and focused.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1162 / Commentary of Ibn Hajar

questionEn: Which famous concise Istighfar dua did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) ask the Prophet ﷺ to teach him for inside Salah?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran wa la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Anta, faghfir li maghfiratan min ‘indika warhamni, innaka Antal-Ghafurur-Rahim
explanationEn: Even Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)—the greatest companion—confessed 'I have wronged myself greatly' before asking Allah for forgiveness directly from Him.

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Abu Bakr (RA) to recite 'Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathira...'?
optionsEn: Only upon entering a marketplace
Only after sneezing
Inside his Salah (before Salam, at the end of Tashahhud, and equally fitting anytime in private dua)
Only when mounting a camel
explanationEn: Reciting this pearl of humility at the end of Tashahhud before Salam brings every Salah to an unforgettable close.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say is the best dhikr and the best dua?
optionsEn: The best dhikr is poetry, and the best dua is counting coins
The best dhikr is 'La ilaha illAllah', and the best dua is 'Alhamdulillah'
The best dhikr is fasting, and the best dua is sleeping
The best dhikr is silence, and the best dua is complaining
explanationEn: Why is 'Alhamdulillah' called the best dua? Because praising the Generous Giver silently attracts more than directly begging—and gratitude invites His increase!

questionEn: When starting the day worried about making mistakes during work or interactions, which morning dua from Sahih Muslim 2725 asks Allah for guidance and uprightness?
optionsEn: Allahummahdini wa saddidni
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
explanationEn: Compact enough to whisper while walking to your car or opening your laptop, 'O Allah, guide me and keep me straight' anchors every morning.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise doing if you forget any part of your regular night worship (Hizb) because you fell asleep (Sahih Muslim 747)?
optionsEn: Wait until next Ramadan to make it up
Double it to forty rak‘ahs at midnight
Give up night prayer for the rest of the year
Whoever sleeps through his nightly portion (of Qur'an or prayer) and recites/prays it between Fajr and Dhuhr will have it recorded as if he prayed it at night
explanationEn: Allah's mercy rewards sincere consistency: making up missed Tahajjud or Witr (in even rak‘ahs during Duha time) preserves the full nightly credit!

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ make up missed night prayer during the daytime according to ‘A'ishah (RA) in Sahih Muslim 746?
optionsEn: He fasted three days without water
He prayed one single rak‘ah at sunset
If overcome by sleep or pain at night, he would pray twelve rak‘ahs during the forenoon (instead of his usual eleven with Witr)
He skipped daytime Sunnahs altogether
explanationEn: Praying an even number (like 12 instead of 11) in the daytime preserves the sanctity of odd Witr belonging to the night.

questionEn: What gentle daily remembrance did the Prophet ﷺ say turns ordinary waking moments into constant charity—as narrated in Sahih Muslim 1006?
optionsEn: Only building stone wells counts
Every Tasbihah is charity, every Takbirah is charity, every Tahmidah is charity, every Tahlilah is charity, enjoining good is charity, and forbidding evil is charity
Only silver coins count as charity
Only feasts for hundreds count
explanationEn: People of modest financial means can outpace the wealthy in charity simply through living tongues of dhikr and daily kindness.

questionEn: What concise dua did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah for regarding love—turning morning and night longing solely toward Him?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka
Allahumma aghnini bil-mal wahdahu
Allahumma inni as'aluka hubbaka wa hubba man yuhibbuka, wal-‘amalalladhi yuballighuni hubbak...
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Asking Allah to make His love dearer to us than ourselves, our families, and cold refreshing water captures the essence of spiritual devotion.

questionEn: In that same dua of Prophet Dawud (AS) praised by Muhammad ﷺ (Tirmidhi 3490), what refreshing earthly thing is Allah's love placed above?
optionsEn: Min al-ma'il-barid ('than cold water')
Than bronze shields
Than heavy wool cloaks
Than desert sandstorms
explanationEn: For anyone who has ever felt parched under Arabian heat, placing love of Allah above cold water vividly expresses spiritual thirst.

questionEn: What comprehensive refuge dua in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3591 did the Prophet ﷺ make against internal and behavioral flaws ('munkaratil-akhlaq')?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min munkaratil-akhlaqi wal-a‘mali wal-ahwa' ('O Allah, I seek refuge in You from evil character, evil deeds, and evil desires')
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Guarding character (akhlaq), actions (a‘mal), and inner desires (ahwa') keeps the heart healthy day and night.

questionEn: What short dua / Musnad Ahmad asks Allah to beautify our inner character just as He beautified our creation?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka
Allahumma ahsanta khalqi fa-ahsin khuluqi ('O Allah, just as You made my outward creation good, make my character good')
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
explanationEn: Often recited when looking in a mirror or getting dressed in the morning, this connects self-care directly to moral beauty.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct a companion to say if he feared forgetting the long adhkar, emphasizing quality over overwhelm?
optionsEn: Skip morning prayer to read longer books
Abandon all adhkar unless all 100 are finished in five minutes
Recite in a language you dislike without reflection
Memorize and keep steady a core set of authentic adhkar—like Ayat al-Kursi, Three Quls, Sayyid al-Istighfar, and 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdih'—and grow gradually with presence of heart
explanationEn: Consistency ('qalilun da'im') beats an unsustainable burst followed by burnout.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6408, what joyous news about angels applies to people who gather or sit in morning/evening remembrance of Allah?
optionsEn: Angels avoid homes where children are present
Allah has roaming angels searching the roads specifically for people of dhikr; when they find them, they call out 'Come to what you seek!' and cover them with wings up to the lowest heaven
Angels record only spoken sermons on Fridays
Angels visit only once a year in Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: And when Allah asks what His servants were asking for—Paradise—and seeking refuge from—the Fire—Allah declares: 'I have forgiven them, even anyone who merely sat with them!'

questionEn: In the Hadith Qudsi recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari 7405 & Muslim 2675, how does Allah respond to a servant who remembers Him privately vs. in a gathering?
optionsEn: Allah waits until the end of the month to respond
Private remembrance carries half credit
Only public gatherings are remembered by Allah
If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better gathering (of angels)
explanationEn: This Hadith Qudsi guarantees that no quiet whisper of morning, evening, or midnight dhikr ever goes unnoticed by Allah.

questionEn: In that same Hadith Qudsi (Bukhari 7405), how does Allah respond when a servant draws near to Him by a handspan, an arm's length, or walking?
optionsEn: If he draws near a handspan, I draw near an arm's length; if an arm's length, a fathom; and if he comes walking, I come to him at speed (harwalah)
Allah requires an intermediary to bridge the distance
Allah waits passively until the servant completes forty years
Allah moves away to test endurance
explanationEn: Allah's eagerness to meet a turning servant dwarfs our own small steps in Tahajjud, morning adhkar, or repentance.

questionEn: What gentle bedtime practice did the Prophet ﷺ use regarding lights and food vessels before sleeping (Sahih al-Bukhari 5623, 6295)?
optionsEn: Skip locking doors out of fatalism
Leave uncovered jugs on windowsills
Leave open flames burning unattended all night
Extinguish open lamps/fires, close doors while mentioning Allah's Name, cover drinking/food vessels with 'Bismillah', and then recite bedtime adhkar
explanationEn: Tying safety precautions together with 'Bismillah' exemplifies Prophetic balance between practical prudence and Tawakkul.

questionEn: When closing doors or covering vessels at night while saying 'Bismillah', what spiritual protection does Sahih Muslim 2012 note?
optionsEn: Only silver locks keep homes safe
Nothing happens when Bismillah is said
Winds open doors automatically
Satan cannot open a closed door (shut with Allah's Name), untie a tied waterskin, or uncover a covered vessel
explanationEn: Combining household care with dhikr wraps the entire family's night in quiet protection.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the person who sits on his bed remembering Allah until sleep overtakes him?
optionsEn: He must repeat his morning adhkar at noon

No servant lies down in a state of Wudu remembering Allah until drowsiness overtakes him and wakes during the night asking Allah for any good of this world or the Hereafter except that Allah gives it to him
His Wudu counts only until midnight
He should avoid waking before sunrise
explanationEn: Falling asleep with dhikr on our lips keeps the soul primed for accepted dua all night long.

questionEn: In the bedtime dua 'Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk...', what is the meaning of 'wa fawwadtu amri ilayk'?
optionsEn: And I rely solely on my own planning
And I demand immediate earthly reward
And I entrust/delegate all my affairs completely to You
And I keep my secrets hidden from You
explanationEn: Tafwid (entrusting all outcomes to Allah) is one of the deepest secrets of restful sleep free of overthinking.

questionEn: In 'Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk...', what does 'wa alja'tu zahri ilayk, raghbatan wa rahbatan ilayk' mean?
optionsEn: I fear people more than Allah
I rest only against stone walls
I turn my back away from prayer
I lean my back upon You for support, in hopeful longing (raghbah) and reverent awe (rahbah) toward You
explanationEn: Leaning one's back upon Allah means resting securely against His strength, knowing 'there is no refuge or escape from You except to You' ('la malja'a wa la manja minka illa ilayk').

questionEn: Why does the bedtime dua 'la malja'a wa la manja minka illa ilayk' capture the unique relationship of a believer with Allah?
optionsEn: Because hiding in caves replaces prayer
Because only travelers have homes of refuge
Because when fleeing worldly danger you run AWAY from the threat, whereas when seeking safety from Allah's displeasure you run STRAIGHT TO Allah Himself
Because sleep erases all accountability
explanationEn: There is nowhere outside Allah's mercy to flee—which is why turning toward Him brings instant comfort.

questionEn: According to Sunan Abi Dawud 4856, whoever lies down to sleep without mentioning Allah at all incurs what spiritual loss?
optionsEn: Forfeiture of all past fasts
A source of regret/shortcoming (tirah) from Allah—just like sitting in a gathering without mentioning Allah
A debt of ten silver coins
A permanent ban from morning prayer
explanationEn: Even whispering 'Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya' and 'SubhanAllah' saves the sleeper from ending the day heedlessly.

questionEn: What bedtime dua asks Allah to forgive our sins, drive away our devil, free our soul from pledges, and join us with the highest assembly?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahummaghfir li dhanbi, wa akhsi' shaytani, wa fukka rihani, waj‘alni fin-nadiyyil-a‘la
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
explanationEn: Taught by the Prophet ﷺ to Abu al-Azhar al-Anmari (RA) when lying down to sleep, this potent four-part dua protects faith and freedom.

questionEn: What morning/evening remembrance from Hisn al-Muslim opens with 'Asbahna wa asbahal-mulku lillahi...' and specifically seeks refuge from what two trials of the unseen?
optionsEn: Storms at sea and dust in markets
The torment in the Fire (‘adhabin fin-nar) and the torment in the grave (‘adhabin fil-qabr)
Forgetting poetry and losing sandals
Cold winters and dry wells
explanationEn: Pairing daily optimism ('its victory, aid, light, blessing, and guidance') with sober awareness of the grave and Akhirah keeps life balanced.

questionEn: Which brief phrase in the morning/evening dhikr 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi' is paired in Sahih Muslim 2692 with 'whoever says it 100 times morning and evening'—what exact Arabic addition appears in Bukhari 6405?
optionsEn: Only if recited while standing in rain
Only if written on parchment
Only during the month of Muharram
SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi — even if one's sins are like the foam of the sea (mithla zabadil-bahr), they are forgiven
explanationEn: Two effortless words repeated during a morning walk or commute wash away mountains of daily slips.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach his daughter Fatimah (RA) in Sunan al-Nasa'i / Mustadrak when she came seeking help with exhausting housework—besides Tasbih Fatimah—for morning and evening?
optionsEn: Stop all household care immediately
Hire ten servants before sunset
Ya Hayyu ya Qayyumu bi-rahmatika astaghith, aslih li sha'ni kullahu wa la takilni ila nafsi tarfata ‘ayn
Sleep throughout the entire afternoon
explanationEn: Fatimah (RA) received spiritual fuel far richer than worldly ease: Tasbih Fatimah at night and total reliance on Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum by day.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1154, why does the Prophet ﷺ pair 'La ilaha illAllah' with 'SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illAllah, Allahu Akbar, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' upon waking briefly at night?
optionsEn: Because only five phrases exist in Arabic
Because it replaces Witr prayer
Because long sentences are forbidden at night
Because glorifying and praising Allah first—before saying 'Allahummaghfir li' or making personal dua—honors Allah's majesty and opens immediate acceptance
explanationEn: Praising Allah before asking is the universal golden key to answered dua—even at 3:00 AM.

questionEn: When praying Witr in three rak‘ahs, which three surahs did the Prophet ﷺ frequently recite after Al-Fatihah according to Sunan Abi Dawud 1423 & Nasa'i 1735?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah, Al ‘Imran, and An-Nisa only
Surah Al-A‘la (87) in the 1st, Surah Al-Kafirun (109) in the 2nd, and Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) in the 3rd (sometimes adding Al-Falaq and An-Nas)
Surah Al-‘Asr repeated three times
Surah Al-Fil, Quraysh, and Al-Masad
explanationEn: Notice the beauty: glorifying Allah (Al-A‘la), declaring pure loyalty (Al-Kafirun), and affirming pure Oneness (Al-Ikhlas) right before Qunut!

questionEn: What is the proper posture and timing for Qunut in Witr prayer according to the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Lying down after finishing Witr
Standing in the final rak‘ah either right after completing recitation before Ruku‘, or after rising from Ruku‘ (both are authentically practiced among scholars), raising the hands humbly
Seated outside the prayer mat after Salam
While bowing in Ruku‘
explanationEn: Keeping focus on heartfelt humility in Qunut matters far more than disputing whether it occurs before or after Ruku‘.

questionEn: In Qunut al-Witr, what does 'wa barik li fima a‘tayt' ('and bless me in what You have given') teach us about happiness?
optionsEn: Stop striving for lawful livelihood
True satisfaction comes not from having huge quantities, but from Allah placing barakah inside whatever health, family, time, and income He already gave us
Blessing only enters huge palaces
Never be content with modest provision
explanationEn: Barakah turns little into plenty and turns ordinary days into peaceful gifts.

questionEn: In Qunut al-Witr, what does 'wa qini sharra ma qadayt' ('and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed') mean?
optionsEn: Demanding exemption from every earthly test
Asking Allah to shield us from the painful harm or spiritual ruin of trials decreed in creation, while affirming 'fa-innaka taqdi wa la yuqda ‘alayk' (all His decrees are wise and just)
Claiming Allah creates evil injustice
Refusing to accept Allah's sovereignty
explanationEn: Clarified later by 'wa sh-sharru laysa ilayk' (Sahih Muslim 771), pure evil is never attributed to Allah's essence, yet we ask protection from any created harm.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sahih Muslim 771 as an opening dua (Istiftah) especially loved in night prayer—starting with 'Wajjahtu wajhiya...'?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka
Wajjahtu wajhiya lilladhi fataras-samawati wal-arda hanifan wa ma ana minal-mushrikin; inna salati wa nusuki wa mahyaya wa mamati lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin...
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: In this majestic opening, the worshipper declares: 'O Allah, You are the King; there is no deity except You. You are my Lord and I am Your servant...'

questionEn: In that same Sahih Muslim 771 night-prayer opening, what deeply comforting phrase acknowledges that only Allah guides to noble character?
optionsEn: Wahdini li-ahsanil-akhlaqi la yahdi li-ahsaniha illa Anta, wasrif ‘anni sayyi'aha la yasrifu ‘anni sayyi'aha illa Anta
Only travelers have good manners
Character cannot be changed after youth
I perfected my manners through philosophy alone
explanationEn: Realizing that even good manners are a direct gift from Allah keeps us humble and prayerful about our temper, patience, and kindness.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 771, what joyful phrases follow 'wahdini li-ahsanil-akhlaq...' expressing readiness before Allah?
optionsEn: Accept my apologies without my repentance
Labbayka wa sa‘dayk, wal-khayru kulluhu fi yadayk, wash-sharru laysa ilayk, ana bika wa ilayk, tabarakta wa ta‘alayt, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk
Wait until sunrise before standing
Keep my flaws hidden from myself
explanationEn: Saying 'Labbayka wa sa‘dayk' ('Here I am at Your service, joyfully responding to You!') fills private night worship with warmth.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ recite in Ruku‘ and Sujud especially in late life after Surah An-Nasr was revealed (Sahih al-Bukhari 794)?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
SubhanakAllahumma Rabbana wa bihamdika, Allahummaghfir li ('Glory be to You, O Allah our Lord, and praise be to You; O Allah, forgive me')
Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
explanationEn: He put the Qur'an directly into practice inside his Ruku‘ and Sujud, fulfilling 'fasabbih bi-hamdi Rabbika wastaghfirh'.

questionEn: What did ‘A'ishah (RA) hear the Prophet ﷺ say in Sujud during Tahajjud when she reached out in the dark and touched the soles of his upright feet (Sahih Muslim 486)?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni a‘udhu bi-ridaka min sakhatika, wa bi-mu‘afatika min ‘uqubatika, wa a‘udhu bika minka...
Ghufranaka
Allahumma hab li mulkan ‘azima
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
explanationEn: Even in deep darkness when no one could see him, the Prophet's ﷺ Sujud overflowed with awe and intimacy with Allah.

questionEn: What short phrase of praise in Ruku‘ and Sujud was narrated by ‘A'ishah (RA) in Sahih Muslim 487 that glorifies Allah as Lord of angels and Jibril?
optionsEn: Subbuhun Quddusun Rabbul-mala'ikati war-ruh ('Most Glorious, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit [Jibril]')
Alhamdulillah rabbil-‘alamin
Allahu Akbar kabira
Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil
explanationEn: Repeating 'Subbuhun Quddusun Rabbul-mala'ikati war-ruh' in bowing and prostration elevates Salah into heavenly reverence.

questionEn: What dua between the two prostrations (Jalsah) gathers seven vital human needs according to Sunan Abi Dawud 850 and Tirmidhi 284?
optionsEn: Rabbighfir li, warhamni, wajburni, warfa‘ni, wahdini, wa ‘afini, warzuqni (Forgive me, have mercy on me, mend/restore me, elevate me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide for me)
Grant me silver, palaces, speed, fame, sleep, silence, and rain
Delay mercy until winter
Forgive only my mistakes from yesterday
explanationEn: Paused briefly between the two sujuds, these short words ask Allah to mend every broken place ('wajburni') and sustain body and soul.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 850 / Sunan al-Tirmidhi 284 / Ibn Majah 898

questionEn: What four things did the Prophet ﷺ instruct believers to seek refuge from right after the final Tashahhud before saying Salam?
optionsEn: Torment of Hellfire, torment of the grave, trials of life and death, and the trial of Al-Masih ad-Dajjal
Missing feasts, losing keys, and cloudy skies
Speaking gently and helping guests
Cold weather, long flights, quiet mornings, and hard work
explanationEn: Protecting oneself against these four trials at the end of every Salah—including Witr and Tahajjud—fortifies faith across life and death.

questionEn: When waking up before Fajr to eat Suhoor in Ramadan or for voluntary fasting, why is that pre-dawn window doubly blessed for dua?
optionsEn: Because it combines the last third of the night (when Allah descends to answer callers) with the barakah of Suhoor and the fasting person's uprightness
Because prayers during daylight are invalid
Because only Ramadan Suhoor counts
Because angels sleep after sunrise
explanationEn: Using ten quiet minutes before Suhoor for two rak‘ahs of Tahajjud and heartfelt dua transforms Ramadan mornings.

questionEn: Which short seven-times plea for protection from Hellfire is widely recited morning and evening after Fajr and Maghrib (rooted in Qur'an 3:191 and Sunan Abi Dawud 5079)?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma ajirni minan-nar ('O Allah, save/protect me from the Fire')
explanationEn: Saying 'Allahumma ajirni minan-nar' sincerely asks Allah for the greatest ultimate deliverance (Qur'an 3:185: whoever is spared the Fire and admitted to Paradise has truly succeeded).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ advise reciting 'Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika an ushrika bika shay'an a‘lamuh, wa astaghfiruka lima la a‘lam' (Musnad Ahmad 19606) morning and evening?
optionsEn: To seek protection against minor/hidden shirk (riya'—showing off) that creeps stealthily like a black ant on a black stone in dark night
To excuse forgetting Wudu before Dhuhr
To shorten Friday sermons
To replace reciting Surah Al-Fatihah
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr (RA) asked in alarm how anyone escapes hidden shirk, the Prophet ﷺ gifted him this protective istighfar.

questionEn: What short four-item dua did Anas (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ recited more often than any other dua?
optionsEn: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina ‘adhaban-nar
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
explanationEn: Whenever Anas (RA) himself made any dua—morning, evening, or during pilgrimage—he always included this comprehensive Qur'anic gem.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6398 & Muslim 2719, what comprehensive dua did Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ made asking forgiveness for errors out of ignorance, haste, and excess?
optionsEn: Forgive only my deliberate good deeds
Allahummaghfir li khati'ati wa jahli, wa israfi fi amri, wa ma Anta a‘lamu bihi minni; Allahummaghfir li jiddi wa hazli, wa khata'i wa ‘amdi, wa kullu dhalika ‘indi
Leave past sins unmentioned
I have never made any unintentional slip
explanationEn: Asking forgiveness for seriousness and jest, error and intent, ignorance and excess—closing with 'wa kullu dhalika ‘indi' ('and all of that is with me')—models unmatched humility.

questionEn: What closing petition in that same Sahih Muslim 2719 dua affirms that Allah alone advances or delays a servant?
optionsEn: Others hold keys to my progress
Time decides everything without Your leave
I advance myself solely through ambition
Antal-Muqaddimu wa Antal-Mu'akhkhir, wa Anta ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir
explanationEn: Trusting Al-Muqaddim Al-Mu'akhkhir removes jealousy and impatience when others seem ahead in worldly milestones.

questionEn: What two priceless states of heart did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah for in 'Allahumma inni as'aluka khashyataka fil-ghaybi wash-shahadah...'?
optionsEn: Reverent awe of Allah both in secret (when nobody watches) and in public, truthful speech in both anger and contentment, and moderation in both poverty and wealth
Silence in public and boastfulness in private
Isolation from all people forever
Harshness when angry and laziness when wealthy
explanationEn: Narrated in Sunan an-Nasa'i 1305, this magnificent dua also asks for 'na‘iman la yanfad' (unending bliss), 'qurrata ‘aynin la tanqati‘' (uninterrupted joy), and 'ladhdhatan-nazari ila wajhik' (the delight of gazing upon Your Countenance).

questionEn: In that same Sunan an-Nasa'i 1305 dua ('Allahumma bi-‘ilmikal-ghayb...'), what wise criterion did the Prophet ﷺ give for asking Allah for long life versus death?
optionsEn: Keep me alive forever regardless of trials
End my life before hardship begins
Ignore life's spiritual purpose
Keep me alive so long as You know life is better for me, and cause me to die when You know death is better for me
explanationEn: This submission to Allah's knowledge of the unseen teaches complete peace about lifespan.

questionEn: In Sunan an-Nasa'i 1305, what final blessing of unity and spiritual beauty closes the dua: 'wa zayyinna bi-zinatil-iman...'?
optionsEn: Adorn us strictly with silk and gold
Adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us rightly guided guides (hudatan muhtadin)
Make us indifferent to others' guidance
Keep guidance hidden inside private books
explanationEn: Asking Allah to make us both guided ourselves ('muhtadin') and gentle lights guiding others ('hudah') turns personal adhkar into loving service.

questionEn: What short dua asks Allah to benefit us with what He taught us and teach us what benefits us?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi ma razaqtana
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma-nfa‘ni bima ‘allamtani, wa ‘allimni ma yanfa‘uni, wa zidni ‘ilma
explanationEn: Knowledge without implementation becomes a burden; this dua pairs learning with practical benefit and thankful increase.

questionEn: What short Prophetic plea asks Allah exclusively for His bounty and mercy: 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlika wa rahmatik'?
optionsEn: Keep Your mercy inside mountains
Delay bounty until old age
Fa-innahu la yamlikuha illa Anta ('For none possesses Your bounty and mercy except You')—or asking specifically for '‘ilman nafi‘an'
Share Your mercy only with wealthy elders
explanationEn: Recited when a guest saw only water at home or whenever seeking Allah's provision, knowing none owns bounty and mercy except Him keeps hope alive.

questionEn: What gentle daily discipline did Ibn al-Qayyim compare morning and evening adhkar to in Al-Wabil al-Sayyib?
optionsEn: An optional ornament worn only on Eid
A custom restricted to elderly scholars
A heavy weight that slows travelers down
A sturdy coat of armor (dir‘) protecting the heart and limbs all day and all night against arrows of anxiety, envy, and Satan
explanationEn: Just as armor works best when worn BEFORE entering the battlefield, morning adhkar work best before diving into daily notifications and stress.

questionEn: What bedtime habit did the Prophet ﷺ say brings peace when a believer cannot fall asleep due to stress about tomorrow's tasks?
optionsEn: Entrusting the outcome to Allah ('wa fawwadtu amri ilayk'), making Istighfar, and reminding oneself of 'HasbiyAllahu la ilaha illa Huwa'
Eating heavy sweets at 2 AM
Checking worries repeatedly until dawn without praying
Making angry resolutions for morning
explanationEn: Combining Istighfar, Tawakkul, and bedtime adhkar releases mental tension into Allah's care.

questionEn: What short plea from the Sunnah heritage asks Allah not to allow enemies or envious people to rejoice over our hardship?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Allahumma la tushmit bi ‘aduwwan wa la hasida (part of Prophetic pleas for protection and honor)
Ghufranaka
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Asking Allah for dignity and protection while keeping one's own heart clean of rancor reflects balanced Prophetic wisdom.

questionEn: When starting a busy morning, what short Prophetic dua asks Allah to spare us from unlawful provision through lawful sufficiency?
optionsEn: Allahummak-fini bi-halalika ‘an haramik, wa aghnini bi-fadlika ‘amman siwak
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Taught by ‘Ali (RA) to an indebted slave seeking freedom—'even if you have debt as huge as Mount Sir, Allah will pay it off for you!'

questionEn: Who taught the debt-relief dua 'Allahummak-fini bi-halalika ‘an haramik, wa aghnini bi-fadlika ‘amman siwak' directly to ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)?
optionsEn: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself
Zayd ibn Harithah (RA)
Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA)
explanationEn: ‘Ali (RA) promised that sincerely reciting it with honest effort brings Allah's aid even under mountain-sized debt.

questionEn: Why is reciting 'Ayat al-Kursi' after every obligatory prayer AND morning/evening AND before sleep considered one of the strongest daily habits?
optionsEn: Because it exempts one from afternoon prayers
It guards the believer continuously—between every prayer until the next (promising entry to Paradise upon death, Nasa'i al-Kubra 9928), throughout day/night, and throughout sleep
Because it is recited only in Ramadan
Because it is the shortest verse in the Qur'an
explanationEn: Three minutes across the whole day to recite Ayat al-Kursi weaves an unbroken canopy of Tawhid and protection.

questionEn: What gentle reminder encourages beginners who stumble slightly while reciting Arabic morning/evening adhkar or Qur'an?
optionsEn: Stop reciting aloud until you master classical grammar
Only native Arab scholars receive reward
The one who recites the Qur'an proficiently is with the noble, obedient angels; and the one who struggles and stammers with difficulty gets TWO rewards
Switch permanently to silence
explanationEn: Allah honors effort and sincerity even more tenderly than effortless fluency—earning double reward for every earnest struggle.

questionEn: In Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3375, what short dhikr did a Bedouin ask the Prophet ﷺ for because he found the wider laws of Islam overwhelming to memorize all at once?
optionsEn: La yazalu lisanuka ratban min dhikrillahi (‘Azza wa Jall) — 'Keep your tongue constantly moist with the remembrance of Allah'
Stop talking to neighbors completely
Memorize three volumes of history first
Fast without breaking for forty days
explanationEn: Keeping the tongue gently moist with SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illAllah, Allahu Akbar, and Istighfar makes dhikr the heartbeat of every hour.

questionEn: Why is 'SubhanAllahi wal-hamdulillah wa la ilaha illAllahu wallahu Akbar' loved by the Prophet ﷺ more than everything the sun rises upon?
optionsEn: Because praising Allah's perfection, thanking His grace, declaring His Oneness, and magnifying His greatness surpasses every fleeting earthly possession
Because it replaces all charitable donations
Because it turns desert sand into gold
Because it shortens afternoon work
explanationEn: Saying those four words sincerely from the heart outweighs owning the whole sunlit earth!

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about saying 'La ilaha illAllah wallahu Akbar, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah'?
optionsEn: It counts only on snowy mornings
It requires standing on Mount Safa
It applies only inside Masjid al-Haram
Not a soul on earth says it except that his sins are forgiven—even if they are like the foam of the sea
explanationEn: Combining Tawhid, Takbir, and surrender of power ('La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah') cleanses daily slips with ease.

questionEn: What morning/evening dua did Ibn ‘Umar (RA) say the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned—asking for ‘afiyah in religion, dunya, family, and wealth—plus what request about one's head/heart?
optionsEn: Asking for immunity from ever feeling tired
Asking Allah to protect him from front, back, right, left, and above, and seeking refuge in His greatness from being unexpectedly destroyed from beneath
Asking for double inheritance shares
Asking to bypass travel inspections
explanationEn: Ibn ‘Umar (RA) emphasized: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never left off saying these words in the evening and in the morning.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5074 / Sunan Ibn Majah 3871

questionEn: Which closing praise (Kaffarat al-Majlis) is recommended before parting from an evening study circle or family sitting?
optionsEn: Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil only
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa Anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
explanationEn: Sealing evening family conversations with Kaffarat al-Majlis turns even casual chats into forgiven, blessed gatherings before bedtime.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ practice Istighfar at the end of his gatherings—including late evening sittings—according to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3434 and Abu Dawud 1516?
optionsEn: He asked everyone to fast the next day
He forbade smiling during evening gatherings
He fined anyone who spoke out of turn
Companions counted him saying up to 100 times in a single sitting: 'Rabbighfir li wa tub ‘alayya, innaka Antat-Tawwabur-Rahim'
explanationEn: Modeling effortless, frequent 'Rabbighfir li wa tub ‘alayh' kept gatherings humble and spiritually refreshing.

questionEn: What morning mindset does reciting 'Allahumma ma asbaha bi min ni‘matin...' foster before checking morning news or social feeds?
optionsEn: Gratitude-first awareness: pausing to honor Allah as the sole Source of life, sight, breath, and blessings before worldly comparisons begin
Envy toward wealthier friends
Panic about missing trivial trends
Indifference toward daily blessings
explanationEn: Starting the morning with Allah's adhkar before scrolling brings emotional steadiness all day.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ love ending his day with Surah Al-Baqarah's last two verses (2:285–286) even if a person was too tired for long Tahajjud?
optionsEn: Because they forbid sleeping past 4 AM
Because those two verses reaffirm full Iman ('Sami‘na wa ata‘na'), beg pardon ('Ghufranaka'), ask mercy ('Wa‘fu ‘anna waghfir lana warhamna'), and suffice the sleeper completely
Because they replace the five daily prayers
Because they list travel distances in Arabia
explanationEn: Even on the most exhausting day, reciting 2:285–286 before closing your eyes seals the night in faith, forgiveness, and divine sufficiency.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6311, what is the very first line of the final bedtime dua taught to Al-Bara' ibn ‘Azib (RA)?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Allahumma hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk ('O Allah, I have submitted my soul to You')
explanationEn: Submission (Islam) is both the beginning of faith and the last conscious word before sleep.

questionEn: What serene morning and evening dua from Sunan Abi Dawud 5074 & Ibn Majah encourages steadfast adhkar even during busy travel or Hajj?
optionsEn: Consistency in these brief Prophetic supplications guards heart, body, family, and journey—requiring less than ten minutes total morning and evening
Adhkar are suspended whenever one boards a plane
Adhkar work only in winter
Only residents inside Madinah need morning adhkar
explanationEn: Keeping a simple daily checklist—like Duya's Morning & Evening Adhkar tracker—makes Prophetic protection effortless anywhere.

questionEn: What three Takbirs does the Sunnah prescribe right before reciting 'Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha...' upon boarding a vehicle, train, or airplane?
optionsEn: Astaghfirullah three times
Amin three times
SubhanAllah three times
Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim 1342, the Prophet ﷺ magnified Allah three times before praising Him for subjecting the means of transport.

questionEn: After praising Allah in the Travel Dua (Muslim 1342), what three inner and moral qualities does the traveler ask for along the journey?
optionsEn: Fastest speed, luxury seats, and tax-free shopping
Silence, solitude, and zero delays
Fame in foreign cities and silver coins
Righteousness (al-birr), God-consciousness (at-taqwa), and deeds that Allah is pleased with (wa minal-‘amali ma tarda)
explanationEn: Even on business or holiday travel, asking for birr, taqwa, and pleasing deeds sanctifies every mile.

questionEn: What does the traveler ask Allah to do to the physical distance in the Travel Dua: 'Allahumma hawwin ‘alayna safarana hadha...'?
optionsEn: Double its mileage so we stay away longer
Watwi ‘anna bu‘dah ('And fold up / roll up its distance for us' so it feels light and easy)
Cancel the return ticket automatically
Hide every landmark along the highway
explanationEn: Asking Allah to 'fold up' the distance reflects how divine barakah makes arduous journeys feel effortless.

questionEn: In the Travel Dua (Muslim 1342), what two beloved roles does the traveler entrust to Allah during their absence?
optionsEn: Antas-Sahibu fis-safar, wal-Khalifatu fil-ahl ('You are the Companion in the journey, and the Guardian/Successor left behind over our family')
Protect only my luggage and ignore neighbors
Manage my trade ledger and polish my armor
Keep rain away from my hometown only
explanationEn: Knowing Allah travels beside you while simultaneously guarding your loved ones at home eases separation anxiety.

questionEn: What three painful outcomes does the Travel Dua seek refuge from at its close?
optionsEn: Walking across paved plazas
Meeting fellow pilgrims on the road
Hardship of travel (wa‘tha'is-safar), depressing/grievous sights (ka'abatil-manzar), and finding an ill reversal upon returning to wealth and family (su'il-munqalabi fil-mali wal-ahl)
Cloudy skies, simple meals, and early mornings
explanationEn: Asking safety from bad news awaiting back home guards the entire trip until one steps back through the front door.

questionEn: When returning home from Umrah, Hajj, or any trip, what four joyous words are added right at the beginning of the Travel Dua?
optionsEn: Hasbunallah, tawakkaltu, amin, shukran
Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, ‘abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun ('Returning, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord')
Ghufranaka, labbayk, bismillah, salam
MashaAllah, tabarakAllah, subhanAllah, amin
explanationEn: Coming home in repentance, worship, and gratitude prevents pilgrimage pride and keeps humility bright.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when climbing ascending mountain passes versus descending into valleys while traveling (Sahih al-Bukhari 2993)?
optionsEn: He remained silent on mountains and clapped in valleys
He said 'Allahu Akbar' when ascending heights, and 'SubhanAllah' when descending into valleys
He said 'Astaghfirullah' going up and 'Amin' going down
He faced backwards while riding
explanationEn: Magnifying Allah's greatness when rising high prevents ego, and glorifying His perfection when dropping low prevents gloom.

questionEn: Upon arriving safely at a hotel, camp, or rest stop during travel, what six-word shield did the Prophet ﷺ promise protects against every harm there until departure?
optionsEn: A‘udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi ‘adada khalqih
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
explanationEn: Narrated by Khawlah bint Hakim (RA), reciting this upon settling at any destination guarantees nothing there harms you until you move on.

questionEn: What parting dua did the Prophet ﷺ say when bidding farewell to a departing traveler (Sunan Abi Dawud 2600 / Tirmidhi 3443)?
optionsEn: Do not pray while crossing borders
Astawdi‘ullaha dinaka, wa amanataka, wa khawatima ‘amalik ('I entrust to Allah your religion, your trust/family, and the final outcomes of your deeds')
Bring back expensive souvenirs for everyone
Forget your hometown until next year
explanationEn: Notice the order: placing the traveler's religion (din) first reminds us that returning with intact faith matters most.

questionEn: How should the departing traveler reply when bidding farewell to family and friends staying behind (Sunan Ibn Majah 2825)?
optionsEn: Astawdi‘ukumullaha alladhi la tadi‘u wada'i‘uh ('I entrust you to Allah, whose entrusted deposits are never lost')
Keep my room locked until spring
Pray only once I arrive
Send letters every morning
explanationEn: Depositing loved ones into Allah's safekeeping gives peace because Allah never loses anything placed in His trust.

questionEn: What additional three-part farewell blessing did the Prophet ﷺ give to a companion departing on a journey (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3444)?
optionsEn: May your ship sail twice as fast without prayer
May you never encounter strangers
May you find silver coins in every inn
ZawwadakAllahut-taqwa, wa ghafara dhanbaka, wa yassara lakal-khayra haythuma kunta ('May Allah provision you with Taqwa, forgive your sin, and make goodness easy for you wherever you are')
explanationEn: Provisioning a friend with Taqwa, forgiveness, and ease in goodness is the finest travel send-off.

questionEn: When catching sight of a city or town you are about to enter—such as Makkah or Madinah—what dua of blessing and refuge did the Prophet ﷺ recite (Nasa'i al-Kubra 8788)?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir
Allahumma Rabbas-samawatis-sab‘i wa ma azlalna... as'aluka khayra hadhihil-qaryati wa khayra ahliha wa khayra ma fiha, wa a‘udhu bika min sharriha wa sharri ahliha wa sharri ma fiha
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
explanationEn: Asking Allah for the best of a new city, its residents, and whatever is inside it—while seeking refuge from its harm—sets a respectful arrival tone.

questionEn: If a riding mount or travel vehicle stumbles, what should a Muslim say instead of cursing Satan—and why (Sunan Abi Dawud 4982)?
optionsEn: Shout angrily at the driver
Remain completely silent for an hour
Say 'Bismillah'—because cursing Satan makes him swell with pride like a house thinking he caused it, whereas saying 'Bismillah' shrinks him down like a fly
Curse the road and weather
explanationEn: Turning sudden travel hiccups into 'Bismillah' keeps patience sweet and starves Shaytan's ego.

questionEn: When returning from a long journey, what courtesy toward one's spouse and family did the Prophet ﷺ practice before walking unannounced into the house late at night (Sahih al-Bukhari 5244)?
optionsEn: Burst through the door at 2 AM without warning
Stop at the market for five hours before greeting family
Wait till morning/daytime or send word ahead—and upon arriving near home, pray two rak‘ahs in the neighborhood masjid first as he used to do
Skip saying Salam inside the home
explanationEn: Starting homecoming with two rak‘ahs of gratitude at the local masjid and giving family thoughtful notice reflects prophetic tenderness.

questionEn: In the Prophetic Talbiyah ('Labbayk Allahumma labbayk...'), what three universal realities are declared belongs exclusively to Allah?
optionsEn: Time, calendars, and poetry
Mountain passes, rivers, and clouds
All praise (al-hamd), all grace/favor (an-ni‘mah), and all sovereignty (al-mulk)—with zero partner (la sharika lak)
Gold, silver, and coral
explanationEn: Repeating 'inal-hamda wan-ni‘mata laka wal-mulk' reminds the pilgrim that even the privilege of being invited to Makkah is pure favor from Allah.

questionEn: What happens around a pilgrim whenever they raise their voice in Talbiyah?
optionsEn: Everything to their right and left—stones, trees, and clods of earth—joins in reciting the Talbiyah until the earth ends on either side
Birds flee from Makkah
Echoes fade inside the Masjid only
Angels silence the valley immediately
explanationEn: Knowing creation itself echoes our Talbiyah turns every bus ride and walk toward Makkah into a cosmic choir.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ respond when Jibril (AS) advised him regarding how companions should recite the Talbiyah (Sunan Abi Dawud 1814)?
optionsEn: To replace it with silence
To sing it only after Tawaf ends
He instructed his companions to raise their voices in the Talbiyah (for men), while women recite it softly audible to themselves
To whisper it only in secret rooms
explanationEn: Men raising their voices warmly in Talbiyah spreads pilgrimage joy while women preserve modesty.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1814 / Sunan Ibn Majah 2922

questionEn: What wording did the Prophet ﷺ say when boarding his mount or setting out in Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah (or Miqat) to begin Umrah or Hajj?
optionsEn: Labbayka ‘Umratan (for Umrah) or Labbayka Hajjan (for Hajj), followed by the Talbiyah
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Stating the specific rite concisely with 'Labbayk' aligns intention smoothly before beginning the Talbiyah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim fears illness or visa/route obstruction might prevent completing Hajj or Umrah, what conditional clause did the Prophet ﷺ teach Dubā‘ah bint az-Zubayr (RA) to add at Ihram?
optionsEn: Transfer my Ihram to a friend
Cancel my intention if rain falls
Allahumma mahilli haythu habastani ('O Allah, my place of exiting Ihram is wherever You detain me')
Wait until next year automatically
explanationEn: This compassionate Sunnah allowance protects sick or vulnerable pilgrims from penalty if genuinely prevented from reaching the Haram.

questionEn: Upon entering Al-Masjid al-Haram (and any mosque), what full Prophetic entry dua combines refuge, Salawat, and seeking mercy?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
A‘udhu billahil-‘Azim wa bi-wajhihil-Karim wa sultanihil-Qadim minash-Shaytanir-rajim; Bismillahi was-salatu was-salamu ‘ala Rasulillah; Allahumma-ftah li abwaba rahmatik
explanationEn: Entering with the right foot while asking for the doors of Allah's mercy protects focus inside the Sacred Mosque.
reference: Sahih Muslim 713 / Sunan Abi Dawud 466 / Ibn Majah 771

questionEn: Is there one single mandatory scripted dua that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ required pilgrims to recite upon first seeing the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Yes, a 40-line poem in classical meter is obligatory
Making any dua upon seeing the Kaaba is forbidden
Only scholars over fifty may speak there

No—there is no single mandatory Prophetic wording; one may raise hands and make heartfelt personal dua, such as ‘Umar's (RA) 'Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minkas-salam...' or asking Allah to increase the House in honor and accept our pilgrimage
explanationEn: Knowing there is no fixed rigid script frees your heart to pour out sincere, tearful personal prayers the moment your eyes meet the Kaaba!
reference: Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah / Fiqh of Hajj & Umrah

questionEn: What short phrase did Ibn ‘Umar (RA) narrate as the Sunnah utterance when touching, kissing, or pointing toward Al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Black Stone) at the start of every Tawaf circuit?
optionsEn: Bismillahi wallahu Akbar (or Allahu Akbar)
Ghufranaka Rabbana
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
explanationEn: Kissing or gently pointing from afar when crowded with 'Bismillahi Allahu Akbar' honors the Sunnah without pushing or harming fellow pilgrims.

questionEn: When pointing toward the Black Stone from a distance during crowded Tawaf, what gentle etiquette should replace shoving through crowds?
optionsEn: Push elders aside to force your way to the stone
Simply face it briefly, raise your right hand toward it saying 'Allahu Akbar' (without kissing your hand unless touching the stone directly), and keep moving smoothly
Stop walking in the middle lane for ten minutes
Skip saying Allahu Akbar altogether
explanationEn: ‘Umar (RA) and the Prophet ﷺ taught that harming a fellow Muslim cancels spiritual beauty; pointing calmly when crowded is pure Sunnah.

questionEn: Which exact portion of every Tawaf circuit did the Prophet ﷺ consistently dedicate to reciting 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina ‘adhaban-nar'?
optionsEn: Inside the Hijr Isma‘il exclusively
While walking backward away from the Kaaba
Only behind Maqam Ibrahim after finishing all seven rounds
Between the Yemeni Corner (Rukn al-Yamani) and the Black Stone (Al-Hajar al-Aswad)
explanationEn: In the rest of each Tawaf round, you are completely free to make heartfelt personal duas, recite Qur'an, or make dhikr in your own words!

questionEn: Did the Prophet ﷺ prescribe seven separate printed booklet duas—one fixed script per circuit—during the seven rounds of Tawaf?
optionsEn: Yes, missing one word invalidates Tawaf
No; assigning seven rigid circuit-specific booklets has no basis in the Sunnah—rather, the pilgrim speaks directly to Allah in personal dua, Qur'an, and dhikr throughout Tawaf
Speaking in any non-Arabic language silently is prohibited
Yes, only circuit 4 allows personal language
explanationEn: Pouring your real heart out to Allah—even in your native tongue alongside Qur'anic duas—makes Tawaf deeply alive rather than reading a checklist mechanically.

questionEn: After completing seven circuits of Tawaf, what verse did the Prophet ﷺ recite as he walked toward Maqam Ibrahim to pray two rak‘ahs (Sahih Muslim 1218)?
optionsEn: Wattakhidhu min Maqami Ibrahima musalla ('And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer' — Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125)
Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun
Innas-Safa wal-Marwata min sha‘a'irillah
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: And inside those two rak‘ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, he recited Surah Al-Kafirun in the first and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the second!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ recite Surah Al-Kafirun and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the two rak‘ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: Because they may only be read in Makkah
To shorten Tawaf to three rounds
Because no other surahs were revealed yet
To anchor the entire pilgrimage in pure Tawhid—renouncing all shirk (Al-Kafirun) and affirming Allah's absolute Oneness (Al-Ikhlas)
explanationEn: Those same two surahs of Tawhid also grace the Sunnah of Fajr, Maghrib Sunnah, and Witr.

questionEn: Upon approaching Mount Safa for the very first time to begin Sa‘i, which Qur'anic verse and Sunnah phrase did the Prophet ﷺ recite (Sahih Muslim 1218)?
optionsEn: Wattakhidhu min Maqami Ibrahima musalla
Innas-Safa wal-Marwata min sha‘a'irillah — Abda'u bima bada'Allahu bih ('I begin with what Allah began with')
Rabbana taqabbal minna
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
explanationEn: Beginning at Safa because Allah mentioned Safa first honors the exact order of revelation while recalling Hajar's (AS) faithful search.

questionEn: When standing atop Safa and Marwah facing the Kaaba, what victory-and-Tawhid dhikr did the Prophet ﷺ recite between his long personal duas (Sahih Muslim 1218)?
optionsEn: Allahu Akbar (3x), La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir; la ilaha illallahu wahdah, anjaza wa‘dah, wa nasara ‘abdah, wa hazamal-ahzaba wahdah
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: He praised Allah with these words, then raised his hands in long personal dua, and repeated that entire cycle THREE times on Safa and THREE times on Marwah!

questionEn: What heartfelt dua did Ibn Mas‘ud (RA) and Ibn ‘Umar (RA) often recite while walking briskly between the green lights during Sa‘i?
optionsEn: Rabbighfir warham, innaka Antal-A‘azzul-Akram (or 'wa tajawaz ‘amma ta‘lam, innaka Antal-A‘azzul-Akram'—'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the Most Mighty, Most Generous')
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: While not obligatory, many pilgrims love alternating this humble Athar of the Companions with their own personal prayers during Sa‘i.
reference: Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah / Athar of Ibn Mas‘ud & Ibn ‘Umar

questionEn: On the Day of Arafah (9th of Dhul-Hijjah), what did the Prophet ﷺ declare in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3585 is the 'best dua' and the finest words spoken by himself and all earlier prophets?
optionsEn: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Praising Allah's absolute sovereignty and power on Arafah softens the heart and opens the gates of divine generosity before asking our needs.

questionEn: How long did the Prophet ﷺ remain standing in earnest dua on the Day of Arafah during his Farewell Pilgrimage (Sahih Muslim 1218)?
optionsEn: Only for five minutes before noon
Only until ‘Asr adhan
From after praying Dhuhr and ‘Asr combined until the yellow disc of the sun had completely set below the horizon
Seated silently inside his tent all afternoon
explanationEn: He raised his hands to chest height like a humble beggar asking for food, pouring his heart out for his Ummah until sunset!

questionEn: What moving assurance did the Prophet ﷺ receive on Arafah and Muzdalifah when he begged Allah to forgive his Ummah's shortcomings (Sunan Ibn Majah 3013)?
optionsEn: Allah forgave sins between Himself and His servants—and at Muzdalifah, promised even to compensate oppressed claimants from His own bounty so believers are pardoned!
Nobody's wrongs were pardoned
Only scholars received forgiveness
Forgiveness was withheld until next year
explanationEn: Even the Prophet's ﷺ own tears at Arafah were spent praying for YOU and his entire Ummah.

questionEn: At Muzdalifah (Al-Mash‘ar al-Haram) on the morning of Eid (10th Dhul-Hijjah), when and how did the Prophet ﷺ engage in dua (Sahih Muslim 1218)?
optionsEn: He slept until midday
He faced west without raising his hands
Right after praying Fajr at its earliest light, he stood facing the Qiblah making dua, Takbir, Tahlil, and declaring Allah's Oneness until the sky grew very bright before sunrise
He left immediately before Fajr without praying
explanationEn: Fulfilling Surah Al-Baqarah 2:198 ('Remember Allah at Al-Mash‘ar al-Haram'), that quiet Fajr-to-sunrise hour in Muzdalifah is deeply serene.

questionEn: During the Days of Tashriq at Mina when stoning the three Jamarat, after which pillars did the Prophet ﷺ pause, face the Qiblah, raise his hands, and make lengthy dua (Sahih al-Bukhari 1753)?
optionsEn: After the FIRST (al-Sughra) and SECOND (al-Wusta) Jamarah—as long as reading Surah Al-Baqarah—while walking directly away without stopping after the THIRD (Jamrat al-‘Aqabah)
Only at midnight after all three
Only after Jamrat al-‘Aqabah
Before throwing any pebbles at all
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ exact pauses at the first and second Jamarah leaves space for long, peaceful dua during Mina's busy days.

questionEn: What short phrase is spoken aloud with each individual pebble thrown at the Jamarat (Sahih al-Bukhari 1753)?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka
Labbayk
SubhanakAllahumma
Allahu Akbar
explanationEn: Throwing small pebbles gently while saying 'Allahu Akbar' symbolizes rejecting Shaytan's temptations and obeying Allah calmly—never throwing shoes or anger!

questionEn: What heartfelt dua did Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) regularly recite whenever drinking sacred Zamzam water (Ad-Daraqutni / Athar)?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Allahumma inni as'aluka ‘ilman nafi‘an, wa rizqan wasi‘an, wa shifa'an min kulli da' ('O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and healing from every illness')
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Coupled with the Hadith 'Zamzam is for whatever purpose it is drunk for' (Ibn Majah 3062), this supplication asks for mind, livelihood, and body together.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah 3062 / Athar of Ibn ‘Abbas

questionEn: What dua did the Prophet ﷺ recite when slaughtering his sacrificial animal (Hady / Udhiyah) at Mina during Hajj or Eid al-Adha (Sahih Muslim 1967)?
optionsEn: Bismillahi wallahu Akbar, Allahumma minka wa laka, Allahumma taqabbal minni (or from Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and his Ummah)
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Saying 'Bismillahi wallahu Akbar' shows mercy and reverence for life while seeking Allah's acceptance.

questionEn: When visiting Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah and standing respectfully before the grave of the Prophet ﷺ, what greeting did companions like Ibn ‘Umar (RA) offer?
optionsEn: Shouting loudly and clinging to iron grilles
Skipping the mosque greeting two-rak‘ah prayer
Turning toward the grave to beg worldly favors directly from the Prophet ﷺ
As-salamu ‘alayka ya RasulAllah (or ayyuhan-Nabiyyu wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh), followed by concise salam upon Abu Bakr (RA) and ‘Umar (RA)
explanationEn: Remember: when making personal dua for yourself in Madinah, turn toward the Qiblah and ask Allah alone—honoring pure Tawhid.
reference: Muwatta Imam Malik / Sunan al-Bayhaqi / Adab al-Ziyarah

questionEn: Upon returning from Hajj or Umrah and approaching one's home city, what short three-part praise did Anas (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ recited when Madinah came into view (Sahih al-Bukhari 1797)?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Ghufranaka
Allahu Akbar (3x), La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah... Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, ‘abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun; sadaqAllahu wa‘dah, wa nasara ‘abdah, wa hazamal-ahzaba wahdah
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Greeting home with joyful Takbir, repentance, and praise turns homecoming itself into worship.

questionEn: What ten-word dua spoken upon stepping out of one's house brings the angelic announcement: 'You have been guided, sufficed, and protected' (Sunan Abi Dawud 5095)?
optionsEn: SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Bismillahi tawakkaltu ‘alallah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
explanationEn: Immediately upon saying this at your doorstep, Satan steps aside saying to another devil: 'How can you get to a person already guided, sufficed, and protected?'

questionEn: Which additional stepping-out-of-home dua did Umm Salamah (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ NEVER left his house without looking skyward and saying (Abu Dawud 5094 / Tirmidhi 3427)?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika an adilla aw udall, aw azilla aw uzall, aw azlima aw uzlam, aw ajhala aw yujhala ‘alayya
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Allahumma hab li mulkan ‘azima
explanationEn: Seeking protection equally from misleading OR being misled, slipping OR being tripped, wronging OR being wronged, and acting ignorantly OR being treated ignorantly sets the gold standard of public ethics.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 2018, what happens when a person enters their home and mentions Allah's Name both when entering AND when eating?
optionsEn: Guests stop arriving at that house
Lamps burn twice as fast
Meals lose flavor until morning
Satan tells his companions: 'You have no place to spend the night here and no dinner!'
explanationEn: Mentioning Allah at the front door ('Bismillahi walajna...') and at the dining table locks Shaytan out of the home's peace.

questionEn: What full wording did Sunan Abi Dawud 5096 preserve for entering one's home before greeting family with Salam?
optionsEn: Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Allahumma inni as'aluka khayral-mawlaji wa khayral-makhraj; bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna, wa ‘ala Rabbina tawakkalna
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Asking for the goodness of both entering and exiting turns daily thresholds into portals of blessing.

questionEn: When walking on foot or commuting to the Mosque for prayer, what luminous dua did the Prophet ﷺ recite asking for light across every sense (Sahih Muslim 763)?
optionsEn: Allahummaj‘al fi qalbi nura, wa fi lisani nura, waj‘al fi sam‘i nura, waj‘al fi basari nura, waj‘al min khalfi nura wa min amami nura, waj‘al min fawqi nura wa min tahti nura; Allahumma a‘tini nura
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
explanationEn: Walking to Salah asking for inner and outer light prepares the mind for Khushu‘ before even stepping inside.

questionEn: Why is it Sunnah to enter a mosque with the right foot saying 'Allahumma-ftah li abwaba rahmatik' and exit with the left foot saying 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik'?
optionsEn: Honoring the masjid as a house of Allah's Mercy (Rahmah) upon entry, and seeking Allah's lawful Bounty (Fadl) as we return to work, study, and daily livelihood
Because exiting prayers prohibit making dua
Because mercy exists only inside stone buildings
Because right foot entry replaces Wudu
explanationEn: Notice how Surah Al-Jumu‘ah 62:10 similarly uses 'Fadl' ('seek from Allah's bounty') for livelihood right after finishing Friday prayer!

questionEn: What short addition did Sunan Abi Dawud 466 record the Prophet ﷺ said at the mosque entrance to shield himself from Shaytan?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
A‘udhu billahil-‘Azim, wa bi-wajhihil-Karim, wa sultanihil-Qadim, minash-Shaytanir-rajim
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Upon hearing that refuge, Satan cries: 'He has been protected from me for the rest of the day!'

questionEn: What short dua is whispered BEFORE entering the restroom—starting with 'Bismillah' (per ‘Ali RA, Tirmidhi 606) and continuing in Bukhari 142?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka Rabbana
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Bismillah — Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith ('O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female foul devils/impurities')
explanationEn: Stepping in with the left foot after saying this outside the door guards modesty and spiritual cleanliness.

questionEn: Upon stepping OUT of the restroom with the right foot, what single Arabic word of humility did the Prophet ﷺ utter (Sunan Abi Dawud 30 / Tirmidhi 7)?
optionsEn: Amin
Ghufranaka ('I seek Your forgiveness')
MashaAllah
Labbayk
explanationEn: Scholars beautifully note two reasons for 'Ghufranaka': thanking Allah for relieving bodily harm safely while apologizing for pausing verbal dhikr briefly—or recognizing our shortfall in thanking Him for effortless digestion!

questionEn: What single phrase opens ablution (Wudu) according to Sunan Abi Dawud 101 and Tirmidhi 25?
optionsEn: Alhamdulillah only
Allahu Akbar
Bismillah ('In the Name of Allah')
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Saying 'Bismillah' before washing turns a routine wash into an act of sacred purification.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 234, what extraordinary reward awaits anyone who performs Wudu thoroughly and then looks up/recites the Shahadah after Wudu?
optionsEn: All eight gates of Paradise are opened for him so he may enter through whichever one he wishes
His next fast is shortened by two hours
He never needs to renew Wudu again
He earns reward only on Fridays
explanationEn: Saying 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasuluh' right after Wudu takes five seconds and opens all eight gates of Jannah!

questionEn: What extra phrase does Sunan al-Tirmidhi 55 add immediately after the Shahadah upon completing Wudu?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Allahummaj‘alni minat-tawwabin waj‘alni minal-mutatahhirin ('O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent and make me among those who purify themselves')
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Water washes outward dust during Wudu, while this dua asks Allah to wash inward sin through repentance (tawbah).

questionEn: What third post-Wudu supplication in Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra 9918 resembles Kaffarat al-Majlis?
optionsEn: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa Anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
explanationEn: Sealing Wudu with praise and Istighfar prepares the heart cleanly before standing in Salah.

questionEn: When hearing the Mu'adhdhin call the Adhan, how should the listener respond to every phrase—except 'Hayya ‘alas-Salah' and 'Hayya ‘alal-Falah'?
optionsEn: Remain completely silent until Iqamah
Repeat the exact words spoken by the Mu'adhdhin, and reply 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' to 'Hayya ‘alas-Salah' and 'Hayya ‘alal-Falah'
Say 'SubhanAllah' instead of Allahu Akbar
Say 'Amin' after every single line
explanationEn: Saying 'There is no might nor power except with Allah' when called to prayer and success admits we need Allah's strength just to stand up and pray!

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 386, what short testimony of faith and satisfaction did the Prophet ﷺ teach saying right after the Mu'adhdhin finishes the Shahadatayn ('Ashhadu an la ilaha illAllah...')—promising forgiveness of sins?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Wa ana ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah wa anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasuluh; raditu billahi Rabban wa bi-Muhammadin rasulan wa bil-Islami dina
explanationEn: Repeating this silently right as the Adhan ends washes away past sins and anchors faith five times a day.

questionEn: What two steps immediately follow answering the Adhan according to Sahih Muslim 384 and Sahih al-Bukhari 614 to attain the Prophet's ﷺ intercession?
optionsEn: Wait until after Salah finishes before sending Salawat
First send Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ, then recite 'Allahumma Rabba hadhihid-da‘watit-tammah was-salatil-qa'imah, ati Muhammadanil-wasilata wal-fadilah wab‘athhu maqaman mahmuda alladhi wa‘adtah'
Stand up immediately without sitting
Clap hands and turn toward the west
explanationEn: Saying this dua five times a day secures the Prophet's ﷺ promised Shafa‘ah on the Day of Resurrection.

questionEn: In the post-Adhan dua (Bukhari 614), what is 'Al-Wasilah' that we ask Allah to grant Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: A stone fortress in Madinah
The highest, unique station in Paradise reserved for only one servant of Allah—which the Prophet ﷺ hoped to be
A seasonal caravan route
A silver key to the Kaaba
explanationEn: Every time we pray for Al-Wasilah for the Prophet ﷺ after the Adhan, we honor his love and earn his intercession.

questionEn: What daily dua spoken while putting on everyday clothes asks Allah to forgive past and future sins (or thanks Him for clothing without our own might)?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Alhamdulillahilladhi kasani hadha [ath-thawb] wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Reciting this while getting dressed—as taught in Sunan Abi Dawud 4023—wins forgiveness for past sins while thanking Allah for warmth and dignity.

questionEn: When putting on a brand-new garment (such as Eid clothes or fresh Ihram), what specific dua did the Prophet ﷺ say (Abu Dawud 4020 / Tirmidhi 1767)?
