optionsEn: Allahumma lakal-hamd, Anta kasawtanih, as'aluka min khayrihi wa khayri ma suni‘a lah, wa a‘udhu bika min sharrihi wa sharri ma suni‘a lah
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
explanationEn: Thanking Allah directly ('Anta kasawtanih') and asking for the garment's good purpose turns new clothing into gratitude rather than vanity.

questionEn: What warm, heartfelt dua did the Prophet ﷺ say to Umm Khalid (RA) or to Ibn ‘Umar (RA) when seeing a friend or child wearing new clothes?
optionsEn: Never wash it in summer
Hide it before neighbors see it
Sell it immediately for coins
Tubli wa yukhlifullahu ta‘ala ('Wear it out and may Allah replace it with something better')—or 'Ilbas jadidan wa ‘ish hamidan wa mut shahidan' ('Wear new, live praiseworthily, and die as a martyr')
explanationEn: Complimenting someone's new outfit with a sincere dua spreads affection instead of envy.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 4020 / Sunan Ibn Majah 3558

questionEn: What single word spoken before taking off clothes shields a believer's privacy from the eyes of jinn according to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 606?
optionsEn: Amin
Bismillah
Ghufranaka
SubhanAllah
explanationEn: Saying 'Bismillah' when undressing creates an unseen screen (sitr) protecting human dignity.

questionEn: When entering a busy shopping mall, souq, or marketplace, what weighty dhikr taught in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3428 earns immense reward—one million good deeds written, one million misdeeds erased, and raised a million degrees?
optionsEn: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu yuhyi wa yumitu wa Huwa Hayyun la yamutu bi-yadihil-khayru wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Ghufranaka
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
explanationEn: Remembering the Ever-Living who never dies ('Hayyun la yamut') right amidst noisy commerce keeps materialism from stealing the heart.

questionEn: Why does the Marketplace Dua uniquely emphasize 'yuhyi wa yumitu wa Huwa Hayyun la yamut' ('He gives life and causes death, and He is Ever-Living and never dies')?
optionsEn: Because fasting is forbidden in markets
Because markets only open at night
Because marketplaces often tempt people into heedlessness and chasing fleeting wealth; remembering Allah's eternal life puts earthly buying and selling in humble perspective
Because merchants cannot say SubhanAllah
explanationEn: Bringing dhikr into commercial spaces turns errands into acts of remembrance.

questionEn: When looking in a mirror before leaving home, what gentle Prophetic dua connects outward grooming to inner ethics (Musnad Ahmad 3823)?
optionsEn: Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Allahumma kama hassanta khalqi fa-hassin khuluqi ('O Allah, just as You made my physical form handsome/good, make my character good')
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: A quick reflection in the mirror reminds us that noble character matters even more than neat clothing.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ say whenever mounting an animal or starting a journey, right after sitting squarely in the saddle (Sahih Muslim 1342)?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka
Allahumma innaka ‘afuwwun
Alhamdulillah (or Allahu Akbar 3x), Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
explanationEn: Even before saying the travel petitions, recognizing 'we could never have subdued this ourselves' credits Allah for every modern vehicle and aircraft.

questionEn: What extra line in the Travel Dua expresses humble confession before setting out on a trip?
optionsEn: Angels owe me smooth weather
Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li, fa-innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Anta
I am completely free of fault on this road
Other travelers are less worthy
explanationEn: Narrated by ‘Ali (RA), the Prophet ﷺ laughed joyfully seeing a rider add this brief plea for forgiveness as he set off!

questionEn: When traveling with a group, why did the Prophet ﷺ warn against letting a lone person travel needlessly across desolate terrain—and what Sunnah did he urge for travelers?
optionsEn: He urged traveling in righteous companionship (appointing a leader/amir if three or more) and making collective dua for one another's safety
He ordered every traveler to walk miles apart silently
He banned praying congregationally on trips
He forbade travelers from sharing water
explanationEn: Righteous companionship on Umrah, Hajj, or work trips keeps dhikr, kindness, and safety alive.

questionEn: When riding a ship or crossing turbulent waters—like Prophet Nuh (AS) or sea pilgrims—what Qur'anic embarkation phrase does Surah Hud (11:41) teach?
optionsEn: Rabbi hab li mulkan la yanbaghi li-ahad
Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Bismillahi majriha wa mursaha, inna Rabbi la-Ghafurun Rahim ('In the Name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring; indeed my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful')
explanationEn: Starting any sea voyage or flight with Allah's Name over both departure ('majriha') and landing ('mursaha') puts both takeoff and touchdown in His care.

questionEn: When a pilgrim enters Makkah's Sacred Sanctuary (Haram) boundary, what mindset and dua honor the city's sanctity?
optionsEn: Rushing straight to shopping before Umrah
Ignoring the boundaries of the Haram
Entering with humility, awe, and Talbiyah or personal dua, honoring Allah's decree making Makkah a sanctuary where blood is never shed, game is not hunted, and plants are not cut
Arguing over hotel rooms while shouting
explanationEn: Recalling Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) prayer 'Rabbij‘al hadhal-balada aminan' deepens reverence with every step inside Makkah.

questionEn: What warm hospitality gesture did the Prophet ﷺ practice when returning pilgrims, travelers, or delegates arrived safely in Madinah?
optionsEn: Charging an entry fee at the city gate
Ignoring travelers for three days
Asking only about market prices
Receiving them warmly with salam, embraces, and making dua for their acceptance and forgiveness (such as 'QabilAllahu hajjaka' or welcoming prayers)
explanationEn: Celebrating returning pilgrims and asking them for dua—since a sincere pilgrim's heart returns purified—strengthens community love.

questionEn: What dua did the Prophet ﷺ make for Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) or returning travelers, and why did ‘Umar (RA) ask pilgrims for dua?
optionsEn: Because travelers lose their ability to pray at home
Because duas at home are never answered
Because only residents of Makkah can make dua
Because a pilgrim returning from Hajj with accepted worship is like a newborn free of sin, so asking them to make dua for you shares in that spiritual purity
explanationEn: Narrated in Musnad Ahmad 5370, asking a returning Hajji to pray for your forgiveness before they even enter their house is a beloved Sunnah warmth.

questionEn: During Hajj or Umrah, when is it Sunnah to stop reciting the Talbiyah in Umrah versus in Hajj?
optionsEn: Continue Talbiyah for forty days after returning home
Stop immediately upon passing the airport gate
In Umrah, stop reciting Talbiyah upon beginning Tawaf (touching/facing the Black Stone); in Hajj, stop upon throwing the first pebble at Jamrat al-‘Aqabah on Eid morning (10th Dhul-Hijjah)
Never recite Talbiyah after putting on Ihram
explanationEn: Knowing when Talbiyah transitions smoothly into Tawaf Takbir or Eid Takbir keeps pilgrimage worship crisp and Sunnah-aligned.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when putting his foot into the stirrup or starting his mount in Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah regarding avoiding show-off pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Record my name on every pillar
Allahumma hajjatan la riya'a fiha wa la sum‘ah ('O Allah, make it a Hajj with neither showing off nor seeking reputation')
Make everyone praise my generosity
Keep my journey luxurious above all
explanationEn: Reported in Sunan Ibn Majah 2890 (with supporting athar of Anas RA), guarding Hajj and Umrah from riya' protects its reward completely.

questionEn: During Tawaf, what did the Prophet ﷺ ask pilgrims NOT to do with the corners of the Kaaba besides the Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani?
optionsEn: He ordered pilgrims to climb onto the Kaaba roof

He touched/kissed the Black Stone and touched Rukn al-Yamani, and did NOT touch the other two Syrian/Iraqi corners (as they do not sit on the full original Ibrahimic foundations), showing that even devotion follows Sunnah knowledge
He banned facing the Kaaba in prayer
He forbade touching Rukn al-Yamani as well
explanationEn: Walking around the Kaaba praying sincerely while respecting Prophetic boundaries keeps love married to knowledge.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the virtue of touching the Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani humbly during Tawaf (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 959)?
optionsEn: They replace obligatory Zakah
They must be touched only at midnight
They grant magical immunity without repentance
Touching them both removes/expiates sins (yahuttul-khataya)
explanationEn: Touching them gently if uncrowded—or pointing cleanly to the Black Stone when crowded—connects spiritual awe to forgiveness.

questionEn: Why is it forbidden in Islam to touch the Kaaba walls, Kiswah cloth, or Maqam Ibrahim seeking independent magical blessings (tabarruk) outside Sunnah guidance?
optionsEn: Because blessing belongs solely to Allah and follows what the Prophet ﷺ actually practiced—pointing to the Black Stone, touching Rukn al-Yamani, praying behind Maqam Ibrahim, and pouring our hearts into dua to Allah alone
Because silk cloth is impure
Because praying near the Kaaba is discouraged
Because nobody may look at Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: Pure Tawhid means loving the Sacred House deeply while asking Allah—not stone or fabric—to bless and heal us.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1597 (‘Umar's statement at the Black Stone)

questionEn: What famous words did ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) speak aloud while kissing the Black Stone, clarifying Tawhid forever?
optionsEn: Every wish whispered to stones comes true by magic
By Allah, I know you are only a stone that can neither harm nor benefit; had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would never have kissed you
You grant answers independently of Allah
Only kings may kiss the corner
explanationEn: ‘Umar's (RA) lucid declaration ensures every pilgrim honors the Sunnah without ever drifting into superstition.

questionEn: What specific dua is recited when passing through the Hijr Isma‘il (al-Hatim) area for voluntary prayer inside the Kaaba's semi-circular wall?
optionsEn: Only men over forty may pray inside
You must pray seven consecutive rak‘ahs
There is no rigid scripted dua—pray two voluntary rak‘ahs quietly inside (since part of it lies within the original Kaaba foundations) and make any heartfelt personal dua to Allah!
You must recite a 12-verse poem backward
explanationEn: Praying inside Hijr Isma‘il offers the immense joy of praying inside the original Kaaba perimeter.

questionEn: When walking through crowded corridors of Makkah and Madinah, what daily dua and etiquette protects a pilgrim's spiritual reward?
optionsEn: Shouting angrily at slower walkers
Ignoring lost elderly pilgrims
Patience, lowered gaze, gentle speech ('Peace!'), smiling, giving space to elders/wheelchairs, and remembering 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah'
Elbowing through rows to get one meter closer
explanationEn: Protecting fellow pilgrims from harm in a crowd is part of honoring Allah's sanctuary.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ say when descending at a stop along a journey in darkness or approaching nightfall?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Ya ardu Rabbi wa Rabbukillah, a‘udhu billahi min sharriki wa sharri ma fiki wa sharri ma khuliqa fiki wa sharri ma yadibbu ‘alayki...
explanationEn: Recorded in Sunan Abi Dawud 2603, this gentle dua reminds travelers arriving at unfamiliar terrain at night that Allah is Lord of both traveler and land.

questionEn: If a traveler loses an item, misses a connection, or gets confused on an unfamiliar road, what timeless Quranic/Sunnah anchor steadies the heart?
optionsEn: Say 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un' or 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah', recite Musa's dua '‘Asa Rabbi an yahdiyani sawa'as-sabil', and ask Allah calmly for ease ('Allahumma la sahla illa ma ja‘altahu sahla')
Give up Salah for the day
Panic loudly in the terminal
Curse the airport staff immediately
explanationEn: Saying 'Allahumma la sahla illa ma ja‘altahu sahla, wa Anta taj‘alul-hazna idha shi'ta sahla' ('O Allah, there is no ease except what You make easy, and You make difficulty easy whenever You will') brings instant calm.

questionEn: Who narrated the beloved ease dua 'Allahumma la sahla illa ma ja‘altahu sahla, wa Anta taj‘alul-hazna idha shi'ta sahla'?
optionsEn: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)
Anas ibn Malik (RA) from the Prophet ﷺ
Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA)
Salman al-Farsi (RA)
explanationEn: Whether facing a tough exam, visa interview, flight delay, or childbirth, trusting Allah to soften rough terrain ('al-hazn') unlocks serenity.

questionEn: When seeing a fellow Muslim smilingly welcome or help you on your journey, what concise Prophetic thank-you dua returns the highest gratitude?
optionsEn: Thank you solely by luck
JazakAllahu khayran ('May Allah reward you with goodness')
No verbal thanks is needed
Wait until next year to reply
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever says 'JazakAllahu khayran' to someone who did them a kindness has given the ultimate praise!

questionEn: When walking into a Masjid while someone is already offering voluntary prayer or quiet dhikr, how should you enter and recite the masjid entry dua?
optionsEn: Step in with your right foot calmly, say the entry dua softly to yourself without disturbing worshippers, and pray two rak‘ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid before sitting
Sit down immediately without Tahiyyat al-Masjid
Greet everyone loudly across the prayer hall
Step over seated worshippers' shoulders
explanationEn: Keeping voices low inside mosques preserves tranquility for everyone praying or reading Qur'an.

questionEn: When leaving a masjid and hearing or seeing poor people or daily work awaiting outside, how does 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik' shape your attitude?
optionsEn: It permits dishonest trade after prayer
It separates spiritual life completely from work
It encourages ignoring people in need
It reminds you that ethical earnings, career provision, and generosity toward others are all forms of Allah's Bounty (Fadl) flowing straight out of Salah
explanationEn: Connecting Masjid worship to honest work via 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik' integrates faith into every hour.

questionEn: Why is sending peace and blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ ('Bismillahi was-salatu was-salamu ‘ala Rasulillah') included at the door of the Mosque?
optionsEn: Because only Madinah's mosque allows Salawat
Because Salawat replaces Salah itself
Because he built every modern brick building physically
Because every authentic mosque we enter stands upon his Sunnah legacy—so greeting him lovingly at the threshold prepares us to worship as he taught
explanationEn: Combining Bismillah, Salawat, and 'Allahumma-ftah li abwaba rahmatik' creates a seamless three-part mosque doorway ritual.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah 771 / Sunan Abi Dawud 465

questionEn: In the Adhan response, why did the Prophet ﷺ instruct us to say 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' specifically at 'Hayya ‘alas-Salah' and 'Hayya ‘alal-Falah' instead of repeating 'Come to prayer'?
optionsEn: Because angels repeat only the Takbir
Because repeating them cancels Wudu
Because those two phrases are too difficult to pronounce
Because 'Come to prayer, come to success' is the Mu'adhdhin's call to action—so the listener answers with humble dependence on Allah's power to rise and obey!
explanationEn: Saying 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' with sincere heart upon hearing the Adhan brings entry into Paradise according to Sahih Muslim 385.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 384, what does the Prophet ﷺ promise if a listener repeats the Adhan, sends Salawat on him, and asks Allah to grant him Al-Wasilah?
optionsEn: He will earn exemption from fasting
Hallat lahu shafa‘ati ('My intercession will become permissible/assured for him on the Day of Resurrection')
He will become wealthy before sunset
He will never need to pray Fajr
explanationEn: Five daily moments—each taking 20 seconds after the Adhan—anchor our eternal hope in the Prophet's ﷺ Shafa‘ah.

questionEn: What gentle reminder from Sahih Muslim 385 teaches us to keep our hearts open during the Adhan even if we are in the middle of work or conversation?
optionsEn: Mute every reminder of prayer
Talk louder over the Adhan to finish quickly
Pause briefly from idle talk to listen, respond word-for-word from the heart, send Salawat, and recite the post-Adhan dua—turning five interruptions into five sacred pauses
Respond only during Ramadan
explanationEn: Even a quiet pause of 30 seconds five times a day keeps the whole day tethered to eternity.

questionEn: What brief prayer is recommended when putting on shoes or preparing to step out, recalling the Sunnah of putting on the right shoe first and taking off the left shoe first (Sahih al-Bukhari 5856)?
optionsEn: Walk around with only one shoe on
Begin with the right when putting on shoes (and saying Bismillah when starting tasks), and begin with the left when taking them off, keeping both tidy and clean
Always hop barefoot out the door
Put on the left shoe first out of haste
explanationEn: Honoring the right side in noble actions (shoes, garments, entering masjid, eating) while reserving the left for cleansing brings mindful grace to tiny habits.

questionEn: When walking along the street and noticing a harmful obstacle (like glass, a branch, or trash) in people's path, what does removing it have in common with dhikr?
optionsEn: It only counts if cameras record it
It replaces daily Salah
It only applies inside Makkah
Removing harm from the road is itself an act of Sadaqah and branch of Iman that earned one man Allah's forgiveness and Paradise
explanationEn: Serving fellow travelers and pedestrians pairs outward mercy with inward remembrance.

questionEn: What dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sunan Abi Dawud 4023 when someone puts on a garment—showing how deeply gratitude permeates ordinary mornings?
optionsEn: Look how expensive my tailor is
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Alhamdulillahilladhi kasani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah ('Praise be to Allah who clothed me with this and provided it for me with no might or power from me')
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Crediting Allah rather than just our paycheck even for the shirt on our back opens forgiveness for past sins.

questionEn: When visiting Madinah's Masjid Quba—the very first mosque founded on Taqwa—what immense worship reward awaits according to Sunan Ibn Majah 1412 & Nasa'i 699?
optionsEn: Performing Wudu at home/hotel and going out to Masjid Quba to pray two rak‘ahs (or any Salah) earns a reward equal to performing an Umrah
It counts only on Wednesdays
You must walk barefoot ten miles
It replaces the obligatory Hajj
explanationEn: Making Wudu calmly before setting out to Quba and praying there with sincere dua is one of Madinah's sweetest gifts.

questionEn: Inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah, what special sacred area between the Prophet's ﷺ home/grave and his Pulpit (Minbar) did he describe as 'a garden from the gardens of Paradise'?
optionsEn: Mount Uhud's foothills
Bab as-Salam courtyard outside
The southern date market
Ar-Rawdah ash-Sharifah ('Ma bayna bayti wa minbari rawdatun min riyadil-jannah')
explanationEn: When blessed with a turn inside the Rawdah, focus on calm two rak‘ahs and heartfelt dua rather than rushing for photos!

questionEn: When visiting the Baqi‘ cemetery in Madinah (Jannat al-Baqi‘) or any Muslim graveyard, what gentle greeting and dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sahih Muslim 975?
optionsEn: As-salamu ‘alaykum ahlad-diyari minal-mu'minina wal-muslimin, wa inna in sha'Allahu bikum lahiqun; nas'alullaha lana wa lakumul-‘afiyah
Ask the deceased directly to solve worldly debts
Scatter coins over gravestones
Wail loudly and tear clothing
explanationEn: Greeting the deceased with peace, recalling our shared journey to Allah, and asking Allah for ‘afiyah for them and ourselves reflects serene Sunnah dignity.

questionEn: What extra line appears in ‘A'ishah's (RA) narration of the cemetery visit dua in Sahih Muslim 974?
optionsEn: Forget all who passed before last year
Build marble domes over every grave
Visit cemeteries only at midnight
Wa yarhamullahul-mustaqdimina minna wal-musta'khirin ('And may Allah have mercy on those who went ahead of us and those who follow later')
explanationEn: Praying for Allah's mercy upon past and future generations binds the living and departed Ummah in love.

questionEn: When walking through the streets of Makkah toward Safa/Marwah or the Kaaba, why did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize keeping the tongue busy with Talbiyah, Takbir, or personal dua rather than idle chatter?
optionsEn: Because pilgrims may never smile
Because talking gently with family is forbidden
Because walking silently earns zero reward
Because every step toward the Sacred House—and every moment inside Ihram—is precious worship time not to be wasted on trivial disputes or gossip
explanationEn: Warm brotherhood combined with constant dhikr makes pilgrimage deeply restorative.

questionEn: What extraordinary promise did the Prophet ﷺ give for an Umrah followed by another Umrah, and for Hajj Mabrur?
optionsEn: Reward depends on hotel luxury
Hajj removes only minor slips in business
Only one Umrah in a lifetime brings reward
One Umrah to the next is expiation for sins committed in between; and Hajj Mabrur has no reward less than Paradise itself
explanationEn: Maintaining sincere dua, patience, and gentle kindness during Umrah and Hajj helps earn the honor of 'Mabrur' (accepted and blessed).

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ define 'Birr' (the goodness of Hajj Mabrur) in Musnad Ahmad 14482 when asked what makes a Hajj truly accepted?
optionsEn: Posting daily boastful updates
Shouting over others at the Black Stone
Buying the finest silk robes in Makkah
Feeding people (it‘amut-ta‘am) and speaking gentle, peaceful words (wa tibul-kalam / ifsha'us-salam)
explanationEn: Generosity with food and sweetness of speech turn an outward trip into a transformed character.

questionEn: When a pilgrim sees the Well of Zamzam or drinks from it inside Al-Masjid al-Haram, which Sunnah posture and etiquette did Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) observe from the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Avoiding dua while drinking
Gulping in one breathless rush without Bismillah
Pouring leftover Zamzam into drains

Saying 'Bismillah', drinking with the right hand (the Prophet ﷺ drank Zamzam standing near the well in Sahih al-Bukhari 1637, though sitting when uncrowded is general dining etiquette), pausing to breathe three times outside the cup, making sincere dua, and saying 'Alhamdulillah'
explanationEn: Drinking Zamzam slowly with gratitude and clear personal dua honors the miraculous spring sent for Hajar and Isma‘il (AS).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1637 / Sahih Muslim 2028 / Ibn Majah 3062

questionEn: When leaving Masjid al-Haram or Masjid an-Nabawi for the final time before flying home, what farewell attitude reflects the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Walk backward out of the mosque gates
Refuse to say goodbye in prayer

Make the farewell (Tawaf al-Wada‘ for Hajj; optional heartfelt prayer/salam before leaving Madinah), step out calmly with left foot saying 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik', and pray Allah accepts your visit and invites you back soon
Touch every pillar aggressively
explanationEn: There is no Sunnah basis for walking backward out of the mosque; walking calmly with a longing heart and sincere dua honors the Prophet's ﷺ way.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1755, who was granted a compassionate exemption from Tawaf al-Wada‘ (Farewell Tawaf) when leaving Makkah at the end of Hajj?
optionsEn: Young men wanting extra sleep
Scholars leaving early
Wealthy merchants hurrying home
Menstruating women (and women in postnatal bleeding), so they would not be delayed from their caravan or feel burdened
explanationEn: Remembering Allah's mercy even in pilgrimage rulings reassures women pilgrims that their Hajj remains 100% complete and accepted.

questionEn: If a woman enters menstruation during Umrah or Hajj, which acts of worship and dua remain completely open to her until she attains purity?
optionsEn: She cannot stand at Arafah
She must stop all dhikr, Talbiyah, and dua completely

ALL forms of dhikr, Talbiyah, personal dua, Qur'an reflection/remembrance, standing at Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina, Jamarat, and charitable service—everything except Salah and Tawaf around the Kaaba until pure!
She must leave Makkah immediately without completing Hajj
explanationEn: Knowing she can still pour out her heart in Talbiyah, Arafah dua, and Istighfar prevents unnecessary panic and sadness!

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach for a pilgrim offering his own Hajj or Umrah vs. on behalf of an elderly/deceased loved one?
optionsEn: Skipping Ihram altogether
Saying 'Labbayka ‘an [Name]' at the Miqat (per Sunan Abi Dawud 1811 when a companion made Hajj on behalf of Shubrumah), after having already performed one's own obligatory Hajj first
Substituting only on Thursdays
Charging triple fees without intention
explanationEn: Doing Umrah or Hajj Badal with sincere dua for an incapacitated parent or deceased loved one is a profound gift of loyalty.

questionEn: When starting a road trip or flight, why does the Prophet ﷺ pair 'wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun' ('and indeed, to our Lord we will surely return') inside the Travel Dua?
optionsEn: To predict exact arrival times
To replace seatbelts and travel planning
To discourage ever traveling abroad
To remind the traveler that every earthly trip—airport to airport, home to hotel—mirrors our greater soul-journey back to Allah
explanationEn: Keeping eternity quietly in view makes travelers gentler, more patient in queues, and more mindful of Salah on the road.

questionEn: What simple Sunnah keeps Salah punctual and calm during a long road trip or flight?
optionsEn: Refusing Allah's gift of Qasr out of misplaced guilt

Knowing the concessions of Qasr (shortening 4-rak‘ah prayers to 2) and Jam‘ (combining Dhuhr/‘Asr or Maghrib/‘Isha), making Wudu or Tayammum when needed, and praying on time facing Qiblah as best possible
Waiting three days to make up missed prayers
Skipping all prayers until arriving at the hotel
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ called Qasr 'a charity Allah gave you—so accept His charity!'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say if a traveler feels lonely or anxious in a strange city at night?
optionsEn: Avoid calling family back home
Skip evening prayers
Remember Allah's promise in the Travel Dua—'Antas-Sahibu fis-safar' ('You are the Companion on the journey')—and recite the evening adhkar and Ayat al-Kursi
Stay awake worrying in silence
explanationEn: You are never truly alone in any hotel room or terminal when Allah is your Travel Companion.

questionEn: What three travelers' duas are explicitly listed among those guaranteed never to be rejected?
optionsEn: Only prayers of wealthy merchants
The dua of the oppressed (al-mazlum), the dua of the traveler (al-musafir), and the dua of a parent for their child (da‘watul-walid ‘ala/li-waladih)
Only prayers written in gold ink
Only prayers shouted on mountains
explanationEn: Traveling itself softens the heart with humility and detachment from home comforts—turning every journey into a golden opportunity to pray for family and the Ummah!

questionEn: What caution does that same Hadith (Tirmidhi 1905 / Muslim 3009) imply about a parent's words when frustrated with their children?
optionsEn: Never invoke curses or harm against your children, yourself, or your wealth in anger—rather train your tongue to say 'May Allah guide/bless you' even when correcting them!
Always shout when tired
Never discipline or guide children at all
Refuse to make dua for children
explanationEn: Turning frustration into blessing ('Allahumma aslihhum wahdihim') protects children in case that moment coincides with an hour of acceptance.

questionEn: When stepping outside to start work or errands and seeing someone facing hardship or disability, what quiet compassionate dua taught in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3431 should be whispered to oneself (never loudly to embarrass them)?
optionsEn: Walk past without any gratitude
Boast of your own health publicly
Point and stare while speaking aloud
Alhamdulillahilladhi ‘afani mimmabtalaka bihi wa faddalani ‘ala kathirin mimman khalaqa tafdila
explanationEn: Saying this quietly within yourself protects the person's dignity while thanking Allah for soundness and protecting yourself from that affliction.

questionEn: What gentle dua does Hisn al-Muslim recommend when welcoming or thanking someone who opens their home or serves you on your journey?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lahum fima razaqtahum, waghfir lahum warhamhum ('O Allah, bless them in what You provided them, forgive them, and have mercy on them')
Complain about room temperature immediately
Leave silently without thanking the host
Critique the meal ingredients
explanationEn: Narrated in Sahih Muslim 2042, the Prophet ﷺ blessed his hosts with this warm prayer right after eating.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when climbing Mount Safa during the Conquest of Makkah vs. during Umrah, reminding pilgrims what Safa represents?
optionsEn: A royal fortress built by ancient kings
A market fair for silk traders
A lookout tower for sea captains
A site of Hajar's (AS) desperate yet faithful running in trust that Allah would not abandon her and baby Isma‘il (AS)—crowned by the miracle of Zamzam
explanationEn: Walking between Safa and Marwah connects modern pilgrims to a mother's heroic faith, hustle, and answered dua.

questionEn: When walking briskly (Raml) in the first three circuits of Tawaf al-Qudum/Umrah (for men, when safe and uncrowded), what spirit did that Sunnah commemorate?
optionsEn: Ignoring personal dua to sprint blindly
Showing cheerful spiritual vigor and strength—initially demonstrated at ‘Umrat al-Qada' when polytheists claimed fever had weakened the Muslims—while never pushing or harming others
Requiring elderly pilgrims to run
Racing other pilgrims competitively to finish in five minutes
explanationEn: Sunnah actions always flex with wisdom and mercy: when crowded, walking calmly with Khushu‘ is best.

questionEn: During the Farewell Pilgrimage at Arafah, when the Prophet's ﷺ camel's reins slipped from his hand while he was making dua, how did he retrieve them without breaking his posture of humility?
optionsEn: He shouted for ten companions to stop
He picked them up with one hand while keeping the other hand raised toward heaven in unbroken dua!
He dismounted and walked back to Mina
He stopped making dua for the rest of the day
explanationEn: Even a small practical moment did not interrupt his focused communion with Allah on the greatest day of the year.

questionEn: What concise phrase did the Prophet ﷺ remind pilgrims about the essence of Hajj itself in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 889?
optionsEn: Hajj is valid without attending Arafah
Al-Hajju ‘Arafah ('Hajj is Arafah')—highlighting that standing humbly before Allah in dua at Arafah is the irreplaceable heart of pilgrimage
Hajj is solely buying gifts in Makkah
Hajj is only staying inside hotels
explanationEn: Missing every other optional habit can be mended, but standing at Arafah in sincere dua is the beating heart of Hajj.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 1348, why does Allah boast to the angels about the pilgrims standing in the afternoon heat on the plains of Arafah?
optionsEn: Look at how fast they finish lunch
Look at how expensive their tents are
Look at their embroidered cloaks
Look at My servants who have come to Me disheveled and dusty from every deep valley; I call you to witness that I have forgiven them!
explanationEn: Knowing Allah delights in our dusty, humble, tearful presence on Arafah transforms fatigue into pure honor.

questionEn: What special status does the Day of Arafah hold even for Muslims back home who are NOT performing Hajj?
optionsEn: Fasting the Day of Arafah expiates the sins of the preceding year and the coming year (Sahih Muslim 1162), and making abundant dua and Takbir that afternoon joins the spiritual wave of the Ummah!
Muslims at home may not make dua on Arafah
Fasting Arafah is obligatory upon pilgrims too
Only Makkah residents fast on Arafah
explanationEn: Note the beautiful Sunnah symmetry: pilgrims do NOT fast at Arafah so they have energy for long dua, while non-pilgrims fast at home and share in the blessing!

questionEn: On the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah—leading up to Arafah and Eid al-Adha—what four phrases did the Prophet ﷺ specifically urge multiplying in Musnad Ahmad 5446?
optionsEn: Only poetry recitations
Tahlil (La ilaha illAllah), Takbir (Allahu Akbar), and Tahmid (Alhamdulillah)
Only silent fasting without speech
Only sleeping after Dhuhr
explanationEn: Filling the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah—whose good deeds are unmatched by any other days of the year (Bukhari 969)—with Takbir, Tahlil, and Tahmid fills streets and homes with joy.

questionEn: What wording of the Tashriq / Eid Takbirat did companions like Ibn Mas‘ud (RA) and Salman al-Farsi (RA) chant aloud on Eid and the Days of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka Rabbana
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illAllahu wallahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar wa lillahil-hamd
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Chanting these uplifting Takbirat openly on Eid mornings and after prayers from Fajr of Arafah through ‘Asr of the 13th Dhul-Hijjah unites the Ummah in praise.
reference: Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah / Fiqh of Eid

questionEn: When greeting fellow believers on Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha, what classic greeting of the Companions carries a warm dua for acceptance?
optionsEn: Enjoy the feast and forget prayer
TaqabbalAllahu minna wa minkum ('May Allah accept [good deeds] from us and from you')
Good luck in winter markets
Return straight to work silently
explanationEn: Reported from the Companions by Jubayr ibn Nufayr (Fath al-Bari), wishing each other acceptance keeps focus on Allah's pleasure.

questionEn: When stepping out of your home for Eid prayer (or Jumu‘ah), what small Sunnah adds joy to your steps?
optionsEn: Taking one route to the prayer ground and returning by a different route (Sahih al-Bukhari 986), while reciting Takbirat gently and greeting neighbors with Salam
Walking indoors with curtains closed
Refusing to greet anyone along the road
Skipping Eid prayer to sleep late
explanationEn: More streets, neighbors, and angels witness your footsteps of dhikr and cheerfulness!

questionEn: When preparing to enter a Masjid for Salah, what warning did the Prophet ﷺ give in Sahih Muslim 564 regarding strong raw onions or garlic right before coming to prayer?
optionsEn: Whoever has eaten raw garlic or onion should stay away from our mosque, for the angels are harmed by what harms the children of Adam
Never use clean scent before Jumu‘ah
Skip brushing teeth before Friday prayer
Eat raw garlic right on the prayer rug
explanationEn: Brushing with Siwak/toothpaste and wearing clean clothes honors fellow worshippers and the angels attending Salah.

questionEn: What gentle dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach when offering condolences or parting from someone embarking on a righteous path—or when passing by a mosque one loves?
optionsEn: Taking selfies instead of greeting Allah's house
Praying for Allah's mercy, peace, and steadfastness—just as Ibn ‘Umar (RA) prayed upon arriving at Masjid al-Haram and Masjid an-Nabawi with humility rather than haste
Rushing without pausing for two rak‘ahs
Ignoring elderly visitors at the entrance
explanationEn: Entering Allah's sanctuaries with a quiet heart and sincere dua preserves the sweetness of worship.

questionEn: When boarding a modern airplane toward Jeddah or Madinah, how can a pilgrim seamlessly combine the Prophetic Travel Dua with modern safety awareness?
optionsEn: Skip the Travel Dua because planes did not exist in 632 CE
Make dua only after landing

Fasten your seatbelt calmly, listen respectfully to crew instructions, say 'Allahu Akbar' 3x, recite 'Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha...' and ask Allah for birr, taqwa, ease, and family protection back home
Stand in the aisle refusing crew directions
explanationEn: Notice how Qur'an 43:13 ('He who subjected this for us') applies even more marvelously to modern aviation!

questionEn: What concise Prophetic protection dua combined with Prophet Nuh's (AS) landing prayer is ideal when checking into a hotel room in Makkah or Madinah?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka while unpacking
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya at noon
A‘udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq (Sahih Muslim 2708), alongside Prophet Nuh's landing prayer 'Rabbi anzilni munzalan mubarakan wa Anta khayrul-munzilin' (23:29)
Complain immediately about elevator wait times
explanationEn: Blending Sunnah stopover protection with Qur'anic landing blessing invites serenity into every room you stay in.

questionEn: When seeing a breathtaking view—such as the Kaaba lit at night or the Green Dome in Madinah—what two words express joyful awe rooted in Allah's power (Surah Al-Kahf 18:39)?
optionsEn: Amazing coincidence without a Creator
Purely human luck alone
Silence without gratitude
Ma sha'Allahu la quwwata illa billah (or SubhanAllah / TabarakAllah)
explanationEn: Returning all beauty back to Allah's Will and Power guards the heart from forgetfulness and envy.

questionEn: Why is keeping a personal dua list before traveling for Umrah or Hajj—collecting requests from parents, friends, sick neighbors, and struggling believers—a beloved Sunnah-inspired habit?
optionsEn: Because personal needs cannot be prayed for at the Kaaba
Because praying for others in their absence earns the angel's immediate reply 'Amin, and for you the like thereof!' (Sahih Muslim 2733), multiplying your pilgrimage blessings
Because only written paper counts in Tawaf
Because friends cannot pray for themselves
explanationEn: Carrying loved ones' names in your heart during Tawaf, Sa‘i, and Arafah turns your pilgrimage into mercy for an entire community.

questionEn: What short, joyful dua did the Prophet ﷺ say whenever a fellow Muslim cheerfully greeted him or shared good news during travel?
optionsEn: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
Allahu Akbar / Alhamdulillahilladhi bi-ni‘matihi tatimmus-salihat ('Praise be to Allah by whose favor good deeds are completed/perfected')
Ghufranaka
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Seeing good news—like an approved visa, safe flight, or completed Umrah—invites immediate 'Alhamdulillahilladhi bi-ni‘matihi tatimmus-salihat'!

questionEn: In Sunan Ibn Majah 3803, what contrasting phrase did the Prophet ﷺ say when encountering difficult or unpleasant news instead of good news?
optionsEn: Praise belongs only to sunny days
Stop making dua until ease returns
Why does bad luck always follow me?
Alhamdulillahi ‘ala kulli hal ('Praise be to Allah in every condition/circumstance')
explanationEn: Praising Allah both when things go smoothly ('bi-ni‘matihi tatimmus-salihat') and when plans hit delays (‘ala kulli hal) anchors unshakeable gratitude.

questionEn: When wrapping up your stay in Makkah or Madinah and boarding the flight home, what closing reflection turns the end of pilgrimage into lifelong transformation?
optionsEn: Treating pilgrimage as a temporary holiday after which prayer slows down
Boasting endlessly of how many Umrahs you performed
Forgetting neighbors once home
Reciting the Return Travel Dua ('Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, ‘abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun') and asking Allah for steadfastness (istiqamah) upon daily Salah, adhkar, and kindness back home
explanationEn: Scholars say the clearest sign of an accepted Hajj or Umrah is returning gentler, humbler, and steadier in worship than before you left.

questionEn: When entering or exiting any Masjid—whether local neighborhood prayer room or Al-Masjid al-Haram—how long does it take to practice the full Sunnah doorway etiquette?
optionsEn: Only after reciting a full juz
Ten full minutes of silent waiting
Twenty minutes of standing at the gate
Less than ten seconds: right foot in with 'Bismillahi was-salatu was-salamu ‘ala Rasulillah, Allahumma-ftah li abwaba rahmatik'; left foot out with 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik'
explanationEn: Tiny ten-second Sunnah habits practiced five times a day build an extraordinary life of mindfulness.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach about the person whose heart is attached to the mosques (qalbuhu mu‘allaqun bil-masajid)?
optionsEn: He is among the seven categories whom Allah will shade in His Shade on the Day when there is no shade except His
He must sleep inside the masjid every night
He cannot hold a daily job
He must never travel abroad
explanationEn: Loving the masjid—entering with Rahmah duas, praying calmly, and exiting with Fadl duas—keeps our hearts tethered to Allah's house even during busy workdays.

questionEn: What hospitality from Allah awaits a believer every single time he sets out to the Masjid morning or evening?
optionsEn: Every time he goes to the mosque in the morning or evening, Allah prepares for him a welcoming feast (nuzul) in Paradise for every trip!
Only elderly walkers receive reward
Only trips inside Madinah count
Only Friday trips count
explanationEn: Combining that joyful walk with 'Allahummaj‘al fi qalbi nura...' makes every trip to Salah feel like stepping toward Paradise.

questionEn: What short dua is recommended upon putting on Ihram sandals or walking long distances between Mina, Arafah, and Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Complaining loudly about blistered feet
Racing ahead leaving elderly family behind
Skipping Wudu due to walking
Saying 'Bismillah', remembering 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' when fatigued, and sending abundant Salawat and Talbiyah while helping slower companions
explanationEn: Remembering 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah'—a treasure of Paradise—renews physical and spiritual stamina during pilgrimage walks.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ explain about the purpose of Tawaf around the House, walking between Safa and Marwah, and stoning the Jamarat?
optionsEn: To compete in fast sprinting
To follow tribal ancestry customs
Innama ju‘ila at-tawafu bil-Bayti wa baynas-Safa wal-Marwati wa ramyul-jimar li-iqamati dhikrillah ('They were instituted solely to establish the remembrance of Allah!')
Merely to exercise leg muscles in summer
explanationEn: Never lose sight of the core goal: every single pilgrimage ritual exists to awaken living dhikr and heartfelt dua!

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when climbing onto his camel at the beginning of a military or peaceful travel expedition regarding protection from sudden betrayal or loss?
optionsEn: He forbade travelers from carrying water
He left camp completely unguarded
He invoked 'Antas-Sahibu fis-safar wal-Khalifatu fil-ahl', entrusted his companions to Allah, and stayed vigilant in both prayer and practical security
He refused to consult maps or guides
explanationEn: Prophetic travel always balances deep spiritual dua with smart practical planning.

questionEn: What brief prayer can a traveler recite when boarding a train, bus, or ride-share daily commute—not only international flights?
optionsEn: Bismillah, followed by 'Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun'
Only for journeys over 500 miles
Only when riding camels
Only once a year in Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: Turning every morning commute or taxi ride into a brief moment of Qur'anic gratitude keeps dhikr woven into modern city life.

questionEn: What warm etiquette did the Prophet ﷺ advise if a traveler meets another brother or sister along the road during pilgrimage or daily life?
optionsEn: Speak harshly if crowded
Spread Salam warmly ('As-salamu ‘alaykum'), smile—for smiling at your sibling is charity—and offer a brief prayer for ease on their journey
Greet only people speaking your exact dialect
Avoid eye contact with fellow Muslims
explanationEn: Warm Salam is literally a daily dua for peace, mercy, and blessings upon one another.

questionEn: When concluding Wudu and preparing to step onto the prayer mat for Salah, what gentle reflection links Wudu's 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illAllah...' to standing before Allah?
optionsEn: Salah needs no presence of heart once hands are wet
Just as water washed outward limbs clean, renewing the Shahadah and asking to be among 'at-tawwabin wal-mutatahhirin' washes the heart clean to converse intimately with Allah in Salah
Wudu is purely mechanical hygiene without spiritual meaning
Only scholars recite the post-Wudu Shahadah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that sin falls away with every drop of Wudu water—leaving the believer fresh for heartfelt dua.

questionEn: What short phrase should a Muslim say before eating or drinking—and what should they say if they forget at the start and remember halfway through the meal?
optionsEn: Throw away the rest of the plate
Say 'Bismillah' before starting; if forgotten, say 'Bismillahi fi awwalihi wa akhirih' ('In the Name of Allah at its beginning and its end')
Repeat Bismillah forty times after dessert
Wait until dinner to say Bismillah twice
explanationEn: Saying 'Bismillahi fi awwalihi wa akhirih' caused Satan—who had been sharing the unblessed meal—to vomit everything up, as narrated by ‘A'ishah (RA).

questionEn: What post-meal dua taught in Sunan Abi Dawud 4023 and Tirmidhi 3458 brings forgiveness for past sins right after finishing food?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Alhamdulillahilladhi at‘amani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah
explanationEn: Confessing that even our daily meal came 'without any might or power from us' turns lunch or dinner into gratitude and pardon.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 5458, what rich expression of praise did the Prophet ﷺ say when the dining mat was lifted after eating?
optionsEn: Alhamdulillahi hamdan kathiran tayyiban mubarakan fih, ghayra makfiyyin wa la muwadda‘in wa la mustaghnan ‘anhu Rabbana
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
explanationEn: Meaning: abundant, pure, blessed praise—never feeling we have thanked Him enough, never taking leave of His bounty, and never independent of our Lord!

questionEn: When served milk specifically—compared to any other food—what subtle wording difference did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sunan Abi Dawud 3730 & Tirmidhi 3455?
optionsEn: For general food say 'Allahumma barik lana fihi wa at‘imna khayran minh'; for milk say 'Allahumma barik lana fihi wa zidna minh' ('...and increase us in it'), because nothing substitutes for milk as both food and drink
For fruit say 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un'
For milk say 'Ghufranaka' and skip Bismillah
Never make dua when drinking milk
explanationEn: That affectionate distinction shows the Prophet's ﷺ keen appreciation for Allah's nourishing provisions.

questionEn: After eating at a friend's house or welcoming banquet, what loving prayer did the Prophet ﷺ make for his hosts (Sahih Muslim 2042)?
optionsEn: Keep all guests away from their door
Excuse them from fasting Ramadan
Allahumma barik lahum fima razaqtahum, waghfir lahum warhamhum ('O Allah, bless them in what You provided them, forgive them, and have mercy on them')
Make sure they serve sweeter dates next time
explanationEn: Praying for blessing, forgiveness, and mercy upon those who cook for or feed you spreads barakah in their kitchen and home.

questionEn: What special prayer did the Prophet ﷺ make when someone gave him a refreshing drink of milk or water at night (Sahih Muslim 2055)?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Ghufranaka
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma at‘im man at‘amani wasqi man saqani ('O Allah, feed whoever fed me and give drink to whoever gave me drink')
explanationEn: Narrated by al-Miqdad (RA), reciprocating even a simple cup of water or milk with this short prayer brings joy to hosts and family members.

questionEn: What authentic Sunnah dua did the Prophet ﷺ recite right upon breaking his fast at sunset (Iftar) according to Sunan Abi Dawud 2357?
optionsEn: Dhahaba az-zama'u wabtallatil-‘uruqu wa thabatal-ajru in sha'Allah ('The thirst has gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills')
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Notice this dua is said RIGHT AFTER sipping water/dates to break the fast ('thirst has gone, veins are moistened'), preceded by heartfelt dua just before sunset!

questionEn: When invited to break fast (Iftar) at someone's home or dining together in Ramadan, what three-fold blessing did the Prophet ﷺ say for the host (Sunan Abi Dawud 3854)?
optionsEn: May you fast alone every Monday
May guests leave before Maghrib
May your pots stay empty until winter
Aftara ‘indakumus-sa'imun, wa akala ta‘amakumul-abrar, wa sallat ‘alaykumul-mala'ikah ('May fasting people break fast with you, the righteous eat your food, and angels pray for blessings upon you')
explanationEn: Encouraging hospitality for fasting neighbors turns every Iftar table into a place visited by angelic prayers.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 3854 / Sunan Ibn Majah 1747

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 1431, what should a fasting person do if invited to a dinner feast while observing a voluntary fast (or during Ramadan if someone offers food)?
optionsEn: Criticize the host for cooking food
Hide silently without greeting anyone
Refuse rudely without replying
Accept the invitation respectfully—during voluntary fasts either eat to please the host (or keep fasting if no offense) and make dua for the host's blessing ('yusalli ‘alayhim')
explanationEn: In Arabic, 'yusalli ‘alayhim' in Muslim 1431 means making heartfelt dua for the hosts even if one remains fasting!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ urge sharing meals together ('Eat together and do not eat separately, for barakah is with the group') in Sunan Ibn Majah 3287?
optionsEn: Because mentioning Allah's Name together over a shared meal brings divine barakah so everyone feels nourished and united
Because silence is mandatory at every meal
Because group meals require ten courses
Because eating alone is strictly unlawful
explanationEn: Sharing Iftar or family dinners with 'Bismillah' and warm conversation builds love and blessing.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah 3287 / Sunan Abi Dawud 3764

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ remind companions about drinking water calmly—never blowing into the cup or gulping in one breath like a camel (Sahih Muslim 2028 / Tirmidhi 1885)?
optionsEn: Blow forcefully across hot tea into the cup
Hold breath until the entire pitcher is empty
Say 'Bismillah', drink with the right hand in two or three separate breaths outside the vessel, and praise Allah ('Alhamdulillah') after finishing
Drink strictly with the left hand
explanationEn: Taking gentle breaths away from the cup aids hygiene, calm digestion, and mindfulness of Allah.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 2734, why is Allah so pleased with a servant who praises Him after a single bite of food or sip of water?
optionsEn: Because it cancels the need for Fajr
Because angels only watch dinner tables

InnAllaha la-yarda ‘anil-‘abdi an ya'kulal-aklata fa-yahmadahu ‘alayha aw yashrabash-sharbata fa-yahmadahu ‘alayha ('Indeed, Allah is well-pleased with the servant who eats a meal and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it')
Because praising food turns water into milk
explanationEn: Even a single 'Alhamdulillah' after morning tea or water wins Allah's direct pleasure (Ridwan)!

questionEn: What gentle dua did the Prophet ﷺ say when offered the very first fresh fruit of the season (Sahih Muslim 1373)?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi thamarina, wa barik lana fi madinatina, wa barik lana fi sa‘ina, wa barik lana fi muddina
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Before tasting the season's first fresh dates, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for Allah's blessing on the city's fruit, weights, and measures—then handed it to the youngest child present!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid ever criticizing food set before him (Sahih al-Bukhari 5409)?
optionsEn: Because cooks only worked on Fridays
He never criticized any food at all: if he liked it, he ate it with gratitude; if he disliked it, he simply left it politely without hurting the cook's feelings
Because food tastes identical everywhere
Because criticizing spices invalidates Wudu
explanationEn: Protecting the feelings of parents, spouses, or hosts while thanking Allah for whatever is served reflects refined Sunnah manners.

questionEn: What three-step exchange of duas occurs whenever a Muslim sneezes and praises Allah (Sahih al-Bukhari 6224)?
optionsEn: 1) Sneezer says 'Alhamdulillah'; 2) Listener replies 'YarhamukAllah' ('May Allah have mercy on you'); 3) Sneezer replies 'Yahdikumullahu wa yuslihu balakum' ('May Allah guide you and set right your state/affairs')
1) Sneezer says 'Ghufranaka'; 2) Listener claps; 3) Both stay silent
1) Listener says 'MashaAllah'; 2) Sneezer says 'Labbayk'
1) Sneezer says 'Amin'; 2) Listener says 'SubhanAllah'
explanationEn: Even an involuntary sneeze becomes a miniature circle of mercy, guidance, and mutual blessing among believers!

questionEn: If someone sneezes and does NOT say 'Alhamdulillah', what does the Sunnah teach regarding replying 'YarhamukAllah' (Sahih Muslim 2992)?
optionsEn: Ignore them for the rest of the day
You do not say 'YarhamukAllah' unless they praise Allah first—though you may warmly remind them 'Say Alhamdulillah!'
Tell them they broke their Wudu
Say 'YarhamukAllah' loudly anyway
explanationEn: Anas (RA) noted that when two men sneezed before the Prophet ﷺ, he blessed only the one who said 'Alhamdulillah'.

questionEn: If someone keeps sneezing repeatedly (more than three times) due to a cold or allergy, what did the Prophet ﷺ advise saying after the third sneeze (Sunan Abi Dawud 5034 / Muslim 2993)?
optionsEn: Leave the room immediately
After three times, note gently 'You have a cold' (inna-ka mazkum / shafakAllah—asking Allah to heal them) rather than repeating full Tashmit endlessly
Repeat Tashmit fifty times in a row
Stop talking to them for a week
explanationEn: Prophetic wisdom combines spiritual care with common-sense mercy for someone catching a cold.

questionEn: When a fellow believer tells you 'I love you for the sake of Allah' (Inni uhibbuka fillah), what loving reply did the Prophet ﷺ teach (Sunan Abi Dawud 5125)?
optionsEn: Ahabbakalladhi ahbabtani lah ('May He for whose sake you love me love you too')
Keep that feeling private
Repay them with silver coins
Only parents may say that
explanationEn: Narrated by Anas (RA), expressing pure brotherhood/sisterhood in Allah—and returning it with this dua—strengthens hearts and earns Allah's Shade.

questionEn: What gentle dua did the Prophet ﷺ recommend making for someone who does you a kindness or gives you a gift—besides saying 'JazakAllahu khayran' (Nasa'i al-Kubra / Abu Dawud 1672)?
optionsEn: Forget the favor quickly so you feel independent
Reciprocate with a gift if able; and if unable, continue making sincere dua for them (such as 'BarakAllahu fika fi ahlika wa malik' or 'JazakAllahu khayran') until you know you have repaid them
Only thank people publicly on stage
Refuse all gifts from friends
explanationEn: When ‘Abdur-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA) offered generous help to Sa‘d ibn ar-Rabi‘ (RA), Sa‘d replied with the timeless dua: 'BarakAllahu laka fi ahlika wa malik!'

questionEn: When someone praises you to your face, what humble protective dua did Companions like Abu Bakr (RA) whisper to keep arrogance out of their heart (Al-Adab al-Mufrad 761)?
optionsEn: Write their compliment onto a banner
Stop doing good deeds altogether

Allahumma la tu'akhidhni bima yaqulun, waghfir li ma la ya‘lamun, waj‘alni khayran mimma yazunnun ('O Allah, do not hold me accountable for what they say, forgive me for what they do not know, and make me better than what they assume')
Tell them they forgot half of your virtues
explanationEn: Abu Bakr's (RA) three-part prayer turns compliments into instant humility and self-improvement.

questionEn: What should you say if you feel compelled to praise a brother or sister's character in front of others so you don't accidentally inflate their ego (Sahih al-Bukhari 2662)?
optionsEn: Exaggerate their worship tenfold
Never encourage anyone's goodness at all
Proclaim they are guaranteed Paradise without doubt
Ahsibu fulanan [wallahu hasibuhu wa la uzakki ‘alallahi ahada] ('I think so-and-so is righteous—and Allah is his Reckoner, nor do I declare anyone pure above Allah')
explanationEn: Balanced appreciation honors good people while keeping ultimate judgment with Allah alone.

questionEn: When a Muslim receives an insult or false accusation while fasting, what self-restraining phrase did the Prophet ﷺ command repeating calmly (Sahih al-Bukhari 1904)?
optionsEn: Break your fast immediately out of anger
Inni sa'im, inni sa'im ('Indeed I am fasting, indeed I am fasting')
Respond with a sharper insult
Argue louder until everyone agrees
explanationEn: Reminding both yourself and the provoker that you are fasting cools anger and protects the spirit of Ramadan.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say 'Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah' (Sunan Abi Dawud 4811 / Tirmidhi 1954)?
optionsEn: Because thanking Allah is secondary to thanking kings
Because genuine gratitude to Allah naturally overflows into appreciating parents, spouses, teachers, helpers, and friends—often with warm prayers like 'JazakAllahu khayran'
Because gifts must always be paid back in cash
Because people grant sustenance independently of Allah
explanationEn: Gratitude to Allah and courtesy toward people grow from the very same humble root.

questionEn: What exact Sunnah blessing did the Prophet ﷺ teach saying to a newly married groom or bride instead of pre-Islamic sayings (Sunan Abi Dawud 2130 / Tirmidhi 1091)?
optionsEn: Live happily without ever praying together
May you never face any rainy day
May you own the largest silver mines
BarakAllahu laka, wa baraka ‘alayka, wa jama‘a baynakuma fi khayr ('May Allah bless you, shower blessings upon you, and unite both of you in goodness')
explanationEn: He gently replaced 'With harmony and sons' with a comprehensive prayer for mutual blessing in both ease and trial.

questionEn: When a groom first meets his bride privately after the marriage contract, what tender Prophetic dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach placing his hand gently on her forehead/forelock (Sunan Abi Dawud 2160)?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni as'aluka khayraha wa khayra ma jabaltaha ‘alayh, wa a‘udhu bika min sharriha wa sharri ma jabaltaha ‘alayh
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Followed by praying two peaceful rak‘ahs together (reported from Ibn Mas‘ud RA), starting marriage in prayer invites Allah's sakinah into the home.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 2160 / Sunan Ibn Majah 1918

questionEn: What short dua recited by spouses before marital intimacy protects any child conceived from being harmed by Satan (Sahih al-Bukhari 141 / Muslim 1434)?
optionsEn: Bismillah, Allahumma jannibnash-shaytana wa jannibish-shaytana ma razaqtana
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina qurrata a‘yun
explanationEn: Calling Allah's Name even in marriage intimacy elevates human love into protected worship.

questionEn: What warm traditional blessing (recorded by Hasan al-Basri and widely included in Hisn al-Muslim) is said to parents celebrating the birth of a newborn?
optionsEn: May the child never speak until age ten
Hide the newborn from all family
May the child owe gold to neighbors

BarakAllahu laka fil-mawhubi laka, wa shakartal-wahib, wa balagha ashuddahu, wa ruziqta birrah ('May Allah bless you in what He gifted you, may you thank the Giver, may the child reach maturity, and may you be blessed with their righteousness/kindness')
explanationEn: Thanking 'the Giver' (Al-Wahhab) and praying for the child's mature devotion turns birth announcements into shared dua.

questionEn: What should new parents reply to those congratulating them with 'BarakAllahu laka fil-mawhub...'?
optionsEn: Say 'Ghufranaka' silently
BarakAllahu laka wa baraka ‘alayka wa jazakAllahu khayran wa razaqakAllahu mithlahu wa ajzala thawabak ('May Allah bless you, reward you with goodness, grant you the like, and multiply your reward')
Send a silver plate immediately
No reply is needed
explanationEn: Exchanging warm duas at a baby's arrival strengthens community joy and affection.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ performed Tahnik (softening a date and gently rubbing it on a newborn's palate) and named newborns brought to him, what did he accompany it with (Sahih al-Bukhari 5467)?
optionsEn: He forbade naming children until age five
He asked for expensive gifts from the parents
He smiled warmly, made heartfelt dua for Allah's barakah upon the child, and gently placed the child in his lap
He delayed all prayers for a week
explanationEn: Welcoming infants into the world with prayer for barakah and righteous names reflects Prophetic gentleness.

questionEn: What protective dua did the Prophet ﷺ regularly recite over his young grandsons al-Hasan and al-Husayn (RA) according to Sahih al-Bukhari 3371?
optionsEn: U‘idhukuma bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min kulli shaytanin wa hammah, wa min kulli ‘aynin lammah
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Ghufranaka
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Parents can place their hand affectionately on their child's head morning and evening and recite this exact Prophetic protection!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ instruct us to say 'Allahumma barik ‘alayh' or 'TabarakAllah' when admiring a cute child, smart skill, or friend's new blessing (Muwatta Malik / Ibn Majah 3509)?
optionsEn: Because compliments lose value unless shouted
Because the evil eye (‘ayn) is real, and praying for Allah's blessing ('Allahumma barik fih') shields what we admire from accidental harm!
Because admiring anything is prohibited
Because only scholars have healthy admiration
explanationEn: Saying 'MashaAllah, Allahumma barik lahum' turns natural admiration into loving protection instead of unintended harm.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah 3509 / Muwatta Imam Malik

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 5997, what tender habit did a Bedouin express shock at seeing Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do—prompting the Prophet ﷺ to ask 'What can I do if Allah stripped mercy from your heart?'
optionsEn: Carrying children across deserts without shoes
Kissing his young children/grandchildren affectionately and making loving dua for their mercy
Giving children gold coins every hour
Allowing children to skip all education
explanationEn: Physical affection paired with prayer for children reflects the Sunnah mercy of 'Whoever shows no mercy will not be shown mercy.'

questionEn: What ongoing charity continues bringing reward and answered prayers to deceased parents even after their passing according to Sahih Muslim 1631?
optionsEn: Hosting forty days of loud weeping
Carving expensive marble monuments alone
Leaving debts unpaid for years
Sadaqah Jariyah (ongoing charity), beneficial knowledge left behind, and a righteous child who makes sincere dua for them (waladun salihun yad‘u lah)
explanationEn: Praying daily 'Rabbir-hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira' and 'Allahummaghfir li-walidayya' stays one of the greatest gifts a child can ever send to their parents.

questionEn: When visiting a sick friend or family member, what short, reassuring words did the Prophet ﷺ always speak to lift their spirits (Sahih al-Bukhari 3616)?
optionsEn: Your illness looks far worse than yesterday
Recovery seems impossible this season
La ba'sa, tahurun in sha'Allah ('No need to worry; it is a purification [from sins], if Allah wills')
You must have committed secret crimes
explanationEn: Bringing calm hope rather than gloomy rumors heals the heart of a patient even before medicine acts.

questionEn: What seven-times healing dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sunan Abi Dawud 3106 & Tirmidhi 2083 to recite beside a sick person whose appointed time has not yet come?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
As'alullahal-‘Azima Rabbal-‘arshil-‘azimi an yashfiyak ('I ask Allah the Mighty, Lord of the Mighty Throne, to heal you')—seven times
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ assured that unless death has already been decreed, Allah heals the patient when a sincere believer recites this seven times!

questionEn: When visiting a sick person, what warm physical Sunnah accompanied the Prophet's ﷺ Ruqyah supplication in Sahih al-Bukhari 5743 & Muslim 2191?
optionsEn: Gently wiping with his right hand over the patient (or painful area) and reciting: 'Adhhibil-ba'sa Rabban-nas, ishfi wa Antash-Shafi, la shifa'a illa shifa'uk, shifa'an la yughadiru saqama'
Pouring cold oil without mentioning Allah
Refusing to look at the patient from the doorway
Staying for hours exhausting the patient
explanationEn: Addressing Allah as 'Ash-Shafi' ('The Healer') and asking for a cure that leaves behind no trace of sickness expresses complete trust in divine healing.

questionEn: When feeling sudden physical pain anywhere in your own body, what exact two-part Sunnah Ruqyah did the Prophet ﷺ teach ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As (RA) in Sahih Muslim 2202?
optionsEn: Place your hand directly on the painful spot, say 'Bismillah' 3 times, then say 7 times: 'A‘udhu billahi wa qudratihi min sharri ma ajidu wa uhadhir'
Ignore medical care and avoid speaking
Wrap black thread around the wrist
Wait seven days before making dua
explanationEn: Seeking refuge in Allah's Might and Power from both what you feel right now ('ma ajid') and what you fear later ('wa uhadhir') combines faith with calm self-care.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ himself fell ill, what heartfelt Ruqyah did Angel Jibril (AS) recite over him according to Sahih Muslim 2186?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismillahi arqika min kulli shay'in yu'dhika, min sharri kulli nafsin aw ‘aynin hasid, Allahu yashfika, bismillahi arqik
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Notice how Jibril (AS) emphasized 'Allahu yashfika'—making clear that even angelic Ruqyah begs Allah alone for cure.

questionEn: Which opening surah of the Qur'an did a companion famously recite as Ruqyah over a scorpion-stung tribal chief—earning the Prophet's ﷺ joyful affirmation 'How did you know it is a Ruqyah?' (Bukhari 2276)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kawthar
Surah Al-‘Asr
Surah Al-Fatihah
Surah Al-Masad
explanationEn: Because Al-Fatihah combines praise of Allah, Tawhid, and 'Iyyaka na‘budu wa iyyaka nasta‘in', it is the supreme Qur'anic healing recitation.

questionEn: During the Prophet's ﷺ final illness when his strength waned, how did ‘A'ishah (RA) administer the Mu'awwidhat (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas) over him (Sahih al-Bukhari 5016, 5735)?
optionsEn: She wrote them inside copper rings
She recited the Mu'awwidhat, blew softly into his own blessed palms, and wiped with his hands over his body for their blessing
She forbade visitors from praying for him
She read only historical stories
explanationEn: Using the Mu'awwidhat gently over sick loved ones—children, parents, or spouses—is one of the purest expressions of Islamic care.

questionEn: What clear boundary distinguishes authentic Prophetic Ruqyah (al-Ruqyah ash-Shar‘iyyah) from prohibited superstitious charms (Sahih Muslim 2200)?
optionsEn: Authentic Ruqyah uses ONLY the Qur'an, Allah's Names/Attributes, or clear understandable Prophetic duas with full trust that Allah heals; forbidden Ruqyah involves shirk, jinn-calling, unintelligible symbols, or lucky amulets
Authentic Ruqyah rejects modern doctors and medicine
Authentic Ruqyah must be done only in darkness for payment
Authentic Ruqyah requires secret coded knots
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explicitly taught: 'There is no harm in Ruqyah so long as there is no shirk in it'—while simultaneously encouraging medical treatment ('Seek treatment, O servants of Allah!').

questionEn: What comforting lesson did the Prophet ﷺ share with a sick person in Sahih al-Bukhari 5641 regarding every prick of a thorn, fever, anxiety, or fatigue a believer endures patiently?
optionsEn: Sick people lose all reward of past prayers
Illness proves Allah is angry forever
Only martyrs receive forgiveness through pain
None of them befalls a Muslim except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it, just as a tree sheds its dry leaves in autumn
explanationEn: Moreover, Sahih al-Bukhari 2996 assures that when a believer falls sick or travels, Allah continues recording the exact good deeds they used to do while healthy at home!

questionEn: When visiting someone in hospital or chronically ill, what short compassionate etiquette regarding visit length and asking them for dua did scholars derive from the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Eat the patient's meals without asking
Stay for three hours debating noisy politics
Bring bad news about other patients
Keep the visit light and uplifting rather than exhausting the patient, bring hope and gentle service, make dua for their healing, and lovingly ask the sick person to pray for you too!
explanationEn: Narrated in Sunan Ibn Majah 1441, visiting the sick puts you amidst the fruits of Paradise ('khurfatil-jannah') until you return.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say Allah declares on the Day of Judgment to a servant who neglected visiting a sick neighbor (Sahih Muslim 2569)?
optionsEn: 'Visiting the sick brings no spiritual reward'
'Only doctors need visit patients'
'My servant so-and-so fell ill and you did not visit him; had you visited him, you would have found Me with him!'
'Praying from afar replaces all care'
explanationEn: Knowing Allah's special mercy rests beside the sickbed fills hospital visits and caring phone calls with extraordinary meaning.

questionEn: When a person is severely ill and loses hope of life, what did the Prophet ﷺ strictly forbid praying for—and what balanced dua did he prescribe instead (Sahih al-Bukhari 5671)?
optionsEn: Complain angrily against divine decree
Never wish for death out of hardship; if one must speak, say: 'Allahumma ahyini ma kanatil-hayatu khayran li, wa tawaffani idha kanatil-wafatu khayran li'
Demand immediate death before sunset
Stop eating and stop all medical care
explanationEn: Trusting Allah's wisdom over when life or death is better keeps patience dignified until the very last breath.

questionEn: Which majestic three-part Tahmid and Tawhid dua did the Prophet ﷺ always recite in moments of intense distress/calamity (Du‘a' al-Karb, Bukhari 6346 / Muslim 2730)?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
La ilaha illallahul-‘Azimul-Halim, la ilaha illallahu Rabbul-‘arshil-‘azim, la ilaha illallahu Rabbus-samawati wa Rabbul-ardi wa Rabbul-‘arshil-karim
explanationEn: Remarkably, Du‘a' al-Karb contains not a single direct demand—simply magnifying Allah as the Mighty, Forbearing Lord of the Heavens, Earth, and Noble Throne softens the storm!

questionEn: According to Musnad Ahmad 3712 (narrated by Ibn Mas‘ud RA), what extraordinary promise awaits any anxious or grieving Muslim who recites 'Allahumma inni ‘abduka wabnu ‘abdika wabnu amatik...'?
optionsEn: He will forget all family members forever
Allah will surely remove his grief and anxiety, and replace his sorrow with joy and relief (faraja)
He must wait seven years for relief
His grief will double for forty days
explanationEn: In this profound dua, the believer surrenders to Allah's decree ('madin fiyya hukmuk, ‘adlun fiyya qada'uk') and begs Allah by every Name He revealed, kept hidden, or taught.

questionEn: In Ibn Mas‘ud's (RA) grief-relief dua (Ahmad 3712), what beautiful metaphor is asked regarding the Qur'an?
optionsEn: That the Qur'an stay sealed in gold boxes
That the Qur'an solve business ledgers alone
An taj‘alal-Qur'ana rabi‘a qalbi ('That You make the Qur'an the springtime of my heart'), the light of my chest, the remover of my sorrow, and the departure of my anxiety
That only winter nights contain recitation
explanationEn: Just as spring rain turns cracked desert soil green with blossoms, the Qur'an revives a sorrowful heart.

questionEn: What seven-word plea from Sunan Abi Dawud 5090 teaches total dependence on Allah's mercy in moments of depression or exhaustion?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab
Allahumma rahmataka arju, fa-la takilni ila nafsi tarfata ‘ayn, wa aslih li sha'ni kullahu, la ilaha illa Anta
explanationEn: Called 'the supplication of the distressed' (da‘watul-makrub), it frees us from trying to carry heavy burdens through fragile human willpower alone.

questionEn: What short seven-word distress dua taught by Asma' bint ‘Umays (RA) in Sunan Abi Dawud 1525 reminds the heart instantly of Tawhid?
optionsEn: Hasbi malun wa banun
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahu, Allahu Rabbi, la ushriku bihi shay'a ('Allah, Allah is my Lord; I associate nothing with Him')
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
explanationEn: Repeating 'Allah, Allah is my Lord; I associate nothing with Him' centers panic immediately back on the One who holds every storm.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1525 / Sunan Ibn Majah 3882

questionEn: When feeling overwhelmed by debt, worry, or powerful opposition, what happened when Abu Umamah (RA) practiced the eight-refuge dua ('Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan...') morning and evening as the Prophet ﷺ advised (Sunan Abi Dawud 1555)?
optionsEn: He borrowed even more silver coins
He stopped working and sat in the masjid
He moved to another country secretly
He reported: 'I did so, and Allah removed my anxiety and settled all of my debts!'
explanationEn: Combining sincere morning/evening dua with honest effort unlocks unexpected avenues of relief.

questionEn: What brief prayer did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sunan Abi Dawud 1537 when fearing hostility, injustice, or harm from aggressive people?
optionsEn: Allahumma inna naj‘aluka fi nuhurihim, wa na‘udhu bika min shururihim ('O Allah, we place You before their chests/throats, and we seek refuge in You from their evils')
Ghufranaka
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
explanationEn: Asking Allah to stand between us and bullies or oppressors replaces panic with courageous composure.

questionEn: When a person realizes someone is plotting harm or unfair pressure, what paired Qur'anic remembrance did the Prophet ﷺ say at the Battle of Uhud/Hamra' al-Asad (Sahih al-Bukhari 4563)?
optionsEn: Wait until next spring before praying
Retaliate with unlawful slander
Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil ('Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs')
We are outnumbered and doomed
explanationEn: Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) noted that both Prophet Ibrahim (AS) when thrown into the fire and Muhammad ﷺ when warned of massed armies spoke these exact words.

questionEn: What immediate verbal and physical remedy did the Prophet ﷺ prescribe when two companions began boiling with anger (Sahih al-Bukhari 3282 / Abu Dawud 4782)?
optionsEn: Throw household objects immediately
Seek refuge in Allah saying 'A‘udhu billahi minash-Shaytanir-rajim'; and if standing, sit down—if still angry, lie down (and cool down with Wudu / silence)
Make rushed oaths of divorce or estrangement
Shout back twice as fast to clear the chest
explanationEn: Realizing anger flares from Shaytan's spark helps us step back, say Isti‘adhah, change posture, and protect loved ones from hurtful words.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3282 / Sunan Abi Dawud 4782 / Tirmidhi 2191

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ redefine true strength in Sahih al-Bukhari 6114?
optionsEn: The one who refuses to apologize
The one who carries heavy iron shields
The truly strong person is NOT the one who pins others down in wrestling, but the one who controls himself at the moment of anger
The one who wins every loud argument
explanationEn: Self-restraint backed by 'A‘udhu billahi minash-Shaytanir-rajim' shows authentic spiritual muscle.

questionEn: What phrase in the Prophetic dua of Sunan an-Nasa'i 1305 asks Allah to keep our speech truthful and just in moments of anger as well as contentment?
optionsEn: Avoiding family conversations altogether
Asking for 'kalimatal-haqqi fir-rida wal-ghadab' ('truthful, just speech in both contentment and anger' — Sunan an-Nasa'i 1305) and Allah's forbearance
Asking for sharper sarcasm during disputes
Never feeling any normal emotion
explanationEn: Staying fair and truthful even when frustrated is a mark of mature faith.

questionEn: When Umm Salamah (RA) grieved the passing of her noble husband Abu Salamah (RA), what two-part Prophetic dua did she recite despite thinking no one could ever compare to him (Sahih Muslim 918)?
optionsEn: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un; Allahumma'jurni fi musibati wakhluf li khayran minha ('O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with something better')
Stop all community gatherings for a year
I shall never smile again in this life
Why did You take him so early from Madinah?
explanationEn: Allah answered her sincere dua beyond imagination by honoring her in marriage to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself!

questionEn: When closing the eyes of a loved one who has just passed away, what tender prayer did the Prophet ﷺ offer beside Abu Salamah (RA) in Sahih Muslim 920?
optionsEn: Close the room without making any dua
Allahummaghfir li-Abi Salamah, warfa‘ darajatahu fil-mahdiyyin, wakhlufhu fi ‘aqibihi fil-ghabirin, waghfir lana wa lahu ya Rabbal-‘alamin, wafsah lahu fi qabrihi wa nawwir lahu fih
Ask the departed soul to send gold back home
Wail loudly and strike cheeks in grief
explanationEn: Notice the beauty: praying for their forgiveness, elevated rank, care for their surviving family, and spacious light inside their grave—while reminding family only to say good words because angels say 'Amin' to what is spoken!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ gently urge everyone in the room of a dying or newly deceased person to speak ONLY good and hopeful prayers (Sahih Muslim 919)?
optionsEn: Because the angels present say 'Amin' to whatever you say!
Because crying quietly is forbidden
Because silence lasts forty days
Because strangers cannot visit funerals
explanationEn: Even grieving tears are completely natural and merciful (as the Prophet ﷺ wept for his son Ibrahim), while our words remain hopeful, loving, and prayerful.

questionEn: When offering condolences (ta‘ziyah) to a grieving family, what comforting words did the Prophet ﷺ send to his own daughter when her young child was dying (Sahih al-Bukhari 1284)?
