optionsEn: Inna lillahi ma akhadha, wa lahu ma a‘ta, wa kullu shay'in ‘indahu bi-ajalin musamma, fal-tasbir wal-tahtasib ('Indeed, to Allah belongs what He took, and to Him belongs what He gave, and everything with Him has an appointed time; so be patient and hope for Allah's reward')
Blame doctors for the appointed hour
Host an expensive banquet immediately
Never shed a single tear or feel sadness
explanationEn: Reminding a grieving heart that everything belongs to Allah—both what He lent us and what He reclaimed—brings quiet dignity in loss.

questionEn: During Salat al-Janazah (funeral prayer), which opening surah is recited silently after the first Takbir, and which prayer is recited after the second Takbir?
optionsEn: After the 1st Takbir: Surah Al-Fatihah (with seeking refuge); after the 2nd Takbir: Salawat Ibrahimiyyah upon the Prophet ﷺ
After the 1st Takbir: silence; after the 2nd: Surah Al-Fil
All four Takbirs have no recitation at all
After the 1st Takbir: Ayat al-Kursi; after the 2nd: Tasbih 33x
explanationEn: Praising Allah (Al-Fatihah) and honoring the Prophet ﷺ (Salawat) precede earnestly interceding for the deceased after the 3rd Takbir!

questionEn: After the third Takbir of Salat al-Janazah, what deeply moving Prophetic dua did ‘Awf ibn Malik (RA) memorize verbatim from the Prophet ﷺ (Sahih Muslim 963)?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha

Allahummaghfir lahu warhamhu wa ‘afihi wa‘fu ‘anhu, wa akrim nuzulahu wa wassi‘ mudkhalahu waghsilhu bil-ma'i wath-thalji wal-barad, wa naqqihi minal-khataya kama naqqaytath-thawbal-abyada minad-danas...
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: ‘Awf ibn Malik (RA) said: 'Hearing how tenderly the Prophet ﷺ prayed for that deceased man made me wish I were the one being prayed for!'

questionEn: What inclusive Janazah dua from Sunan Abi Dawud 3201 & Tirmidhi 1024 asks Allah to pardon both the living and the deceased, those present and those absent, young and old?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Forgive only the scholars present in the front row
Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir

Allahummaghfir li-hayyina wa mayyitina, wa shahidina wa gha'ibina, wa saghirina wa kabirina, wa dhakarina wa unthana; Allahumma man ahyaytahu minna fa-ahyihi ‘alal-Islam, wa man tawaffaytahu minna fa-tawaffahu ‘alal-iman
explanationEn: Praying for all living and departed believers turns every funeral into a reminder to live upon Islam and die upon Iman.

questionEn: When praying Janazah over a young child who passed away, what tender prayer is mentioned in Sahih al-Bukhari 1335 and classical Sunnah practice?
optionsEn: Allahummaj‘alhu lana faratan wa salafan wa ajra ('O Allah, make him/her a forerunner, a treasure sent ahead, and a source of reward for us')—and ask Allah to make the child an intercessor for their parents
Pray for them as though they committed major adult sins
Skip Janazah completely for infants
Say only 'Ghufranaka' silently
explanationEn: Children who pass away young precede their patient parents into Paradise, waiting at its gates for them!

questionEn: Immediately after burying a Muslim, what brief counsel did the Prophet ﷺ stand beside the grave and give the companions (Sunan Abi Dawud 3221)?
optionsEn: Leave immediately without pausing for silent dua
Hold a collective recitation over the grave for seven days
Carve golden plaques before departing
Istaghfiru li-akhikum wa salu lahu at-tathbit, fa-innahu al-ana yus'al ('Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask Allah to make him firm, for right now he is being questioned!')
explanationEn: Pausing quietly after burial to ask Allah to forgive and steady the deceased in the grave is pure, compassionate Sunnah.

questionEn: What comforting dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach for visiting the grave of a loved one or walking past Muslim graves?
optionsEn: Knock on headstones to summon spirits
Ask the graves directly to grant wealth or children
Turn away quickly without sending peace
As-salamu ‘alaykum dara qawmin mu'minin, wa inna in sha'Allahu bikum lahiqun; nas'alullaha lana wa lakumul-‘afiyah
explanationEn: Sending Salam and praying for ‘afiyah honors the dead respectfully while preserving pure Tawhid.

questionEn: When gentle or heavy rain begins falling, what concise two-word prayer did the Prophet ﷺ say (Sahih al-Bukhari 1032)?
optionsEn: Allahumma hab li mulkan ‘azima
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Allahumma sayyiban nafi‘an ('O Allah, make it a beneficial downpour')
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
explanationEn: Moreover, the Prophet ﷺ taught in Sunan Abi Dawud 2540 that the moment rain falls is one of the prime times when dua is never turned away—and he even uncovered part of his garment slightly so fresh rain touched him, saying 'It has just come from its Lord!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1032 / Sahih Muslim 898 / Abu Dawud 2540

questionEn: Right after rainfall stops, what short grateful statement distinguishes a believer's gratitude from superstition according to Sahih al-Bukhari 846?
optionsEn: Rain happens purely by chance without Creator
Nature owed us rain this Tuesday
We received rain solely because of such-and-such star
Mutirna bi-fadlillahi wa rahmatih ('We have been given rain by the bounty and mercy of Allah')
explanationEn: Saying 'Mutirna bi-fadlillahi wa rahmatih' credits Allah's mercy rather than luck or astrology.

questionEn: If rain becomes excessive and threatens flooding or damage to homes and farms, what wise prayer did the Prophet ﷺ make on the Minbar (Sahih al-Bukhari 1014)?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Allahumma hawalayna wa la ‘alayna; Allahumma ‘alal-akami waz-zirabi wa butunil-awdiyati wa manabitish-shajar ('O Allah, around us and not upon us; upon hills, plateaus, valley beds, and tree-groves')
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Stop rain permanently across the entire planet
explanationEn: Notice how mercifully he did NOT pray against rain itself, only asking Allah to redirect excess water to hills and valleys where plants need it!

questionEn: During drought, what eloquent rain-seeking dua (Istisqa) did the Prophet ﷺ recite in Sunan Abi Dawud 1169?
optionsEn: Send hailstorms over cities immediately
Grant rain only to wealthy orchards
Allahummasqina ghaythan mughithan mari'an mari‘an nafi‘an ghayra darrin ‘ajilan ghayra ajil ('O Allah, send us saving, wholesome, fertile, beneficial rain—not harmful, promptly without delay')
Dry up every mountain spring
explanationEn: Asking for rain that is soothing, fertile, and harmless ('nafi‘an ghayra darr') shows Prophetic foresight.

questionEn: When strong winds blow, why did the Prophet ﷺ instruct us NOT to curse the wind—and what dua did he recite instead (Sahih Muslim 899)?
optionsEn: Do not curse the wind, for it is commanded by Allah; rather say: 'Allahumma inni as'aluka khayraha wa khayra ma fiha wa khayra ma ursilat bih, wa a‘udhu bika min sharriha wa sharri ma fiha wa sharri ma ursilat bih'
Say 'Ghufranaka' forty times backward
Ignore storms and mock weather warnings
Shout angrily at storms until they calm
explanationEn: Recognizing wind as a messenger under Allah's command turns weather anxiety into respectful dua.

questionEn: When thunder rumbled in the sky, what Qur'anic tasbih did ‘Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr (RA) pause his conversation to recite (Muwatta Malik / Al-Adab al-Mufrad 723)?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Subhanalladhi yusabbihur-ra‘du bi-hamdihi wal-mala'ikatu min khifatih ('Glory be to Him whom thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels too in awe of Him')
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Allahu Akbar only at midnight
explanationEn: Echoing Surah Ar-Ra‘d 13:13 during thunder connects natural awe straight back to the Creator.
reference: Muwatta Imam Malik / Al-Adab al-Mufrad 723 / Surah Ar-Ra‘d 13:13

questionEn: Upon sighting the new crescent moon (Hilal) of Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhul-Hijjah, or any lunar month, what uplifting dua did the Prophet ﷺ recite (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3451)?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
May this moon bring wealth without effort
Allahu Akbar, Allahumma ahillahu ‘alayna bil-amni wal-iman, was-salamati wal-Islam, wat-tawfiqi lima tuhibbu wa tarda; Rabbuna wa RabbukAllah
Ghufranaka Rabbana
explanationEn: Welcoming each new lunar month with prayers for security, faith, peace, Islam, and success in pleasing Allah—while reminding the moon 'Our Lord and your Lord is Allah'—guards pure Tawhid!

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 3303 & Muslim 2729, what should a Muslim do upon hearing a rooster crow at dawn versus hearing a donkey bray?
optionsEn: Ignore both sounds completely

When hearing a rooster crow, ask Allah from His bounty ('Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik') because it has seen an angel; when hearing a donkey bray, seek refuge in Allah from Satan ('A‘udhu billahi minash-Shaytanir-rajim') because it has seen a devil
Chase donkeys inside mosques
Seek refuge from Satan when a rooster crows
explanationEn: Even the morning sounds of nature remind believers to ask Allah's bounty and refuge.

questionEn: When seeing a sudden solar or lunar eclipse, what four acts did the Prophet ﷺ command believers to rush toward instead of superstition (Sahih al-Bukhari 1044)?
optionsEn: Make dua to Allah, proclaim Takbir (magnify Allah), pray (Salat al-Kusuf), and give Sadaqah (charity)
Claim the eclipse happened because someone important died
Bang copper pots to chase dragons away
Lock doors and sleep all afternoon
explanationEn: When the sun eclipsed on the day the Prophet's ﷺ infant son Ibrahim passed away, he clarified eclipses are signs of Allah—not omens of anyone's life or death—turning fear into Salah, dua, and charity.

questionEn: When noticing signs of a solar eclipse or terrifying dark storm clouds in the sky, what deeply sensitive concern showed on the Prophet's ﷺ face according to ‘A'ishah (RA) in Sahih Muslim 899?
optionsEn: He laughed carelessly at storm warnings

He would walk in and out anxiously praying until rain fell peacefully, remembering how past nations saw a cloud thinking it was rain before punishment struck—teaching believers never to take safety for granted
He forbade anyone from looking at the sky
He went straight to sleep
explanationEn: Even simple clouds reminded the Prophet ﷺ of humility before Al-Qadir until gentle rain brought relief.

questionEn: What short phrase did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone expressed amazement at a joyful, pure event without using worldly flattery?
optionsEn: Snap fingers repeatedly
Boast of personal luck
Always whistle loudly in crowds
SubhanAllah (when amazed or awed) or Allahu Akbar (when witnessing greatness or triumph)
explanationEn: Saying 'SubhanAllah' in wonder or 'Allahu Akbar' in joy keeps amazed reactions grounded in Allah's perfection.

questionEn: What gentle dua did the Prophet ﷺ make for Anas ibn Malik (RA) when Anas's mother Umm Sulaym (RA) asked him to pray for her young son (Sahih al-Bukhari 6344)?
optionsEn: May he live alone in caves
May he travel without family
Allahumma akthir malahu wa waladahu wa barik lahu fima a‘taytah ('O Allah, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in what You have given him')
May he never own a single coin
explanationEn: Anas (RA) lived over a century, saw over a hundred children and grandchildren, and had date palms bearing fruit twice a year—a living testament to Prophetic dua!

questionEn: What brief prayer did the Prophet ﷺ make for young ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA) while hugging him close (Sahih al-Bukhari 143 / Ahmad 2397)?
optionsEn: May he avoid speaking in public
May he conquer Persia alone
Allahumma faqqihhu fid-din wa ‘allimhut-ta'wil ('O Allah, grant him deep understanding of the religion and teach him interpretation of the Qur'an')
May he become the richest silk merchant
explanationEn: Answered wonderfully, Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) became known forever as 'Hibr al-Ummah' (Scholar of the Ummah) and 'Tarjuman al-Qur'an'.

questionEn: What affectionate prayer did the Prophet ﷺ make for Abu Hurayrah (RA) when Abu Hurayrah complained of forgetting narrations he heard (Sahih al-Bukhari 119)?
optionsEn: He instructed him to fast forty days silently
He asked Abu Hurayrah to spread his cloak, scooped his blessed hands toward it in dua, and told him to gather it to his chest—and Abu Hurayrah (RA) never forgot a single Hadith afterward!
He told him memory cannot be prayed for
He told him to stop attending lectures
explanationEn: Asking Allah to bless memory and understanding of sacred knowledge remains a cherished student's dua.

questionEn: When Abu Hurayrah (RA) begged the Prophet ﷺ to pray that his mother accept Islam, how quickly was that family dua answered (Sahih Muslim 2491)?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ refused to pray for relatives

The Prophet ﷺ immediately raised his hands praying 'Allahummahdi umma Abi Hurayrah'; when Abu Hurayrah ran straight home, he heard water splashing inside—his mother had bathed and testified 'La ilaha illAllah' at the door!
His mother moved away permanently
It took forty years to see any change
explanationEn: Never underestimate praying persistently—and asking righteous friends to pray—for the guidance of beloved parents or relatives!

questionEn: Even when the tribe of Daws initially rejected Islam and Tufayl ibn ‘Amr asked the Prophet ﷺ to curse them, how did the Prophet of Mercy ﷺ pray instead (Sahih al-Bukhari 2937)?
optionsEn: Ban them from entering Makkah forever
Send famine upon their crops
Allahummahdi Dawsan wa'ti bihim ('O Allah, guide the tribe of Daws and bring them [to Islam]')!
Destroy their valley before sunrise
explanationEn: Praying for guidance rather than destruction softened hearts—and Daws embraced Islam willingly soon after!

questionEn: When stoned and bleeding in Ta'if after ten years of Makkah rejection, how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when the Angel of the Mountains offered to crush the city between two hills (Sahih al-Bukhari 3231)?
optionsEn: Ban their grandchildren from pilgrimage
Turn their springs into salt
Yes, crush their valleys at once
No! Rather I hope Allah will bring forth from their descendants people who worship Allah alone without associating any partner with Him!
explanationEn: Instead of vengeance, he poured out his famous tender Ta'if prayer asking only whether Allah was pleased with him—knowing 'In lam yakun bika ‘alayya ghadabun fa-la ubali' ('If You are not angry with me, I do not mind!')

questionEn: What gentle daily prayer for one's spouse and children keeps home life resilient during busy workdays and parenting fatigue?
optionsEn: Combining Qur'an 25:74 ('Rabbana hab lana min azwajina wa dhurriyyatina qurrata a‘yun...') with praying for mutual mercy, patience, forgiveness, and protection upon each family member by name
Praying only when a major crisis erupts
Complaining daily without ever praying for family
Asking Allah for wealth while neglecting family kindness
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that the best of you are those who are best to their families (Tirmidhi 3895).

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach when comforting someone grieving a child or severe trial—reminding them of Allah's recompense?
optionsEn: A pause in morning prayers
A house of stone in Syria

Assuring every believing parent who patiently endures the loss of young children—saying 'Alhamdulillah' and 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un'—that Allah builds for them a 'House of Praise' (Bayt al-Hamd) in Paradise!
Forgetfulness of all loved ones
explanationEn: In Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1021, Allah asks His angels: 'What did My servant say when you took the fruit of his heart?' 'He praised You and said Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un.' So Allah commands: 'Build for him a House in Paradise and name it Bayt al-Hamd!'

questionEn: When feeling sudden anxiety over an upcoming medical test, job interview, or financial bill, what three-step Prophetic sequence brings calm?
optionsEn: Consult fortune-tellers or horoscopes

Perform Wudu cleanly, pray two calm rak‘ahs (or pause in brief sujud), recite 'Hasbunallahu wa ni‘mal-wakil' / 'Allahumma la sahla illa ma ja‘altahu sahla' / 'Ya Hayyu ya Qayyum', and take practical steps with Tawakkul
Panic endlessly without taking action
Skip prayer until results arrive
explanationEn: Linking Salah, authentic Sunnah duas, and responsible action aligns heart and mind.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ make to protect himself and companions from harsh sudden death or falling from heights?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha

Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minat-taraddi wal-hadmi wal-gharaqi wal-hariq, wa a‘udhu bika an yatakhabbatanish-shaytanu ‘indal-mawt, wa a‘udhu bika an amuta fi sabilika mudbira, wa a‘udhu bika an amuta ladigha
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
explanationEn: Asking safety from falling, collapsing buildings, drowning, fire, and dying heedlessly—while still resting in Allah's Qadar—is deeply reassuring in modern travel and city life.

questionEn: When seeing a tragic accident or hearing devastating community news, what immediate Sunnah response combines spiritual grounding with practical compassion?
optionsEn: Spread graphic rumors carelessly online
Pass by indifferently without praying
Celebrate others' hardship

Say 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un', pray earnestly for mercy, healing, and patience for those affected, and step forward to help with whatever aid, blood donation, charity, or kindness is possible
explanationEn: Empathy in Islam turns 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un' into caring action and sincere dua.

questionEn: What gentle Prophetic dua in Sunan Abi Dawud 1544 & an-Nasa'i 5460 asks Allah for protection from poverty, scarcity, humiliation, and injustice?
optionsEn: Allahumma aghnini bil-kasal
Ghufranaka

Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-faqri wal-qillati wadh-dhillah, wa a‘udhu bika min an azlima aw uzlam ('O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, scarcity, and humiliation, and from wronging others or being wronged')
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik
explanationEn: Narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud 1544 & Nasa'i 5460, dignity and lawful sufficiency allow a believer to give generously rather than suffer exploitation.

questionEn: When sharing food at a banquet or potluck with friends, why does saying 'Bismillah' aloud gently remind everyone at the table without preaching?
optionsEn: Because only hosts may mention Allah
Because whispering silently is forbidden at tables
Because hearing 'Bismillah' softly prompts distracted companions to remember Allah before their first bite, multiplying barakah for the whole table
Because food spoils unless shouted over
explanationEn: A warm, natural 'Bismillah!' invites the entire table—children and elders alike—into shared gratitude.

questionEn: When teaching a young child dining etiquette, what three simple rules did the Prophet ﷺ give young ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari 5376?
optionsEn: Ya ghulam, sammillaha (mention Allah's Name—Bismillah), wa kul bi-yaminik (eat with your right hand), wa kul mimma yalik (eat from what is directly in front of you)
Stand up while running across the room
Eat quickly before elders arrive, use left hand, and criticize dishes
Remain silent without Bismillah or Alhamdulillah
explanationEn: Three gentle sentences shaped a child's lifelong table manners with love and zero harshness.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone broke a vow of anger or realized an oath was less good than another righteous path (Sahih Muslim 1650)?
optionsEn: Stay stubborn forever out of pride
Repeat the angry oath ten more times
Refuse reconciliation with siblings
He instructed them to do what is better, offer the expiation (kaffarah) for the oath, and ask Allah's forgiveness—never using an oath as an excuse to sever family ties or skip goodness!
explanationEn: Choosing goodness and reconciliation over stubborn pride reflects Islamic maturity.

questionEn: What warning did the Prophet ﷺ give regarding severing family ties (qati‘at ar-rahim), and how does dua help heal strained relationships?
optionsEn: No one who severs kinship ties enters Paradise easily; making secret dua for estranged relatives, greeting them gently on Eid, and asking Allah to soften hearts repairs bonds
Never pray for cousins who annoy you
Only visit relatives who gift gold
Cut off relatives permanently whenever disagreements happen
explanationEn: Praying privately for a difficult relative often softens your own heart first—opening doors to peaceful reconciliation.

questionEn: When attending a neighbor's funeral or visiting bereaved non-Muslim friends/neighbors, how can a Muslim express sincere Islamic warmth and lawful prayer?
optionsEn: Offer gentle presence, practical food/help, condolences wishing patience and comfort to the living family, and pray to Allah for their guidance and comfort (while reserving Islamic forgiveness/Janazah prayers specifically for deceased Muslims per Qur'an 9:113)
Stay silent and withhold neighborly kindness
Mock their grief or refuse to help grieving neighbors
Ignore them completely
explanationEn: Islam unites crystal-clear creed with overflowing human compassion, service, and neighborly grace.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the person who truly maintains ties of kinship (al-wasil)?
optionsEn: Keep strict scorecards of favors
Stop sending Eid duas if unreturned
Only greet relatives who call you first
The maintainer of kinship is NOT merely the one who reciprocates equally (al-mukafi'), but the one who reconnects ties even when his relatives cut them off!
explanationEn: Making dua for and checking on a distant relative without keeping score reflects Prophetic Ihsan.

questionEn: What two qualities alongside truthfulness did the Prophet ﷺ link to being beloved and nearest to him on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Loud debating and sharp criticism
Traveling without companions
Husnul-khuluq — the best of manners and gentle character
Hoarding rare manuscripts
explanationEn: Good manners—saying Salam warmly, smiling, thanking hosts, visiting the sick, and praying for others—shine brighter on the Scale than anything except Tawhid.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach when seeking refuge from an evil neighbor (jar as-su') in a permanent residence?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min jaris-su'i fi daril-muqamah, fa-inna jaral-badiyati yatahawwal ('O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a bad neighbor in a permanent home, for a nomad neighbor moves away')
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
explanationEn: Narrated in Sunan an-Nasa'i 5502 & Mustadrak, praying for peaceful neighbors—and striving to BE a good neighbor ourselves—brings deep household peace.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, what three everyday manners prove genuine faith in Allah and the Last Day?
optionsEn: Speaking endlessly about faults of others
Speaking good or remaining silent, honoring one's neighbor, and honoring one's guest generously
Locking doors whenever travelers knock
Posting boastful selfies daily
explanationEn: Each of these three—gentle tongue, caring neighborliness, and warm hospitality—is strengthened by daily dhikr and dua.

questionEn: When seeing a friend experiencing financial success, happy marriage, or children's achievements, what immediate dua protects your heart from jealousy (hasad) and blesses them?
optionsEn: Gossip about their good fortune
Wish secretly for their blessing to vanish
MashaAllah, Allahumma barik lahum wa zidhum min fadlik ('What Allah willed! O Allah, bless them and increase them from Your bounty')
Why did they get that instead of me?
explanationEn: Praying for Allah to bless a friend's success immediately cleanses envy and brings angelic 'Amin, and for you the like thereof!'

questionEn: What comforting reminder from Sahih Muslim 2999 turns every joyful blessing AND every painful trial in a believer's life into pure good?
optionsEn: Amazing is the affair of the believer! All of his affair is good—and that belongs to no one except the believer: if prosperity reaches him, he thanks Allah and it is good for him; if hardship strikes him, he is patient and it is good for him
Only wealthy people have good outcomes
Patience brings reward only in summer
Hardship cancels past gratitude
explanationEn: Shukr in ease and Sabr in trial—wrapped in daily dua—make the believer unbeatable.

questionEn: What profound definition of supplication did the Prophet ﷺ proclaim in Sunan Abi Dawud 1479 & Tirmidhi 2969 before reciting Surah Ghafir 40:60?
optionsEn: Dua is only for travelers facing storms
Dua counts only when written on paper
Dua is merely an optional extra after worship
Ad-du‘a'u huwal-‘ibadah ('Supplication IS worship itself')
explanationEn: Because turning to Allah in need declares His power and our dependence, dua is the very core of worship—not a last-resort backup plan.

questionEn: According to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3370, what rank does dua hold in the sight of Allah compared to other acts?
optionsEn: Nothing is more honorable/noble to Allah the Exalted than dua (Laysa shay'un akrama ‘alallahi ta‘ala minad-du‘a')
Dua ranks below silent fasting alone
Dua matters only during Ramadan nights
Dua holds honor only inside Makkah
explanationEn: Even before an answer arrives visibly, the sheer act of calling upon Allah is deeply beloved and honored by Him.

questionEn: What stark warning did the Prophet ﷺ give in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3373 to anyone who feels too self-sufficient to ask Allah for their needs?
optionsEn: Independent people earn extra rank by staying silent
Allah ignores small requests from healthy people
Man lam yas'alillaha yaghdb ‘alayh ('Whoever does not ask Allah, Allah becomes angry with him')
Only scholars need ask Allah daily
explanationEn: Human beings grow annoyed when asked repeatedly; Allah is the exact opposite—He loves to be asked and is displeased when a servant stops turning to Him!

questionEn: Why does raising one's palms upward in dua bring immense confidence according to Sunan Abi Dawud 1488 & Tirmidhi 3556?
optionsEn: Because silent prayer without hands is invalid
Indeed, Allah is Shy and Generous (Hayiyyun Karim); He feels shy when a servant raises his hands to Him to turn them back empty and disappointed
Because raising hands forces angels to listen faster
Because hands must point strictly northward
explanationEn: Even when feeling unworthy, raising empty palms before Al-Hayiyy Al-Karim taps into His boundless generosity.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ teach us to open a formal supplication right after witnessing a man pray and immediately ask for his need without praising Allah first (Abu Dawud 1481)?
optionsEn: Demand your request abruptly before mentioning Allah's Names
Always start by complaining about other people
Wait until ending all conversation for the week
Let him begin by glorifying and praising Allah (tahmid wa thana'), then send blessings (Salawat) upon the Prophet ﷺ, and THEN ask whatever he wishes
explanationEn: Praising Allah and sending Salawat first opens the royal court of dua with reverence and beauty.

questionEn: When making dua in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3479, what inner certainty must accompany the words on our tongue?
optionsEn: Recite rapidly while checking other conversations
Call upon Allah while being completely certain of His response (wa antum muqinuna bil-ijabah), knowing Allah does not answer a dua from a heedless, distracted heart
Expect rejection before even finishing
Test Allah casually just to see if anything happens
explanationEn: Presence of heart (hudur al-qalb) and certainty in Allah's generosity (husn az-zann billah) fuel answered dua.

questionEn: What fatal attitude blocks the ongoing blessing of dua according to Sahih al-Bukhari 6340 & Sahih Muslim 2735?
optionsEn: Impatient haste (al-‘ajalah)—when a servant says, 'I prayed and prayed and I do not see my prayer answered!' and therefore grows weary and gives up making dua
Asking Allah persistently for ten years
Praising Allah before asking
Praying quietly before Fajr
explanationEn: Every servant's dua IS answered so long as they don't grow impatient and quit!

questionEn: According to Musnad Ahmad 11133, in what three merciful ways does Allah respond to EVERY sincere Muslim's dua free of sin or severing kinship?
optionsEn: Only requests spoken in Arabic poetry receive answers
Either He grants cash within 24 hours, OR He rejects it forever
Either He hastens what they asked in this world, OR He stores it as greater reward in the Hereafter, OR He averts an equivalent evil/harm from them
Two out of three prayers are discarded silently
explanationEn: Nothing prayed sincerely is EVER wasted—when Sahabah heard this they exclaimed 'Then we will make plenty of dua!' and the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'Allah is even More Plentiful!'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid adding the hesitant phrase 'if You will' ('Allahummaghfir li in shi'ta') at the end of a request (Sahih al-Bukhari 6339 / Muslim 2679)?
optionsEn: Because angels refuse conditional sentences
Be firm and decisive in asking ('li-ya‘zimil-mas'alah'), for Allah does whatever He wills—nobody can compel Him!
Because only travelers may be decisive
Because Arabic lacks conditional words
explanationEn: Saying 'if You will' makes it sound as if Allah grants reluctantly or you barely care; asking boldly honors His boundless wealth.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 1015, why was the dusty, disheveled traveler stretching his hands skyward crying 'O Lord, O Lord!' turned away—teaching a critical prerequisite for answered dua?
optionsEn: Because his food was unlawful (haram), his drink was haram, his clothing was haram, and he was nourished with haram—so how could his dua be answered?
Because travelers cannot pray while dusty
Because stretching hands skyward is wrong
Because he failed to wear white robes
explanationEn: Pure, lawful earnings and halal food clear the spiritual channel between the supplicant and heaven.

questionEn: When Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ how to become someone whose duas are always answered (mustajab ad-da‘wah), what single lifestyle counsel did the Prophet ﷺ give him (Tabarani)?
optionsEn: Fast seventy days without fruit
Speak only in rhymed prose
Atib mat‘amaka takun mustajabad-da‘wah ('Make your food/earnings pure and halal, and you will be one whose supplications are answered!')
Move away from Madinah permanently
explanationEn: Integrity in how we earn and spend money empowers every whisper of dua.

questionEn: What two forbidden types of requests explicitly disqualify a dua from acceptance in Sahih Muslim 2735?
optionsEn: Asking for healing from fever
Asking for something sinful (ithm) or asking to sever family ties (qati‘at rahim)
Asking for beneficial knowledge
Asking for lawful marriage or safe travel
explanationEn: Allah's mercy never endorses cruelty, sin, or breaking family bonds.

questionEn: What delightful unseen echo occurs whenever a Muslim prays sincerely for a fellow Muslim behind their back (fi zahril-ghayb) according to Sahih Muslim 2733?
optionsEn: It counts only if the friend pays a fee
Angels remain silent until notified publicly
The request is halved between them
An appointed angel beside his head responds: 'Amin, and for you the like thereof!' (Amin wa laka bi-mithl)
explanationEn: Praying secretly for others' health, guidance, marriage, or rizq is one of the fastest ways to invite angelic 'Amin' upon your own life!

questionEn: How should a supplicant vary the posture of their hands across different Sunnah contexts of dua?
optionsEn: Only clapping hands is authentic
Index finger pointing is mandatory at bedtime

Regular dua: palms raised together around chest/shoulder height facing heaven or face; Friday Khutbah: Imam points with the right index finger only; extreme distress/Istisqa: arms raised very high (sometimes palms facing down in Istisqa)
Hands must always stay locked behind the back
explanationEn: Recognizing these distinct Sunnah hand postures avoids confusion when watching different gatherings or Friday sermons.

questionEn: After finishing personal dua with raised palms, is wiping the face with both hands an obligatory pillar of dua?
optionsEn: Yes, forgetting to wipe the face invalidates the entire dua
Wiping with the left hand only is required

No—raising hands and pouring out the heart is the established Sunnah; wiping the face afterward is reported in weak/hasan-by-corroboration narrations (so some scholars like Ibn Taymiyyah/al-Albani leave it out while others like Ibn Hajar/al-Nawawi consider it mild/acceptable, never obligatory)
Yes, it is a major pillar of Hajj
explanationEn: Focusing on heart presence and sincerity rather than disputing minor hand-wiping customs reflects mature Islamic balance.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1485 / Bulugh al-Maram (Ibn Hajar)

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise regarding shouting at the top of one's lungs during group travel dhikr vs. dignified calm tones (Sahih al-Bukhari 4205)?
optionsEn: Be gentle with yourselves! You are NOT calling upon someone deaf or absent—indeed, He whom you call is All-Hearing and Near, nearer to each of you than the neck of your riding animal!
Shout as loudly as possible to wake distant valleys
Stop making dhikr completely while traveling
Whisper only inside enclosed tents
explanationEn: This touching reminder from Khaybar keeps personal and travel dhikr reverent, soothing, and free of theatrical strain.

questionEn: What did ‘A'ishah (RA) and Sunan Abi Dawud 1482 tell us about the Prophet's ﷺ preference in wording when making dua?
optionsEn: He forbade short two-sentence prayers
He required 500-line rhymed poems every morning
He accepted only complex philosophical terminology
He loved 'Jawami‘ ad-du‘a'—comprehensive, concise, heartfelt supplications—and avoided contrived, overly long, rhymed artificiality (as‘a‘ / takalluf)
explanationEn: Authentic dua needs honesty and depth, not theatrical vocabulary.

questionEn: What humorous yet reassuring exchange occurred when a Bedouin told the Prophet ﷺ he couldn't keep up with all the eloquent phrases the Prophet ﷺ and Mu‘adh whispered in Salah (Sunan Abi Dawud 792)?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ told him his Salah was rejected
Asked what he DID say, the man replied: 'I ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge in Him from the Fire!'—and the Prophet ﷺ smiled warmly: 'Around those two Mu‘adh and I buzz!'
The Prophet ﷺ rebuked him for simple wording
He ordered him to memorize a dictionary first
explanationEn: Never let lack of fancy Arabic stop you from speaking sincerely to Allah—every great dua orbits Paradise and safety from the Fire!
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 792 / Sunan Ibn Majah 910

questionEn: Can a believer make personal, heartfelt dua outside obligatory Salah recitation in their own native language (English, Urdu, Malay, Turkish, French, etc.) if they don't know Arabic fluently?
optionsEn: No, Allah only listens to classical Arabic
Personal duas in English are sinful outside sleep
Non-Arabs must stay mute until fluent
Yes—Allah understands every tongue and unspoken sigh of the heart, so speak honestly to Him in your language while steadily learning key Arabic Qur'anic and Sunnah duas!
explanationEn: Speaking openly to Allah in your mother tongue unlocks deep tears and sincerity while you gradually memorize Sunnah gems.

questionEn: Which posture inside Salah did the Prophet ﷺ declare brings a servant nearest to Allah—making it the premier moment to multiply dua (Sahih Muslim 482)?
optionsEn: While walking quickly out the masjid door
Immediately before saying Takbirat al-Ihram
In prostration (Sujud): 'The closest a servant comes to his Lord is while he is in prostration, so increase your dua therein!'
Only during sitting between rak‘ahs
explanationEn: Putting your forehead humbly on the floor opens the closest intimacy with Al-‘Aliyy Al-A‘la.

questionEn: Which hidden weekly hour on Friday did the Prophet ﷺ promise never fails a Muslim standing in prayer asking Allah for something good (Sahih al-Bukhari 935 / Muslim 852)?
optionsEn: Only midnight between Wednesday and Thursday
Strictly at 9:00 AM on Tuesdays

The Hour of Acceptance on Friday—with the strongest scholarly views placing it either in the final hour after ‘Asr right before Maghrib sunset, or from when the Imam sits on the Minbar until Jumu‘ah Salah finishes
Only during rainy Fridays in winter
explanationEn: Dedicating both Jumu‘ah prayer focus AND the quiet hour before Friday's Maghrib sunset ensures you catch that golden weekly window!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 935 / Sahih Muslim 852 / Sunan Abi Dawud 1048

questionEn: According to Sunan Abi Dawud 521 & Tirmidhi 212, what happens to any dua made during the interval between the Adhan and the Iqamah?
optionsEn: It is delayed until the following month
It is never rejected ('Ad-du‘a'u baynal-adhani wal-iqamati la yuradd')
It counts only if whispered in Madinah
It is reserved only for the Imam
explanationEn: Arriving at the mosque early (or pausing right after the Adhan at home) turns waiting into guaranteed answered dua.

questionEn: In Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3499, when the Prophet ﷺ was asked 'Which dua is most likely to be heard?', what two times did he name?
optionsEn: Only while boarding ships
Only once a year on Muharram 10th
In the depths of the last part of the night (jawf al-layl al-akhir) and at the end of the obligatory prayers (dubur as-salawat al-maktubat)
Only during noon marketplace breaks
explanationEn: Note 'dubur as-salawat' includes both right before Salam (end of Tashahhud) and right after Salam—make both radiant with dua!

questionEn: According to Sunan Abi Dawud 2540 & Mustadrak al-Hakim, which two moments—one occurring five times daily and one occurring with weather—are never or rarely rejected?
optionsEn: At the time of the call to prayer (Adhan) and when rain is falling (tahta al-matar / ‘inda nuzulil-ghayth)
Right after oversleeping past sunrise
During thunderless drought afternoons
While arguing loudly in markets
explanationEn: Next time rain taps your window, pause whatever you are doing for 30 seconds to say 'Allahumma sayyiban nafi‘an' and pour out your deepest prayers!

questionEn: Which three people's duas are explicitly guaranteed never to be rejected according to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3598 & Ibn Majah 1752?
optionsEn: The fasting person until/when he breaks fast (as-sa'imu hatta yuftir / ‘inda fitrih), the just ruler (al-imamul-‘adil), and the oppressed person (da‘watul-mazlum)
The wealthiest merchant, the tallest warrior, and the loudest poet
Only elderly scholars over eighty
Only residents of Makkah during winter
explanationEn: Notice how Allah lifts the oppressed person's dua right above the clouds declaring: 'By My Might, I will surely help you, even after a while!'

questionEn: On Laylat al-Qadr—which falls in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan—why did the Prophet ﷺ teach ‘A'ishah (RA) 'Allahumma innaka ‘afuwwun tuhibbul-‘afwa fa‘fu ‘anni' rather than a worldly checklist?
optionsEn: Because only two words fit on Laylat al-Qadr
Because asking for family health is forbidden on Laylat al-Qadr
Because complete pardon (‘afw) erases sins so thoroughly that every gate of mercy in this world and eternal Paradise opens wide!
Because forgiveness cannot be asked on other nights
explanationEn: Still feel free to add all your personal, family, and Ummah prayers alongside 'Allahumma innaka ‘afuwwun...' throughout the last ten nights.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the moment a person drinks Zamzam water?
optionsEn: Only valid if drunk in midnight darkness
Only thirst relief—never spiritual requests
Prohibited for non-pilgrims back home
Ma'u Zamzama lima shuriba lah ('The water of Zamzam is for whatever purpose it is drunk for' — Sunan Ibn Majah 3062), making it a sacred moment for sincere dua
explanationEn: Whether sipped inside Makkah or poured gently from a bottle gifted at home, pause for heartfelt dua before drinking Zamzam!

questionEn: What condition did the Prophet ﷺ attach to the promise that Allah answers a believer's dua when waking at night ('La ilaha illAllah...') or in Qiyam al-Layl (Sahih al-Bukhari 1154)?
optionsEn: Staying awake until afternoon
Reciting an entire juz before asking
Walking outside to count stars
Sincerity and faith—simply remembering Allah upon waking briefly at night and calling upon Him before going back to sleep or praying
explanationEn: Even waking at 3:30 AM for thirty seconds gives you access to the night's accepted hour (Sahih Muslim 757).

questionEn: Why does the Prophet ﷺ specifically warn oppressors regarding the dua of the oppressed (al-mazlum), even if the oppressed person is weak or even non-Muslim (Musnad Ahmad 12549)?
optionsEn: Because apologies never heal injustice
Because Allah helps only wealthy victims
Because angels record grievances only once a year
Because there is NO veil/barrier between the cry of the oppressed and Allah ('laysa baynaha wa baynallahi hijab')—Allah defends justice above all!
explanationEn: Fearing the cry of anyone we might wrong—workers, spouses, employees, neighbors—keeps us scrupulously fair and gentle.

questionEn: In Sunan Abi Dawud 1495 & Nasa'i 1300, when the Prophet ﷺ heard a companion open his dua with 'Allahumma inni as'aluka bi-anna lakal-hamd, la ilaha illa Antal-Mannan, badi‘us-samawati wal-ard, ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram, ya Hayyu ya Qayyum', what did the Prophet ﷺ exclaim?
optionsEn: He has called upon Allah by His Greatest Name (Ismillahil-A‘zam), by which when He is called He responds, and when He is asked He gives!
That wording applies only on Arafah
Shorten it to one single word next time
He spoke too many praises before asking
explanationEn: Memorizing this opening praise ('Al-Mannan, Originator of Heavens and Earth, Lord of Majesty and Honor, Ever-Living, Sustainer') enriches every urgent dua.

questionEn: In Sunan Abi Dawud 1493 & Tirmidhi 3475, what second wording did the Prophet ﷺ also identify as invoking Allah's Greatest Name (Ism Allah al-A‘zam)?
optionsEn: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma inni as'aluka bi-anni ashhadu annaka Antallahu la ilaha illa Antal-Ahadus-Samad, alladhi lam yalid wa lam yulad wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: Echoing Surah Al-Ikhlas directly inside your opening invocation grounds your plea in absolute Tawhid.

questionEn: In Sunan Abi Dawud 1496 & Tirmidhi 3478, which two Qur'anic verses did Asma' bint Yazid (RA) narrate contain Allah's Greatest Name?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Masad and Surah Al-Kawthar
Surah Al-Fil and Surah Quraysh
Surah Al-‘Asr and Surah At-Takathur
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:163 ('Wa ilahukum ilahun wahid, la ilaha illa Huwar-Rahmanur-Rahim') and the opening of Surah Al ‘Imran 3:1–2 ('Alif-Lam-Mim, Allahu la ilaha illa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum')
explanationEn: Notice the recurring Divine Names across these narrations: Allah, Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum, Al-Ahad As-Samad, Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim!

questionEn: What frequent Prophetic ending phrase did the Prophet ﷺ urge clinging to continuously in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3525 ('Alizzu bi-...')?
optionsEn: Use only numbers instead of Names
Alizzu bi-'Allahu a‘lam' only
Never repeat any Name twice
Alizzu bi-'Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram' ('Hold fast/cling constantly to: O Possessor of Majesty and Honor!')
explanationEn: Calling upon 'Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram' balances awe of Allah's majesty (Jalal) with tender hope in His generosity (Ikram).

questionEn: When Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ 'We already know how to greet you with Salam, so how should we send Salah (blessings) upon you?', what wording did the Prophet ﷺ teach (Sahih al-Bukhari 3370 / Muslim 406)?
optionsEn: Say 'SubhanAllah' thirty-three times instead
Greet only in silent thought without moving lips
Salawat Ibrahimiyyah: 'Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa ‘ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ‘ala Ibrahima wa ‘ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid; Allahumma barik ‘ala Muhammadin...'
Write his name onto stone pillars only
explanationEn: Salawat Ibrahimiyyah—recited in every single Salah during final Tashahhud—connects the family of Muhammad ﷺ to the blessed legacy of Prophet Ibrahim (AS).

questionEn: Why does Salawat Ibrahimiyyah ask Allah to bless Prophet Muhammad ﷺ 'just as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim' (Bukhari 3370)?
optionsEn: Because Ibrahim (AS) is the revered father of monotheistic faith and prophetic honor across generations, so linking Muhammad ﷺ and his followers to that historic blessing honors the unbroken covenant of Tawhid
Because Ibrahim (AS) invented the Arabic language
Because Muhammad ﷺ ranked below every past tribe
Because prayers were forbidden before Ibrahim
explanationEn: Note also that closing with 'innaka Hamidun Majid' invokes Allah as Praiseworthy and All-Glorious.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 408, what ten-fold return does Allah bestow upon any believer who sends ONE single Salawat upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: It counts only on Fridays
Only one minor deed is written
Sallallahu ‘alayhi ‘ashra — Allah sends blessings (mercy and praise) upon that believer TEN times!
It applies only inside Madinah
explanationEn: And Sunan an-Nasa'i 1297 adds that ten sins are erased and the believer is elevated ten ranks in Paradise for each single Salawat!

questionEn: In Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2457, when Ubayy ibn Ka‘b (RA) asked how much of his personal dua time he should dedicate to sending Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ—eventually offering ALL of it—what did the Prophet ﷺ promise him?
optionsEn: Idhan tukfa hammak wa yughfara laka dhanbuk ('Then your anxieties/worries will be sufficed, and your sins will be forgiven!')
Wait until next Ramadan before praying for yourself
Never ask Allah for forgiveness directly
Dedicate no more than one percent of your prayer
explanationEn: Filling your quiet prayer hours with love and Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ makes Allah take care of your unspoken worries directly.

questionEn: Which day and night of the week did the Prophet ﷺ explicitly command sending abundant Salawat upon him because our Salawat are presented directly to him (Sunan Abi Dawud 1047)?
optionsEn: Yawm al-Jumu‘ah and Laylat al-Jumu‘ah (Friday and Thursday night/Friday night)
Strictly once every leap year
Only Wednesday afternoons
Only the last Tuesday of Muharram
explanationEn: Making Friday a day of Surah Al-Kahf, abundant Salawat, and pre-Maghrib dua brings tremendous weekly light.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1047 / Sunan Ibn Majah 1085

questionEn: Who did the Prophet ﷺ describe as 'the stingy/miserly person' (al-bakhil) in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3546?
optionsEn: Someone who eats simple food
Someone who gives moderate charity according to means
Someone who saves honestly for family needs
The one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings (Salawat) upon me
explanationEn: Saying 'Sallallahu ‘alayhi wa sallam' whenever hearing Muhammad's ﷺ name takes one second of love and rescues us from spiritual stinginess.

questionEn: How does your Salam and Salawat reach Prophet Muhammad ﷺ wherever you live on earth according to Sunan an-Nasa'i 1282 & Abi Dawud 2041?
optionsEn: Allah has angels traveling across the earth specifically to convey the Salam of his Ummah to him—and Allah returns his soul to him so he returns the greeting of peace!
It requires mailing written scrolls to Madinah
It works only during Dhul-Hijjah
Only pilgrims standing inside Madinah can send Salam
explanationEn: Every 'As-salamu ‘alayka ayyuhan-Nabiyyu' in Tashahhud and every Salawat at home travels on angelic wings straight to Madinah.

questionEn: What severe reminder did Jibril (AS) bring—and the Prophet ﷺ say 'Amin' to—regarding someone whose parent(s) reach old age or who hears the Prophet's ﷺ name without sending Salawat (Sahih Ibn Hibban / Tirmidhi 3545)?
optionsEn: May he eat unripe dates for a month

May he be humbled in dust who hears the Prophet's ﷺ name and fails to send Salawat, who sees Ramadan pass without gaining forgiveness, or who has elderly parents and fails to enter Paradise through serving them!
May he travel abroad without luggage
May he sleep past noon on Saturdays
explanationEn: Respecting parents, seizing Ramadan, and loving the Prophet ﷺ with Salawat form three urgent gateways to mercy.

questionEn: Immediately after concluding every obligatory prayer with Salam, what three words did the Prophet ﷺ say three times before reciting 'Allahumma Antas-Salam...' (Sahih Muslim 591)?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka once
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk
Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah
SubhanAllah thirty-three times first
explanationEn: Asking forgiveness right after finishing Salah admits that even our best prayer had wandering thoughts and fell short of Allah's majesty!

questionEn: Right after saying 'Astaghfirullah' three times after Salah, what peace-filled praise follows in Sahih Muslim 591?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram ('O Allah, You are Peace and from You comes peace; Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor')
Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
explanationEn: Notice how long the Prophet ﷺ initially sat facing the Qiblah: long enough to say this concise Salam dua before turning warmly to face his companions!

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 844 & Muslim 593, what powerful declaration of divine sovereignty did the Prophet ﷺ recite after every obligatory Salah regarding giving and withholding?
optionsEn: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir; Allahumma la mani‘a lima a‘tayta, wa la mu‘tiya lima mana‘ta, wa la yanfa‘u dhal-jaddi minkal-jadd
Fortune belongs strictly to kings and merchants
Nobody can help neighbors in need
Hard work alone forces outcomes without Allah
explanationEn: Confessing 'None can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and worldly wealth/rank ('al-jadd') cannot benefit against Your decree' frees the heart from chasing people.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 594, what post-Salah remembrance attributed to Ibn az-Zubayr (RA) praises Allah's beauty ('wa lahuth-thana'ul-hasan') even when opposing disbelief?
optionsEn: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir; la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah; la ilaha illallahu wa la na‘budu illa iyyah; lahun-ni‘matu wa lahul-fadlu wa lahuth-thana'ul-hasan; la ilaha illallahu mukhlisina lahud-dina wa law karihal-kafirun
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdika only
explanationEn: Affirming that Allah owns every grace, bounty, and finest praise strengthens sincerity after every Fard prayer.

questionEn: What is the reward promised in Sahih Muslim 597 for reciting SubhanAllah 33x, Alhamdulillah 33x, Allahu Akbar 33x, and completing the 100th with 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay'in qadir' after EVERY obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: It counts only once a week on Fridays
It counts only when counted with emerald beads
It replaces the next prayer
His sins are forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea (mithla zabadil-bahr)
explanationEn: Whether counted on your right-hand fingers (as the Prophet ﷺ taught the women companions in Abu Dawud 1501!) or Duya's Tasbih tracker, this takes barely 90 seconds after Salah.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ specifically encourage counting post-Salah Tasbih on one's fingers ('Wa‘qidna bil-anamil') in Sunan Abi Dawud 1501 & Tirmidhi 3583?
optionsEn: Because fingers grow longer when counting
Because only left-hand fingers count
Fa-innahunna mas'ulatun mustantaqat ('For indeed, the fingers will be questioned and made to testify [for you on the Day of Judgment]!')
Because pebbles are prohibited inside cities
explanationEn: Using your own fingers in Tasbih turns your hands into joyful witnesses on Judgment Day!

questionEn: What shorter, busy-day authentic Sunnah variation of post-Salah Tasbih is recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari 6329 & an-Nasa'i 1348-1350?
optionsEn: Say Amin once and run out the door
SubhanAllah 10 times, Alhamdulillah 10 times, and Allahu Akbar 10 times after each obligatory prayer—bringing 150 on the tongue daily and 1,500 on the Scale!
Say Allahu Akbar once at sunset
Skip Tasbih completely on workdays
explanationEn: Knowing the 10/10/10, 25/25/25/25 (Tahlil included, Nasa'i 1350), 33/33/34, and 33/33/33+Tahlil variations gives flexibility without ever abandoning post-Salah dhikr!

questionEn: What remarkable promise did the Prophet ﷺ give in Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra 9928 for reciting Ayat al-Kursi right after every obligatory Salah?
optionsEn: He is excused from fasting Ramadan
Nothing stands between him and entering Paradise except death ('Lam yamna‘hu min dukhulil-jannati illa an yamut')
He will never feel hungry during travel
His debts double in value
explanationEn: Taking 25 seconds after each of the five daily prayers to recite Ayat al-Kursi builds an unmistakable bridge to Jannah.

questionEn: How many times did the Prophet ﷺ instruct ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir (RA) to recite the Three Quls (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas) after every obligatory prayer according to Sunan Abi Dawud 1523 (and after Fajr & Maghrib)?
optionsEn: Ten times only on Wednesdays
Only before Wudu begins
Never after Fajr prayer
Once after Dhuhr, ‘Asr, and ‘Isha; and three times after Fajr and Maghrib (linking post-Salah adhkar with morning and evening protection)
explanationEn: Pairing Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas with Ayat al-Kursi seals every Salah with Tawhid and spiritual immunity.

questionEn: In Sunan Abi Dawud 1522, what three things did the Prophet ﷺ hold Mu‘adh ibn Jabal's (RA) hand warmly and tell him NEVER to skip saying at the end of every prayer?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma a‘inni ‘ala dhikrika, wa shukrika, wa husni ‘ibadatik ('O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You excellently')
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
explanationEn: Notice this can be recited right before Salam at the end of Tashahhud or right after Salam—either way, never miss it!

questionEn: When ‘A'ishah (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ for a single all-encompassing supplication (Jawami‘ al-Du‘a), what sweeping masterpiece did he teach her in Sunan Ibn Majah 3846?
optionsEn: Rabbana anzil ‘alayna ma'idah
Allahumma inni as'aluka minal-khayri kullihi, ‘ajilihi wa ajilihi, ma ‘alimtu minhu wa ma lam a‘lam; wa a‘udhu bika minash-sharri kullihi, ‘ajilihi wa ajilihi, ma ‘alimtu minhu wa ma lam a‘lam...
Ask only for three gold coins and quiet sleep
Ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir
explanationEn: It asks for ALL good—immediate and future, known and unknown—and refuge from ALL evil, then asks for Paradise and everything bringing us near it in word or deed, and everything Muhammad ﷺ asked for!

questionEn: In that same sweeping Jawami‘ dua taught to ‘A'ishah (RA) (Ibn Majah 3846), what remarkable closing petition handles every decree Allah writes for you?
optionsEn: Erase every decree that requires patience
Tell me every hidden future date tomorrow
Wa as'aluka an taj‘ala kulla qada'in qadaytahu li khayra ('And I ask You to make every single decree You have decreed for me turn out to be good!')
Exempt me from all earthly choices
explanationEn: Even unexpected twists and delays become pathways of mercy when Allah turns every decree into khayr!

questionEn: When a newly converted Bedouin asked the Prophet ﷺ what brief words he should say since he could not memorize long supplications yet (Sahih Muslim 2697), what five-word gem did the Prophet ﷺ teach him?
optionsEn: Allahummaghfir li, warhamni, wahdini, wa ‘afini, warzuqni ('O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide for me')—explaining: 'Indeed these gather your worldly life and your Hereafter!'
Keep silent until next year
Repeat your tribe's name thrice
SubhanAllah once every Friday
explanationEn: Five simple verbs—forgive, mercy, guide, heal/protect, provide—cover every earthly and eternal need of any human being.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2696, when Tariq ibn Ashyam (RA) asked how someone should ask Allah after newly accepting Islam, what four-word core did the Prophet ﷺ give alongside 'Allahummaghfir li warhamni wahdini warzuqni'?
optionsEn: Wait forty days before speaking
Recite tribal poetry before prayer
Ask only for fast horses and silver
Forgiveness, Mercy, Guidance, and Provision (plus ‘Afiyah in Muslim 2697)—first praising Allah with 'SubhanAllah, wal-Hamdulillah, wa la ilaha illAllah, wallahu Akbar'
explanationEn: Every new Muslim can start praying from Day 1 with complete confidence using these five universal words.

questionEn: Which widely cherished pocket compilation of authentic Qur'anic and Sunnah duas—translated into dozens of languages worldwide—is titled 'Hisn al-Muslim' (Fortress of the Muslim)?
optionsEn: A 12th-century travelogue of Andalusia
A collection of pre-Islamic desert poetry
The compilation authored by Shaykh Sa‘id ibn ‘Ali ibn Wahf al-Qahtani (an abridgment of his larger scholarly work Adh-Dhikr wad-Du‘a' wal-‘Ilaj bir-Ruqa)
A medieval treatise on astronomy
explanationEn: Hisn al-Muslim organizes verified adhkar from waking up to sleeping, travel, Hajj, illness, weather, and grief into clear daily chapters.

questionEn: In Imam al-Nawawi's classic 'Al-Adhkar' and Shaykh al-Qahtani's 'Hisn al-Muslim', why is verifying authentic Hadith sources emphasized alongside devotion?
optionsEn: Because personal duas outside books are prohibited
Because non-authentic quotes give double reward
Because only scholars may open dua books
Because worshipping Allah using the exact verified words taught by His Messenger ﷺ protects Tawhid, ensures precision of meaning, and keeps innovation out of sacred habits
explanationEn: Loving authenticity while keeping personal heartfelt dua alive balances Prophetic accuracy with personal intimacy.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach asking Allah to set right our religion, livelihood, and final return?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka Rabbana
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Allahumma aslih li dini alladhi huwa ‘ismatu amri, wa aslih li dunyaya allati fiha ma‘ashi, wa aslih li akhirati allati fiha ma‘adi...
explanationEn: Calling our religion '‘ismatu amri' ('the safeguard of my affairs') shows that faith is not one compartment among many—it protects everything else.

questionEn: What short phrase did the Prophet ﷺ often include in his comprehensive duas asking Allah for steadfastness and joy in Paradise?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni as'alukal-fawza fil-qada', wa nuzulash-shuhada', wa ‘ayshas-su‘ada', wan-nasra ‘alal-a‘da' (or asking Allah for 'Jannat al-Firdaws al-a‘la' per Sahih al-Bukhari 2790)
Asking for worldly kingdoms without peace
Avoiding asking for high ranks out of false modesty
Asking only for the lowest gate of Paradise
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ expressly encouraged aiming high in dua: 'When you ask Allah, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle and highest part of Paradise!'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ encourage believers in Sahih al-Bukhari 2790 to ask specifically for 'Al-Firdaws al-A‘la' (the highest Paradise) rather than settling for less?
optionsEn: Because only martyrs enter Al-Firdaws
Because asking for Al-Firdaws replaces Salah
Because lower levels of Paradise do not exist
Because Allah's treasures never run low, and aspiring to Al-Firdaws—above which is the Throne of the Most Merciful—inspires higher character and sincere devotion
explanationEn: Dream big in dua—you are asking the Infinite Owner of the Heavens and Earth!

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about how long a believer can keep repeating a righteous dua—never giving up even after years?
optionsEn: Change religion if delays occur
Stop asking after three days if nothing changed
Keep asking patiently without haste—for Allah responds to the patient supplicant in one of three merciful ways, and never grows tired of your voice until you grow tired of asking!
Repeat only once per lunar year
explanationEn: Prophet Zakariyya (AS) prayed for a child into white-haired old age before Yahya (AS) arrived—and Allah praised him for never losing hope!

questionEn: What gentle dua asks Allah to make our deeds end beautifully before death?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha

Allahummaj‘al khayra ‘umri akhirahu, wa khayra ‘amali khawatimahu, wa khayra ayyami yawma alqaka fih ('O Allah, make the best part of my life its end, the best of my deeds their closing deeds, and the best of my days the Day I meet You')
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Make my youth idle and my old age wealthy
explanationEn: Because deeds are judged by their endings (al-a‘malu bil-khawatim), praying for a luminous closing chapter keeps us mindful in every age.
reference: Al-Mu‘jam al-Awsat / Ibn as-Sunni / Bukhari 6493 principle

questionEn: What profound reminder about endings in Sahih al-Bukhari 6493 motivates that prayer for a good ending (husn al-khatimah)?
optionsEn: Forgiveness closes after age forty
Innamal-a‘malu bil-khawatim ('Indeed, deeds are judged by their conclusions/endings')
Only youthful deeds count before Allah
A good start excuses a careless end
explanationEn: Constantly asking Allah for 'husn al-khatimah' (a righteous ending upon La ilaha illAllah) keeps humility alive at any age.

questionEn: What short, vivid dua asks Allah for both forgiveness and wellness without leaving any loophole for heedlessness?
optionsEn: Allahummaghfir li, warhamni, wahdini, wa ‘afini, warzuqni—and in Tirmidhi 3235: 'Allahumma inni as'aluka fi‘lal-khayrat, wa tarkal-munkarat, wa hubbal-masakin...'
Keep my prayers secret from my own heart
Excuse me from helping the poor
Grant me wealth even if unlawful
explanationEn: Loving the poor ('wa hubbal-masakin') inside Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3235 keeps compassion anchored inside our spiritual aspirations!

questionEn: In that same luminous Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) (Tirmidhi 3235), what astonishing gift did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah for regarding how to love Him?
optionsEn: Let me postpone repentance until winter
Grant me indifference toward righteous friends

Wa as'aluka hubbaka, wa hubba man yuhibbuka, wa hubba ‘amalin yuqarribuni ila hubbik ('I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the love of every deed that brings me closer to Your love')
Grant me earthly applause above all
explanationEn: Notice the three-fold ripple: loving Allah, loving Allah-lovers, and loving the habits that draw us near to Him!

questionEn: In Tirmidhi 3235, what subtle request concludes that same dua when a community faces spiritual trial (fitnah)?
optionsEn: Wa idha aradta bi-‘ibadika fitnatan faqbidni ilayka ghayra maftun ('And if You intend a trial for Your servants, take me to You without being put to trial/corrupted in faith!')
Let me profit from community division
Delay all faith until trials pass
Keep me indifferent to trials of faith
explanationEn: Preferring death with intact faith over living through spiritual corruption shows how dearly the Prophet ﷺ valued pure Iman.

questionEn: What short dua in Sahih Muslim 2717 & al-Bukhari 7383 did the Prophet ﷺ say when seeking refuge in Allah's Honor from ever being led astray?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bi-‘izzatika la ilaha illa Anta an tudillani; Antal-Hayyulladhi la yamut, wal-jinnu wal-insu yamutun
explanationEn: Seeking refuge in Allah's Mighty Honor ('bi-‘izzatika')—remembering He alone is Ever-Living while jinn and humans perish—anchors guidance in pure Tawhid.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to swear with emphasis or express awe in speech, which Name of Allah did he most famously invoke (Sahih al-Bukhari 6628)?
optionsEn: La wa Muqallibil-qulub ('No, by the Turner of hearts!')—often turning ordinary oaths into reminders of Allah's tenderness over our hearts
By the desert stars and winds
By his forefathers' swords
By the gold of Makkah
explanationEn: Even in everyday conversation, calling Allah 'Muqallib al-Qulub' reminds listeners who steadies human hearts.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ warn regarding swearing oaths by anyone or anything OTHER than Allah (such as 'by my mother's life' or 'by the Kaaba')?
optionsEn: Swearing by ancestors brings extra barakah
Casual oaths hold no spiritual weight
Swearing by mountains is Sunnah
Whoever swears by anything other than Allah has fallen into shirk (or minor shirk/disobedience)—so swear ONLY by Allah or remain silent!
explanationEn: Keeping our tongues pure in oaths honors Allah's exclusive majesty alongside sincere dua.

questionEn: What three-part phrase in Sahih Muslim 2698 did the Prophet ﷺ tell a man was BETTER than worldly camels, pearls, or gold?
optionsEn: Debating endlessly without acting
Hoarding silver chests beneath floors
Traveling solely for sightseeing
Reading or teaching even two verses from the Book of Allah, OR gathering in a mosque remembering Allah, OR keeping daily Tasbih/Tahmid/Tahlil/Takbir alive!
explanationEn: Priceless eternal wealth is available free to everyone with a sincere heart and a moving tongue.

questionEn: What short four-word dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach his uncle al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib (RA) when al-‘Abbas asked: 'Teach me something I should ask Allah for'?
optionsEn: Ask solely for political power over Syria

Salillahal-‘afiyah ('Ask Allah for well-being/soundness — Allahumma inni as'alukal-‘afiyah!')—and when al-‘Abbas came back days later asking again, the Prophet ﷺ repeated: 'O uncle of the Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for ‘Afiyah in this world and the Hereafter!'
Ask for exemption from charity
Ask for magical control over rain
explanationEn: That repeated emphasis teaches that health, safety, faith, and peace—‘Afiyah—outweigh every dramatic wish.

questionEn: What concise dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach ‘Imran ibn Husayn's (RA) father Husayn right when Husayn embraced Islam (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3483)?
optionsEn: Allahumma alhimni rushdi, wa a‘idhni min sharri nafsi ('O Allah, inspire me with my right guidance, and protect me from the evil of my own soul')
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
explanationEn: Even before embracing Islam, Husayn answered 'How many gods do you worship?' with six on earth and one in heaven—and upon becoming Muslim, received this laser-focused two-line gem!

questionEn: In Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3502, what tender prayer did the Prophet ﷺ make asking Allah to keep his sight and hearing sound throughout life?
optionsEn: Allahumma matti‘ni bi-sam‘i wa basari waj‘alhumal-waritha minni ('O Allah, let me enjoy my hearing and my sight [throughout life], and make them my inheritors [keeping them sound until death]')
Grant me wealth without eyesight
Silence my ears from advice
Take away my senses before old age
explanationEn: Recited in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3502, this moving dua asks Allah to keep our eyes and ears vibrant until our final day so we never lose access to Qur'an and prayer!

questionEn: In that same Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3502 dua ('Allahummas-qim lana min khashyatika...'), what five extraordinary spiritual protections does the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah to 'apportion' (iqsim lana) for us?
optionsEn: 1) Fear of You enough to bar us from disobeying You; 2) Obedience to You enough to reach Your Paradise; 3) Certainty (yaqin) enough to make earthly calamities feel light; 4) Enjoyment of hearing, sight, and strength as long as You keep us alive; and 5) Making our calamity NOT in our religion!
Fame in five capitals
Five chests of gold, five orchards, five ships, five palaces, and five crowns
Exemption from every test, fast, charity, travel, and effort
explanationEn: Praying 'wa la taj‘al musibatana fi dinina' ('and do not make our calamity be in our religion!') puts every financial or health setback into calm eternal perspective.

questionEn: Why is 'wa la taj‘alid-dunya akbara hammina wa la mablagha ‘ilmina' (also inside Tirmidhi 3502) such a liberating daily prayer for modern professionals and students?
optionsEn: Because it tells workers to quit their jobs
Because it forbids studying science or medicine
Because only monks avoid worldly worries
Asking Allah NOT to make worldly success our biggest worry or the ceiling of our knowledge keeps ambition healthy without letting it enslave our soul!
explanationEn: Islam honors excellence at work while refusing to let worldly metrics become our god.

questionEn: What concise refuge dua asks Allah for safety from four painful spiritual and moral conditions?
optionsEn: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-‘ajzi wal-kasal, wal-jubni wal-bukhl, wal-harami wa ‘adhabil-qabr
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
explanationEn: And in Sunan an-Nasa'i 5466, the Prophet ﷺ also sought refuge from 'qalbin la yakhsha‘' (a hard heart), 'nafsin la tashba‘' (an insatiable ego), '‘ilmin la yanfa‘' (useless knowledge), and 'du‘a'in la yusma‘' (unheard dua).

questionEn: What four harrowing afflictions did the Prophet ﷺ seek refuge from in Sahih al-Bukhari 6347 & Muslim 2707 alongside 'min su'il-qada''?
optionsEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6347 & Muslim 2707, he sought refuge from: 'jahdil-bala', wa darakish-shaqa', wa su'il-qada', wa shamatatil-a‘da'' (crushing trial, overtaking misery, an evil turn of decree, and malicious rejoicing of enemies)
From neighbors greeting warmly
From rainy Fridays and cool evenings
From modest meals and walking to prayer
explanationEn: Four short phrases in Sahih al-Bukhari 6347 shield against overwhelming burnout, despair, harsh outcomes, and mockery.

questionEn: What gentle dua asks Allah to unite believers' hearts and mend broken communities?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Allahumma allif bayna qulubina, wa aslih dhata baynina, wahdina subulas-salam, wa najjina minaz-zulumati ilan-nur... (from Ibn Mas‘ud's narration in Abu Dawud 969 / Mustadrak)
Divide households into competing camps
explanationEn: Praying 'O Allah, reconcile our hearts and guide us to paths of peace' makes you a peacemaker in family and community alike.

questionEn: When feeling spiritually cold, dry, or distracted in prayer, what brief Prophetic plea taught in Sunan an-Nasa'i 1305 asks Allah to sweeten worship?
optionsEn: Skip morning adhkar when busy
Wait until next Ramadan before praying attentively
Asking Allah for 'khashyataka fil-ghaybi wash-shahadah' alongside 'ladhdhatan-nazari ila wajhik, wash-shawqa ila liqa'ik' ('the delight of gazing upon Your Countenance and eager longing to meet You')
Replace Salah with loud music
explanationEn: Longing to meet Allah turns Salah from mechanical repetition into love.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in Sahih Muslim 2674 about the reward of someone who guides another person to a righteous dua, dhikr, or good deed?
optionsEn: Sharing duas reduces your own credit by half
Only the original scholar receives reward
Only spoken sermons count—never digital apps or messages
Man dalla ‘ala khayrin fa-lahu mithlu ajri fa‘ilih ('Whoever guides someone to goodness will have a reward equal to the one who does it!')
explanationEn: Sharing an authentic dua card, Tasbih habit, or Seerah lesson with a friend lets their every repetition add light to your scale too!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ warn against inventing rigid, unverified numbers or unauthentic rituals in worship while keeping heartfelt spontaneous dua wide open?
optionsEn: Because spontaneous tears invalidate Salah

Because specific counts/times (like 33x Tasbih or Friday afternoon) are fixed strictly by revelation (Tawqifi), whereas personal spontaneous dua in your own heartfelt words has zero rigid script limit!
Because only 10 words exist in Islam
Because personal dua outside books is banned
explanationEn: Distinguishing fixed Sunnah adhkar (followed cleanly as taught) from wide-open personal munajat (pouring out your heart freely) gives both accuracy and emotional freedom.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ teach ‘A'ishah (RA) to view Allah's gentleness (ar-rifq) in every interaction—including how we call others to dua and prayer?
optionsEn: Criticize guests publicly for forgetting adhkar
Indeed, Allah is Gentle (Rafiq) and loves gentleness in ALL affairs—giving through gentleness what He never gives through harshness!
Force family members awake with anger
Mock beginners who mispronounce Arabic
explanationEn: Gentle encouragement draws children, spouses, and friends warmly toward Salah and daily adhkar.

questionEn: What short, empowering phrase did the Prophet ﷺ advise saying when struck by a setback or missed opportunity instead of saying 'If only I had done X, then Y would have happened' (Sahih Muslim 2664)?
optionsEn: Give up trying any new projects
QaddarAllahu wa ma sha'a fa‘al ('Allah decreed it, and whatever He wills, He does'), because 'If only...' (law) opens the door to Shaytan's paralyzing regret
Blame everyone around you for ten days
Wait passively without striving
explanationEn: Combine striving hard for what benefits you ('ihris ‘ala ma yanfa‘uk'), seeking Allah's help ('wasta‘in billah'), and never losing heart—then trusting Qadar if an outcome shifts!

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2664, what three-word encouragement right before 'wasta‘in billah' guards a believer against both laziness and regret?
optionsEn: Avoid planning altogether
Sleep until opportunities knock
Depend exclusively on luck
Ihris ‘ala ma yanfa‘uk ('Strive eagerly for whatever benefits you'), seek Allah's help, and do not feel helpless (wa la ta‘jaz)
explanationEn: True Tawakkul is active courage backed by prayer—never passive resignation.

questionEn: What brief prayer did the Prophet ﷺ say whenever seeing someone he loved leave on a mission or wanting to keep faith vibrant in a busy community?
optionsEn: Keep affection hidden in silence
Compete bitterly over small honors

Asking Allah for steadfastness, sincerity, mercy, and mutual love—remembering that 'no two people love each other for Allah except that the more beloved to Allah is the one who loves his companion more!'
Never pray for coworkers or classmates
explanationEn: Making secret dua for friends, mentors, students, and neighbors builds radiant communities.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sahih al-Bukhari 7507 (Hadith Qudsi) that a servant who commits a sin, realizes he has a Lord who forgives and holds accountable, and begs 'O my Lord, forgive my sin' is met with tender divine welcome?
optionsEn: Never ask forgiveness twice for the same weakness
Forgiveness ends permanently after the second slip

Allah says: 'My servant knows he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes to account for them; I have forgiven My servant!'—even if the servant slips again and repents sincerely repeatedly without giving up!
Hide sins by pretending perfection
explanationEn: Never let shame trick you into abandoning Istighfar—keep turning back sincerely, fighting the habit, and trusting Al-Ghaffar.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2747, how joyfully does Allah welcome a servant's sincere repentance (Tawbah) and Istighfar?
optionsEn: Only if witnessed by an entire city

More delighted than a traveler stranded in a barren desert whose camel—carrying all his food and water—ran away, who falls asleep expecting death and wakes to find his camel standing right beside him!
Reluctantly after thirty years of probation
Indifferently without notice
explanationEn: In utter ecstasy that man accidentally says 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your Lord!'—showing how deeply Allah loves when you come home to Him in dua.

questionEn: What four conditions did scholars summarize from the Qur'an and Sunnah for sincere Tawbah when making Istighfar?
optionsEn: 1) Stop the sin immediately; 2) Feel genuine remorse; 3) Resolve sincerely never to return to it; and 4) If it wronged another person's rights/property/honor, restore their right or seek their pardon!
Ignoring people whose property you took
Waiting until old age to apologize
Merely saying 'Astaghfirullah' while planning to repeat the sin tonight
explanationEn: Istighfar coupled with repairing wrongs toward people cleanses both heavenward and earthward accounts.
reference: Imam al-Nawawi, Riyad as-Salihin / Surah At-Tahrim 66:8

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2749, what astonishing truth did the Prophet ﷺ swear by Allah regarding human imperfection and Istighfar?
optionsEn: Sinless angels are the only creatures Allah loves
Anyone who sins once can never pray again
Istighfar is optional only for elders
By Him in whose Hand is my soul, if you did NOT sin, Allah would sweep you away and bring a people who sin, then seek Allah's forgiveness, and He forgives them!
explanationEn: This never encourages sinning; rather, it teaches that Allah loves the humble brokenness of a servant who keeps returning to Al-Ghafur Ar-Rahim!

questionEn: In the Prophet's ﷺ supplication after the Battle of Uhud (Musnad Ahmad 15492), what plea asks Allah to place love of faith and beauty of Islam inside our hearts?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
Ghufranaka Rabbana
Allahumma habbib ilaynal-imana wa zayyinhu fi qulubina, wa karrih ilaynal-kufra wal-fusuqa wal-‘isyan, waj‘alna minar-rashidin
explanationEn: Echoing Surah Al-Hujurat 49:7 directly, asking Allah to make faith deeply lovable and sin naturally distasteful transforms obedience from struggle into joy!
reference: Al-Adab al-Mufrad 699 / Musnad Ahmad 15492 / Surah Al-Hujurat 49:7

questionEn: In that same Uhud dua (Musnad Ahmad 15492), what humble confession opens the Prophet's ﷺ prayer for his Companions?
optionsEn: No test can ever touch Madinah

Allahumma lakal-hamdu kulluh; Allahumma la qabida lima basatta wa la basita lima qabadta... ('O Allah, to You belongs ALL praise; none can constrict what You expand, and none can expand what You constrict...')
We defeated our foes strictly by swords
Pause all prayer until winter
explanationEn: Even right after the pain of Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ stood praising Allah's total sovereignty and asking for love of Iman!

questionEn: What concise supplications—including Sahih Muslim 2722—ask Allah to grant the soul piety (taqwa) and purify the heart from hypocrisy, show-off, lying, and betrayal?
optionsEn: Allahumma ati nafsi taqwaha wa zakkiha Anta khayru man zakkaha (Sahih Muslim 2722)—alongside asking purification from hypocrisy, showing off, lying, and betrayal
Grant me praise even when insincere
Let me boast silently in crowds
Keep my flaws hidden from myself forever
explanationEn: Checking heart (nifaq), deeds (riya'), tongue (lying), and eyes (betrayal) keeps spiritual integrity crystal clear.

questionEn: What grateful Qur'anic praise—echoed by the inhabitants of Paradise in Surah Al-A‘raf—thanks Allah specifically for guiding us to Islam?
optionsEn: Guidance belongs only to birthright
I discovered truth strictly through clever debate
Thank Allah only for material wealth

Alhamdulillahilladhi hadana li-hadha wa ma kunna li-nahtadiya lawla an hadanAllah ('Praise be to Allah who guided us to this; we would never have been guided had Allah not guided us!' — Surah Al-A‘raf 7:43)
explanationEn: Recognizing Islam, Salah, and the Qur'an as pure gifts from Al-Hadi keeps gratitude radiant every single day.
