questionEn: When closing a Quran khatam (completing a full reading of the Qur'an), what authentic Sunnah approach is practiced by the Companions like Anas ibn Malik (RA)?
optionsEn: Wait forty days before making any dua

Anas (RA) gathered his family together upon finishing the Qur'an and made heartfelt, comprehensive dua for mercy, guidance, and forgiveness (Darimi 3474)—because mercy descends at the completion of the Qur'an!
Read strictly alone in secret without family
Close the mushaf silently without praying for family
explanationEn: Finishing the Qur'an with a warm family dua circle leaves a lifelong loving memory for children and elders alike.

questionEn: What authentic dua did the Prophet ﷺ say when asking Allah to keep him steady in gratitude and not turn away from remembrance?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka
Rabbighfir li wa tub ‘alayya innaka Antat-Tawwabur-Rahim—plus 'Allahumma inni as'aluka th-thabata fil-amri wal-‘azimata ‘alar-rushd' (Tirmidhi 3407)
Let me rest from worship after youth
explanationEn: Asking for firmness (thabat) and resolution upon guidance (‘azimah ‘alar-rushd) protects consistency across decades.

questionEn: Why did ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (RA) warn believers never to let their hearts grow heedless when making repeated daily duas?
optionsEn: Because fast pronunciation cancels fasting
Because the Prophet ﷺ reminded that Allah answers hearts that are awake, humble, and attentive ('min qalbin ghaflin lahin' is rejected)—so slow down just enough to mean what you whisper!
Because slow reading doubles the mandatory count
Because angels only hear loud shouting
explanationEn: Thirty seconds of deeply felt 'Allahumma inni as'alukal-jannah' moves mountains compared to five minutes of autopilot muttering.

questionEn: What gentle daily habit helps keep Arabic Sunnah duas alive if you struggle to memorize long paragraphs at once?
optionsEn: Never read translations so meaning stays mysterious

Learn ONE short Sunnah dua per week (like Sayyid al-Istighfar, Travel Dua, or 'Allahumma a‘inni ‘ala dhikrika'), understand its English meaning deeply, and tie it to its daily trigger (doorstep, car, masjid, pillow)!
Wait until retirement before starting adhkar
Try memorizing 200 long pages in one night then quit
explanationEn: Habit-stacking one short dua at a time onto daily routines makes lifelong Sunnah practice effortless and joyful.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6464 ('Most beloved deeds are consistent even if small')

questionEn: When feeling overwhelmed by how many sins or missed prayers one has from past years, what hopeful dua and Hadith Qudsi (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3540) breaks despair instantly?
optionsEn: Past years can never be forgiven
Forgiveness requires seventy years of silence

Allah declares: 'O son of Adam, so long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever you have done and I do not mind; even if your sins reached the clouds of the sky and you asked My forgiveness, I would forgive you!'
Only people without major sins are heard
explanationEn: Even if you arrive before Allah with an earth-full of sins—provided you meet Him associating zero partners with Him (Tawhid)—He meets you with an earth-full of forgiveness!

questionEn: In that same majestic Hadith Qudsi (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3540), what two wings lift a broken sinner back into Allah's embrace?
optionsEn: Hiding from mosques out of guilt
Blaming others for personal choices
Paying silver coins to strangers without repentance
Calling upon Allah and maintaining hope in Him ('ma da‘awtani wa rajawtani')—never despairing of His mercy!
explanationEn: Guilt should drive you TOWARD the prayer mat in dua, never AWAY from Allah.

questionEn: Why is ending personal duas—just like the Qur'an's Surah As-Saffat 37:180–182—with praise to Allah ('Wal-hamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin') and Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ a timeless Sunnah finish?
optionsEn: Because framing your requests between two wings of Salawat and praise (‘hamd’ at start and end) honors the Prophet's ﷺ counsel and seals your prayer in gratitude
Because Amin must never be spoken
Because only Fridays allow Salawat at the end
Because requests without Salawat are punishable sins
explanationEn: Just as you begin with 'Alhamdulillah' and Salawat, closing with Salawat and 'Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin' creates a luminous ring around every petition.

questionEn: When an Imam or friend finishes making a heartfelt supplication on behalf of the gathering, what brief Hebrew/Arabic-rooted word means 'O Allah, respond/accept!'?
optionsEn: Amin
SubhanAllah
Labbayk
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Saying 'Amin' sincerely joins your heart to the speaker's prayer—and in Sahih al-Bukhari 780, whoever's 'Amin' after Al-Fatihah coincides with the angels' 'Amin' has all past sins forgiven!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ call 'La ilaha illAllah' the heaviest scale-tipper in the famous 'Card Hadith' (Hadith al-Bitaqah, Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2639)?
optionsEn: Because deeds are never weighed on the Scale
Because scrolls were empty
Because written cards replace daily Salah intentionally

Ninety-nine giant scrolls of sins were placed on one pan of the Scale, while one tiny card bearing 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illAllah wa anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasuluh' outweighed ALL ninety-nine scrolls—for nothing outweighs Allah's Name!
explanationEn: Pure, sincere Tawhid spoken from a broken, truthful heart carries weight beyond human comprehension.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6406, what role does consistent daily dhikr play on that same Day of the Scale (Al-Mizan)?
optionsEn: Dhikr counts only when spoken by scholars
Effortless words like 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil-‘Azim' tip the Scale heavily while keeping the believer's tongue pure in daily life
Only physical weight of stone monuments counts
Scale weights are fixed at birth regardless of dhikr
explanationEn: Every commute, chore, and walk becomes an effortless opportunity to brighten your eternal Scale.

questionEn: What touching prayer did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) teach—and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ fulfill—regarding remembering Allah at the Sacred Mosque in Makkah and every mosque worldwide?
optionsEn: Combining pure Tawhid, heartfelt prayer, grateful reflection, hospitality, and compassionate dua for the whole Ummah so every masjid becomes an oasis of mercy
Turning mosques into exclusive private clubs
Closing doors to travelers and youth
Separating worship from daily mercy
explanationEn: Duas and Sunnah tie mosque, home, journey, and heart into one seamless tapestry of devotion.

questionEn: What short phrases from Surah Al ‘Imran 3:8 and Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2140 guard a believer against ever taking guidance for granted?
optionsEn: Once guided, a person can never slip
Only scholars need guidance prayers
Hearts stay steady without prayer

Allahumma la tazigh qulubana ba‘da idh hadaytana, wa ya Muqallibal-qulub thabbit qulubana ‘ala dinik ('O Allah, let not our hearts swerve after You guided us, and O Turner of hearts, keep our hearts firm upon Your religion!')
explanationEn: Even the Prophet ﷺ himself begged Allah daily to keep his heart firm upon the truth.

questionEn: When someone feels tempted to postpone starting a daily dua and adhkar routine until 'life slows down', what timeless Prophetic reminder from Sahih al-Bukhari 6416 urges starting TODAY?
optionsEn: Busy careers excuse abandoning dhikr forever
Wait until retirement before learning daily adhkar

Take advantage of five before five (Hakim / Sahih al-Jami‘ 1077)—your youth before old age, health before sickness, wealth before poverty, free time before busyness, and life before death—and 'Be in this world like a stranger or a traveler!'
Postpone morning prayers until next Ramadan
explanationEn: Starting with just three minutes after Fajr and before sleep today transforms years to come.

questionEn: How did Ibn ‘Umar (RA) expand on the Prophet's ﷺ counsel 'Be in this world like a stranger or a traveler' in Sahih al-Bukhari 6416?
optionsEn: If you reach the evening, do not expect to see the morning; and if you reach the morning, do not expect to see the evening—take from your health for your sickness, and from your life for your death!
Never sleep inside a sturdy home
Neglect your family and career completely
Stop planning honest provisions for tomorrow
explanationEn: Living with gentle urgency makes every morning and evening adhkar feel precious rather than routine.

questionEn: What Sunnah habit frames beginning and completing any noble task so Allah blesses both the effort and the outcome?
optionsEn: Rely strictly on personal luck
Begin with 'Bismillah' (and sincere niyyah), seek Allah's aid with 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah', and conclude with 'Alhamdulillah'!
Avoid praising Allah for small tasks
Begin silently without intention and boast at the end
explanationEn: Bracketing work, study, travel, and worship between 'Bismillah' and 'Alhamdulillah' turns every ordinary hour into worship.

questionEn: What short dua asks Allah to guard against being overwhelmed by debt OR humiliated by enemies?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min ghalabatid-dayn, wa ghalabatil-‘aduww, wa shamatatil-a‘da' ('O Allah, I seek refuge in You from overwhelming debt, overpowering enemies, and the gloating of foes')
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
explanationEn: Pairing financial dignity with calm strength in adversity keeps believers upright and generous.

questionEn: What serene dua in Sunan an-Nasa'i 1305 asks Allah for contentment AFTER His decree arrives ('ar-rida ba‘dal-qada')?
optionsEn: Wa as'alukar-rida ba‘dal-qada', wa bardal-‘ayshi ba‘dal-mawt ('And I ask You for contentment after decree strikes, and the coolness/peace of life after death!')
Delay patience until ease arrives
Demand answers before accepting any trial
Reject difficult outcomes silently
explanationEn: True contentment ('rida ba‘dal-qada'') isn't resignation before effort—it's trusting Allah's mercy even after unexpected news arrives.

questionEn: In Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3558, what short dua did a companion ask to learn—receiving the counsel: 'Ask Allah for ‘Afiyah'—and why did the Prophet ﷺ explain nothing equals faith except ‘Afiyah?
optionsEn: Because fame eliminates sorrow
Because wealth replaces faith
Because 'Ma u‘tiya ahadun ba‘dal-yaqini khayran minal-‘afiyah' ('No one has been given anything after certainty of faith better than well-being/soundness!')
Because travel replaces health
explanationEn: Certainty of Iman (Yaqin) and all-around well-being (‘Afiyah) are the two supreme treasures to ask Allah for daily.

questionEn: What well-known classical supplication cited in Tafsir Ibn Kathir asks Allah to show us truth as truth and grant us to follow it, and falsehood as falsehood and grant us to avoid it?
optionsEn: Allahumma arinal-haqqa haqqan warzuqnat-tiba‘ah, wa arinal-batila batilan warzuqnaj-tinabah ('O Allah, show us truth as truth and grant us to follow it, and show us falsehood as falsehood and grant us to avoid it'—attributed in classical scholarly du‘a' tradition of ‘Umar RA / Ibn Kathir)
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Let me follow popular crowds blindly
Hide difficult truths from my sight
explanationEn: Seeing truth clearly AND having the courage to follow it protects integrity in confusing times.

questionEn: What brief, tender prayer did the Prophet ﷺ say whenever a believer offered sincere hospitality or did a small favor—even giving a sip of water?
optionsEn: JazakAllahu khayran / BarakAllahu fika / Allahumma at‘im man at‘amani wasqi man saqani
Repay kindness strictly with criticism
Remain silent to show independence
Wait until next year to reply
explanationEn: Turning every everyday favor into a loving dua fills households and neighborhoods with barakah.

questionEn: What happens in the heavens according to Sahih al-Bukhari 3209 & Muslim 2637 when Allah loves a servant who worships Him sincerely and turns to Him in dua?
optionsEn: Angels hide their love until death

Allah calls Jibril saying: 'Indeed, I love so-and-so, so love him!'—then Jibril loves him and announces to the inhabitants of heaven: 'Allah loves so-and-so, so love him!'—and acceptance (al-qabul) is placed for him on earth!
The servant becomes invisible to neighbors
The servant earns exemption from Salah
explanationEn: Loving Allah quietly through Salah, Qur'an, and sincere dua brings unseen divine love radiating into human hearts around you.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ assure that whoever relieves a believer of one worldly distress (kurbah), Allah will relieve him of a distress on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Because only judges help people in distress
Because helping others reduces one's own reward
Because charity replaces personal dua
Because serving others practically—and making dua for their relief—invites Allah's direct help into our own anxieties ('Wallahu fi ‘awnil-‘abdi ma kanal-‘abdu fi ‘awni akhih')
explanationEn: Helping a friend, spouse, or stranger out of a tight spot is one of the fastest ways to unlock Allah's help in your own life.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6502 (Hadith al-Wali), how does Allah honor the servant who draws close to Him first through obligatory worship and then through abundant voluntary acts (nawafil) like dhikr, Tahajjud, and dua?
optionsEn: Allah says: 'I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks; if he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks My refuge, I will surely protect him!'
He stops needing daily Salah
He never faces any earthly test again
He receives prophetic revelation
explanationEn: Drawing close through Fard + consistent Nawafil (dhikr, Sunnah prayers, Tahajjud) makes a servant's dua overwhelmingly beloved to Allah!

questionEn: What gentle dua asks Allah for love of righteous people and forgiveness for ALL believers—living and departed?
optionsEn: Ignore believers in distant countries
Pray only for wealthy donors

Allahummaghfir lil-mu'minina wal-mu'minat, wal-muslimina wal-muslimat, al-ahya'i minhum wal-amwat ('O Allah, forgive all believing men and women, and all submitting men and women, the living among them and the deceased')
Forgive only my immediate relatives
explanationEn: Narrated by ‘Ubadah ibn as-Samit (RA) in Tabarani (authenticated by al-Albani), whoever seeks forgiveness for all believing men and women earns a good deed for EVERY believer!

questionEn: When feeling uncertain which of two equally permissible good paths to choose—say, two job offers or two charitable causes—what two Prophetic tools work together seamlessly?
optionsEn: Doing nothing forever out of fear
Flipping coins while ignoring wisdom
Salat al-Istikharah (asking Al-‘Alim Al-Qadir for guidance) combined with Shura (consulting wise, trustworthy people), then moving forward calmly with Tawakkul
Consulting star charts or palm readers
explanationEn: Istikharah + Shura + Tawakkul turns stressful crossroads into serene clarity.

questionEn: Why does the Qur'an pair 'Al-Hamd' (Praise) at the start of Surah Al-Fatihah with 'Iyyaka na‘budu wa iyyaka nasta‘in' before teaching 'Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim'?
optionsEn: Because praise replaces asking for guidance
Because Surah Al-Fatihah is only for funerals
Because it teaches the universal architecture of every Prophetic dua: first praise and glorify Allah, second affirm loyalty and dependence on Him, and third present your heartfelt request!
Because guidance cannot be requested outside Makkah
explanationEn: Every time you pray Al-Fatihah in Salah, you are literally walking through the master template of answered dua.

questionEn: In the Hadith Qudsi of Sahih Muslim 395 ('Qasamtu as-salata bayni wa bayna ‘abdi nisfayn'), how does Allah respond line by line as you recite Surah Al-Fatihah?
optionsEn: Allah responds only during Friday congregations

When you say 'Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin', Allah says 'My servant has praised Me'; at 'Ar-Rahmanir-Rahim', 'My servant has extolled Me'; at 'Maliki yawmid-din', 'My servant has glorified Me'; at 'Iyyaka na‘budu wa iyyaka nasta‘in', 'This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks!'
Only scholars receive responses during Al-Fatihah
Allah remains silent until the whole surah finishes
explanationEn: Pausing slightly at the end of each verse of Al-Fatihah—imagining Allah Himself replying to you—transforms every rak‘ah of Salah into a living conversation!

questionEn: What immediate practical effect did pausing verse-by-verse in Surah Al-Fatihah have on the Prophet's ﷺ own recitation according to Sunan Abi Dawud 4001?
optionsEn: He recited slowly and distinctly, stopping cleanly at the end of every single verse rather than rushing multiple verses into one breathless blur
He raced through all seven verses in two seconds
He whispered without moving his tongue
He skipped Al-Fatihah whenever tired
explanationEn: Slowing down Al-Fatihah by even five extra seconds lets your heart actually hear Allah's tender reply.

questionEn: Why is 'La ilaha illAllah' combined with 'SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar' called 'the best speech after the Qur'an'?
optionsEn: Because they apply only during travel
Because they replace learning the Qur'an

Because those four phrases summarize the entire cosmos's relationship with Allah: He is free of flaw (SubhanAllah), worthy of all thanks (Alhamdulillah), One without partner (La ilaha illAllah), and Greater than everything (Allahu Akbar)
Because they are the longest Arabic sentences
explanationEn: Living by those four words keeps wonder, gratitude, loyalty, and perspective alive all day.

questionEn: What gentle dua asks Allah to cover our shortcomings in this world and on the Day of Judgment?
optionsEn: Allahummas-tur ‘awrati wa amin raw‘ati ('O Allah, conceal my faults/vulnerabilities and calm my fears')—and remember Sahih Muslim 2590: whoever covers a Muslim's fault in this world, Allah will cover his faults in this world and the Hereafter!
Gossip privately about neighbors' flaws
Expose others' mistakes publicly to feel superior
Ignore your own repentance
explanationEn: Just as we beg Al-Sattir to conceal our private slips, practicing discretion and mercy toward others earns His loving cover.

questionEn: What brief, comprehensive Prophetic duas in Sahih Muslim 2697 & Sunan Abi Dawud 850 unite asking for forgiveness, mercy, guidance, well-being, and provision?
optionsEn: All of them converge in 'Allahummaghfir li warhamni wahdini wa ‘afini warzuqni' (Muslim 2697) and 'Rabbighfir li warhamni wajburni warfa‘ni wahdini wa ‘afini warzuqni' (between the two sujuds)!
Only merchants need ask for provision
Only sick people ask for ‘afiyah
Only scholars ask for guidance
explanationEn: Mastering those few concise Arabic phrases gives any Muslim a complete prayer toolkit for Salah, travel, and life.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ was asked what deed most commonly admits people into Paradise, what two things did he join together?
optionsEn: Boastful debates and loud speeches
Traveling without companions
Taqwallah wa husnul-khuluq ('Fear/mindfulness of Allah and good character')
Hoarding wealth and avoiding neighbors
explanationEn: Good character—warmth, patience, truthfulness, generosity, and forgivingness—is the living fruit of sincere dua.

questionEn: When closing a personal dua list at night, on Friday, or during Umrah/Hajj, why is including parents, teachers, spouses, children, sick friends, and the entire struggling Ummah a mark of Prophetic generosity?
optionsEn: Because praying for others shrinks your own share

Because Prophet Muhammad ﷺ consistently prayed for his Ummah—even weeping through entire nights reciting 'My Ummah, My Ummah!' (Sahih Muslim 202)—and praying for others draws angelic 'Amin, and for you the like thereof!'
Because only Imams may pray for the community
Because private prayers must stay strictly selfish
explanationEn: Expanding your heart in dua to embrace family, neighbors, and the global Ummah mirrors the boundless mercy of Muhammad ﷺ.

questionEn: What deeply moving Hadith Qudsi in Sahih Muslim 202 shows the Prophet's ﷺ tearful dua for YOU across centuries?
optionsEn: Only martyrs receive his care
When he wept reciting Ibrahim's and ‘Isa's words for his people, Allah sent Jibril to tell him: 'Indeed, We will please you regarding your Ummah and will NEVER grieve/disappoint you!'
Allah rejected intercession for sinners
Allah told him prayers apply only to Madinah's generation
explanationEn: Knowing Prophet Muhammad ﷺ wept in dua for his Ummah's forgiveness fills our Salawat upon him with lifelong love and gratitude.

questionEn: Which four foundational remembrance phrases—combining gratitude, Salawat, pure Tawhid, and repentance—anchor a believer's daily worship?
optionsEn: Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-‘alamin, Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa ‘ala ali Muhammad, La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, Astaghfirullaha wa atubu ilayh
Relying solely on human applause
Complaining daily until conditions look perfect
Postponing gratitude until next year
explanationEn: Gratitude, Salawat, Tawhid, and Istighfar form the four golden strings of a heart tuned constantly to Allah.

questionEn: When learning and practicing all these Duas & Sunnahs in daily life, what single secret ensures they never turn into dry mechanical checklists?
optionsEn: Separating dhikr from ethics at home and work
Racing through 200 phrases as quickly as possible without thinking
Keeping score solely to boast to friends

Presence of heart (hudur al-qalb): knowing WHO you are speaking to—Al-Sami‘ Al-Qarib Al-Karim—understanding the meaning of what you say, and pairing your words with gratitude, patience, and kindness to creation
explanationEn: When your tongue and heart agree together before Allah, every dua becomes a living doorway of peace.

questionEn: Which surah is it Sunnah to recite every Friday (Yawm al-Jumu‘ah) as a spiritual light from one Friday to the next?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kahf (18)
Surah Al-Fil (105)
Surah At-Takathur (102)
Surah Al-Masad (111)
explanationEn: Narrated in Al-Mustadrak (al-Hakim) & al-Bayhaqi (authenticated by al-Albani), reciting Surah Al-Kahf on Friday illuminates the week and recalls the Cave youths' dua (18:10).

questionEn: What two surahs did the Prophet ﷺ regularly recite in the Fajr prayer every Friday morning (Sahih al-Bukhari 891 / Muslim 879)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Mulk and Surah Al-Qalam
Surah Yusuf and Surah Nuh
Surah As-Sajdah (32) in the first rak‘ah and Surah Al-Insan (76) in the second rak‘ah
Surah Al-Kawthar and Surah Al-‘Asr
explanationEn: Starting Friday Fajr with creation, prostration, and the bliss of Paradise prepares the heart for Friday's special hour of dua.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in Sahih Muslim 854 regarding the blessings packed into Yawm al-Jumu‘ah (Friday)?
optionsEn: Duas on Friday count only inside Makkah
It is merely an ordinary workday without special virtues
Only morning hours before sunrise are blessed on Friday

It is the best day on which the sun has risen: on it Adam was created, on it he entered Paradise, on it he was sent to earth—and in it lies an hour when no Muslim prays asking Allah for good except He gives it!
explanationEn: Treating Friday afternoon—especially between ‘Asr and Maghrib—as an unmissable appointment for dua transforms weekly spirituality.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid fasting ONLY on Friday by itself unless paired with Thursday or Saturday (Sahih al-Bukhari 1985)?
optionsEn: Because Friday is a weekly Eid and day of joyful worship, prayer, gathering, and abundant dua/Salawat—so fasting it alone without Thursday or Saturday is discouraged
Because eating breakfast is mandatory before Jumu‘ah
Because Fridays have fewer prayers
Because fasting prevents sending Salawat
explanationEn: Honoring Friday as the believers' weekly celebration balances fasting with joy, perfume, bath (ghusl), and early mosque arrival.

questionEn: When entering a Friday congregation and finding the Imam already delivering the Khutbah, what brief Sunnah prayer should you still perform quietly before sitting down (Sahih al-Bukhari 930 / Muslim 875)?
optionsEn: Pray two brief, light rak‘ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid, then sit silently to listen attentively to the Khutbah
Sit down immediately without praying
Walk around shaking hands during the Khutbah
Recite tasbih aloud over the Imam's voice
explanationEn: Even when the Prophet ﷺ was speaking on the Minbar, he paused to tell a latecomer: 'Stand and pray two light rak‘ahs!'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ warn against even telling a noisy friend 'Be quiet!' (Sah) while the Imam is delivering the Friday Khutbah (Sahih al-Bukhari 934)?
optionsEn: Because speaking during the Khutbah causes you to lose the special reward of Jumu‘ah (laghawta)—listen silently and respond to the Imam's closing dua silently with 'Amin' in your heart!
Because Jumu‘ah requires loud applause
Because Khutbahs last only thirty seconds
Because friends are allowed to chat softly
explanationEn: Deep attentive silence during the Khutbah opens the heart to join the Imam's Friday dua cleanly.

questionEn: During Ramadan's spiritual retreat (I‘tikaf) in the last ten nights, what primary activities did the Prophet ﷺ focus on inside the Masjid (Sahih al-Bukhari 2024)?
optionsEn: He debated politics with visitors
He hosted loud worldly markets inside the mosque
He slept throughout the entire night until Dhuhr
He tightened his waist-wrapper, stayed awake through the nights in prayer, Qur'an, dhikr, and heartfelt dua, and woke his family gently to share in those blessed nights
explanationEn: Unplugging from worldly distractions during the last ten nights turns the Masjid—or a quiet home prayer corner—into a haven of munajat.

questionEn: What gentle encouragement in Sahih al-Bukhari 2014 applies to anyone praying Qiyam during Ramadan nights—and specifically on Laylat al-Qadr—with faith and hope of reward?
optionsEn: Reward applies only if you stay standing without sitting all night
Man qama Ramadana / Laylatal-Qadri imanan wahtisaban ghufira lahu ma taqaddama min dhanbih ('Whoever stands in prayer with faith and hoping for reward will have all his past sins forgiven!')
Past sins stay unforgiven until next year
Only scholars in Madinah receive pardon
explanationEn: Combining 'imanan' (sincere belief) and 'ihtisaban' (hoping solely for Allah's reward) unlocks complete cleansing.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ encourage hastening to break fast right at sunset (ta‘jil al-fitr) and delaying Suhoor toward dawn (ta'khir as-sahur) in Sahih al-Bukhari 1957?
optionsEn: Because fasting continues until stars appear
Because Suhoor is discouraged in Ramadan
Because sunset duas are invalid
Because people remain upon goodness so long as they hasten to break fast—taking water/dates right at sunset with sincere dua rather than delaying unnecessarily
explanationEn: Sharing dates and water at sunset while saying 'Dhahaba az-zama'u...' captures the joy of Sunnah obedience.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1923, what did the Prophet ﷺ call Suhoor ('Eat Suhoor, for indeed in Suhoor there is...')?
optionsEn: Barakah ('Indeed, in the pre-dawn meal there is blessing!')—coupled with Allah and His angels sending blessings upon those who eat Suhoor (Musnad Ahmad 11086)
Forbidden after midnight
A burden that weakens fasting
An optional habit only for athletes
explanationEn: Even a sip of water at Suhoor accompanied by pre-dawn Istighfar brings angelic prayers upon you!

questionEn: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise anyone who provides even a date, a sip of water, or a meal to break a fasting person's fast (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 807)?
optionsEn: It counts only if the meal costs silver
He loses half of his own fast's reward
He receives the exact same reward as the fasting person without diminishing the fasting person's reward in the slightest!
It applies only to family members
explanationEn: Sharing dates and water at your local masjid Iftar triggers countless grateful duas ('Aftara ‘indakumus-sa'imun...')!

questionEn: When using the Siwak (miswak tooth-stick) before Wudu, Salah, waking up, or reading the Qur'an, what spiritual pleasure did the Prophet ﷺ connect to this tiny hygiene Sunnah (Sunan an-Nasa'i 5 / Bukhari 887)?
optionsEn: It replaces Wudu completely
As-siwaku matharatun lil-fami mardatun lir-Rabb ('The Siwak is a purification for the mouth and a source of pleasure to the Lord!')
It is discouraged before prayer
It is used only once a year on Eid
explanationEn: Entering prayer and reciting Qur'an with a clean, fresh mouth honors Allah's words and the angels listening nearby.

questionEn: According to Sunan Abi Dawud 4855, what happens when people sit together in a social gathering and part without remembering Allah or sending Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Their past fasts are automatically doubled
That gathering will be a source of regret/shortcoming (hasrah / tirah) for them on the Day of Resurrection—unless rectified with Kaffarat al-Majlis
Only formal lectures need dhikr
Silence erases social kindness
explanationEn: Even adding 'SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdika...' at the end of a dinner chat or work meeting turns it into a blessed circle!

questionEn: What five mutual rights of a Muslim over another Muslim weave daily life into care and dua?
optionsEn: Avoiding all community invitations
Returning the Salam, visiting the sick, following funeral processions, accepting invitations, and saying 'YarhamukAllah' when someone sneezes and says Alhamdulillah
Competing over houses, ignoring sick neighbors, and avoiding greetings
Paying silver fines at every meeting
explanationEn: Notice how three of those five rights—Salam, Tashmit, and visiting the sick/Janazah—are literally built around making dua for one another!

questionEn: When walking through the streets and passing someone sitting or working, how did the Prophet ﷺ teach greetings of Salam should flow (Sahih al-Bukhari 6231)?
optionsEn: Wait silently until strangers salute first
Walk past elders without nodding or greeting
The rider greets the walker, the walker greets the one sitting, and the smaller group greets the larger group
Greet only close coworkers
explanationEn: Initiating 'As-salamu ‘alaykum' first frees the heart from pride—the Prophet ﷺ noted the closer person to Allah is the one who starts with Salam!

questionEn: What joyful spiritual promise did the Prophet ﷺ link to spreading Salam warmly among people who don't yet know each other well (Sahih Muslim 54)?
optionsEn: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not truly believe until you love one another—shall I guide you to something that, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread Salam among yourselves!
Avoid smiling in public streets
Greet only people in your own family
Keep silent unless formally introduced
explanationEn: Every 'As-salamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullah' is a real dua planting love between strangers.

questionEn: When shaking hands warmly upon meeting a brother or sister in faith, what gentle blessing happens before their hands separate (Sunan Abi Dawud 5212)?
optionsEn: No two Muslims meet and shake hands except that their sins are forgiven before they part!
Shaking hands invalidates Wudu
Only left-handed greetings count
Only kings shake hands after travel
explanationEn: Combining a warm handshake with 'As-salamu ‘alaykum' and a smile wipes away minor sins on the spot.

questionEn: What warning did the Prophet ﷺ give regarding two believers who stop speaking out of anger for more than three days?
optionsEn: Hold grudges for at least one full year
Wait for elders to apologize before speaking
It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother beyond three nights, each turning away when they meet; and the better of the two is the one who initiates the Salam first!
Never forgive minor slights
explanationEn: Offering the first 'As-salamu ‘alaykum' after a disagreement takes courage and wins the higher honor before Allah.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 2565, on which two days every week are human deeds presented before Allah—and who has forgiveness temporarily paused until reconciling?
optionsEn: Once a year in Muharram only
Every Wednesday and Saturday; only travelers are forgiven
Daily at noon regardless of grudges
Every Monday and Thursday; Allah forgives everyone who associates nothing with Him EXCEPT two people holding hostility against each other—Allah says: 'Leave these two until they reconcile!'
explanationEn: Remembering Monday and Thursday motivates clearing resentments swiftly and praying 'Rabbana la taj‘al fi qulubina ghillan lilladhina amanu'!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ love fasting Mondays and Thursdays alongside making extra dua on those days (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 747)?
optionsEn: Because only merchants fasted Thursdays
Because food was banned on Mondays
Because Tuesday prayers don't count
Because Monday was the day he was born and first received revelation, and Mondays and Thursdays are the days deeds are presented to Allah—so he loved his deeds being raised while fasting!
explanationEn: Pairing Monday/Thursday fasting with pre-sunset dua turns ordinary workweeks into weekly renewal.

questionEn: What merciful Prophetic teaching in Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim illustrates Allah's immense reward for kindness to animals and every living creature?
optionsEn: Animals feel nothing and deserve no care

Teaching that a woman was punished over starving a cat while a sinful person was forgiven all sins simply for giving water to a panting, thirsty dog—for 'in every living creature with a moist liver there is a reward for kindness!'
Only horses carry spiritual value
Kindness to animals brings zero reward
explanationEn: Placing a bowl of water outside in summer heat or caring gently for pets invites Allah's mercy upon our own prayers.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in Sahih al-Bukhari 2320 when a Muslim plants a tree or sows crops and birds, people, or animals eat from it?
optionsEn: It counts as charity only if sold for gold
Only date palms in Madinah count
Every single fruit or grain eaten from it is recorded for the planter as ongoing charity (Sadaqah)!
Birds eating fruit removes your reward
explanationEn: Combining 'Bismillah' when planting a garden or supporting green trees with grateful dua invests in lasting charity.

questionEn: During Hajj's Wadi Muhassar (between Muzdalifah and Mina), why did the Prophet ﷺ quicken his pace gently while continuing dhikr?
optionsEn: To race other pilgrims to tents
Out of mindful awe remembering it was the valley where Abraha's army of the Elephant met Allah's punishment—never lingering casually where Allah's wrath once fell
Because the road was paved with ice
Because Talbiyah was banned in valleys
explanationEn: Quickening step through places of past punishment while lingering calmly in places of mercy (Arafah, Muzdalifah, Safa/Marwah) shows spiritual sensitivity.

questionEn: When performing Umrah or Hajj in one of the three forms (Tamattu‘, Qiran, or Ifrad), how do their opening Talbiyah declarations differ?
optionsEn: Ifrad begins only after Eid
Tamattu‘ skips Ihram completely
Tamattu‘ says 'Labbayka ‘Umratan' (then later 'Labbayka Hajjan' on 8th Dhul-Hijjah); Ifrad says 'Labbayka Hajjan'; Qiran says 'Labbayka ‘Umratan wa Hajjan'
All three forbid saying Talbiyah
explanationEn: Clear intention with 'Labbayk' at the Miqat aligns every step of your pilgrimage smoothly.

questionEn: What three things did the Prophet ﷺ say wipe out sins like water puts out fire according to Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2616?
optionsEn: Arguing over tribal honors
Charity (as-sadaqah) extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire—paired with rising in the stillness of the night for Salah and dua!
Sleeping through afternoon prayers
Boasting loudly about fasts
explanationEn: Combining quiet charity with pre-dawn prayer turns repentance into action.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1423, how secretly should voluntary charity ideally be given so it earns Allah's Shade on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Only when cameras record every coin
Only to wealthy public leaders
Only after announcing amounts on stages
So secretly that your left hand does not know what your right hand has spent—alongside remembering Allah in solitude until your eyes overflow with tears!
explanationEn: Private tears in dua ('dhakarAllaha khaliyan fa-fadhat ‘aynah') and quiet charity are two of the seven traits shaded beneath Allah's Throne.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say 'Two eyes will never be touched by the Fire' in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1639?
optionsEn: Eyes that refused sleep for fame
Eyes that watched marketplace bargains
An eye that wept out of awe/fear of Allah ('aynun bakat min khashyatillah) and an eye that stayed awake guarding in the path of Allah
Eyes that avoided reading Qur'an
explanationEn: Even a single warm tear shed sincerely during private night dua carries immense value before Allah.

questionEn: When feeling ashamed that tears don't come easily during dua, what comforting counsel did early scholars and Sunnah texts teach?
optionsEn: Force loud dramatic wailing in public
Never fake tears for people—yet soften the heart by pondering Allah's favors, confessing sins honestly, reciting Qur'an slowly, and asking Allah humbly for a soft, tender heart (qalban khashi‘an)
Assume Allah hates dry eyes
Stop making dua unless you cry aloud
explanationEn: Sincerity matters far more than outward tears; asking 'Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min qalbin la yakhsha‘' gradually softens any stone-hard heart.

questionEn: What gentle dua did the Prophet ﷺ make asking Allah for emotional stability and contentment with lawful provision?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka Rabbana
Double my neighbor's bills
Let me chase every new luxury

Allahumma qanni‘ni bima razaqtani, wa barik li fih, wakhluf ‘alayya kulla gha'ibatin li bi-khayr ('O Allah, make me content with what You provided me, bless me in it, and replace every absent/lost blessing for me with good')
explanationEn: Reported from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) in Al-Mustadrak (al-Hakim 1878), praying for Qana‘ah (contentment) brings instant inner wealth.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, how did the Prophet ﷺ redefine true wealth (al-ghina) when people equated richness solely with bank balances?
optionsEn: Richness comes strictly from inherited gold
Richness means owning at least ten camels
Content people lose ambition to work
Laysal-ghina ‘an kathratil-‘arad, wa lakinnal-ghina ghinan-nafs ('Richness is NOT having abundant possessions; rather, true richness is richness/contentment of the soul!')
explanationEn: Praying for 'al-ghina' in 'Allahumma inni as'alukal-huda wat-tuqa wal-‘afafa wal-ghina' seeks this exact richness of soul.

questionEn: What short dua did the Prophet ﷺ advise looking toward in Sahih Muslim 2963 to protect gratitude and kill envy when scrolling or comparing lifestyles?
optionsEn: Compare your home daily to billionaires' palaces
Look at those who have LESS than you in worldly comfort, and do NOT look upward at those who have more—for that keeps you from belittling Allah's favors upon you!
Stop thanking Allah until your income triples
Complain whenever a friend buys a new car
explanationEn: And in spiritual matters—Salah, Qur'an, charity, dua—look upward at those striving harder so they inspire your soul!

questionEn: When starting a new job, project, or school year, what brief Prophetic habit pairs ambition with pure intention (Sahih al-Bukhari 1)?
optionsEn: Keeping motives purely for vanity
Skipping morning prayers during busy exams
Working hastily without Bismillah

Renewing intention purely for Allah ('Innamal-a‘malu bin-niyyat'), opening with 'Bismillah', reciting Musa's (AS) 'Rabbish-rah li sadri wa yassir li amri', and asking for '‘ilman nafi‘an wa rizqan tayyiba'
explanationEn: Pure niyyah converts study, coding, parenting, medicine, and trade into worship.

questionEn: When a student or writer faces a tough exam or complex problem and pauses briefly, what two short duas combine calm focus with divine help?
optionsEn: Ghufranaka
Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya
Prophet Musa's dua 'Rabbish-rah li sadri wa yassir li amri...' (20:25–28) alongside 'Allahumma la sahla illa ma ja‘altahu sahla, wa Anta taj‘alul-hazna idha shi'ta sahla'
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un
explanationEn: After studying diligently, trusting Allah to unlock clarity and ease removes exam panic.

questionEn: What short phrase protects against superstition when noticing unlucky numbers, black cats, broken mirrors, or bad omens (tiyarah)?
optionsEn: Cancel all trips on Tuesday the 13th
Turn back home if a bird flies left

Reject bad omens completely (no tiyarah in Islam!) and trust good hopefulness (al-fa'l—a kind, optimistic word); or say: 'Allahumma la khayra illa khayruk, wa la tayra illa tayruk, wa la ilaha ghayruk' (Ahmad 7045)
Carry lucky rabbit charms
explanationEn: Tawakkul liberates a believer from every superstitious fear of dates, birds, or omens!

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ love 'Al-Fa'l' (optimistic good words) while condemning 'Tiyarah' (superstitious bad omens) in Sahih al-Bukhari 5756?
optionsEn: Because optimism replaces effort
Because bad omens come from stars
Because hearing an encouraging word ('Good morning, O Successful one!') nurtures hopeful trust in Allah's mercy (husn az-zann billah), whereas bad omens breed paralyzing suspicion
Because silent pessimism is Sunnah
explanationEn: Speaking hopeful, faith-filled words uplifts others and mirrors trust in Ar-Rahman.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 7405 (Hadith Qudsi), what foundational rule governs how Allah treats a servant's expectations of Him?
optionsEn: Hope in Allah's mercy is discouraged
Expectations have zero role in dua
Allah treats servants strictly by pessimism
Ana ‘inda zanni ‘abdi bi ('I am as My servant expects/thinks of Me')—so expect abundant mercy, forgiveness, and answered dua from Al-Karim!
explanationEn: Having beautiful, hopeful expectation of Allah ('husn az-zann billah')—backed by obedience—opens extraordinary doors.

questionEn: When closing his prayers before saying Salam—right after Tashahhud and Salawat Ibrahimiyyah—did the Prophet ﷺ restrict worshippers to only one scripted dua?
optionsEn: No! After Tashahhud and Salawat, he explicitly said: 'Thumma li-yatakhayyar minad-du‘a'i a‘jabahu ilayhi fa-yad‘u' ('Then let him choose whatever supplication pleases him most and call upon Allah!')
Yes, only one four-word phrase is permitted
Only the Imam may make dua before Salam
Any personal prayer inside Tashahhud breaks Salah
explanationEn: That blessed minute right before Salam is one of the highest-ranked windows for personal dua in every single Salah!

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 588, what four-part refuge dua did the Prophet ﷺ urge saying right before Salam at the end of Tashahhud?
optionsEn: Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min ‘adhabi jahannam, wa min ‘adhabil-qabr, wa min fitnatil-mahya wal-mamat, wa min sharri fitnatil-masihid-dajjal
Ghufranaka
explanationEn: Notice how Tawus (the Tabi‘i) told his son to repeat his Salah if he omitted this protection dua—showing how seriously early Muslims cherished it!

questionEn: What gentle dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach in Sahih al-Bukhari 6389 when concluding a prayer or sitting, asking Allah for mercy that gathers scattered hearts?
optionsEn: Allahumma allif bayna qulubina, wa aslih dhata baynina—or reciting 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina ‘adhaban-nar'
Scatter neighbors into distant valleys
Wait until next season to reconcile
Remember only personal gains
explanationEn: Keeping both personal salvation and community unity inside our prayers reflects the Prophet's ﷺ own balanced heart.

questionEn: What brief morning or evening prayer did ‘A'ishah (RA) narrate the Prophet ﷺ often made asking Allah for easy reckoning?
optionsEn: Judge every slip with maximum severity
Exempt me from recording deeds

Allahumma hasibni hisaban yasira ('O Allah, reckon me with an easy reckoning!')—explaining that an easy reckoning means Allah merely looks at one's record and pardons without strict cross-examination!
Delay reckoning for ten thousand years
explanationEn: Because whoever is cross-examined in strict detail on Judgment Day is ruined, asking for 'hisaban yasira' inside Salah or dua is pure mercy.

questionEn: When walking out of a Masjid or finishing a night of Tahajjud in Makkah or Madinah, what should replace any worry that 'I didn't feel emotional enough'?
optionsEn: Remember that acceptance rests on Allah's generosity and sincerity, not emotional theatrics—keep asking humbly ('Rabbana taqabbal minna'), keep returning steadily, and trust As-Sami‘ Al-‘Alim!
Force loud cries for onlookers
Discard all daily adhkar
Assume all prayers were wasted and stop praying
explanationEn: Consistent, humble devotion—day after day, whether feelings soar or feel quiet—is what builds unshakeable nearness to Allah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in Sahih Muslim 2564 about Allah's gaze when evaluating our prayers, deeds, and duas?
optionsEn: Only eloquent accents reach heaven
Allah judges prayers by wardrobe elegance

InnAllaha la yanzuru ila suwarikum wa amwalikum, wa lakin yanzuru ila qulubikum wa a‘malikum ('Indeed Allah does not look at your outward appearances or your wealth, rather He looks at your hearts and your deeds!')
Allah values expensive prayer rugs above sincerity
explanationEn: Whether whispered in worn clothes or inside a grand mosque, a sincere heart captures Allah's gaze immediately.

questionEn: When teaching children to love Duas & Sunnah, what joyful Prophetic approach builds lifelong fondness instead of resentment?
optionsEn: Force toddlers to sit rigidly for two-hour lectures

Model cheerful short duas aloud together (Bismillah before snacks, Alhamdulillah after, travel dua in the car, 3 Quls at bedtime), praise their small efforts warmly, and make dua FOR them gently in their hearing!
Scold children harshly whenever they forget a phrase
Hide translations so children never know what they say
explanationEn: Children absorb the warmth of Sunnah naturally when parents pair tiny daily duas with hugs and encouragement.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ advise teachers and parents: 'Yassiru wa la tu‘assiru, wa bashshiru wa la tunaffiru'?
optionsEn: Make worship look intimidating and harsh
Refuse encouragement to beginners
Make things easy and do NOT make them difficult; give glad tidings and do NOT drive people away!
Overload newcomers on their very first day
explanationEn: Warm encouragement keeps hearts eager to return to Allah's remembrance day after day.

questionEn: What gentle dua asks Allah for protection against sudden evil of tongue, ear, eye, heart, and desires?
optionsEn: Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min sharri sam‘i, wa min sharri basari, wa min sharri lisani, wa min sharri qalbi, wa min sharri maniyyi
Allahumma barik lana fi ta‘amina
explanationEn: Narrated by Shakal ibn Humayd (RA) in Sunan Abi Dawud 1551 & Tirmidhi 3492, guarding all five sensory gateways keeps the heart clean for worship.

questionEn: When someone apologizes sincerely to you for hurting your feelings, what Prophetic reminder in Sahih Muslim 2588 encourages forgiving them while praying for peace?
optionsEn: Forgiving others makes you look weak
Ma zadaAllahu ‘abdan bi-‘afwin illa ‘izza ('Allah never increases a servant who pardons except in honor/dignity!')
Never pardon anyone who errs once
Hold apologies hostage for six months
explanationEn: Forgiving others mirrors our own plea 'Allahumma innaka ‘afuwwun tuhibbul-‘afwa fa‘fu ‘anni'—and elevates our honor before Allah!

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 2588, what three extraordinary assurances did the Prophet ﷺ swear to—including pardon, charity, and humility?
optionsEn: Humility invites disrespect permanently
Forgiving reduces reward
Hoarding doubles dignity and pride elevates hearts
Charity never decreases wealth; Allah increases a forgiving servant in honor; and whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him high!
explanationEn: Generosity, pardon, and humility form the golden trio of Prophetic character.

questionEn: What brief prayer asks Allah to protect us from turning backward after making spiritual progress?
optionsEn: Stop learning once you finish one course
Leave morning adhkar after Ramadan ends
Avoid good company in winter
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika minal-hawri ba‘dal-kawr ('O Allah, I seek refuge in You from decreasing/retreating after abundance/progress' — Sahih Muslim 1343 in Travel Dua!)
explanationEn: Found in ‘Abdullah ibn Sarjis's (RA) narration of the Travel Dua, 'al-hawri ba‘dal-kawr' warns against backsliding after spiritual highs like Ramadan or Hajj!

questionEn: In ‘Abdullah ibn Sarjis's (RA) Travel Dua (Sahih Muslim 1343), what touching phrase warns against being cursed or harmed by an oppressed person's cry?
optionsEn: And from sharing water with travelers
Wa da‘watil-mazlum ('and from the supplication of the oppressed')—alongside su'il-manzari fil-ahli wal-mal!
And from modest meals on journeys
And from walking briskly in sunlight
explanationEn: Praying never to wrong anyone—even unintentionally while tired on a trip—keeps us fair to drivers, cleaners, servers, and neighbors.

questionEn: What brief, joyful greeting did the Prophet ﷺ utter when entering his home to greet his wives and daughters—turning domestic life into warmth (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2698)?
optionsEn: Walking silently past family without greeting
Waiting for children to bow silently

Greeting everyone warmly with 'As-salamu ‘alaykum', asking how they are, and teaching Anas (RA): 'O my son, when you enter upon your family, say Salam—it will be a barakah upon you and upon the people of your house!'
Greeting only business colleagues outside
explanationEn: Starting every homecoming with a smiling 'As-salamu ‘alaykum' fills the home with peace and angelic blessing.

questionEn: When starting or ending the day, what simple reminder from Sahih Muslim 223 summarizes how Purity, Praise, Prayer, Charity, Patience, and Qur'an work together?
optionsEn: At-tuhuru shatrul-iman (Purity is half of faith), Alhamdulillah fills the Scale, SubhanAllah & Alhamdulillah fill heaven and earth, Salah is light, Sadaqah is proof, Sabr is radiance, and the Qur'an is a proof FOR you or against you!
Patience brings darkness to the soul
Outward cleanliness has nothing to do with faith
Dhikr carries negligible weight on the Scale
explanationEn: Living cleanly, gratefully, charitably, patiently, and prayerfully ties every Sunnah dua into one harmonious life.

questionEn: What concise Prophetic criterion in Sunan Abi Dawud 4681 defines perfection of faith through aligning love, dislike, giving, and withholding purely for Allah?
optionsEn: Withhold kindness whenever tired
Give only to win earthly applause
Love only according to tribal lineage

Man ahabba lillah, wa abghada lillah, wa a‘ta lillah, wa mana‘a lillah fa-qadistakmalal-iman ('Whoever loves for Allah, dislikes for Allah, gives for Allah, and withholds for Allah has perfected faith!')
explanationEn: Aligning motives purely 'lillah' (for Allah) turns relationships, charity, and boundaries into pure worship.

questionEn: When concluding a lifelong commitment to Duas & Sunnah, which short Prophetic prayer sums up seeking Allah's light across life, grave, and Resurrection (Sahih al-Bukhari 6316)?
optionsEn: Allahummaj‘al fi qalbi nura, wa fi basari nura, wa fi sam‘i nura, wa ‘an yamini nura, wa ‘an yasari nura, wa fawqi nura, wa tahti nura, wa amami nura, wa khalfi nura, waj‘al li nura
Allahumma barik lana fi asfarina
Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha
Ghufranaka Rabbana
explanationEn: Walking surrounded on all six sides—plus heart, tongue, sight, and hearing—by Allah's Light guides a believer safely home to Jannah.
